name: Abolition of the Punishment of Whipping Act, 1996

metadata.short_title: Abolition of the Punishment of Whipping Act, 1996
metadata.long_title: An Act to abolish and restrict the punishment of whipping
repeals: The Whipping Act, 1909(IV of 1909)
key_definitions: hadd: the punishment of crimes laid down in the Holy Quran and Sunnah
metadata.one_line: Abolishes whipping as a punishment except for hadd cases and repeals the Whipping Act, 1909.
metadata.summary: This Act abolishes the punishment of whipping under any existing law, rule, or regulation in Pakistan. It retains whipping only when awarded as 'hadd' based on the Holy Quran and Sunnah. Any unexecuted whipping sentences at the time of commencement are remitted, and the Whipping Act, 1909 is repealed.

metadata.short_title: The Acceding State (Property) Order, 1961
metadata.one_line: An Order by the President to decide property disputes involving acceding states and rulers.
metadata.summary: This Order empowers the Federal Government to decide questions regarding the devolution and distribution of property belonging to acceding states or their rulers. It excludes courts from jurisdiction over these specific disputes and allows for the recovery of money as land revenue arrears or attachment of other property. The Order applies retrospectively to August 15, 1947, but comes into force immediately.

name: Abolition of the Discretionary Quotas in Housing Schemes Act, 2013

metadata.short_title: The Abolition of the Discretionary Quotas in Housing Schemes Act, 2013
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the abolition of all discretionary quotas in housing schemes in the public sector
key_definitions: housing scheme in the public sector
metadata.one_line: Abolishes discretionary quotas in public sector housing schemes to ensure fair and transparent allotments.
metadata.summary: This Act abolishes all discretionary quotas in housing schemes within the public sector to ensure that plot allotments are made fairly, equitably, and transparently. It applies specifically to schemes owned, controlled, or financed by the Federal Government, its departments, agencies, state-owned enterprises, or where public funds are invested. The provisions override any inconsistent laws, rules, or policies, with immediate effect, while excluding specific categories such as widows, disabled persons in service, and their legal heirs.

metadata.short_title: The Abandoned Properties (Management) Act, 1975
metadata.long_title: An Act provide for the management of certain properties and for matters connected therewith
metadata.one_line: This Act provides for the management, vesting, and administration of abandoned properties in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: The Abandoned Properties (Management) Act, 1975 establishes a Board of Trustees and an Administrator to manage specific properties deemed abandoned. It vests such properties in the Federal Government from December 16, 1971, and outlines the powers of the Administrator to take possession, evaluate assets, and handle legal processes related to these properties. The Act also empowers the Federal Government to make rules for its administration and to exempt persons or properties from its provisions.

name: Access to the Media (Deaf) Persons Act, 2022

metadata.short_title: The Access to the Media (Deaf) Persons Act, 2022
metadata.long_title: An Act to ensure access of media to persons in all matters of public importance through Pakistan sign language
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to five years, or with fine which shall not be below one hundred thousand rupees per month or both
metadata.one_line: Ensures access to media for deaf persons via Pakistan sign language on all broadcast platforms.
metadata.summary: This Act ensures that deaf persons can access information in matters of public importance through Pakistan sign language on all broadcast media. It mandates the appointment of sign language interpreters by the Government and private media houses within six months and establishes a National Policy Board to oversee these efforts. The Act prohibits broadcasting news, programs, or advertisements without interpreters after specific timelines and prescribes penalties for violations.

name: Acting as Agents of Moallims (Prohibition) Ordinance, 1980

metadata.short_title: The Acting as Agents of Moallims (Prohibition) Ordinance, 1980
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to prohibit persons from acting as agents of Moallims.
metadata.max_penalty: simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine which may extend to five thousand rupees, or with both
metadata.one_line: Prohibits persons from acting as agents for Moallims and regulates their selection by intending Haj pilgrims.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance prohibits any person or group from acting as an agent, attorney, or representative of a Moallim. It also forbids soliciting the appointment of specific Moallims or influencing a pilgrim's choice to secure personal advantage. The Federal Government is empowered to publish a list of approved Moallims and make rules for carrying out the Ordinance's purposes.

metadata.short_title: The Administrator General's Act, 1913
metadata.long_title: An Act to consolidate and amend the Law relating to the office and duties of Administrator General.
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Federal Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, direct
repeals: The Schedule
metadata.one_line: This Act consolidates and amends the law regarding the office, duties, powers, and liabilities of the Administrator General in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: The Administrator General's Act, 1913 consolidates and amends laws concerning the office and duties of the Administrator General. It outlines the appointment, powers, and liabilities of the Administrator General regarding grants of letters of administration and probate, estate distribution, and audits. The Act also covers fees, the role of consular officers in specific cases, and savings for other relevant acts like the Succession Act.

name: Admiralty Jurisdiction of High Courts Ordinance, 1980

metadata.short_title: The Admiralty Jurisdiction of High Courts Ordinance, 1980
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to consolidate and amend the law relating to Courts of Admiralty
repeals: Courts of Admiralty (Pakistan) Act, 1891
Admiralty Court Act, 1840
Admiralty Court Act, 1861
metadata.one_line: Consolidates and amends admiralty law, defining High Court jurisdiction over maritime claims and repealing older acts.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance consolidates and amends the law relating to Courts of Admiralty in Pakistan. It grants specific Admiralty jurisdiction to the Sind, Baluchistan, Lahore, and Peshawar High Courts for various maritime causes including salvage, collision, and personal injury claims. The document defines key terms such as 'ship', 'master', and 'internal waters' and sets limitations on bringing actions for maritime liens. It also repeals earlier Admiralty Court Acts applicable in Pakistan.

name: Agha Khan University Examination Board Ordinance, 2002

metadata.short_title: The Agha Khan University Examination Board Ordinance, 2002
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to establish the Agha Khan University Examination Board
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Agha Khan University Examination Board to conduct national examinations and issue certifications.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Agha Khan University Examination Board to enhance educational standards in Pakistan. The Board is authorized to conduct examinations at all academic levels up to higher secondary, following the national curriculum, for both private candidates and government schools. It has the power to charge fees, issue recognized certificates, and make rules and regulations under the supervision of the Board of Trustees.

name: Agricultural Census Act, 1958 (Repealed by Act XiV of 2011 s.3(w.e.f 31-05-2011))

metadata.short_title: The Agricultural Census Act, 1958
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for certain matters for the purpose of taking agricultural census.
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Federal Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, appoint
repeals: Agricultural Census Act, 1958
metadata.status_evidence: (Repealed by Act XiV of 2011 s.3(w.e.f 31-05-2011))
metadata.max_penalty: fine which may extend to five hundred rupees
metadata.one_line: Provides for taking an agricultural census throughout Pakistan and defines the powers of census officers.
metadata.summary: This Act provides for the taking of an agricultural census in pursuance of a decision by the Food and Agricultural Organization of the United Nations. It empowers the Federal Government to appoint various census officers, define their duties, and collect specific information regarding land, crops, livestock, and agriculture. The Act outlines procedures for access to premises, penalties for obstruction or false returns, and provisions for the preparation of statistical abstracts.

name: Agricultural Development Bank of Pakistan (Reorganization and Conversion) Ordinance, 2002

metadata.short_title: The Agricultural Development Bank of Pakistan (Reorganization and Conversion) Ordinance, 2002
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for reorganization and conversion of the Agricultural Development Bank of Pakistan into a public limited company incorporated under the Companies Ordinance, 1984
repeals: Agricultural Development Bank Ordinance, 1961 (IV of 1961)
metadata.one_line: Reorganizes and converts the Agricultural Development Bank of Pakistan into a public limited company, transferring its assets and liabilities.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance provides for the reorganization and conversion of the Agricultural Development Bank of Pakistan (ADBP) into a public limited company under the Companies Ordinance, 1984. It mandates the transfer and vesting of all ADBP assets, contracts, liabilities, and proceedings to the new Company while exempting it from stamp duties. The Federal Government is empowered to issue orders specifying the effective date for these transfers and the subsequent dissolution of ADBP.

metadata.short_title: The Agricultural Produce Cess Act, 1940
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the levy and collection of a cess on certain agricultural products exported from Pakistan
metadata.one_line: This Act provides for the levy and collection of a cess on specific agricultural products exported from Pakistan.
metadata.summary: The Agricultural Produce Cess Act, 1940 establishes a customs duty of one-half of one per cent ad valorem on certain agricultural products exported from Pakistan. The Federal Government is empowered to vary duty rates, fix tariff values, and exclude specific articles from the Schedule via notification. The Act also provides mechanisms for the refund of duty in cases where goods are exported by land and subsequently re-imported into Pakistan.

metadata.short_title: The Agriculturists' Loans Act, 1884
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend and provide for the extension of the Northern India Takkavi Act, 1879.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of Pakistan (originally extended to Sind, Punjab, N.W.F.P., Sylhet; later amended for West Pakistan and specific areas)
repeals: Act X of 1879
sections 4 and 5 of Act XV of 1880
metadata.status_evidence: Section 3: '[Repeal of Act X of 1879, and sections 4 and 5 of Act XV of 1880.] Rep. by the Repealing Act, 1938 (I of 1938), s. 2 and Schedule.'
key_definitions: loans to owners and occupiers of arable land
metadata.one_line: Amends the Northern India Takkavi Act, 1879 and provides for agricultural loans and their recovery in British India provinces.
metadata.summary: This Act amends and extends the Northern India Takkavi Act, 1879 to various provinces of British India. It empowers Provincial Governments to make rules regarding agricultural loans for distress relief or purchasing seed/cattle. Loans made under these rules are recoverable as arrears of land revenue, and joint borrowers' internal liabilities are defined by signed statements.

metadata.short_title: The Agricultural Produce (Grading and Marking) Act, 1937
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the grading and marking of agricultural [and other] produce.
metadata.max_penalty: rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both
metadata.one_line: Provides for the grading and marking of agricultural produce with penalties for unauthorized or incorrect marking.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes a framework for the grading and marking of agricultural produce to ensure quality standards. It empowers the appropriate Government to prescribe grade designations and marks through rules made under the Act. The legislation imposes penalties for unauthorized marking, incorrect marking, and counterfeiting grade designation marks. It applies to the whole of Pakistan and covers various scheduled articles including fruits, vegetables, dairy products, and others.

metadata.short_title: The Agricultural Pesticides Ordinance, 1971
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to regulate the import, manufacture, formulation, sale, distribution and use of pesticides.
metadata.one_line: Regulates the import, manufacture, sale, and use of pesticides in Pakistan through registration and inspection.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance regulates the import, manufacture, formulation, sale, distribution, and use of pesticides to ensure safety and uniformity. It establishes a registration system for pesticides, requiring applications and fees before they can be sold or used. The law creates an Agriculture Pesticide Technical Advisory Committee and a Pesticide Laboratory to oversee testing and analysis. It also defines various terms related to pesticides and sets out offences and penalties for violations such as adulteration or unregistered sales.

metadata.short_title: The Air University Ordinance, 2002
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the establishment of the Air university at Islamabad and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Air University at Islamabad comprising constituent units managed by the Pakistan Air Force.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Air University at Islamabad as a body corporate with perpetual succession. It incorporates existing degree colleges and service institutions managed by the Pakistan Air Force as constituent units. The document defines the purposes, powers, functions, and governing bodies of the University, including the Board of Governors, Academic Council, and various committees.

name: AirCraft (Removal of Danger to Safety) Ordinance, 1965

metadata.short_title: The Aircraft (Removal of Danger to Safety) Ordinance, 1965
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to make provision for the removal of danger to the safety of aircraft.
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to ten thousand rupees, or with both
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance empowers the Federal Government to remove dangers to aircraft safety caused by bird-attracting sites.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance provides for the removal of danger to the safety of aircraft caused by bird-attracting sites around airfields. It authorizes the Federal Government to issue orders requiring owners or controllers of specific locations, such as tanneries and slaughter-houses, to take measures to avoid attracting birds. The Ordinance also restricts the construction or extension of these facilities within specified areas without prior permission and outlines penalties for non-compliance.

metadata.short_title: The Airports Security Force Act, 1975
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the constitution and regulation of the Airports Security Force.
metadata.territorial_extent: all aerodromes and airports, all civil aviation stations, centres or offices in Pakistan, all Pakistan air services and activities relating to civil aviation
establishes: Director General of the Airports Security Force
metadata.one_line: This Act provides for the constitution, regulation, and functions of the Airports Security Force to ensure civil aviation security.
metadata.summary: The Airports Security Force Act, 1975 establishes the Airports Security Force under the Federal Government to ensure security at airports, aerodromes, and aircraft. It defines the force's functions, including safeguarding against unlawful interference and maintaining law and order within airport limits. The Act outlines the constitution of the force, the appointment of a Director General, and the powers to make rules and regulations for its administration.

metadata.short_title: The Akhuwat Institute Kasur Act, 2026
metadata.long_title: An Act for the establishment of Akhuwat Institute Kasur and to provide for matters connected therewith and ancillary thereto
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Akhuwat Institute Kasur as a body corporate with academic and administrative autonomy.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Akhuwat Institute Kasur as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal. It grants the Institute academic, financial, and administrative autonomy to employ staff, acquire property, and manage its affairs independently. The Act defines various authorities including the Board of Directors, Board of Governors, and Academic Council, outlining their powers and functions. It also provides for the creation of an Institute Fund, mechanisms for making Statutes and Regulations, and a Discipline Committee to handle student conduct complaints.

metadata.short_title: The Al-Karam International Institute Act, 2021
metadata.long_title: An act to provide for the establishment of the Al-Karam International institute in the private sector for promotion of special studies and for matters ancillary thereto
establishes: Board of Advanced Studies and Research
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Al-Karam International Institute in the private sector with academic autonomy for special studies.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Al-Karam International Institute as a body corporate in the private sector to promote special studies, particularly in Islamic Shariah. The Institute is granted academic, financial, and administrative autonomy, including the power to employ staff and manage property. It creates various governing bodies such as the Senate, Syndicate, and Academic Council to oversee functions like curriculum development, examinations, and financial planning.

metadata.short_title: The Allama Iqbal Open University Act, 1974
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of an Allama lqbal Open University at Islamabad.
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Allama Iqbal Open University at Islamabad and defines its powers, officers, and authorities.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Allama Iqbal Open University (originally named People's Open University) as a specialized educational institution with its principal seat at Islamabad. It defines the university's structure, including its Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, Executive Council, and Academic Council, and outlines their respective powers and duties. The legislation also provides for the creation of various committees to oversee academic planning, finance, and development, while granting the university the power to acquire property and make rules consistent with the Act.

metadata.short_title: The Allied Health Professionals Council Act, 2022
metadata.long_title: An Act to make the provisions for the establishment of the Allied Health Professionals Council
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Allied Health Professionals Council to regulate qualifications, registration, and practice of allied health professionals in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Allied Health Professionals Council (AHP Council) to set uniform standards for basic and higher qualifications in various allied health disciplines. It provides for the registration and licensing of allied health professionals, recognizes institutions and foreign qualifications, and regulates education, training, and practice to ensure public health safety. The Council is empowered to make rules regarding fees, codes of conduct, quality assurance, and inspection of healthcare establishments.

metadata.short_title: The Allopathic System (Prevention of Misuse) Ordinance, 1962
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to prevent the misuse of the allopathic system of medicine and to provide for matters connected therewith.
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment which may extend to one year or with fine not exceeding two thousand rupees, or with both
metadata.one_line: Prevents misuse of allopathic medicine by regulating titles, degrees, surgeries, prescriptions, and drug sales.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance prevents the misuse of the allopathic system of medicine by prohibiting unqualified persons from using the title 'doctor', displaying medical degrees, performing surgeries (except minor ones), prescribing antibiotics, or selling certain medicines without proper labeling. It empowers the Provincial Government to make rules and imposes penalties including imprisonment up to one year or fines for violations. Prosecutions are restricted to specific inspectors or authorized persons.

metadata.short_title: The Alternative Dispute Resolution Act, 2017
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for alternative dispute resolution
repeals: Section 89A of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (Act V of 1908)
metadata.one_line: Establishes an ADR system in Islamabad for resolving civil disputes through arbitration, mediation, and conciliation.
metadata.summary: This Act provides a framework for alternative dispute resolution (ADR) within the Islamabad Capital Territory to ensure inexpensive and expeditious justice. It mandates courts to refer eligible civil matters listed in the Schedule to ADR processes unless specific exceptions apply. The Act establishes panels of neutrals comprising lawyers, judges, and experts, and allows for referrals to designated ADR Centres. It defines various ADR mechanisms including arbitration, mediation, and conciliation, while also repealing Section 89A of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.

name: Alternative Energy Development Board Act, 2010 (Repealed by Act No.XXVI of 2023)

metadata.short_title: Alternative Energy Development Board Act, 2010
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for establishment of Alternative Energy Development Board
metadata.status_evidence: Alternative Energy Development Board Act, 2010 (Repealed by Act No.XXVI of 2023)
establishes: Institute of Alternative and Renewable Energy Technologies
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Alternative Energy Development Board as an autonomous body for renewable energy development.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Alternative Energy Development Board (AEDB) as an autonomous body to implement policies and projects in alternative or renewable energy technologies. The Board aims to facilitate sustainable economic growth through technology transfer and generation of alternative energy across Pakistan. It defines the Board's composition, including government nominees and private sector experts, and outlines its administrative and financial powers.

metadata.short_title: The Anand Marriage Act, 1909
metadata.long_title: An Act to remove doubts as to the validity of the marriage ceremony common among the Sikhs called Anand.
metadata.one_line: Validates Sikh Anand marriages and exempts non-Sikhs or prohibited degree unions.
metadata.summary: This Act validates marriage ceremonies solemnized according to the Sikh tradition known as Anand. It applies to the whole of Pakistan but excludes marriages involving non-Sikhs or those already declared null and void. The legislation also preserves the validity of other customary Sikh marriage ceremonies while ensuring that prohibited degrees of relationship remain invalid.

metadata.short_title: The Anti Narcotics Force Act, 1997
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the constitution of Anti Narcotics Force
metadata.one_line: This Act constitutes the Anti Narcotics Force to investigate narcotics offences and prosecute related crimes.
metadata.summary: The Anti Narcotics Force Act, 1997 establishes a specialized force under the superintendence of the Federal Government to investigate and prosecute narcotics-related offences. The Force consists of a Director-General appointed by the Federal Government and other officials who possess police powers throughout Pakistan for search, arrest, and seizure. It merges previous entities like the Pakistan Narcotics Control Board and Anti-Narcotics Task Force, granting them successor status in all cases and assets. The Act outlines specific functions including asset tracing, international liaison, and coordination of poppy cultivation elimination projects, while also providing a framework for internal disciplinary punishments.

metadata.short_title: The Anti-Terrorism Act, 1997
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the prevention of terrorism, sectarian violence and for speedy trial of heinous offences;
metadata.one_line: An Act to prevent terrorism and sectarian violence in Pakistan and establish Anti-terrorism Courts for speedy trials.
metadata.summary: This Act provides legal mechanisms to prevent terrorism and sectarian violence within Pakistan. It establishes specialized Anti-terrorism Courts with specific powers to try heinous offences related to abduction, use of explosives in places of worship, and other terrorist acts. The legislation also outlines procedures for the proscription of organizations, seizure of funds, and cooperation with police forces.

metadata.short_title: The Anti Dumping Duties Act, 2015
metadata.long_title: An Act to reform and repeal the Anti Dumping Duties Ordinance, 2000
repeals: Anti Dumping Duties Ordinance, 2000
metadata.one_line: This Act establishes the framework for imposing anti-dumping duties on imported goods causing injury to domestic industry.
metadata.summary: The Anti Dumping Duties Act, 2015 reforms and consolidates the law regarding the imposition of anti-dumping duties in Pakistan. It provides a comprehensive framework for investigating dumping and injury in respect of goods imported into the country. The Act establishes an Appellate Tribunal to hear appeals and outlines procedures for provisional measures, price undertakings, and the duration of duties.

name: Anti-Dumping Duties Ordinance, 2000 (Repealed by Act XIV of 2015)

metadata.short_title: The Anti-Dumping Duties Ordinance, 2000
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend and consolidate the Law relating to imposition of anti dumping duties to offset such dumping, to provide a framework for investigation and determination of dumping and injury in respect of goods imported into Pakistan and for matters ancillary thereto or connected therewith.
amends: General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade, 1994
repeals: Anti-Dumping Duties Ordinance, 2000 (Repealed by Act XIV of 2015)
metadata.status_evidence: [Repealed by Act XIV of 2015]
metadata.one_line: An Ordinance to amend and consolidate laws on anti-dumping duties, investigations, and injury determination in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends and consolidates the law regarding the imposition of anti-dumping duties to offset injurious dumping in Pakistan. It provides a framework for investigating dumping and injury related to imported goods, aligning with World Trade Organization provisions. The document establishes procedures for price undertakings, provisional measures, and the review of duties, administered by the National Tariff Commission.

metadata.short_title: Anti-Money Laundering Act, 2010
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for prevention of money laundering
metadata.one_line: This Act prevents money laundering, combats terrorism financing, and establishes mechanisms for property forfeiture and international cooperation.
metadata.summary: The Anti-Money Laundering Act, 2010 provides a comprehensive framework to prevent money laundering and combat the financing of terrorism within Pakistan. It establishes key bodies such as the National Executive Committee and the Financial Monitoring Unit to oversee reporting entities and conduct investigations. The Act defines specific offences, outlines procedures for attaching and forfeiting property derived from illicit activities, and mandates customer due diligence and record-keeping obligations for financial institutions and designated non-financial businesses.

metadata.short_title: The Anti-Rape (Investigation and Trial) Act, 2021
metadata.long_title: An Act to ensure expeditious redressal of rape and sexual abuse crimes in respect of women and children through special investigation teams and special Courts providing for efficacious procedures, speedy trial, evidence and matters connected therewith or incidental thereto;
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Federal Government may appoint
metadata.one_line: Establishes special courts and crisis cells to ensure speedy trial and redressal for rape and sexual abuse crimes.
metadata.summary: This Act ensures the expeditious redressal of rape and sexual abuse crimes against women and children. It establishes Special Courts, Anti-rape Crisis Cells in public hospitals, and a Fund for victim support. The Act provides for special procedures, evidence rules, witness protection, and preventive police actions to handle scheduled offences efficiently.

metadata.short_title: The Antiquities Act, 1975
metadata.long_title: An Act to repeal and re enact the law relating to the preservation and protection of antiquities.
repeals: The law relating to the preservation and protection of antiquities
metadata.max_penalty: fine which may extend to two hundred thousand rupees
metadata.one_line: This Act repeals and re-enacts laws for preserving, protecting, and regulating the trade and export of antiquities in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: The Antiquities Act, 1975 repeals and re-enacts previous laws regarding the preservation and protection of antiquities. It defines various terms related to antiquities, establishes an Advisory Committee and a Director General, and grants powers for inspection, acquisition, and licensing. The Act prohibits unauthorized excavation, export, and destruction of antiquities while providing penalties for offenses.

metadata.short_title: The Apostille Act, 2024
metadata.long_title: An Act to give effect to the Convention on abolishing the requirement of legalization for the foreign public documents and for matters connected therewith
metadata.one_line: This Act gives effect to the Hague Apostille Convention for certifying foreign public documents in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: The Apostille Act, 2024 implements the Hague Convention of 1961 to abolish legalization requirements for foreign public documents. It empowers the Federal Government to designate competent authorities and set fees for issuing apostille certificates. The Act ensures that certification authenticates document origins rather than contents, while allowing non-recognition of documents contrary to Islamic law or national interests.

name: Apprenticeship Ordinance, 1962 (Repeal by Act I of 2019,s.18)

metadata.short_title: The Apprenticeship Ordinance, 1962
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to make provision for promoting, developing and regulating systematic apprenticeship programmes in the industries and for securing certain minimum standards of skill.
metadata.commencement: on such date or dates and in respect of such undertakings as the Provincial Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, appoint
metadata.status_evidence: [Repeal. Omitted by the Federal Laws (Revision and Declaration) Ordinance, 1981 (XXVII of 1981), s. 3 and Sch., II.] [Catalogue Entry: Repeal by Act I of 2019,s.18]
establishes: Provincial and Regional Tripartite Advisory Committees
metadata.one_line: Promotes and regulates apprenticeship programmes in industries to secure minimum skill standards.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance provides for the promotion, development, and regulation of systematic apprenticeship programmes across industries. It establishes minimum standards of skill and defines the obligations of employers, including training proportions and costs. The Provincial Government is empowered to constitute advisory committees, appoint competent authorities, and make rules to carry out the Ordinance's purposes.

metadata.short_title: The Arbitration (International Investment Disputes) Act, 2011
metadata.long_title: An Act to implement the International Convention on the Settlement of Investment Disputes between States and Nationals of other States
repeals: Arbitration Act, 1940
metadata.one_line: Implements the ICSID Convention in Pakistan for registering and enforcing international investment dispute awards.
metadata.summary: This Act implements the International Convention on the Settlement of Investment Disputes between States and Nationals of other States. It provides for the registration of awards rendered pursuant to the Convention in the High Court, granting them the same force and effect as a judgment. The Act binds the Government regarding these awards, except where the Government is not a party, and charges necessary expenses on the Government budget. It excludes the application of the Arbitration Act, 1940 to proceedings under this Convention.

metadata.short_title: The Arbitration Act, 1940
metadata.long_title: An Act to consolidate and amend the law relating to Arbitration.
repeals: THE THIRD SCHEDULE
THE FOURTH SCHEDULE
metadata.one_line: This Act consolidates and amends the law relating to arbitration in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: The Arbitration Act, 1940 consolidates and amends the law relating to arbitration in Pakistan. It provides for the appointment of arbitrators, the authority of appointed arbitrators, and the powers of courts in relation to arbitration proceedings. The Act also covers the making of awards, the setting aside of awards, and the enforcement of awards.

name: Archival Material (Preservation and Export Control) Act, 1975

metadata.short_title: The Archival Material (Preservation and Export Control) Act, 1975
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the preservation, and control of the export, of archival material
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to three months, or with fine which may extend to five thousand rupees, or with both
metadata.one_line: This Act preserves archival material and controls its export from Pakistan via licensing.
metadata.summary: This Act provides for the preservation and control of the export of archival material of national significance. It defines archival material as documents at least twenty-five years old with historical significance to Pakistan. The Director, with Advisory Committee approval, manages purchases, gifts, and grants export licences. Penalties include imprisonment up to three months or fines for unauthorized exports.

metadata.short_title: The Area Study Centres Act, 1975
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of Area Study Centres in the Universities for the study of contemporary societies particularly those which effect the national interest of Pakistan.
metadata.one_line: Establishes Area Study Centres in universities for research and teaching on contemporary societies affecting national interest.
metadata.summary: This Act provides for the establishment of Area Study Centres within universities to study contemporary societies relevant to Pakistan's national interest. It outlines the functions of these centres, including high-level teaching, research training, and program development. The Act establishes a Board of Governors for management and an Academic Committee for academic oversight, with funding sourced from federal grants, provincial contributions, and donations.

metadata.short_title: The Armed Forces (Emergency Duties) Act, 1947
metadata.long_title: An Act to enable duties in connection with vital services to be imposed in an emergency on the Armed Forces of Pakistan.
repeals: The Armed Forces (Emergency Duties) Act, 1947
metadata.status_evidence: [Repealed by the Federal Laws (Revision and Declaration) Act, 1951 (XXVI of 1951), s. 3 and Second Schedule]
metadata.repealed_by: The Federal Laws (Revision and Declaration) Act, 1951
metadata.one_line: Enables the Federal Government to impose emergency duties on Armed Forces for vital services.
metadata.summary: This Act empowers the Federal Government to declare specific services as vital during emergencies and impose duties on the Armed Forces. It mandates that personnel subject to relevant military acts must obey commands related to these declared services, treating such commands as lawful under their respective statutes. The notification remains in force for one month initially but can be extended by further notifications.

name: Armed Forces Civil General Transport Companies and Requisition of Civil Transport Ordinance, 2002

metadata.short_title: The Armed Forces Civil General Transport Companies and Requisition of Civil Transport Ordinance, 2002
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for raising of civil general transport companies and for requisition of civil transport for the Armed Forces
metadata.commencement: at once and shall be deemed to have taken effect on the twenty-third day of December, 2001
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance empowers the Federal Government to raise civil general transport companies and requisition civil transport for the Armed Forces.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance provides legal authority for the raising of civil general transport companies and the requisition of civil transport specifically for the Armed Forces. It allows these actions to be taken at short notice, even prior to a formal declaration of emergency, to meet logistical requirements. The Prescribed Authority within the Ministry of Defence is empowered to exercise these powers, with provisions for compensation to owners of requisitioned transport.

metadata.short_title: The Arms Act, 1878
metadata.long_title: An Act to consolidate and amend the law relating to Arms, Ammunition and Military Stores.
metadata.commencement: on such day as the Federal Government by notification in the official Gazette appoints
repeals: The Repealing Act, 1938 (I of 1938)
The Amending Act, 1891 (XII of 1891)
metadata.one_line: Consolidates and amends laws regarding arms, ammunition, military stores, licensing, import/export, and penalties.
metadata.summary: This Act consolidates and amends the law relating to arms, ammunition, and military stores in Pakistan. It regulates the manufacture, conversion, sale, import, export, transport, possession, and carrying of these items, requiring licenses for most activities. The Act establishes powers for the Federal Government to create searching stations and imposes penalties for breaches of its provisions.

metadata.short_title: The Arya Marriage Validation Act, 1937
metadata.long_title: An Act to recognise and remove doubts as to the validity of intermarriages current among Arya Samajists.
metadata.one_line: Validates intermarriages among Arya Samajists regardless of caste, sub-caste, or prior religious affiliation.
metadata.summary: This Act recognizes and removes doubts regarding the validity of marriages among Arya Samajists. It declares that such marriages are not invalid based on differences in caste, sub-caste, or if parties belonged to a non-Hindu religion before the marriage. The legislation applies to all citizens of Pakistan wherever they may be.

metadata.short_title: The Asaan Karobar Act, 2025
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for reforms of the regulatory regime applicable to business, trade and investment by removing cumbersome and complex regulatory requirements and to establish the Pakistan Regulatory Registry and the Pakistan Business Portal.
metadata.max_penalty: three hundred thousand Rupees and such other penalties as may be prescribed, including termination of appointment
metadata.one_line: This Act establishes the Pakistan Regulatory Registry and Business Portal to reform the regulatory regime for business, trade, and investment.
metadata.summary: The Asaan Karobar Act, 2025 aims to simplify the regulatory environment for businesses by removing complex requirements. It establishes the Pakistan Regulatory Registry and the Pakistan Business Portal to manage laws and regulations. The Act creates the Asaan Karobar Technical Unit to review existing laws and propose amendments or repeals based on regulatory impact assessments. Government Agencies are required to comply with these reforms, while specific entities like courts and law enforcement remain exempt.

metadata.short_title: The Asian Development Bank Ordinance, 1971
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to implement the international agreement for the establishment and operation of the Asian Development Bank and for matters connected therewith.
metadata.commencement: at once; deemed to have taken effect from 19th December, 1966
metadata.one_line: Implements the international agreement for establishing and operating the Asian Development Bank in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance implements the international agreement for the establishment and operation of the Asian Development Bank. It grants the Bank full juridical personality, immunity from legal process (with exceptions), and exemption from taxation within Pakistan. The Federal Government is responsible for financial provisions and making rules to carry out the Ordinance's purposes.

metadata.short_title: The Assets Declaration Act, 2019
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for voluntary declaration of undisclosed assets, sales and expenditure
repeals: The Assets Declaration Ordinance, 2019 (III of 2019)
metadata.one_line: Provides for voluntary declaration of undisclosed assets, sales and expenditure to encourage tax compliance.
metadata.summary: This Act facilitates the voluntary declaration of undisclosed assets, sales, and expenditure held domestically or abroad up to June 30, 2018. It establishes specific valuation methods for these assets and imposes corresponding taxes and default surcharges based on the timing of payment. The legislation aims to integrate the non-documented economy into the taxation system to support economic revival while ensuring confidentiality for declarants.

metadata.short_title: The Associated Cement (Vesting) Act, 1974
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the vesting of the Associated Cement in the State Cement Corporation of Pakistan Limited.
establishes: State Cement Corporation of Pakistan Limited
metadata.administering_body: State Cement Corporation of Pakistan Limited
metadata.one_line: This Act vests Associated Cement assets and liabilities in the State Cement Corporation of Pakistan Limited.
metadata.summary: The Associated Cement (Vesting) Act, 1974 provides for the transfer of Associated Cement undertakings from the Federal Government to the State Cement Corporation of Pakistan Limited. It details the continuation of employee services with favorable terms, the treatment of provident funds, and the recognition of federal investments as corporate equity. The Act also grants the Corporation powers to administer the cement assets while providing indemnity for actions taken in good faith under the legislation.

name: Associated Press of Pakistan (Taking over) Ordinance, 1961(Repeal by ordinance 20 of 2002,s.23))

metadata.short_title: Associated Press of Pakistan (Taking Over) Ordinance, 1961
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to enable the Central Government to take over the Associated Press of Pakistan Limited.
key_definitions: Associated Press (the company registered on the 28th day of May, 1960)
metadata.one_line: Enables the Federal Government to take over and manage the Associated Press of Pakistan Limited.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance empowers the Central Government to take over the Associated Press of Pakistan Limited due to its administrative and financial breakdown. Upon taking over, the company is dissolved, and all its assets, liabilities, and contracts are transferred to the Federal Government. The government is authorized to manage the undertaking as a separate institution to ensure free news flow and stability.

name: Associated Press of Pakistan Corporation Ordinance, 2002

metadata.short_title: Associated Press of Pakistan Corporation Ordinance, 2002
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for reconstitution of the Associated Press of Pakistan
repeals: Associated Press of Pakistan (Taking over) Ordinance, 1961
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance reconstitutes the Associated Press of Pakistan as a corporation with enhanced professionalism and autonomy.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance provides for the reconstitution of the Associated Press of Pakistan to ensure effective operation and streamline its functions as a public information medium. It establishes the Associated Press of Pakistan Corporation as a body corporate with perpetual succession, granting it powers to collect, transmit, and circulate news both within Pakistan and abroad. The document outlines the establishment of a Board of Directors, defines the functions of the corporation including research, training, and international agreements, and repeals the previous Associated Press of Pakistan (Taking over) Ordinance, 1961.

name: Auditor General´s (Functions, Powers, Terms and Conditions of Service) Ordinance, 2001

metadata.short_title: The Auditor General's (Functions, Powers and Terms and Conditions of Service) Ordinance, 2001
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to determine the terms and conditions of service, the term of office and the powers and functions of the Auditor General of Pakistan
repeals: The Pakistan (Audit and Accounts) Order, 1973
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance defines the terms, powers, and functions of the Auditor General of Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance determines the terms and conditions of service, term of office, and powers for the Auditor General of Pakistan. It applies to the whole of Pakistan and establishes the Auditor General's authority to certify accounts, audit federal and provincial expenditures, and audit public sector companies. The document also outlines salary structures, leave provisions, and the power to make rules and regulations.

metadata.short_title: The Auqaf (Federal Control) (Repeal) Ordinance, 1979
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to repeal the Auqaf (Federal Control) Act, 1976 and to provide for matters incidental thereto
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of Pakistan, except the Islamabad Capital Territory
metadata.commencement: on such day as the Federal Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, specify
repeals: Auqaf (Federal Control) Act, 1976
metadata.one_line: Repeals the Auqaf (Federal Control) Act, 1976 and transfers waqf administration to Provinces.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance repeals the Auqaf (Federal Control) Act, 1976 to transfer control of waqf property from the Federal Administrator-General to the respective Provincial Governments. It provides for the immediate vesting of rights, assets, and liabilities in the provinces where the property is situated and deems prior contracts made by the Administrator-General to be made on behalf of the Province. The Ordinance also authorizes the Federal Government to allocate specific officers to the Provinces and make necessary orders to remove any difficulties arising from the transfer.

metadata.short_title: The Bahria University Ordinance, 2000
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the establishment of Bahria University at Islamabad and to provide for the matters connected therewith or incidental thereto
metadata.one_line: Establishes Bahria University Islamabad as a fully autonomous body with perpetual succession.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Bahria University at Islamabad as a body corporate with perpetual succession. It grants the University full autonomy to govern its academic and administrative functions, including determining courses of study and awarding degrees. The document defines various authorities such as the Board of Governors, Executive Committee, and Academic Council, outlining their composition and powers.

metadata.short_title: The Bankers' Books Evidence Act, 1891
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Law of Evidence with respect to Bankers' Books.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Law of Evidence regarding the admissibility and inspection of bankers' books in legal proceedings.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Law of Evidence specifically concerning Bankers' Books. It defines key terms such as 'bank', 'banker', and 'bankers' books', which include various ledgers and account books used in ordinary banking business. The legislation establishes that certified copies of entries in a banker's book are admissible as prima facie evidence in all legal proceedings. Furthermore, it grants Courts or Judges the power to order the inspection of these books by parties involved in a proceeding and outlines provisions regarding costs associated with applications under the Act.

metadata.short_title: The Banking Companies Ordinance, 1962
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to consolidate and amend the law relating to banking companies
metadata.max_penalty: Upto Rs. 1,000,000 per day during which the default continues
metadata.one_line: Consolidates and amends laws relating to banking companies, licensing, supervision, and winding up in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance consolidates and amends the law regarding banking companies in Pakistan. It establishes the regulatory framework for banking business, including capital requirements, deposit rules, and the role of the State Bank of Pakistan in supervision and resolution. The document also covers provisions for Islamic banking, winding up procedures, and penalties for non-compliance.

metadata.short_title: The Banking Tribunals (Validation of Orders) Act, 1994
metadata.long_title: An Act to validate certain order passed by the Banking Tribunals
metadata.one_line: Validates orders passed by Banking Tribunals under the 1992 Amendment Act prior to this Act's commencement.
metadata.summary: This Act validates certain orders, judgments, decisions, proceedings, and recoveries made by the Banking Tribunal before its commencement. It applies to actions taken under the Banking Tribunals (Amendment) Act, 1992. The validation is deemed to have always been valid despite any contrary court order or decision.

metadata.short_title: The Banks (Nationalization) Act, 1974
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the nationalization of banking business in Pakistan.
repeals: Ordinance I of 1974
establishes: Board of Directors constituted under this Act
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to five years, or with fine or with both
metadata.one_line: This Act nationalizes all banking business in Pakistan, transferring ownership to the Federal Government.
metadata.summary: The Banks (Nationalization) Act, 1974 provides for the immediate transfer of ownership, management, and control of all banks in Pakistan to the Federal Government. It defines 'bank' to include various registered companies and specific institutions while excluding cooperative and government savings banks. The Act outlines provisions for compensating shareholders, dissolving existing banking councils, and adapting other laws to align with the nationalization process.

name: Banks (Transfer of Assets and Liabilities) Act, 1974

metadata.short_title: The Banks (Transfer of Assets and Liabilities) Act, 1974
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the transfer to the National Bank of Pakistan of certain assets and liabilities of the Eastern Mercantile Bank Limited and the Eastern Banking Corporation Limited.
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both
key_definitions: undertaking of a specified office or branch
metadata.one_line: Transfers assets and liabilities of two specific banks to the National Bank of Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Act provides for the transfer of certain assets and liabilities from the Eastern Mercantile Bank Limited and the Eastern Banking Corporation Limited to the National Bank of Pakistan. It vests all specified offices and branches in the National Bank, ensuring that existing contracts and legal proceedings continue against or in favor of the National Bank. The Federal Government retains the power to exclude specific liabilities from the transfer and to direct the disposal of any excess assets or shortfalls.

metadata.short_title: The Benami Transactions (Prohibition) Act, 2017
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for prohibition of holding property in Benami and restrict right to recover or transfer property held Benami and provide mechanism and procedure for confiscation of property held Benami and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto
metadata.one_line: Prohibits holding property in Benami names and provides for confiscation of such properties.
metadata.summary: This Act prohibits the holding of property in Benami (fictitious or undisclosed) names to prevent money laundering and tax evasion. It establishes an Adjudicating Authority and a Federal Appellate Tribunal to investigate, attach, and confiscate Benami properties. The legislation outlines penalties for false information, rewards whistleblowers, and grants authorities powers to search premises and impound documents.

metadata.short_title: The Benazir Income Support Programme Act, 2010
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for establishment of the Benazir Income Support Programme and to regulate its affairs and matters connected therewith or incidental thereto
metadata.commencement: at once and deemed to have taken effect on and from the thirtieth day of April 2009
repeals: Benazir Income Support Programme Ordinance, 2009 (XIX of 2009)
Benazir Income Support Programme Ordinance, 2009 (LXI of 2009)
establishes: Board of the Benazir Income Support Programme
metadata.administering_body: Federal Government (via Secretary appointed by Federal Government)
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Benazir Income Support Programme as a body corporate to provide financial assistance to poor families.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Benazir Income Support Programme as a body corporate with perpetual succession to provide financial assistance and social protection to economically distressed persons and families. It defines the governance structure including a Board, Council, and Management, outlines eligibility criteria for benefits, and sets up mechanisms for grievance redressal and internal control. The Act also empowers the Board to make regulations regarding financial assistance schedules and operations.

metadata.short_title: The Bills of Lading Act, 1856
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Law relating to Bills of Lading
metadata.territorial_extent: all the Provinces and the Capital of the Federation except the Scheduled Districts; Sind (See Gazette of India, 1880)
metadata.one_line: Amends the law relating to bills of lading by vesting rights in consignees and endorsee.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the law regarding bills of lading to ensure that rights under such documents pass with the property to the consignee or endorsee. It clarifies that a bill of lading held by a bona fide holder for value is conclusive evidence of shipment, even if goods were not actually laden, unless there was actual notice of non-ladenment. The Act preserves existing rights regarding stoppage in transitu and freight claims against the original shipper.

name: Biological and Toxin Weapons Convention (Implementation) Act, 2026

metadata.short_title: The Biological and Toxin Weapons Convention (Implementation) Act, 2026
metadata.long_title: An Act to give effect to the Convention on the Prohibition of the Development, Production and Stockpiling of Bacteriological (Biological) and Toxin Weapons and on their Destruction, 1972
metadata.one_line: This Act implements the 1972 Biological Weapons Convention in Pakistan by prohibiting biological weapons and regulating their peaceful use.
metadata.summary: The Act gives effect to the 1972 Convention on the Prohibition of the Development, Production and Stockpiling of Bacteriological (Biological) and Toxin Weapons. It prohibits the development, production, and stockpiling of biological weapons while permitting their use for peaceful purposes such as research, medicine, and agriculture. The Act establishes an oversight committee under the Ministry of Foreign Affairs to ensure implementation and designates enforcement agencies with powers to investigate offences and seize prohibited materials.

name: Births, Deaths and Marriages Registration Act, 1886

metadata.short_title: The Births, Deaths and Marriages Registration Act, 1886
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the voluntary Registration of certain Births and Deaths, for the establishment of General Registry Offices for keeping Registers of certain Births, Deaths and Marriages, and for certain other purposes
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of Pakistan and applies also to citizens of Pakistan in Acceding States
metadata.commencement: on such day as the Provincial Government, by notification in the official Gazette, directs
metadata.one_line: Establishes general registry offices for voluntary registration of births, deaths, and marriages across Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Act provides for the voluntary registration of births and deaths among certain classes of persons and establishes General Registry Offices to maintain registers. It also covers the authentication of existing registers and ensures that certified copies of entries are admissible in evidence. The Act empowers Provincial and Federal Governments to appoint Registrars and make rules regarding fees, forms, notice periods, and record custody.

metadata.short_title: The Board of Investment Ordinance, 2001
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the establishment of the Board of Investment as an apex agency to promote, encourage and facilitate both local and foreign investment
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Board of Investment to promote and facilitate local and foreign investment in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Board of Investment (BOI) as an apex agency to promote, encourage, and facilitate both local and foreign investment. It defines the composition of the Board, including ex-officio members from the Federal Government and non-official members from the private sector. The document also creates a Special Investment Facilitation Council (SIFC) with specific functions and grants immunity to its members for acts done in performance of their duties.

name: Boilers Act, 1923(Repeal by Ord. 52 of 2001, s,610)

metadata.short_title: The Boilers Act, 1923
metadata.long_title: An Act to consolidate and amend the law relating to steam-boilers.
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Federal Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, appoint
repeals: THE SCHEDULE
metadata.status_evidence: [Repeal by Ord. 52 of 2001, s,610]
metadata.max_penalty: fine which may extend to one hundred rupees
metadata.one_line: Consolidates and amends the law relating to steam-boilers, covering registration, inspection, and penalties.
metadata.summary: This Act consolidates and amends laws regarding steam-boilers and steam-pipes. It establishes a framework for the registration of boilers, appointment of inspectors, and issuance of certificates. The Act outlines procedures for reporting accidents, appeals processes, and penalties for illegal use or tampering with boiler registers. It also provides powers to make regulations and rules for local administration.

metadata.short_title: The Boilers and Pressure Vessels Ordinance, 2002
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend and consolidate the law relating to boilers and pressure vessels; provide for regulation, use, construction, installation and repair of boilers and pressure vessels; prescribe uniform rules and regulations for boilers and pressure vessels and for matters ancillary thereto or connected therewith.
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Federal Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, specify
repeals: The Boilers Act, 1923 (V of 1923)
establishes: Federal Boilers and Pressure Vessels Safety Board
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment which may extend to two years, or with a fine which may extend to fifty thousands rupees or with both
key_definitions: Chief Inspector and Deputy Chief Inspector
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance regulates boilers and pressure vessels, establishes a safety board, mandates registration and inspection, and repeals the 1923 Act.
metadata.summary: The Boilers and Pressure Vessels Ordinance, 2002 amends and consolidates laws regarding the regulation, use, construction, installation, and repair of boilers and pressure vessels. It establishes the Federal Boilers and Pressure Vessels Safety Board to oversee inspections and certifications by approved authorities or insurance companies. The Ordinance mandates registration for all applicable boilers, sets out penalties for tampering with registration numbers or using unregistered equipment, and repeals the earlier Boilers Act, 1923.

metadata.short_title: The Bonded Labour System (Abolition) Act, 1992
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for abolition of bonded labour system
metadata.one_line: Abolishes the bonded labour system in Pakistan and extinguishes all bonded debts.
metadata.summary: This Act abolishes the bonded labour system throughout Pakistan to prevent economic and physical exploitation of the labour class. It declares all agreements, customs, and contracts related to bonded labour void and extinguishes liability for any bonded debt existing at the time of commencement. The Act establishes Vigilance Committees to advise administration on implementation and assist in the rehabilitation of freed labourers while defining specific offences and penalties for enforcing such systems.

metadata.short_title: The Canal and Drainage Act, 1873
metadata.long_title: An Act to regulate Irrigation, Navigation and Drainage
repeals: Acts repealed by the Repealing Act, 1873 (XII of 1873)
metadata.status_evidence: 2. [Repeal of Acts.] Rep. by the Repealing Act, 1873 (XII of 1873), s. 1 and Sch., Pt.II.
metadata.one_line: Regulates irrigation, navigation, and drainage in the Punjab, including water supply rules and canal offences.
metadata.summary: This Act regulates the use of water for public purposes, the construction and maintenance of canals, and drainage works within the Punjab. It establishes rules for water rates, compensation for interruptions in supply, and procedures for obtaining labor for canal works. The Act also defines offences related to damaging canals or obstructing water flow and outlines penalties and recovery mechanisms for dues.

name: Cannabis Control and Regulatory Authority Act, 2024

metadata.short_title: The Cannabis Control and Regulatory Authority Act, 2024
metadata.long_title: An Act to regulate the cultivation of cannabis plant, extraction, refining, manufacturing and sale of derivatives of the plant for medicinal and industrial use
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Cannabis Control and Regulatory Authority to regulate cannabis cultivation, manufacturing, and sale for medicinal and industrial use.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Cannabis Control and Regulatory Authority to oversee the cultivation, extraction, refining, manufacturing, and sale of cannabis derivatives. It defines key terms related to cannabis and its variants, sets up a Board of Governors, and outlines functions regarding licensing, inspections, and penalties for contraventions. The Authority is empowered to make rules and regulations while coordinating with relevant forces.

metadata.short_title: The Cantonments (House-Accommodation) Act, 1923
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend and to consolidate the law relating to the provision of house-accommodation for military officers in cantonments.
metadata.max_penalty: fine which may extend to fifty rupees, and for continuing offences, five rupees per day
metadata.one_line: This Act consolidates laws regarding house accommodation for military officers in cantonments, including appropriation, leases, and repairs.
metadata.summary: The Cantonments (House-Accommodation) Act, 1923 amends and consolidates laws concerning the provision of housing for military officers in cantonments. It defines key terms such as 'house', 'military officer', and 'Cantonment Board', and outlines procedures for appropriating houses for official use, including lease conditions and repair responsibilities. The Act empowers the Federal Government to make rules applicable to all or specific cantonments and establishes protections for persons acting under the Act.

metadata.short_title: The Cantonments (Requisitioning of Immoveable Property) Ordinance, 1948
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the requisitioning of immoveable property within the limits of Cantonments for purposes other than of the Cantonment Boards.
metadata.territorial_extent: all the Cantonments excluding places of religious worship therein, in the territories of Pakistan
repeals: Section 2A
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment up to six months or fine up to five hundred rupees or both
metadata.one_line: Empowers the Federal Government to requisition immoveable property in Cantonments during an emergency.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance was promulgated by the Governor-General to address an emergency requiring the requisition of immovable property within Cantonment limits for purposes other than those of the Cantonment Boards. It grants the Federal Government broad powers to take possession, use, or deal with such property and to determine compensation either by agreement or through rules framed by the Government. The Ordinance also provides legal immunity for actions taken in good faith under its provisions and outlines procedures for releasing property from requisition.

metadata.short_title: The Cantonments Act, 1924
metadata.long_title: An Act to consolidate and amend the law relating to the administration of cantonments.
repeals: Act No. XII of 1927
establishes: Directorate of military lands and cantonments
metadata.one_line: This Act consolidates and amends laws regarding the administration, taxation, and property management of cantonments in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: The Cantonments Act, 1924 consolidates and amends legislation concerning the administration of military cantonments. It establishes Cantonment Boards with Executive Officers to manage local affairs, including land use, building plans, and public services. The Act grants powers to levy various taxes and fees on property, transactions, and services within cantonments while defining offences related to unauthorized liquor sales and illegal construction.

name: Cantonments Local Government (Elections) Ordinance, 2002 (LXXIX of 2002) (Repealed by Act No. XLVII of 2023)

metadata.short_title: The Cantonments Local Government (Elections) Ordinance, 2002
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the conduct of local government elections in cantonments for the purposes of grass-root level participation and to provide adequate linkages and fiscal arrangements between Cantonments Local Government and the District Government within the basic spirit of the Cantonment Act, 1924
repeals: Cantonments Local Government (Elections) Ordinance, 2002
metadata.status_evidence: [Repealed by Act No. XLVII of 2023]
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to five thousand rupees, or with both
metadata.one_line: Provides for the conduct of local government elections in cantonments including franchise, delimitation, and offences.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance regulates local government elections within all cantonments in Pakistan to ensure grassroots participation. It establishes the composition of councils, defines electoral wards, sets qualifications for candidates, and outlines procedures for elections. The document also prescribes various offences related to corrupt practices, bribery, and undue influence, along with their penalties.

name: Cantonments Ordinance, 2002 (CXXXVII)(Repealed by Act No. XLVII of 2023)

metadata.short_title: The Cantonments Ordinance, 2002
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to consolidate and amend the law relating to cantonments.
repeals: The Cantonments Act, 1954
metadata.status_evidence: [Repealed by Act No. XLVII of 2023]
metadata.one_line: An Ordinance consolidating laws for cantonment administration, safety, sanitation, and local governance in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance consolidates and amends the law relating to cantonments in Pakistan. It establishes the structure of Cantonment Boards, Union Administrations, and Citizen Community Boards to manage local affairs. The document covers a wide range of topics including building control, public safety, sanitation, market regulation, and the conduct of local elections within cantonment areas.

metadata.short_title: The Cantonments Pure Food Act, 1966
metadata.long_title: An Act to make provision for preventing the adulteration of food in cantonments.
establishes: Director of Military Lands and Cantonments
metadata.administering_body: Federal Government (via Director of Military Lands and Cantonments)
metadata.one_line: This Act prevents food adulteration in Pakistani cantonments by regulating manufacture, sale, and inspection.
metadata.summary: The Cantonments Pure Food Act, 1966 is designed to prevent the adulteration of food specifically within cantonments in Pakistan. It establishes a framework for licensing manufacturers and sellers, appointing inspectors and public analysts, and setting strict standards for food quality and labelling. The Act defines various food terms, outlines penalties for violations, and grants powers to local authorities and federal officers to ensure food safety.

metadata.short_title: The Cantonments Rent Restriction Act, 1963
metadata.long_title: An Act to make provisions for the control of rents of certain class of buildings within the limits of the cantonment areas and for the eviction of tenants therefrom.
metadata.max_penalty: fine which may extend to five hundred rupees
key_definitions: house in a state of reasonable repair
metadata.one_line: This Act controls rents and regulates evictions for specific buildings within Pakistan's cantonment areas.
metadata.summary: The Cantonments Rent Restriction Act, 1963 establishes a legal framework to control rents and manage tenancies within cantonment areas in Pakistan. It empowers the Federal Government to appoint a Controller of Rents who has the authority to determine fair rents, hear inquiries, and order evictions under specific circumstances. The Act defines various terms related to buildings and tenants, outlines procedures for rent fixation and dispute resolution, and prescribes penalties for landlords or tenants who fail to comply with its provisions.

name: Capital Development Authority (Abatement of Arbitration Proceedings) Act, 1975

metadata.short_title: The Capital Development Authority (Abatement of Arbitration Proceedings) Act, 1975
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the annulment of certain references to arbitration and abatement of certain arbitration proceedings
metadata.one_line: This Act annuls arbitration references and abates proceedings involving the Capital Development Authority.
metadata.summary: The Capital Development Authority (Abatement of Arbitration Proceedings) Act, 1975 provides for the annulment of certain arbitration references and the abatement of specific arbitration proceedings. It applies to agreements entered into by the Capital Development Authority regarding project execution, supply of goods or labour, where disputes were referred to arbitration. The Act abrogates arbitration clauses in such agreements, causes pending proceedings to abate, and annuls awards made under these agreements unless already implemented. Additionally, it addresses the determination of fees for arbitrators whose proceedings have abated and excludes specific time periods from limitation calculations.

metadata.short_title: The Capital Development Authority Ordinance, 1960
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to establish a Capital Development Authority.
establishes: Board of the Capital Development Authority
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Capital Development Authority to plan and develop Islamabad within a regional development plan.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Capital Development Authority (CDA) to make arrangements for the planning and development of Islamabad. It defines the constitution of the Authority and its Board, outlines powers regarding land acquisition and master planning, and sets out financial provisions including borrowing powers and audit requirements. The document also prescribes penalties for offenses such as causing damage to property or disobeying orders, and empowers the Federal Government to make rules to carry out the Ordinance's purposes.

name: Capital of the Republic (Determination of Area) Ordinance, 1963

metadata.short_title: The Capital of the Republic (Determination of Area) Ordinance, 1963
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to determine the area of the Capital of the Republic
metadata.territorial_extent: the Province of West Pakistan (now the Punjab)
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance determines the area of Islamabad as the Capital of the Republic within the District of Rawalpindi.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance was promulgated by the President to determine the specific area of the Capital of the Republic, Islamabad. It defines the boundary lines measuring approximately three hundred and fifty square miles within the District of Rawalpindi in the Province of West Pakistan. The determination is based on a detailed schedule describing the route starting from the Nicholson Monument and following various landmarks and boundaries.

name: Capital Territory Local Government Ordinance, 1979(Repealed by Act,X at 2015)

metadata.short_title: The Capital Territory Local Government Ordinance, 1979
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the constitution of Local Government institutions in the Capital Territory.
metadata.territorial_extent: the rural areas of the Capital Territory
repeals: Order 3[and the Conciliation Courts Ordinance, 1961 (XLIV of 1961)]
metadata.status_evidence: [Repealed by Act,X at 2015]
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance establishes Local Government institutions in the rural areas of the Capital Territory.
metadata.summary: The Capital Territory Local Government Ordinance, 1979 provides for the constitution of Local Government institutions specifically within the rural areas of the Capital Territory. It defines various terms related to local governance, including Union Councils, Chairmen, and specific roles like Election Authorities. The document outlines powers for the Federal Government to declare local areas, levy taxes, and make rules, while also establishing a framework for offences and bye-laws to maintain public order and health.

name: Capital University of Science and Technology Act, 2015

metadata.short_title: The Capital University of Science and Technology Act, 2015
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for establishment of the Capital University of Science and Technology
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of Islamabad Capital Territory
establishes: Capital University of Science and Technology
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Capital University of Science and Technology in Islamabad with perpetual succession.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Capital University of Science and Technology at Islamabad as a body corporate. It defines the university's structure, including its Patron, Chancellor, Vice Chancellor, Board of Governors, and Academic Council. The legislation outlines the powers to acquire property, set up campuses in Pakistan, and make Statutes, Regulations, and Rules.

metadata.short_title: The Carriage by Air Act, 2012
metadata.long_title: An Act to give effect in Pakistan to the Conventions concerning international carriage by air known as the Montreal Convention for the Unification of Certain Rules for International Carriage by Air 1999 and consolidate the law and applicable international conventions in relation to international carriage by air
repeals: The Carriage by Air Act, 1934 (XX of 1934)
The Carriage by Air (International Convention) Act, 1966 (X of 1966)
The Carriage by Air (Supplementary Convention) Act, 1968 (V of 1968)
metadata.one_line: This Act gives effect to international air carriage conventions in Pakistan and consolidates related laws.
metadata.summary: The Carriage by Air Act, 2012 gives legal force in Pakistan to international conventions regarding air carriage, specifically the Montreal, Warsaw, Guadalajara, and earlier conventions. It applies to the whole of Pakistan and covers both international and non-international carriage, with specific exceptions for military operations. The Act incorporates provisions for electronic documents and establishes mechanisms for handling claims and succession certificates following passenger deaths.

name: Carriage of Goods by Sea Act, 1925

metadata.short_title: Carriage of Goods by Sea Act, 1925
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the law with respect to the carriage of goods by sea
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Federal Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, appoint (not being earlier than the first day of January, 1926)
metadata.one_line: Amends the law regarding carriage of goods by sea, establishing carrier liabilities and bill of lading rules.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the law concerning the carriage of goods by sea in Pakistan, incorporating international rules relating to bills of lading. It establishes the responsibilities, liabilities, rights, and immunities of carriers while excluding absolute warranties of seaworthiness. The Act applies to contracts for carrying goods from any port in Pakistan to any other port, subject to specific notifications and commencement dates.

metadata.short_title: The Carriers Act, 1865
metadata.long_title: An Act relating to the rights and liabilities of Common Carriers
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of Pakistan (except Scheduled Districts initially; extended later)
metadata.one_line: Defines rights and liabilities of common carriers regarding loss or damage to goods exceeding one hundred rupees.
metadata.summary: This Act regulates the rights and liabilities of common carriers transporting property for hire. It limits carrier liability for certain high-value goods unless declared and paid for at a higher rate, while holding carriers fully liable for losses caused by their own negligence or fraud. The Act also establishes time limits for claiming damages and allows carriers to limit liability via special contracts for specific types of property.

metadata.short_title: The Caste Disabilities Removal Act, 1850
