metadata.long_title: An Act for extending the principle of section 9, Regulation VII, 1832, of the Bengal Code throughout the Territories subject to the Government of the East India Company.
metadata.territorial_extent: the Territories subject to the Government of the East India Company
repeals: section 9, Regulation VII, 1832, of the Bengal Code
key_definitions: impair or affect any right of inheritance
metadata.administering_body: Courts of the East India Company and Courts established by Royal Charter
metadata.one_line: Prohibits forfeiture of property or impairment of inheritance rights due to change of religion or loss of caste.
metadata.summary: This Act extends the principle that laws inflicting forfeiture of property or impairing inheritance rights due to a change in religion or loss of caste shall cease to be enforced. It applies to all territories under the Government of the East India Company, covering civil suits involving parties of different religious persuasions. The legislation ensures that such discriminatory laws and usages are no longer valid in the Courts of the East India Company or those established by Royal Charter.

metadata.short_title: The Cattle-trespass Act, 1871
metadata.long_title: An Act to consolidate and amend the law relating to Trespasses by Cattle
repeals: Acts relating to Trespasses by Cattle (consolidated)
metadata.one_line: Consolidates and amends laws regarding cattle trespass, impounding, fines, and compensation.
metadata.summary: This Act consolidates the law relating to trespasses by cattle. It establishes pounds and appoints pound-keepers to manage seized animals. The legislation outlines procedures for seizing damaging cattle, imposing fines, and providing compensation for crop damage. It also defines penalties for opposing seizures or causing mischief with cattle.

metadata.short_title: The Central Depositories Act, 1997
metadata.long_title: An Act to make provision for the establishment and operation of book‑entry systems for the transfer of securities by central depository companies
metadata.one_line: Establishes and regulates the central depository system for book-entry transfer of securities in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Act provides for the establishment and operation of book-entry systems to facilitate the transfer of securities via a central depository. It defines key terms such as 'central depository', 'book-entry security', and 'account-holder' while outlining the powers of the Corporate Law Authority to regulate these entities. The legislation also amends the Companies Ordinance, 1984, to integrate central depositories into existing corporate frameworks regarding share registration and subsidiary definitions.

name: Central Excise Duty on Sugar (Validation) Ordinance, 1979

metadata.short_title: The Central Excise Duty on Sugar (Validation) Ordinance, 1979
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to validate the levy and collection of excise duty on enhanced rate on stocks of sugar held by sugar mills on the 7th June, 1975.
key_definitions: stocks of sugar held by sugar mills on the 7th June, 1975
enhanced rate (twenty-seven rupees and twenty-two paisa per cwt)
metadata.one_line: Validates the levy and collection of enhanced central excise duty on sugar stocks held by mills on June 7, 1975.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance validates the levy and collection of an enhanced central excise duty on stocks of sugar held by sugar mills as of June 7, 1975. It deems this specific duty to have been validly levied and collected at a rate of twenty-seven rupees and twenty-two paisa per cwt in addition to the standard duty for the year 1974-75. The Ordinance ensures that any unpaid portion of this duty remains recoverable under existing provisions of the Central Excise and Salt Act, 1944.

metadata.short_title: The Central Law Officers Ordinance, 1970
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for appointment of Central Law Officers
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance provides for the appointment, qualifications, and rights of Central Law Officers in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: The Central Law Officers Ordinance, 1970 establishes the framework for appointing Additional Attorneys-General, Deputy Attorneys General, and Assistant Attorneys General. It defines their qualifications, such as eligibility to be a Supreme Court Judge or having seven years of High Court advocacy experience. The document grants these officers the right of audience in all courts in Pakistan and deems them public prosecutors competent to conduct proceedings on behalf of the Federal Government.

metadata.short_title: The Centres of Excellence Act, 1974
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of centres of excellence in the universities for conducting high level teaching and research.
metadata.one_line: Establishes Centres of Excellence in universities for high-level teaching and research.
metadata.summary: This Act provides for the establishment of Centres of Excellence within universities to conduct high-level teaching and research. It outlines the functions of these centres, including training research workers and establishing advanced degree programmes. The Act establishes a Board of Governors for each centre, appoints a Director, and details funding sources and audit requirements.

name: Chairman and Members of Federal Land Commission (Validation of Orders) Ordinance, 1981

metadata.short_title: The Chairman and Members of Federal Land Commission (Validation of Orders) Ordinance, 1981
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to validate certain orders passed by the Chairman or a Member of Federal Land Commission.
key_definitions: Federal Government order under Dir and Swat (Devolution and Distribution of Property) Regulation, 1972
Federal Government order under Dir and Swat (Settlement of Disputes of Immovable Property) Regulation, 1972
Federal Government order under Distribution of Property (Chitral) Regulation, 1974
Federal Government order under Settlement of Disputes of Immovable Property (Chitral) Regulation, 1974
metadata.one_line: Validates orders passed by the Chairman or Members of the Federal Land Commission before this Ordinance came into force.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance validates certain orders previously passed by the Chairman or a Member of the Federal Land Commission. It applies to orders issued at any time before the commencement of this law, regardless of any contrary court decisions. The validation covers orders made under specific regulations regarding property devolution and dispute settlement in Dir, Swat, and Chitral.

name: Chairman and Speaker (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) Act, 1975

metadata.short_title: The Chairman and Speaker (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) Act, 1975
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the salaries, allowances and privileges of the Chairman of the Senate and the Speaker of the National Assembly.
metadata.commencement: at once and shall be deemed to have taken effect on the fourteenth day of August, 1975
metadata.one_line: This Act provides for the salaries, allowances, and privileges of the Chairman of the Senate and the Speaker of the National Assembly.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the financial compensation and official privileges for the Chairman of the Senate and the Speaker of the National Assembly. It details specific amounts for salary, equipment allowance, sumptuary allowance, transport, and official residence usage. The legislation also outlines rules regarding travelling expenses, medical facilities, leave entitlements, and discretionary grants to ensure these officials can perform their duties effectively.

metadata.short_title: The Charitable and Religious Trusts Act, 1920
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide more effectual control over the administration of Charitable and Religious Trusts.
metadata.one_line: Provides court control over charitable and religious trusts in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes a legal framework for obtaining information regarding charitable and religious trusts created for public purposes. It empowers interested persons to petition the Court of the District Judge or High Court for directions on trust management, audits, and income details. The legislation outlines specific procedures for petitions, including notice requirements, hearings, and provisions for costs in suits against trustees, while also defining the scope of the Code of Civil Procedure applicable to these proceedings.

metadata.short_title: The Charitable Endowments Act, 1890
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the Vesting and Administration of Property held in trust for charitable purposes.
metadata.one_line: Provides for the vesting and administration of property held in trust for charitable purposes by a Treasurer.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the office of the Treasurer of Charitable Endowments to manage property held in trust for charitable purposes. It defines 'charitable purpose' to include relief of the poor, education, and medical relief, while excluding religious teaching or worship. The appropriate Government may order property to vest in the Treasurer and settle schemes for its administration, which remain in force until modified or superseded.

metadata.short_title: The Charitable Funds (Regulation of Collection) Act, 1953
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the regulation, administration and accounting of collections of charitable donations and for the prevention of frauds.
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months or with fine or with both
metadata.one_line: Regulates collections of charitable and private donations in Karachi Division to prevent fraud.
metadata.summary: This Act provides for the regulation, administration, and accounting of collections of charitable donations while aiming to prevent fraud. It applies specifically to the Karachi Division and distinguishes between private funds and charitable funds based on donation amounts and beneficiaries. The legislation mandates declarations before collection, requires sanctioning authority approval for charitable funds, and outlines penalties for contraventions.

metadata.short_title: Chartered Accountants Ordinance, 1961
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to make provision for the regulation of the profession of accountants.
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Federal Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, appoint
subjects: Institute of Chartered Accountants of Pakistan
establishes: Institute of Chartered Accountants of Pakistan
metadata.max_penalty: fine
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance establishes the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Pakistan and regulates the profession.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance provides for the regulation of the accountancy profession in Pakistan by establishing the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Pakistan. It incorporates the Institute, defines its Council and Regional Committees, and sets out rules for membership, registration, and professional conduct. The document also prescribes penalties for misconduct, false claims, and unqualified practice.

metadata.short_title: The Chemical Fertilizers (Development Surcharge) Act, 1973
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the levy and collection of a development surcharge on chemical fertilizers and for matters connected therewith.
metadata.one_line: This Act levies a development surcharge on chemical fertilizers and sets maximum sale prices.
metadata.summary: The Chemical Fertilizers (Development Surcharge) Act, 1973 provides for the levy and collection of a development surcharge on chemical fertilizers produced or held in stock by companies and stockists. It defines key terms such as 'differential margin' and 'ex-factory price', authorizes exemptions or refunds by the Federal Government, and sets maximum sale prices to prevent profiteering. The Act also allows for income-tax deductions regarding the surcharge paid and empowers the Federal Government to make rules and delegate powers.

metadata.short_title: The Chemical Weapons Convention Implementation Ordinance, 2000
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to give effect in Pakistan to the Convention on the Prohibition of the Development, Production, Stockpiling and use of Chemical Weapons and on their Destruction signed at Paris on the 13th January, 1993
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance implements the Chemical Weapons Convention in Pakistan by prohibiting development and establishing a National Authority.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance gives effect to the Chemical Weapons Convention signed at Paris on January 13, 1993. It prohibits the development, production, stockpiling, use, or transfer of chemical weapons within Pakistan. The document establishes a National Authority to oversee verification activities and manage inspections under the Convention.

name: Chief Election Commissioner (Salary, Allowances and Privileges) Act, 1975

metadata.short_title: The Chief Election Commissioner (Salary, Allowances and Privileges) Act, 1975
metadata.long_title: An Act to determine the salary, allowances and privileges of the Chief Election Commissioner.
metadata.one_line: This Act determines the salary, allowances, and privileges of the Chief Election Commissioner.
metadata.summary: This Act determines the salary, allowances, and privileges applicable to the Chief Election Commissioner. It grants the Commissioner the same benefits as a Judge of the Supreme Court, with specific provisions for those who were previously Chief Justices. The Act also outlines rules regarding the Provident Fund subscription and various types of leave entitlements.

metadata.short_title: The Child Marriage Restraint Act, 1929
metadata.long_title: An Act to restrain the solemnisation of child marriages
metadata.status_evidence: Sub. and Omitted by the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance No. VIII of 1961, s.12 (with effect from the 15th July, 1961), applicable to all Muslim citizens of Pakistan wherever they may be.
metadata.repealed_by: Muslim Family Laws Ordinance No. VIII of 1961
metadata.max_penalty: three months imprisonment or fine of one thousand rupees or both
metadata.one_line: This Act restrains the solemnisation of child marriages and prescribes punishments for offenders.
metadata.summary: The Child Marriage Restraint Act, 1929 was enacted to restrain the solemnisation of child marriages. It defines a 'child' as a male under eighteen or a female under sixteen years of age. The Act prescribes punishments for adults marrying children, those who solemnise such marriages, and parents or guardians involved in them. It also grants courts power to issue injunctions to prevent contravention.

metadata.short_title: The Children (Pledging of Labour) Act, 1933
metadata.long_title: An Act to prohibit the pledging of the labour of children
metadata.commencement: at once for sections 1, 2, and 3; on the first day of July, 1933 for remaining sections
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment up to six months and fine up to fifty thousand rupees
key_definitions: agreement to pledge the labour of a child
metadata.one_line: Prohibits agreements to pledge children's labour and penalizes parents, guardians, and employers involved.
metadata.summary: This Act prohibits the making of agreements to pledge the labour of children and the employment of such children. It defines 'child' as a person under fifteen years and voids any agreement contrary to the Act. The legislation imposes severe penalties, including fines and imprisonment, on parents, guardians, or others who make such agreements or employ pledged children.

name: China Pakistan Economic Corridor Authority Act, 2021

metadata.short_title: China Pakistan Economic Corridor Authority Act, 2021
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of China Pakistan Economic Corridor Authority
repeals: China Pakistan Economic Corridor Authority Ordinance, 2019 (XII of 2019)
metadata.one_line: Establishes the China Pakistan Economic Corridor Authority to implement CPEC activities.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the China Pakistan Economic Corridor Authority as a body corporate with perpetual succession. The Authority is responsible for planning, facilitating, coordinating, enforcing, monitoring, and evaluating all activities related to the China Pakistan Economic Corridor in accordance with relevant Memorandums of Understanding. It defines the composition, powers, and functions of the Authority, including its reporting structure to the Prime Minister and provisions for making rules and regulations.

metadata.short_title: The Christian Marriage Act, 1872
metadata.long_title: An Act to consolidate and amend the law relating to the solemnization of the marriages of persons professing the Christian religion
repeals: Enactments repealed by the Repealing Act, 1938 (1 of 1938), s. 2 and Sch.
metadata.status_evidence: SCHEDULE V.—[ENACTMENTS REPEALED.] Rep. by the Repealing Act, 1938 (I of 1938), s. 2 and Sch.
metadata.one_line: Consolidates and amends laws regarding solemnization and registration of marriages for Christians in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Act consolidates and amends the law relating to the solemnization of marriages among persons professing the Christian religion. It establishes procedures for granting licenses, issuing certificates, and registering marriages performed by ministers or Marriage Registrars. The Act also outlines penalties for false declarations and unauthorized solemnization of marriages.

name: Church of Scotland Kirk Sessions Act, 1899

metadata.short_title: The Church of Scotland Kirk Sessions Act, 1899
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the Incorporation of Kirk Sessions of the Church of Scotland in [Pakistan].
repeals: the word 'and' and sub-section (3) of the original Act
metadata.one_line: Incorporates Kirk Sessions of the Church of Scotland in Pakistan as bodies corporate with property powers.
metadata.summary: This Act incorporates Kirk Sessions of the Church of Scotland operating in Pakistan into the legal system as bodies corporate. It grants them perpetual succession, a common seal, and the power to hold and dispose of property for their congregations or trusts. The Federal Government is authorized to issue notifications confirming the constitution of these sessions, which serve as conclusive proof of their status.

metadata.short_title: The Cigarettes (Printing of Warning) Ordinance, 1979
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for printing of a health warning on packets of cigarettes.
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine which may extend to ten thousand rupees, or with both
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance mandates health warnings on cigarette packets and advertisements, prohibiting sale without them.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance requires that legible health warnings be printed in English and Urdu on cigarette packets and advertisements. It prohibits the manufacture, sale, or possession of cigarettes from packets lacking these required warnings. The law establishes penalties including imprisonment up to two years or fines up to ten thousand rupees for contraventions, with provisions for forfeiture of offending goods.

metadata.short_title: The Civil Commotion Compensation Fund (Repeal) Act, 1972
metadata.long_title: An Act to repeal the Civil Commotion Compensation Fund Ordinance, 1971.
metadata.commencement: at once; deemed to have taken effect on the third day of August, 1972
repeals: Civil Commotion Compensation Fund Ordinance, 1971 (XXI of 1971)
metadata.status_evidence: An Act to repeal the Civil Commotion Compensation Fund Ordinance, 1971.
metadata.one_line: Repeals the Civil Commotion Compensation Fund Ordinance, 1971 and directs insurers to pay outstanding amounts.
metadata.summary: This Act repeals the Civil Commotion Compensation Fund Ordinance, 1971. It mandates that insurers must pay into the established Fund any unpaid surcharges and amounts specified under the repealed Ordinance within a time specified by the Federal Government. Any remaining moneys in the Fund are to be credited to the Federal Consolidated Fund after paying off loans and advances obtained under the said Ordinance.

metadata.short_title: The Civil Aviation Ordinance, 1960
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to make better provision for the control of manufacture, possession, use, operation, sale, import and export of aircraft, the control and regulation of air transport services, and the control and development of aerodromes in Pakistan.
repeals: The Civil Aviation Ordinance, 1956 (XXXI of 1956)
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment and fine not exceeding one lakh rupees
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance regulates aircraft operations, air transport services, and aerodromes in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: The Civil Aviation Ordinance, 1960 provides comprehensive provisions for controlling the manufacture, possession, use, operation, sale, import, and export of aircraft. It also regulates air transport services and the development of aerodromes within Pakistan. The document empowers the Federal Government to make rules, issue exemptions, detain aircraft, and impose penalties for non-compliance or dangerous flying.

metadata.short_title: The Civil Defence Act, 1952
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for powers to secure the civil defence of Pakistan.
repeals: Civil Defence Ordinance, 1951
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to five years, or with fine
metadata.one_line: Provides powers to secure civil defence against hostile attacks and disasters in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Act empowers the Federal Government to take measures for civil defence against hostile attacks by foreign powers or during calamities. It allows for the requisition of property, evacuation of areas, and control over lights, sounds, and vehicles to ensure public safety. The Act also outlines principles for compensation regarding compulsory acquisition and repeals the earlier Civil Defence Ordinance, 1951.

metadata.short_title: The Civil Pioneer Force Ordinance, 1965
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to constitute a Civil Pioneer Force for service in Pakistan and to provide for the organization, control and discipline thereof.
metadata.one_line: Constitutes the Civil Pioneer Force for service in Pakistan and provides for its organization, control, and discipline.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Civil Pioneer Force to perform duties essential for the defence of Pakistan, public safety, and maintenance of public order. It defines the roles of officers and enrolled persons, outlines specific duties such as repairing communications and constructing shelters, and sets out procedures for offences, trials, and rule-making powers vested in the Federal Government.

metadata.short_title: The Civil Servants (Validation of Rules) Ordinance, 2001
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to validate certain rules made under the Civil Servant Act, 1973 and certain actions taken thereunder
metadata.one_line: Validates rules made under the Civil Servants Act, 1973 and related actions taken before its commencement.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance validates certain rules made under the Civil Servants Act, 1973 that were issued during a period when Parliament was suspended. It affirms the validity of specific rules regarding occupational groups, probation, training, seniority, and confirmation, as well as all notifications amending them prior to this Ordinance's commencement. Furthermore, it deems all orders, proceedings, acts, instructions, powers, and appointments made under these validated rules immediately before its commencement to have been validly made and to have had effect accordingly.

metadata.short_title: The Civil Servants Act, 1973
metadata.long_title: An Act to regulate the appointment of persons to, and the terms and conditions of service of persons in, the service of Pakistan
metadata.territorial_extent: all civil servants wherever they may be
establishes: Federal Board of Revenue (for asset declaration)
Service Tribunals (referenced in jurisdiction barred section)
metadata.one_line: Regulates the appointment, terms, conditions, and service of civil servants in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Act regulates the appointment of persons to the service of Pakistan and defines their terms and conditions of service. It covers probation, confirmation, pay, leave, pension, conduct, and retirement for all civil servants wherever they may be. The Act also provides for indemnity for officials acting in good faith and bars court jurisdiction over certain decisions made under it.

name: Civil Services (Qualification for appointment as High Court Judge) Act, 1965

metadata.short_title: The Civil Services (Qualification for Appointment as High Court Judge) Act, 1965
metadata.long_title: An Act to prescribe the Civil Service of Pakistan to be a civil service for the purposes of paragraph (b) of clause (2) of Article 92 of the Constitution.
metadata.one_line: Prescribes the Civil Service of Pakistan as qualifying for High Court Judge appointment under Article 92(2)(b).
metadata.summary: This Act prescribes that the Civil Service of Pakistan is a civil service for the purposes of paragraph (b) of clause (2) of Article 92 of the Constitution. It specifically includes the Secretariat Group and District Management Group of the All Pakistan Unified Grades, along with their successors, within this definition. The legislation aims to achieve uniformity in administration as required by national interest.

metadata.short_title: The Claims for Maintenance (Recovery Abroad) Ordinance, 1959
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to give effect to the United Nations Convention on the Recovery Abroad of Claims for Maintenance.
metadata.one_line: Gives effect to the UN Convention on the Recovery Abroad of Claims for Maintenance in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance gives legal force to the United Nations Convention on the Recovery Abroad of Maintenance within Pakistan. It designates judicial or administrative authorities as Transmitting Agencies and public or private bodies as Receiving Agencies to facilitate maintenance recovery between Contracting Parties. The Federal Government is empowered to publish information, amend the Schedule regarding the Convention, and make rules for carrying out the Ordinance's purposes.

metadata.short_title: The Co-operative Societies Act, 1912
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Law relating to Co-operative Societies
repeals: Section 50 of this Act (Repealed by the Second Repealing and Amending Act, 1914)
metadata.status_evidence: It has been rep. in its application to the Province of W. Pakistan, see W.P. Ord. No. VII of 1965.
metadata.max_penalty: fine which may extend to fifty rupees, and in the case of a continuing offence with further fine of five rupees for each day on which the offence is continued after conviction therefor
metadata.one_line: This Act amends the law relating to co-operative societies, facilitating their formation and regulating registration, rights, liabilities, and dissolution.
metadata.summary: The Co-operative Societies Act, 1912 amends the law relating to co-operative societies to facilitate their formation for thrift and self-help among agriculturists and artisans. It establishes a Registrar appointed by the Provincial Government to oversee registration and management of registered societies. The Act defines key terms such as 'member', 'officer', and 'bye-laws', regulates the investment of funds, restricts loans and borrowing, and outlines procedures for dissolution and winding up. It also prohibits non-registered entities from using the word 'co-operative' in their business names without sanction.

name: Coal Mines (Fixation of Rates of Wages) Ordinance, 1960

metadata.short_title: The Coal Mines (Fixation of Rates of Wages) Ordinance, 1960
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the fixation of rates of wages in respect of labour employed in coal mines and for matters connected therewith.
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance empowers the Provincial Government to fix minimum wage rates for coal mine workers.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance provides for the fixation of minimum wage rates for labour employed in coal mines across Pakistan. It authorizes the Provincial Government to issue notifications setting these rates, which must be paid by mine owners without exception. The provisions are additional to existing laws like the Payment of Wages Act, 1936, and do not affect higher wages agreed upon in contracts or awards.

name: Coasting-Vessels Act,(XIX of 1838)(Repeal by 52 of 2001 s.610 & sch (pp-1-5)))

metadata.short_title: The National Tariff Commission Act, 1990
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of the National Tariff Commission and for matters connected therewith or ancillary thereto
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three months, or with fine not exceeding fifteen thousand rupees, or with both
metadata.one_line: Establishes the National Tariff Commission to advise on tariff measures and protect indigenous industry.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the National Tariff Commission as a body corporate with perpetual succession. The Commission's primary function is to advise the Federal Government on tariff measures, protection for indigenous industries, improving competitiveness, and promoting exports. It also handles matters related to countering dumping and unfair trade practices. The Commission consists of a Chairman and two members appointed by the Federal Government and has powers to conduct inquiries, summon witnesses, and make rules.

metadata.short_title: The Coconut Committee Act, 1944
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the levy and collection of a cess on copra consumed in mills.
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment which may extend to six months and fine; or fine not exceeding one thousand rupees
metadata.one_line: This Act provides for the levy and collection of a cess on copra consumed in mills across Pakistan.
metadata.summary: The Coconut Committee Act, 1944 establishes a duty of excise on all copra consumed in mills within Pakistan. It empowers the Federal Government to fix the rate of this cess via notification and requires mill owners to submit monthly returns detailing copra consumption. The Act outlines procedures for assessment, collection, and penalties for non-compliance or disclosure of confidential information obtained during inspections.

metadata.short_title: The Code of Civil Procedure, 1908
metadata.long_title: An Act to consolidate and amend the laws relating to the Procedure of the Courts of Civil Judicature.
metadata.one_line: Consolidates and amends laws relating to the procedure of civil courts in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Act consolidates and amends laws regarding the procedure of civil courts. It covers jurisdiction, institution of suits, execution of decrees, appeals, and special proceedings involving the government or foreign entities. The Code also outlines powers for Collectors in executing decrees against immovable property.

metadata.short_title: The Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898
metadata.long_title: An Act to consolidate the law relating to the procedure of Courts of Session and Judges of Small Causes, Magistrates, Police Officers and other persons in criminal matters.
metadata.one_line: Consolidates criminal procedure laws regarding courts, arrests, warrants, and sentencing in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Act consolidates the law relating to the procedure of criminal courts, magistrates, and police officers. It defines the classes of criminal courts, their territorial divisions, and the powers exercisable by them. The Code outlines procedures for arrest, issuance of summons and warrants, production of documents, unlawful assemblies, and sentencing, including provisions for bonds for good behaviour and forfeiture.

metadata.short_title: The Commercial Documents Evidence Act, 1939
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Law of Evidence with respect to certain commercial documents.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Law of Evidence regarding presumptions and relevance of specific commercial documents.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Law of Evidence to establish that statements in scheduled commercial documents are themselves relevant facts. It creates legal presumptions regarding the genuineness of documents related to shipping, aviation, customs, and trade issued by recognized authorities or chambers of commerce. The Act distinguishes between documents where a court 'shall presume' accuracy (Part I) and those where it 'may presume' accuracy (Part II).

metadata.short_title: The Companies (Appointment of Legal Advisers) Act, 1974
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the appointment of Legal Advisers to companies and matters connected therewith
metadata.max_penalty: two hundred thousand rupees or imprisonment for one year
metadata.administering_body: Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan
metadata.one_line: This Act mandates companies to appoint Legal Advisers, sets eligibility criteria, and defines penalties for non-compliance.
metadata.summary: The Companies (Appointment of Legal Advisers) Act, 1974 requires every company to appoint at least one Legal Adviser on retainership. It specifies that only advocates or registered firms consisting entirely of advocates can be appointed, with limits on the number of companies an individual or firm may serve. The Act outlines penalties for contravention, including fines payable to the Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan, and grants the Federal Government power to make rules and exempt specific companies.

metadata.short_title: The Companies (Appointment of Trustees) Act, 1972
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the management of the affairs of certain companies.
metadata.one_line: Provides for the appointment of trustees to manage affairs and assets of certain companies in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Act empowers the Federal Government to appoint a trustee to manage the affairs of specific companies when deemed necessary in the public interest. Upon appointment, management and all company assets vest in the trustee, while transfers of these assets are prohibited. The Act overrides other laws and agreements regarding these companies and grants the trustee broad powers to handle business, liabilities, and accounts.

metadata.short_title: The Companies Act, 2017
metadata.long_title: An Act to consolidate and amend the law relating to companies.
repeals: The Companies Ordinance, 1984
establishes: Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment or fine as per sections regarding offences (specific amounts not detailed in excerpts)
metadata.administering_body: Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan
metadata.one_line: Consolidates and amends the law relating to companies, covering incorporation, capital, winding up, and regulation.
metadata.summary: This Act consolidates and amends laws regarding companies in Pakistan. It covers incorporation procedures, share capital management, prospectus requirements, and winding-up processes. The Act establishes the jurisdiction of courts and powers of the Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan.

name: Companies Ordinance, 1984 (Repealed by Act XIX of 2017)

metadata.short_title: The Companies Ordinance, 1984
repeals: The Companies Act, 1913
The Companies (Foreign Interests) Act, 1918
The Undesirable Companies Act, 1958
The Securities and Exchange Ordinance, 1969
The Companies (Managing Agency and Election of Directors) Order, 1972
The Companies (Shifting of Registered Office) Ordinance, 1972
metadata.status_evidence: name: "Companies Ordinance, 1984 (Repealed by Act XIX of 2017)"
metadata.one_line: An Ordinance regulating the incorporation, management, winding up, and regulation of companies in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance provides a comprehensive legal framework for the formation and operation of companies in Pakistan. It covers preliminary matters such as definitions and jurisdiction, followed by detailed provisions on corporate law authority, incorporation procedures, share capital management, prospectus requirements, and winding up processes. The text establishes specific authorities like the Corporate Law Authority and Company Benches to oversee these functions.

metadata.short_title: The Companies Profits (Workers Participation) Act, 1968
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for Participation of workers in the profits of companies.
metadata.one_line: This Act establishes a Workers Participation Fund to allow workers in companies to share in the company's profits.
metadata.summary: The Companies Profits (Workers Participation) Act, 1968 provides for the participation of workers in the profits of companies. It mandates the establishment of a Workers Participation Fund by eligible companies and the constitution of a Board of Trustees to manage it. The Act outlines procedures for funding the scheme, auditing accounts, settling disputes, and making special provisions for seasonal industries.

metadata.short_title: The Competition Act, 2010
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for free competition in all spheres of commercial and economic activity to enhance economic efficiency and to protect consumers from anti competitive behavior.
repeals: Monopolies and Restrictive Trade Practices (Control and Prevention) Ordinance, 1970
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Competition Commission of Pakistan to ensure free competition and protect consumers from anti-competitive behavior.
metadata.summary: This Act provides for free competition in all spheres of commercial and economic activity to enhance efficiency and protect consumers. It establishes the Competition Commission of Pakistan with powers to prohibit abuse of dominant position, certain agreements, deceptive marketing practices, and to approve mergers. The Act defines key terms such as 'undertaking', 'relevant market', and 'dominant position' and sets out penalties for contravention while repealing the Monopolies and Restrictive Trade Practices (Control and Prevention) Ordinance, 1970.

name: Compulsory Service in the Armed Forces Ordinance, 1971

metadata.short_title: The Compulsory Service in the Armed Forces Ordinance, 1971
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for compulsory service in the Armed Forces of essential persons and ex-servicemen.
repeals: The Compulsory Service in the Armed Forces Ordinance, 1971
metadata.status_evidence: [Repeal] Omitted by the Federal Laws (Revision and Declaration) Ordinance, 1981 (XXVII of 1981), s. 3 and Sch., II.
metadata.repealed_by: The Federal Laws (Revision and Declaration) Ordinance, 1981
metadata.max_penalty: rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to seven years, or with fine which may extend to ten thousand rupees, or with both
metadata.one_line: Provides for compulsory service in the Armed Forces of essential persons and ex-servicemen.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance mandates compulsory service in the Armed Forces for essential personnel and ex-servicemen who are not over sixty years of age. It defines key terms such as 'Armed Forces', 'essential persons', and 'ex-servicemen' while establishing procedures for call-up notices, interviews, and exemptions. The document outlines penalties for non-compliance, grants indemnity to officials acting in good faith, and empowers the Federal Government to make necessary rules.

name: Compulsory Teaching of the Holy Quran Act, 2017

metadata.short_title: The Compulsory Teaching of the Holy Quran Act, 2017
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for making compulsory teaching of the Holy Quran to Muslim students in all educational institutions
metadata.territorial_extent: the Islamabad Capital Territory and all public sector educational institutions owned and controlled by the Federal Government wherever they may be
metadata.one_line: Mandates compulsory Holy Quran teaching for Muslim students in Islamabad and Federal public sector schools.
metadata.summary: This Act mandates the compulsory teaching of the Holy Quran to Muslim students in educational institutions located in the Islamabad Capital Territory and those owned or controlled by the Federal Government. It requires Naazrah Quran (recitation) for grades I to V and translation of the entire Holy Quran for grades VI to XII. The Minister-in-charge of the appropriate Government is responsible for ensuring implementation, with powers to make rules under the Act.

name: COMSATS Institute of Information Technology Ordinance, 2000

metadata.short_title: The COMSATS Institute of Information Technology Ordinance, 2000
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the establishment of the COMSATS Institute of Information Technology
metadata.one_line: Establishes the COMSATS Institute of Information Technology as a body corporate with powers to educate and award degrees.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the COMSATS Institute of Information Technology as a body corporate with perpetual succession. It grants the Institute powers to provide instruction in computer and information technology, admit students, hold examinations, and confer degrees. The document also defines various authorities within the Institute, including the Board of Governors, Academic Council, and specific committees for finance, affiliation, and discipline.

metadata.short_title: The COMSATS University Islamabad Act, 2018
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for upgradation of the status of COMSATS institute of Information Technology, Islamabad as COMSATS University and matters connected therewith and ancillary thereto.
repeals: The COMSATS Institute of Information Technology Ordinance, 2000 (XXXVIII of 2000)
metadata.one_line: Upgrades COMSATS Institute of Information Technology to COMSATS University Islamabad and establishes its governing bodies.
metadata.summary: This Act upgrades the COMSATS Institute of Information Technology in Islamabad to the status of COMSATS University Islamabad. It establishes the university as a body corporate with perpetual succession, defining its officers, authorities, and powers. The legislation outlines the structure for Statutes, Regulations, and Rules, while repealing the previous 2000 Ordinance governing the institute.

metadata.short_title: The Conciliation Courts Ordinance, 1961
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to make provision for the establishment of Conciliation Courts.
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Federal Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, appoint
metadata.one_line: Establishes Conciliation Courts to enable people to settle certain civil and criminal disputes through conciliation.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes Conciliation Courts to allow the settlement of specific civil and criminal disputes through conciliation. It defines the jurisdiction of these courts, their composition, and the types of cases they can hear, excluding matters involving minors or government duties. The document outlines procedures for summoning witnesses, enforcing decrees, and handling cases where conciliation fails.

name: Constitution of the Islamic  Republic of Pakistan

metadata.short_title: The Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan and to define its fundamental rights, principles of policy, structure of government, and other matters.
repeals: Constitution of Pakistan, 1956
Constitution (Provisional) Act, 1973
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Islamic Republic of Pakistan and defines its fundamental rights, government structure, and principles.
metadata.summary: This document establishes the Islamic Republic of Pakistan and outlines its fundamental rights, principles of policy, and the structure of its federation. It details the composition and functions of the President, Parliament (Majlis-e-Shoora), Federal Government, Provincial Assemblies, and Judiciary. The Constitution also provides for the establishment of independent bodies such as the Election Commission and defines the powers and duties of various state organs.

metadata.short_title: The Contempt of Court Ordinance, 2003
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to regulate the exercise of the powers of courts to punish for contempt of court
metadata.commencement: at once; deemed to have taken effect from the ninth day of November, 2003
repeals: The Contempt of Court Act, 1976 (LXIV of 1976)
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment which may extend to six months simple imprisonment, or with fine which may extend to one hundred thousand rupees, or with both
metadata.one_line: Regulates court powers to punish for contempt and repeals the 1976 Act.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance regulates the exercise of judicial powers to punish for contempt of court in Pakistan. It defines three types of contempt: civil, criminal, and judicial, and outlines the jurisdiction of superior courts to punish such acts. The document establishes procedures for filing charges, presenting defenses including apologies or truth, and allows for appeals within the court system.

metadata.short_title: The Contract Act, 1872
metadata.long_title: An Act to define and amend certain parts of the law relating to contracts
repeals: Partnership Act, 1932 (IX of 1932)
Repealing and Amending Act, 1914 (X of 1914)
metadata.one_line: Defines and amends the law relating to contracts, agreements, sale of goods, partnership, agency, indemnity, and guarantee.
metadata.summary: This Act defines and amends the law relating to contracts in Pakistan. It covers preliminary concepts such as communication, acceptance, and revocation of proposals, as well as voidable and void agreements. The legislation also addresses contingent contracts, performance obligations, breach consequences, sale of goods, indemnity, guarantee, agency relations, and partnership.

metadata.short_title: The Control of Employment Ordinance, 1965
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the collection of information relating to employment in industrial undertakings and availability of persons therefor, and for the control and distribution of such employment, and matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance regulates employment in industrial undertakings to control manpower distribution during an emergency.
metadata.summary: The Control of Employment Ordinance, 1965 was promulgated by the President under emergency powers to collect employment information and control manpower distribution. It establishes a Manpower Council for policy-making and a Manpower Board at the provincial level to coordinate labor supply. The law defines industrial undertakings broadly and creates offences for false statements or non-compliance, punishable by imprisonment up to six months or fines.

metadata.short_title: The Control of Narcotic Substances Act, 1997
metadata.long_title: An Act to consolidate and amend the laws relating to narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances
repeals: Control of Narcotic Substances Ordinance, 1996
establishes: National Fund for Control of Drug Abuse
metadata.max_penalty: Imprisonment which may extend to two years but shall not be less than one year along-with fine
metadata.one_line: Consolidates and amends laws regarding narcotic drugs, psychotropic substances, trafficking, and addict rehabilitation.
metadata.summary: This Act consolidates and amends existing laws concerning narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances in Pakistan. It prohibits cultivation, possession, import/export, and trafficking of these substances while establishing special courts for their prosecution. The legislation also provides for the freezing and forfeiture of assets derived from illicit drug activities and outlines measures for the treatment and rehabilitation of addicts.

name: Controller General of Accounts (Appointment Functions and Powers) Ordinance, 2001

metadata.short_title: The Controller General of Accounts (Appointment, Functions and Powers) Ordinance, 2001
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for separation of accounting functions and appointment of Controller-General of Accounts and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto
metadata.commencement: on the first day of July, 2001
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance establishes the Controller General of Accounts and separates accounting functions from audit functions.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance provides for the separation of accounting functions and the appointment of a Controller General of Accounts in Pakistan. It transfers accounting duties from the Auditor General to the newly appointed Controller General, who is responsible for maintaining accounts for the Federation, Provinces, and district Governments. The document outlines the specific functions of the Controller General, including authorizing payments, preparing financial statements, and coordinating audit observations, while ensuring that provincial employees' terms of service are not adversely affected.

metadata.short_title: The Co-operative Farming Act, 1976
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the formation, working and promotion of co-operative farming
repeals: The Co-operative Farming Ordinance, 1976 (XXII of 1976)
metadata.one_line: This Act provides for the formation, working, and promotion of co-operative farming societies across Pakistan.
metadata.summary: The Co-operative Farming Act, 1976 establishes a legal framework for forming and managing co-operative farming societies based on self-help and mutual aid. It defines the structure of these societies, including their managing committees, membership rights, and liability. The Act also creates higher-level bodies like District and Provincial Co-operative Federations and Councils to oversee these societies. Furthermore, it outlines procedures for registration, liquidation, tax exemptions, and the power to make rules.

metadata.short_title: The Cooperative Societies (Repayment of Loans) Ordinance, 1960
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the repayment of certain unsecured loans or loans insufficiently secured.
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance mandates the repayment and securing of unsecured loans taken from Cooperative Banks and Societies.
metadata.summary: The document provides a legal framework for the repayment of specific unsecured or insufficiently secured loans taken from Cooperative Banks and other Cooperative Societies. It applies to borrowers who have failed to repay such loans according to agreed terms, requiring partial repayment within six months and full security within two years. The Ordinance empowers the Registrar to make inquiries, summon witnesses, and issue notices, with decisions being final and not subject to court challenge. Non-compliance attracts penalties including imprisonment up to two years or fines.

metadata.short_title: The Copyright Ordinance, 1962
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend and consolidate the law relating to copyright
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance amends and consolidates the law relating to copyright in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: The Copyright Ordinance, 1962 was promulgated to amend and consolidate existing laws regarding copyright. It defines various types of works, establishes the term of copyright, and outlines the rights of owners, performers, and broadcasting organizations. The document also sets out provisions for registration, infringement remedies, and penalties for unauthorized use.

metadata.short_title: The Corporate and Industrial Restructuring Corporation Ordinance, 2000
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to make provisions for the acquisition, restructuring, rehabilitation, management, disposition and realization of non-performing loans and other assets of various banks and financial institutions and for matters ancillary or incidental thereto.
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both
metadata.one_line: Establishes a corporation to acquire and restructure non-performing assets of banks with Federal Government equity.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Corporate and Industrial Restructuring Corporation to manage non-performing loans and distressed enterprises. It applies to financial institutions where the Federal Government holds significant equity, such as Habib Bank Limited and United Bank Limited. The Corporation has powers to acquire assets, issue bonds, and recover debts as arrears of land revenue, while its members are treated as public servants.

metadata.short_title: The Corporate Rehabilitation Act, 2018
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for rehabilitation and re-organisation of distressed corporate entities
metadata.administering_body: Minister-in-charge of the Federal Government; Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan
metadata.one_line: Provides for the rehabilitation and re-organisation of distressed corporate entities in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes a legal framework for the rehabilitation and re-organisation of distressed corporate entities to encourage economic growth. It grants the High Court specific jurisdiction over cases involving debtors, administrators, and insolvency experts appointed by the Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan. The legislation outlines procedures for submitting plans of rehabilitation, mediating disputes, staying actions against debtors, and managing the administration of debtor property.

metadata.short_title: The Corporate Restructuring Companies Act, 2016
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment and regulation of corporate restructuring companies
metadata.commencement: at once for this section; on such date as the Federal Government may appoint by notification for remaining provisions
establishes: Commission (Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan)
metadata.max_penalty: fine imposed by the Commission
metadata.administering_body: Federal Government / Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan (SECP)
metadata.one_line: This Act establishes and regulates corporate restructuring companies to manage non-performing assets of financial institutions.
metadata.summary: The Corporate Restructuring Companies Act, 2016 provides for the establishment, licensing, and regulation of corporate restructuring companies in Pakistan. These companies are authorized to acquire, manage, restructure, and resolve non-performing assets held by financial institutions, as well as reorganize distressed commercial entities. The Act defines key terms such as 'financial institution', 'non-performing asset', and 'corporate restructuring company', and grants powers to the Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan (SECP) to oversee these operations.

metadata.short_title: The Corporation Employees (Special Powers) Ordinance, 1978
metadata.long_title: An ordinance to invest the President with certain powers in respect of persons in Corporation service
key_definitions: institution set up established, managed or controlled by the Federal Government
metadata.one_line: Invests the President with powers to remove or revert certain corporation employees without notice.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance empowers the President to take immediate action regarding persons in Corporation service. It allows for the removal or reversion of individuals appointed or promoted between January 1, 1972, and July 5, 1977, without prior notice. The Ordinance also declares that service in these corporations is deemed to be service of Pakistan and treats affected employees as civil servants under the Service Tribunals Act, 1973.

metadata.short_title: The Cost and Management Accountants Act, 1966
metadata.long_title: An Act to make provision for the regulation of the profession of cost and management accountants and for that purpose to establish an Institute of management accountants.
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Federal Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, appoint
repeals: Act VII of 1913
establishes: Institute of Cost and Management Accountants of Pakistan
metadata.one_line: This Act regulates the profession of cost and management accountants and establishes the Institute of Cost and Management Accountants of Pakistan.
metadata.summary: The Act provides for the regulation of the profession of cost and management accountants in Pakistan. It establishes the Institute of Cost and Management Accountants of Pakistan, constituting its members as a body corporate with perpetual succession. The legislation outlines the constitution, functions, and finances of the Council, defines key terms such as 'associate' and 'fellow', and sets penalties for falsely claiming membership or using the Council's name without qualification.

metadata.short_title: The Costs of Litigation Act, 2017
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 and the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Federal Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, specify
amends: Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (Act V of 1908)
Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898 (Act V of 1898)
key_definitions: proceedings (includes suit, appeal, review, revision, execution or any other proceedings and any matter incidental thereto)
metadata.one_line: Amends the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 and Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898 to regulate litigation costs and adjournment penalties in Islamabad.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 and the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898 to introduce a structured regime for awarding actual costs of litigation. It applies specifically to courts within the Islamabad Capital Territory. The legislation mandates that parties file details of actual costs before final orders and grants courts power to impose penalties for repeated adjournments or false averments.

metadata.short_title: The Cotton Act, 1957
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for measures for the promotion of international trade in cotton.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of Pakistan (except section 6 extends to the Karachi Division)
repeals: The Cotton Act, 1938
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years or with fine or with both
metadata.one_line: This Act promotes international trade in cotton by establishing a Board and regulating contracts.
metadata.summary: The Cotton Act, 1957 provides measures to promote international trade in cotton. It establishes a Cotton Board with members nominated by provincial governments to supervise dealings in cotton connected with export. The Federal Government has powers to requisition factories, secure contract fulfillment, call for information, and recognize associations to control contracts. The Act also defines key terms like 'cotton' and 'contract', prescribes penalties for false statements, and allows the government to make rules.

metadata.short_title: The Cotton Cess Act, 1923
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the creation of a fund for the improvement and development of the growing, marketing and manufacture of cotton
repeals: The Cotton Cess Act, 1923
metadata.status_evidence: this Act shall be deemed to have been repealed.
metadata.one_line: This Act creates a fund for the cotton industry and establishes the Pakistan Central Cotton Committee to levy and manage a cess on cotton.
metadata.summary: The Cotton Cess Act, 1923 provides for the creation of a fund dedicated to the improvement and development of the growing, marketing, and manufacture of cotton. It establishes the Pakistan Central Cotton Committee as a body corporate to manage this fund and oversee industry-related activities. The Act imposes a cess on all cotton exported from Pakistan or consumed in mills within the country, with collection handled by the Collector. It also grants powers to the Federal Government and the Committee to make rules regarding assessments, returns, inspections, and the application of proceeds.

metadata.short_title: The Cotton Cloth Act, 1918
metadata.long_title: An Act to take powers to provide for the cheap supply of cotton cloth to the poorer classes of the community.
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment which may extend to six months, or with fine or with both
metadata.one_line: This Act empowers the Provincial Government to regulate cotton cloth supply and pricing for poorer classes.
metadata.summary: The Cotton Cloth Act, 1918 provides powers to ensure a cheap supply of locally manufactured cotton cloth to the poorer classes. It establishes Controllers appointed by the Provincial Government who can issue orders regarding manufacture, transport, distribution, and sale of standard cloth. The Act allows for price fixing, licensing of sellers, and the appointment of Advisory Committees to assist Controllers. Non-compliance with Controller orders is punishable by imprisonment up to six months or a fine.

metadata.short_title: The Cotton Cloth and Yarn (Contracts) Ordinance, 1944
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to regulate the prices which may be charged in sales of cotton cloth and yarn under contracts.
metadata.one_line: Regulates maximum prices for cotton cloth and yarn sales under contracts between wholesale and retail dealers.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance regulates the prices charged in sales of cotton cloth and yarn made under contracts between wholesale and retail dealers. It ensures that prices do not exceed maximum limits fixed by the Cotton Cloth and Yarn (Control) Order, 1943, or the price paid on the last preceding transfer. Buyers who paid excess prices are entitled to recover the difference from sellers.

name: Cotton Ginning and Pressing Factories Act, 1925

metadata.short_title: The Cotton Ginning and Pressing Factories Act, 1925
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the better regulation of cotton ginning and cotton pressing factories
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Federal Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, appoint
metadata.max_penalty: five hundred rupees
metadata.one_line: Regulates cotton ginning and pressing factories, requiring registers, marked bales, and returns.
metadata.summary: This Act provides for the better regulation of cotton ginning and cotton pressing factories in Pakistan. It mandates the maintenance of specific registers by factory owners, requires the marking of pressed bales with serial numbers and prescribed marks, and establishes return systems for data collection. The Act defines key terms such as 'cotton', 'bale', and 'occupier', and outlines penalties for non-compliance, including fines up to five hundred rupees for false entries or failure to produce registers.

name: Cotton Ginning Control and Development (Repeal) Ordinance, 1977

metadata.short_title: The Cotton Ginning Control and Development (Repeal) Ordinance, 1977
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to repeal the Cotton Ginning Control and Development Act, 1976 (LIX of 1976)
repeals: Cotton Ginning Control and Development Act, 1976 (LIX of 1976)
metadata.max_penalty: rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance repeals the Cotton Ginning Control and Development Act, 1976 and provides for the return of establishments and compensation.
metadata.summary: The Cotton Ginning Control and Development (Repeal) Ordinance, 1977 was promulgated to repeal the Cotton Ginning Control and Development Act, 1976. It mandates the return of establishments acquired by the Corporation to their previous management within a specified period, subject to the recovery of outstanding amounts. The Ordinance also outlines provisions for employee continuance in service, compensation calculations based on asset values, and penalties for obstructing the enforcement of its provisions.

metadata.short_title: The Cotton Industry (Statistics) Act, 1926
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the regular submission of returns of quantities of cotton goods manufactured and cotton yarn spun in Pakistan
repeals: Cotton Duties Act, 1896
metadata.max_penalty: five hundred rupees or one thousand rupees depending on the offence
metadata.one_line: This Act mandates mill owners to submit monthly statistics on cotton production and allows government inspection.
metadata.summary: The Cotton Industry (Statistics) Act, 1926 requires mill owners to prepare and deliver monthly returns detailing the quantities of cotton goods manufactured and yarn spun. The Provincial Government is empowered to inspect mills, verify the accuracy of these returns, and publish aggregate statistics. The Act also outlines penalties for falsifying records or refusing to submit returns, while ensuring confidentiality of acquired information.

metadata.short_title: The Cotton Standardization Ordinance, 2002
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the establishment of the Pakistan Cotton Standards Institute and to promote quality control of cotton
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Pakistan Cotton Standards Institute to promote cotton quality control and standardization.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Pakistan Cotton Standards Institute as a body corporate with perpetual succession. It sets up a Board of Directors comprising representatives from various ministries, provinces, and industry associations to manage the Institute. The document defines key terms related to cotton grading, contamination, and bale specifications, and empowers the Institute to make rules for quality control, fee levying, and staff appointments.

metadata.short_title: The Cotton Transport Act, 1923
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the restriction and control of the transport of cotton in certain circumstances.
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment which may extend to three months, or fine which may extend to five thousand rupees, or both
metadata.one_line: This Act restricts and controls the transport of cotton to maintain quality and reputation in specific areas.
metadata.summary: The Cotton Transport Act, 1923 provides for the restriction and control of cotton transport by rail and prohibits the import of cotton into designated protected areas without a licence. It empowers the appropriate Government to issue notifications banning cotton imports and to make rules regarding licences and their conditions. The Act outlines procedures for refusing carriage or delivery of unlicensed cotton, penalties for contravention, and requires previous approval from Parliament or the Provincial Assembly for notifications and rules.

metadata.short_title: The Countervailing Duties Act, 2015
metadata.long_title: An Act to reform and repeal the Countervailing Duties Ordinance, 2001
repeals: Countervailing Duties Ordinance, 2001
establishes: National Tariff Commission (referenced as established under existing law)
Appellate Tribunal (referenced as established under Anti-Dumping duties Law)
metadata.one_line: This Act establishes the framework for imposing countervailing duties to offset injurious subsidies on imported goods.
metadata.summary: The Countervailing Duties Act, 2015 reforms and repeals the Countervailing Duties Ordinance, 2001 to align Pakistan's laws with WTO agreements. It provides a comprehensive framework for investigating subsidies, determining injury to domestic industries, and imposing provisional or definitive countervailing duties. The Act outlines procedures for verification visits, interim reviews, and the acceptance of undertakings from exporters to mitigate injurious subsidization.

name: Countervailing Duties Ordinance, 2001(Repealed by Act XIII of 2015)

metadata.short_title: The Countervailing Duties Ordinance, 2001
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend and consolidate the law relating to imposition of countervailing duties to offset subsidies.
amends: General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade, 1994
Agreement on Subsidies and Countervailing Measures
repeals: Countervailing Duties Act, 2015 (XIII of 2015)
metadata.status_evidence: [Repealed by Act XIII of 2015]
establishes: Appellate Tribunal (referenced as established under Anti-Dumping Ordinance, 2000)
National Tariff Commission (referenced as established under National Tariff Commission Act, 1990)
metadata.one_line: Amends and consolidates laws on countervailing duties to offset subsidies on imported goods in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends and consolidates the legal framework for imposing countervailing duties to offset injurious subsidies on imported goods into Pakistan. It provides a mechanism for investigating subsidies, determining injury to domestic industries, and imposing provisional or definitive duties. The document incorporates provisions from WTO agreements regarding subsidies and includes specific rules for agricultural payments and developing countries.

metadata.short_title: The Court-fees Act, 1870
metadata.long_title: An Act to consolidate the enactments relating to court-fees and stamps.
repeals: Act XIV of 1870
metadata.one_line: This Act consolidates laws regarding court fees, stamps, and procedures for probate and administration of estates.
metadata.summary: The Court-fees Act, 1870 consolidates enactments relating to court fees and stamps payable in High Courts, other courts, and public offices. It specifies the levy of fees on documents filed, appeals, and processes, as well as procedures for probate and letters of administration. The Act also outlines rules for stamping documents, valuation of property for fee purposes, and the recovery of penalties for under-payment.

metadata.short_title: The COVID-19 (Prevention of Hoarding) Act, 2021
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the prevention of hoarding in respect of scheduled articles, in the wake of an emergent situation resulting from the outbreak of the Corona virus pandemic (COVID-19) and for matters connected therewith and ancillary thereto
metadata.max_penalty: simple imprisonment up to three years and fine equivalent to fifty percent of the value of the scheduled articles involved in the case or one million Rupees
metadata.one_line: Prevents hoarding of essential items in Islamabad during the COVID-19 pandemic with penalties for offenders.
metadata.summary: This Act prevents hoarding of scheduled articles in the Islamabad Capital Territory during the COVID-19 pandemic. It defines dealers and hoarding, empowers officers to search premises without warrants, and allows for the auction of seized goods. The Act prescribes criminal offences including imprisonment and fines for hoarding or false reporting, and grants powers to make rules and amend the schedule.

metadata.short_title: The Credit Bureaus Act, 2015
metadata.long_title: A Bill to provide for the incorporation and functioning of credit bureaus and to provide for matters connected therewith and incidental thereto
metadata.commencement: at once on such dates as the Federal Government may, by notification in the official Gazette appoint
metadata.one_line: An Act to provide for the incorporation and functioning of credit bureaus in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the legal framework for the incorporation and operation of credit bureaus in Pakistan. It defines key terms related to banking, credit information, and credit institutions, while outlining the licensing requirements and eligibility criteria for establishing a credit bureau. The legislation empowers the State Bank of Pakistan to supervise credit bureaus, including the power to remove directors and appoint administrators if necessary. Furthermore, it outlines the obligations of credit bureaus regarding the accuracy of data, consumer rights to dispute information, and penalties for non-compliance.

metadata.short_title: The Criminal Law Amendment (Special Court) Act, 1976
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the trial by a special Court of certain offences affecting the security, integrity or sovereignty of Pakistan or any part thereof, including offences of high treason, and for matters connected therewith
key_definitions: Special Court (court set up under section 4)
metadata.one_line: Establishes Special Courts to try offences against Pakistan's security and sovereignty.
metadata.summary: This Act provides for the establishment of Special Courts composed of three High Court Judges to try specific offences affecting the security, integrity, or sovereignty of Pakistan. It grants these courts special powers and procedures, including the ability to appoint defense counsel at state expense and restrict appeals to the Supreme Court only. The Act overrides other laws regarding jurisdiction and evidence admissibility for cases tried by these Special Courts.

metadata.short_title: The Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1908
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the more speedy trial of certain offences, and for the Prohibition of associations dangerous to the public peace.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of Pakistan (extended by notification)
repeals: The Indian Criminal Law Amendment Repealing Act, 1922 (V of 1922), s.3
establishes: Board appointed by the Chief Justice of the High Court of the Province
metadata.max_penalty: seven years imprisonment or fine or both
metadata.administering_body: Federal Government or the Provincial Government
metadata.one_line: Provides for speedy trial of offences and prohibition of associations dangerous to public peace.
metadata.summary: This Act enables the Federal or Provincial Government to declare associations unlawful if they encourage terrorism, sectarianism, violence, or endanger public order. It outlines penalties for members and managers of such associations, including imprisonment up to seven years. The Act also grants powers to notify places used by unlawful associations, seize property, and forfeit funds, while establishing a Board for appeals against declarations.

name: Customs Act, 1969 (Same as on the official website of FBR dated 30-06-2025)

metadata.short_title: The Customs Act, 1969
metadata.long_title: An Act to consolidate the law relating to customs and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
establishes: Directorate General Intelligence and Risk Management, Customs
Directorate General of China Pakistan Economic Corridor
Directorate General of Reform and Automation
Directorate General of Communication and Public Relations, Customs
Directorate General of Customs Academy of Pakistan
Directorate General of Intellectual Property Rights
Directorate General of Law and Prosecution
Directorate General of National Nuclear Detection Architecture
Directorate General of National Targeting Centre
Directorate General of Combating Trade Based Money Laundering
Directorate General of Post Clearance Audit(PCA)
Directorate General of Input Output Co-efficient
metadata.one_line: Consolidates laws relating to customs, duties, import/export control, and licensing in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Act consolidates the law relating to customs in Pakistan. It establishes various directorates within the Customs department, defines ports and stations, regulates the levy of duties, and provides for exemptions and drawbacks. The Act also covers procedures for the arrival and departure of conveyances, licensing of agents, and the prevention of fiscal fraud.

metadata.short_title: The Cutchi Memons Act, 1938
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide that all Cutchi Memons shall be governed in matters of succession and inheritance by the Muslim Law.
metadata.status_evidence: Rep. by the Repealing and Amending Act, 1942 (XXV of 1942), s.2 and First Schedule.
metadata.one_line: This Act governs succession and inheritance for Cutchi Memons under Muslim Law.
metadata.summary: The Cutchi Memons Act, 1938 provides that all Cutchi Memons shall be governed by Muslim Law in matters of succession and inheritance. It includes savings provisions to protect rights acquired before the Act's commencement and allows existing legal proceedings to continue as if the Act had not been passed. The Act came into force on November 1, 1938, but was later repealed by the Repealing and Amending Act, 1942.

metadata.short_title: The Cutting of Trees (Prohibition) Act, 1992
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the prohibition of cutting of trees near the external frontiers of Pakistan and matters ancillary thereto
repeals: The Cutting of Trees (Prohibition) Act, 1975
metadata.max_penalty: fine which may extend to five thousand rupees
metadata.one_line: Prohibits cutting of trees near Pakistan's external frontiers and prescribes penalties for violations.
metadata.summary: This Act prohibits the cutting, felling, or damaging of trees near the external frontiers of Pakistan without prior written approval from an authorised officer. It defines specific zones adjacent to the frontier where tree density limits apply and establishes penalties ranging up to five thousand rupees for violations in the first zone. The Act empowers provincial governments to demarcate zones, allows authorised officers to enter land for surveys, and provides mechanisms for seizing and confiscating illegally cut trees and tools used in the offence.

metadata.short_title: The Daanish Schools Authority Act, 2026
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment and management of the Daanish Schools
metadata.territorial_extent: the Islamabad Capital Territory and to Daanish Schools wherever they may be
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Daanish Schools Authority to manage schools for destitute children in Islamabad and elsewhere.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Daanish Schools Authority to regulate and manage Daanish Schools, focusing on providing quality education to destitute children. The Authority is a body corporate with members including the Prime Minister, Federal Ministers, and prominent educationists. It has powers to prescribe courses, award scholarships, maintain hostels, and conduct examinations. The Act also outlines the composition of the Authority, its functions, financial management, and provisions for rules and regulations.

metadata.short_title: Daanish University Islamabad Act, 2026
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of Daanish University, Islamabad and to provide for matters ancillary thereto and connected therewith
metadata.one_line: Establishes Daanish University Islamabad with full autonomy and defines its structure, governance, and functions.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Daanish University, Islamabad as a body corporate with perpetual succession and academic, financial, and administrative autonomy. It outlines the composition of the university, including the Chancellor, Senate, Rector, and various authorities, while defining their powers and functions. The legislation also provides for the establishment of a University Fund, the making of Statutes and Regulations by the Senate, and procedures for staff appointments and research degree examinations.

metadata.short_title: The Dangerous Cargoes Act, 1953
