metadata.long_title: An Act to make further provision for the safety of ports in respect of the transit, working and storage of dangerous cargoes and matters incidental thereto.
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years or with fine which may extend to five thousand rupees or with both
metadata.one_line: This Act provides for the safety of ports regarding dangerous cargoes, defining them and empowering authorities to take measures against fire and explosions.
metadata.summary: The Dangerous Cargoes Act, 1953 was enacted to ensure port safety concerning the transit, working, and storage of dangerous cargoes. It defines dangerous cargoes including explosives, petroleum, and other goods liable to fire or explosion. The Act empowers the Federal Government, Chief of the Naval Staff, and Fortress Commander to issue orders for safety measures, declare emergencies, and control vessels in ports.

metadata.short_title: The Dar-ul-Madina International University Islamabad Act, 2013
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of Dar-ul-Madina International University and for matters ancillary thereto
metadata.one_line: Establishes Dar-ul-Madina International University Islamabad with academic autonomy and defines its structure.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Dar-ul-Madina International University in Islamabad as a body corporate with perpetual succession. It grants the university academic, financial, and administrative autonomy while defining its officers, authorities, and governing bodies such as the Board of trustees and Academic Council. The legislation also outlines the powers to set up campuses abroad, make statutes and regulations, and manage the university fund.

metadata.short_title: The Day Care Centres Act, 2023
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the facility of day care centres in public and private establishments
metadata.max_penalty: fine of one hundred thousand rupees or imprisonment for six months
metadata.one_line: Provides for the establishment of day care centres in public and private establishments with penalties for non-compliance.
metadata.summary: This Act facilitates the provision of day care centres for employees in public and private establishments. It mandates that all establishments with at least seventy employees must establish a day care centre. The Federal Government is responsible for ensuring compliance, while non-compliance attracts warnings, fines up to one hundred thousand rupees, or imprisonment for six months.

metadata.short_title: The Decorations Act, 1975
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the conferment by the President of decorations in recognition of gallantry, meritorious service in the Armed Forces [, academic distinction or distinction in the field of sports or nursing.]
metadata.commencement: at once; deemed to have taken effect on 1973-08-14
metadata.max_penalty: fine which may extend to twenty thousand rupees
key_definitions: meritorious service in the Armed Forces
metadata.one_line: Provides for the conferment by the President of decorations for gallantry, meritorious service, academic distinction, sports, or nursing.
metadata.summary: This Act empowers the President to institute and create decorations recognizing gallantry, meritorious service in the Armed Forces, academic distinction, or achievements in sports and nursing. It outlines the conditions for awarding, withdrawing, or restoring these honors and restricts citizens from accepting foreign titles without Federal Government approval. The Act also prescribes penalties for contravention of its provisions regarding decorations and establishes that only Courts of Session can try related offences.

metadata.short_title: The Defamation Ordinance, 2002
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to make provisions in respect of defamation and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance defines defamation, sets out defences and remedies including apologies and damages for libel and slander.
metadata.summary: The Defamation Ordinance, 2002 provides legal provisions regarding defamation in Pakistan. It defines key terms such as broadcasting, editor, newspaper, publication, and publisher. The document outlines that defamation can be actionable without proof of special damage and establishes defences including truth, public interest, and privilege. It also specifies remedies like apologies and minimum damages, along with procedural rules for filing actions and appeals.

metadata.short_title: Defence Housing Authority Islamabad Act, 2013
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for establishment of Defence Housing Authority Islamabad
metadata.territorial_extent: the specified area in Islamabad Capital Territory
metadata.commencement: at once and deemed to have taken effect on and from the 15th August, 2010
repeals: Defence Housing Authority Islamabad Ordinance, 2010 (XV of 2010)
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Defence Housing Authority Islamabad to carry out land development schemes for defence forces personnel and their families in Islamabad.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Defence Housing Authority Islamabad as a body corporate with perpetual succession. Its primary purpose is to carry out land development schemes, specifically for the welfare of bereaved families of martyrs, war injured, disabled, and other persons of the defence forces of Pakistan. The Authority has powers to borrow, manage an Authority Fund, cancel allotments for non-payment, and make regulations, subject to adherence to the master plan of Islamabad.

metadata.short_title: The Defence Services (Inquiry) (Special Provisions) Ordinance, 1969
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to make provision for a uniform procedure for inquiring into the conduct of a member of a Defence Service serving otherwise than in an organization or unit of his service.
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Central Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, appoint
metadata.one_line: Provides uniform procedure for inquiring into the conduct of Defence Service members serving outside their own units.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes a uniform procedure for conducting inquiries into the conduct of Defence Service members who are serving outside their primary organization or unit. It defines key terms such as 'board of inquiry', 'Chief of Staff', and 'commanding officer' to clarify roles during investigations. The document outlines the composition of inquiry boards, the process for convening them, and the subsequent actions required by commanding officers and the Chief of Staff based on the inquiry findings.

metadata.short_title: The Defense Forces of Pakistan Act, 2026
metadata.long_title: An Act to enact the Defense Forces of Pakistan Act, 2026
metadata.commencement: at once and deemed to have taken effect from the thirteenth day of November two thousand and twenty-five
repeals: Pakistan Army Act, 1952
Pakistan Air Force Act, 1953
Pakistan Navy Ordinance, 1967
Cantonments Act, 1924
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Defense Forces Headquarters and defines powers of the Chief of Defense Forces to integrate armed forces.
metadata.summary: This Act enacts provisions to give effect to the constitutional mandate regarding the Chief of the Army Staff as Commander of the Armed Forces. It establishes the Defense Forces Headquarters under the command of the Chief of Defense Forces, who will oversee multidomain integration and joint operations. The Act empowers the Federal Government to make rules and regulations while overriding inconsistent provisions in previous laws like the Pakistan Army Act, 1952.

name: Degree Awarding Status to Dawood College of Engineering and Technology, Karachi Act, 2010

metadata.short_title: The Degree Awarding Status to Dawood College of Engineering and Technology, Karachi Act, 2010
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for Degree Awarding Status to Dawood College of Engineering and Technology, Karachi
metadata.commencement: at once; deemed to have taken effect on the 29th of November, 2009
repeals: The Dawood College of Engineering and Technology Karachi Resolution No. F.3/82 N 1, dated the 27th September, 1987
establishes: Dawood College of Engineering and Technology, Karachi (as a body corporate)
metadata.one_line: This Act grants degree awarding status and autonomy to Dawood College of Engineering and Technology, Karachi.
metadata.summary: This Act reconstitutes Dawood College of Engineering and Technology, Karachi as a degree awarding institution with perpetual succession. It grants the college academic, financial, and administrative autonomy, including the power to employ staff and manage its budget without external interference. The Act establishes governing bodies such as the Senate, Syndicate, and Academic Council, while repealing an earlier resolution from 1987.

metadata.short_title: The Dekkhan Agriculturists' Relief Act, 1879
metadata.long_title: An Act for the relief of Indebted Agriculturists in certain parts of the Dekkhan.
repeals: Section 9, clause first, of Bombay Regulation V of 1827
metadata.one_line: Relieves indebted agriculturists in the Dekkhan through modified civil procedures, insolvency rules, and registration requirements.
metadata.summary: This Act provides relief to indebted agriculturists in specific parts of the Dekkhan by regulating how suits are heard, mortgages are handled, and debts are collected. It establishes Village-munsifs and Village-registrars to manage local disputes and instrument registration, while also introducing conciliation mechanisms to settle cases before they reach higher courts. The legislation modifies standard civil procedure codes and insolvency rules to protect farmers from harsh execution measures like imprisonment or the sale of essential agricultural produce.

metadata.short_title: The Delimitation of Constituencies Act, 1974
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the delimitation of constituencies for elections to the National Assembly and the Provincial Assemblies.
metadata.one_line: Provides for the delimitation of constituencies for elections to the National Assembly and Provincial Assemblies.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes a Commission to delimit territorial constituencies for elections to the National Assembly and Provincial Assemblies based on population. It outlines the Commission's procedure, powers to delegate functions, and authority to receive representations from voters regarding constituency boundaries. The Act also covers the allocation of reserved seats for women and non-Muslims, the preparation of final lists, and includes a bar on judicial jurisdiction over the validity of delimitation proceedings.

metadata.short_title: The Deposit Protection Corporation Act, 2016
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of Deposit Protection Corporation as a subsidiary of the State Bank of Pakistan and for the management and control thereof
repeals: Banks (Nationalization) Act, 1974 (XIX of 1974)
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Deposit Protection Corporation as a State Bank subsidiary to protect eligible depositors and ensure financial stability.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Deposit Protection Corporation as a body corporate and a subsidiary of the State Bank of Pakistan. Its primary objectives are to protect eligible depositors from losses in failed institutions, contribute to financial stability, and maintain public trust in the financial system. The Corporation is empowered to reimburse protected deposits, provide financial support for resolution processes, and manage its resources under the direction of the State Bank.

name: Deputy Chairman and Deputy Speaker (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) Act, 1975

metadata.short_title: The Deputy Chairman and Deputy Speaker (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) Act, 1975
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the salaries, allowances and privileges of the Deputy Chairman of the Senate and the Deputy Speaker of die The National Assembly.
metadata.commencement: at once and shall be deemed to have taken effect on the fourteenth day of August, 1975
subjects: Deputy Speaker of the National Assembly
metadata.one_line: This Act provides for the salaries, allowances, privileges, and official residences of the Deputy Chairman of the Senate and the Deputy Speaker of the National Assembly.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the financial terms and privileges for the Deputy Chairman of the Senate and the Deputy Speaker of the National Assembly. It specifies rates for salary, equipment allowance, sumptuary allowance, and transport, while also defining official residence rights and medical facilities. The legislation further outlines provisions for leave, discretionary grants, and the power to make rules for its implementation.

metadata.short_title: The Destruction of Records Act, 1917
metadata.long_title: An Act to consolidate and amend the law providing for the destruction or other disposal of certain documents in the possession or custody of Courts and Revenue and other public officers.
repeals: Destruction of Records Act, 1879 (III of 1879)
key_definitions: Courts of Civil or Criminal jurisdiction
metadata.one_line: Consolidates laws allowing authorities to make rules for the destruction or disposal of public documents.
metadata.summary: This Act consolidates and amends the law regarding the destruction or other disposal of certain documents held by Courts, Revenue officers, and other public officers. It empowers specific authorities, such as High Courts, Chief Controlling Revenue-authorities, Provincial Governments, and the Federal Government, to make rules for disposing of documents deemed not of sufficient public value. The Act validates former rules made under previous legislation and saves certain documents from destruction if required by other laws.

metadata.short_title: The Development of Industries (Federal Control) (Repeal) Ordinance, 1979
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to repeal the Development of Industries (Federal Control) Act, 1972
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Federal Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, appoint
repeals: The Development of Industries (Federal Control) Act, 1972
metadata.status_evidence: An Ordinance to repeal the Development of Industries (Federal Control) Act, 1972
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance repeals the Development of Industries (Federal Control) Act, 1972 and dissolves the Board.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance was promulgated to repeal the Development of Industries (Federal Control) Act, 1972. It provides for the dissolution of the Board established under that Act and the transfer of its assets, liabilities, and employees to a designated corporation or managed company. The document also ensures the continuation of pending legal proceedings against the Board and grants indemnity to relevant authorities.

metadata.short_title: The Development of Industries (Government Control) Act, 1949
metadata.long_title: An Act to make provision for certain matters connected with the development of industries under Government Control.
metadata.one_line: This Act provides for government control over the development of specified industries in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: The Development of Industries (Government Control) Act, 1949 empowers the Federal Government to regulate the development of specific industries deemed expedient in the public interest. It defines key terms such as 'industry' and 'specified', lists various controlled sectors in the Schedule, and grants the government power to make rules subject to prior publication. The Act extends to the whole of Pakistan and came into force immediately upon enactment.

metadata.short_title: The Digital Nation Pakistan Act, 2025
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the transformation of Pakistan into a digital nation, enabling a digital society, digital economy, and digital governance
metadata.one_line: Establishes the National Digital Commission and Pakistan Digital Authority to transform Pakistan into a digital nation.
metadata.summary: This Act transforms Pakistan into a digital nation by establishing the National Digital Commission and the Pakistan Digital Authority. It creates a framework for digital society, economy, and governance through secure digital public infrastructure. The Act defines key terms like 'digital citizen journeys' and establishes funds and oversight mechanisms to ensure efficient public service delivery.

metadata.short_title: Digital Presence Proceeds Tax Act, 2025
metadata.long_title: An Act for the enactment of Digital Presence Proceeds Tax Act, 2025
metadata.max_penalty: one million rupees for each default regarding non-filing of statements; recovery along with default surcharge for failure to deduct or deposit tax
metadata.administering_body: Inland Revenue Department of the Board
metadata.one_line: Imposes a tax on foreign vendors with significant digital presence in Pakistan for digitally ordered goods and services.
metadata.summary: This Act introduces a Digital Presence Proceeds Tax to ensure tax fairness for foreign vendors generating revenue from Pakistani users without physical presence. It applies to digitally delivered services and goods supplied from outside Pakistan, requiring payment intermediaries and social media platforms to collect and report transactions. The legislation establishes penalties for non-compliance, including suspension of remittances to foreign advertisers who fail to pay the tax after a specified period.

name: Diplomatic and Consular Officers (Oaths and Fees) Act, 1948

metadata.short_title: The Diplomatic and Consular Officers (Oaths and Fees) Act, 1948
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the administration of oaths by diplomatic and consular Officers and to prescribe the fees leviable in respect of certain of their official duties.
metadata.commencement: at once; deemed to have taken effect from 15th August, 1947
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years and fine (up to Rs. 3,000 for excessive fees)
metadata.one_line: This Act regulates oaths, notarial acts, and fees for Pakistani diplomatic and consular officers abroad.
metadata.summary: The Diplomatic and Consular Officers (Oaths and Fees) Act, 1948 provides the legal framework for administering oaths and taking affidavits by diplomatic and consular officers in foreign countries. It empowers the Federal Government to fix fees for these official duties and mandates their exhibition at customs ports and in offices. The Act also establishes penalties for taking excessive fees or committing fraud related to oaths and documents.

metadata.short_title: The Diplomatic and Consular Privileges Act, 1972
metadata.long_title: An Act to give effect in Pakistan to the Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations, 1961, and the Vienna Convention on Consular Relations, 1963.
repeals: The Diplomatic and Consular Privileges Ordinance, 1972 (XV of 1972)
key_definitions: members of the staff of the mission
members of the administrative and technical staff
metadata.one_line: This Act gives effect in Pakistan to the Vienna Conventions on Diplomatic and Consular Relations.
metadata.summary: The Act provides for the implementation of the Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations, 1961, and the Vienna Convention on Consular Relations, 1963 within Pakistan. It grants force of law to the provisions of these conventions regarding privileges, immunities, and protections for diplomatic and consular missions. The legislation also empowers the Federal Government to restrict privileges if reciprocity is not maintained and outlines specific exemptions from taxation and personal services.

name: Diplomatic Immunities (Common wealth Countries Representatives), Act, 1957

metadata.short_title: The Diplomatic Immunities (Commonwealth Countries Representatives) Act, 1957
metadata.long_title: An Act to declare and confer certain immunities on representatives in Pakistan of Commonwealth Countries and on certain other persons.
metadata.one_line: This Act declares and confers immunities on Commonwealth representatives in Pakistan and provides for related rules.
metadata.summary: The Diplomatic Immunities (Commonwealth Countries Representatives) Act, 1957 declares and confers specific immunities on representatives from Commonwealth countries residing in Pakistan. It defines key terms such as 'chief representative', 'envoy', and 'staff', and grants immunity from suit and legal process to these individuals and their families under certain conditions. The Act also empowers the President to make rules regarding consular immunity and allows for the waiver of immunity by representatives or through prescribed rules.

name: Diplomatic Immunities (Conferences with Common wealth Countries) Act, 1963

metadata.short_title: The Diplomatic Immunities (Conferences with Commonwealth Countries) Act, 1963
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for conferring certain immunities on representatives of governments of Commonwealth countries attending conferences in Pakistan and on their official staffs.
metadata.administering_body: the Secretary to the Government of Pakistan in the Ministry concerned with the convening or sponsoring of a conference
metadata.one_line: Confers diplomatic immunities on Commonwealth representatives and staff attending conferences in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Act provides for conferring specific immunities on representatives of Commonwealth countries and their official staffs when they attend conferences in Pakistan. It applies reciprocally if similar provisions exist in the other country's laws. The Secretary to the Government of Pakistan compiles and publishes lists of eligible representatives and staff, which serve as conclusive proof of their entitlement to immunity from suit, legal process, and inviolability of residence and premises.

metadata.short_title: The Disabled Persons (Employment and Rehabilitation) Ordinance, 1981
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the employment, rehabilitation and welfare of disabled persons.
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Federal Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, appoint
establishes: National Council for the Rehabilitation of Disabled Persons
Provincial Council for the Rehabilitation of Disabled Persons
metadata.max_penalty: fine which may extend to one thousand rupees and, in the case of non-payment of fine, with an additional fine which may extend to ten rupees for every day during which the payment of fine is not made
metadata.administering_body: National Council (in consultation with the Federal Government)
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance establishes councils and a fund to provide employment, rehabilitation, and welfare for disabled persons in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: The Disabled Persons (Employment and Rehabilitation) Ordinance, 1981 was promulgated by the President to ensure the employment, rehabilitation, and welfare of disabled persons. It establishes a National Council and Provincial Councils comprising representatives from various government divisions, trade unions, and social welfare organizations. The Ordinance creates a Rehabilitation Fund financed by establishments employing over one hundred workers, grants, and donations, which is utilized for training centers, medical treatment, stipends, and artificial limbs. It also defines key terms such as 'disabled person' and 'establishment', outlines the functions of the councils, and prescribes penalties for non-compliance with payment obligations into the Fund.

metadata.short_title: The Discontinuance of Medical Reimbursement Act, 1972
metadata.long_title: An Act for the discontinuance of reimbursement of medical expenses incurred by Government servants and certain other employees
metadata.one_line: Discontinues reimbursement of medical expenses for government servants and employees of public corporations.
metadata.summary: This Act discontinues the reimbursement of medical expenses incurred by Government servants and employees of other bodies in Pakistan. It applies to all employees of Federal and Provincial Governments as well as those working in public corporations and statutory bodies. While claiming reimbursement for purchased medicines is prohibited, employees may still receive prescribed medicines under specific rules and within allocated budgetary limits.

metadata.short_title: The Dissolution of Muslim Marriages Act, 1939
metadata.long_title: An Act to consolidate and clarify the provisions of Muslim law relating to suits for dissolution of marriage by women married under Muslim law and to remove doubts as to the effect of the renunciation of Islam by a married Muslim woman on her marriage tie.
repeals: The Dissolution of Muslim Marriages Act, 1939 (as amended by the Repealing and Amending Act, 1942)
metadata.repealed_by: The Repealing and Amending Act, 1942 (XXV of 1942)
key_definitions: Lian: where the husband has accused his wife of zina and the wife does not accept the accusation as true
Muslim Law: law relating to suits for dissolution of marriage by women married under Muslim law
metadata.one_line: Consolidates provisions for Muslim women to obtain decrees dissolving their marriages on specific grounds.
metadata.summary: This Act consolidates and clarifies the provisions of Muslim law regarding suits for the dissolution of marriage by women married under that law. It specifies various grounds upon which a woman is entitled to obtain a decree, including the husband's whereabouts being unknown for four years, failure to provide maintenance, imprisonment, impotence, insanity, leprosy, cruelty, or conversion to another faith. The Act also addresses procedural aspects such as serving notice on heirs when the husband's whereabouts are unknown and ensures that dower rights remain unaffected by the dissolution.

metadata.short_title: The Disturbed Areas (Special Powers) Ordinance, 1962
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to confer certain special powers upon officers in respect of disturbed areas.
key_definitions: officer of the Civil Armed Forces
metadata.one_line: Confers special powers on magistrates and police officers to use force in disturbed areas.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance was promulgated to confer special powers upon officers regarding disturbed areas. It extends to the whole of Pakistan and comes into force immediately. The law defines specific terms such as 'disturbed area' and grants magistrates, police officers, and armed forces members powers to use force, arrest without warrant, and search premises in these areas.

metadata.short_title: The Divorce Act
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the law relating to Divorce and Matrimonial Causes
metadata.one_line: An Act to amend the law relating to divorce and matrimonial causes for Christians domiciled in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the law regarding divorce and matrimonial causes specifically for persons professing the Christian religion. It grants jurisdiction to certain courts to make decrees of dissolution or nullity of marriage where parties are domiciled in Pakistan. The legislation covers various aspects including petitions for dissolution, grounds for nullity, judicial separation, protection orders for deserted wives, alimony, settlements, and custody of children.

metadata.short_title: The Dock Labourers Act, 1934
metadata.long_title: An Act to give effect in [Pakistan] to the Convention concerning the protection against accidents of workers employed in loading and unloading ships.
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Federal Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, appoint
metadata.max_penalty: fine which may extend to five hundred rupees
metadata.one_line: This Act provides safety measures and regulations for workers employed in loading and unloading ships in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: The Dock Labourers Act, 1934 was enacted to implement an international convention regarding worker safety during ship loading and unloading operations. It empowers the Federal Government to appoint inspectors and make regulations concerning safety appliances, access means, lighting, and machinery conditions. The Act defines specific processes and workers, outlines penalties for non-compliance, and establishes jurisdictional limits for prosecuting offences under the legislation.

metadata.short_title: The Dock Workers (Regulation of Employment) Act, 1974
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for regulating the employment of dock workers
repeals: The Dock Workers (Regulation of Employment) Ordinance, 1973
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for one year or fine up to five thousand rupees or both
metadata.one_line: This Act regulates dock worker employment to ensure efficient ship operations and speedy goods transit.
metadata.summary: The Dock Workers (Regulation of Employment) Act, 1974 provides for the regulation of dock worker employment to ensure efficient performance of work and speedy transit of goods. It empowers the Federal Government to make schemes for registering dock workers, regulating their recruitment, conduct, remuneration, and welfare, including health and safety measures. The Act also mandates the transfer of funds created for dock workers to the Federal Government and establishes specific procedures for cognizance of offences and recovery of money due.

metadata.short_title: The Domestic Violence (Prevention and Protection) Act, 2026
metadata.long_title: An Act to establish an effective system of protection, relief and rehabilitation of women, men, transgender, children and any vulnerable person against domestic violence.
metadata.one_line: Establishes a legal framework for protection, relief, and rehabilitation against domestic violence in the Islamabad Capital Territory.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes an effective system to protect women, men, transgender persons, children, and vulnerable individuals from domestic violence. It defines domestic violence as physical, psychological, or sexual abuse within a domestic relationship and grants courts powers to issue protection, residence, custody, and monetary relief orders. The legislation creates Protection Committees and officers to facilitate medical examinations, shelter provision, and enforcement of orders, while also defining the duties of service providers.

metadata.short_title: The Dormant Funds (Administration) Act, 1966
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the administration of certain dormant funds and matters connected therewith
metadata.one_line: This Act vests certain dormant public funds in the President for relief purposes or specific causes.
metadata.summary: The Dormant Funds (Administration) Act, 1966 provides for the administration and proper utilization of specific dormant funds raised by public subscriptions and donations. It vests these funds, along with accrued interest and profit, in the President immediately upon enactment. The amounts are then transferred to the President's Relief Fund or utilized for their original intended purposes, such as relief work or the Palestine cause.

metadata.short_title: The Dourine Act, 1910
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the prevention of the spread of dourine
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to five hundred rupees, or with both
metadata.one_line: This Act prevents the spread of dourine by regulating horse registration, inspection, and breeding prohibitions.
metadata.summary: The Dourine Act, 1910 provides for the prevention of the spread of dourine in horses. It empowers the Provincial Government to appoint inspectors and veterinary practitioners to register horses and inspect them for the disease. The Act allows for the castration or destruction of infected horses with compensation paid to owners, while also establishing penalties for using infected horses for breeding or vexatious searches.

metadata.short_title: The Dowry and Bridal Gifts (Restriction) Act, 1976
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for restrictions on dowry and bridal gifts.
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment up to six months or fine not less than the excess amount spent, or both
metadata.one_line: This Act restricts dowry and bridal gifts to five thousand rupees and sets marriage expenditure limits.
metadata.summary: The Dowry and Bridal Gifts (Restriction) Act, 1976 imposes strict monetary limits on dowry, bridal gifts, presents, and total marriage expenditure in Pakistan. It defines key terms such as 'dowry' and 'bridal gift' to exclude inheritance and Mehr, ensuring that all such property vests absolutely in the bride. The Act establishes penalties for violations, including imprisonment and fines, and mandates that offences be tried exclusively by Family Courts within a specific timeframe after the marriage.

metadata.short_title: The Dramatic Performances Act, 1876
metadata.long_title: An Act for the better control of public dramatic performances
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to three months, or with fine, or with both
metadata.one_line: Empowers the Provincial Government to prohibit scandalous, defamatory, seditious, or obscene public dramatic performances.
metadata.summary: This Act empowers the Provincial Government to prohibit public dramatic performances that are scandalous, defamatory, seditious, or likely to corrupt persons. It grants Magistrates and police specific powers to serve prohibition orders, enter premises, arrest individuals, and seize articles used in prohibited performances. The Act outlines penalties for disobedience, including imprisonment up to three months or fines, while excluding performances at religious festivals from its scope.

metadata.short_title: The Drug Regulatory Authority of Pakistan Act, 2012
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of Drug Regulatory Authority of Pakistan
repeals: The Drug Regulatory Agency of Pakistan Ordinance, 2012 (Ordinance I of 2012)
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Drug Regulatory Authority of Pakistan to regulate therapeutic goods across Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Drug Regulatory Authority of Pakistan to coordinate and enforce drug regulations. It regulates the manufacture, import, export, storage, distribution, and sale of therapeutic goods throughout the country. The Act creates various boards including a Policy Board, Licensing Board, and Appellate Board to manage specific regulatory functions.

metadata.short_title: The Drugs Act, 1976
metadata.long_title: An Act to regulate the import, export, manufacture, storage, distribution and sale of drugs
repeals: The Drugs Act, 1940 (XXIII of 1940)
the Drugs (Generic Names) Act, 1972 (XXIV of 1972)
the Drugs Ordinance, 1976 (IV of 1976)
metadata.one_line: Regulates the import, export, manufacture, storage, distribution and sale of drugs in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Act regulates the entire lifecycle of drugs including their import, export, manufacture, storage, distribution, and sale. It establishes various boards and laboratories for quality control and licensing while defining specific terms like 'adulterated drug' and 'counterfeit drug'. The Act also outlines offences, penalties, and procedures for inspectors to enforce these regulations across the whole of Pakistan.

metadata.short_title: The Drugs and Medicines (Indemnity) Act, 1957
metadata.long_title: An Act to Indemnify certain Government servants and other persons.
metadata.one_line: This Act indemnifies government servants and others from legal proceedings regarding acts done under a specific 1955 notification on drugs.
metadata.summary: The Drugs and Medicines (Indemnity) Act, 1957 was enacted to provide legal protection to government servants and other persons. It specifically addresses actions taken in pursuance of a 1955 order regarding the distribution of drugs and medicines, which previously lacked legal validity. The Act ensures that no suits, prosecutions, or legal proceedings can be instituted against anyone for acts done under that specific order.

metadata.short_title: The Dyslexia Special Measures Act, 2022
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for special measures for the education of children suffering from dyslexia and /or associated disorders
metadata.one_line: Provides special educational measures, screening, and support for children with dyslexia in Islamabad.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the right of children with dyslexia or associated disorders to inclusive education without discrimination. It mandates the Federal Government to identify these children through screening tests and appoint professional therapists in schools. The legislation also requires special educators, specific instructional accommodations, a ban on disciplinary measures like physical punishment, and the development of awareness programs.

name: Earthquake Reconstruction and Rehabilitation Authority Act, 2011

metadata.short_title: The Earthquake Reconstruction and Rehabilitation Authority Act, 2011
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of the Earthquake Reconstruction and Rehabilitation Authority (ERRA)
metadata.commencement: at once and shall be deemed to have taken effect on the 1st day of July, 2007
repeals: Prime Minister's Secretariat's Notification No. F.1(4)/2005 Admin, dated 24th October, 2005
Ordinance XCI of 2002
metadata.one_line: Establishes an autonomous authority for earthquake reconstruction, rehabilitation, and recovery in affected areas.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Earthquake Reconstruction and Rehabilitation Authority (ERRA) as an autonomous body corporate to manage post-disaster assessment, recovery, and reconstruction. The Authority is responsible for formulating development programs, approving projects, monitoring schemes, and preparing resettlement plans for earthquake-affected regions. It operates under the administrative attachment of the Prime Minister's Secretariat while retaining autonomy in its functions and operations.

metadata.short_title: The Easements Act, 1882
metadata.long_title: An Act to define and amend the Law relating to Easements and Licenses.
metadata.one_line: Defines and amends the law relating to easements and licenses in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Act defines easements as rights for beneficial enjoyment of land over other land not owned by the holder. It outlines how easements may be imposed, acquired, transferred, and extinguished, including rules on necessity, prescription, and unity of ownership. The legislation also details the nature of licenses, their revocation, and the rights of licensees upon eviction or revocation.

metadata.short_title: The Ehtram-e-Ramazan Ordinance, 1981
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for measures observe the sanctity of the month of Ramazan
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for six months or fine of five thousand rupees or both
metadata.one_line: Prohibits eating and serving food in public places during Ramazan fasting hours to observe Islamic sanctity.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance provides measures to observe the sanctity of the month of Ramazan throughout Pakistan. It prohibits persons obligated to fast from eating, drinking, or smoking in public places and forbids hotels and restaurants from serving eatables to such persons during fasting hours. The law also mandates the closure of cinema houses and theatres from sunset until three hours after, while granting specific authorities powers to enter public places and arrest offenders.

metadata.short_title: The Elections Act, 2017
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend, consolidate and unify laws relating to the conduct of elections.
metadata.one_line: This Act consolidates and unifies laws regarding the conduct of elections in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: The Elections Act, 2017 amends, consolidates, and unifies all laws relating to the conduct of elections in Pakistan. It establishes the Election Commission of Pakistan, outlines procedures for delimiting constituencies and preparing electoral rolls, and regulates the conduct of elections to the National Assembly, Provincial Assemblies, and Senate. The Act also covers election expenses, statements of assets and liabilities, and provides for the resolution of election disputes through designated tribunals.

name: Electoral Rolls Act, 1974(Repeal by No.F.8(9)/2017 dated 23-10-2017)

metadata.short_title: The Electoral Rolls Act, 1974
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the preparation and revision of electoral rolls for elections to the National Assembly and the Provincial Assemblies.
repeals: P.O. No. 6 of 1969
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to five years, with fine which may be extend to five million rupees, or with both
metadata.one_line: This Act provides for the preparation, revision, and computerization of electoral rolls for National and Provincial Assembly elections.
metadata.summary: The Electoral Rolls Act, 1974 establishes the legal framework for preparing and revising electoral rolls for elections to the National Assembly and Provincial Assemblies. It defines key terms such as 'electoral area' and 'Registration Officer', and outlines procedures for lodging claims, objections, and corrections. The Act empowers the Election Commission to prepare rolls, computerize data, and appoint officers, while also prescribing offences related to breach of official duty or misuse of information.

metadata.short_title: The Electricity Act, 1910
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the law relating to the supply and use of electrical energy
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Federal Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, direct
metadata.one_line: This Act regulates the supply and use of electrical energy, licensing, penalties for theft or misuse, and establishes an Electricity Board.
metadata.summary: The Electricity Act, 1910 amends the law regarding the supply and use of electrical energy in Pakistan. It establishes a framework for granting licenses to supply energy, defining consumers and areas of supply, and regulating non-licensees. The Act creates offences such as theft of energy and malicious waste, prescribing penalties and establishing an Electricity Board and Advisory Boards. It also details requirements for meters, notices for new works, and the protection of infrastructure.

metadata.short_title: The Electricity Control Ordinance, 1965
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for powers to control the production, distribution, use and consumption of electrical energy during an emergency throughout Pakistan
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine, or with both
metadata.one_line: Provides emergency powers to control electricity production, distribution, use and consumption throughout Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance empowers the Federal Government to regulate or prohibit the production, distribution, use, or consumption of electrical energy during an emergency. It allows for the collection of statistics, issuance of licenses, and inspection of premises to ensure compliance with orders made under the Act. The Ordinance applies to the whole of Pakistan and comes into force immediately upon promulgation.

metadata.short_title: The Electronic Transactions Ordinance, 2002
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to recognize and facilitate documents, records, information, communications and transactions in electronic form, and to provide for the accreditation of certification service providers.
metadata.one_line: Recognizes electronic transactions and establishes the Certification Council for accreditation.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance provides legal recognition to documents, records, and communications in electronic form. It establishes the Certification Council to accredit service providers and defines terms like 'advanced electronic signature' and 'appropriate authority'. The law amends existing legislation regarding evidence and cryptography to facilitate digital transactions across Pakistan.

metadata.short_title: The Elephants' Preservation Act, 1879
metadata.long_title: An Act for the preservation of wild elephants.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of Pakistan (extendable to any local area by the Provincial Government)
metadata.commencement: on the first day of April, 1879 (except for power to make declarations and rules which comes into force on passing thereof)
repeals: The Repealing and Amending Act, 1930 (VIII of 1930), s. 3 and Sch. II
metadata.status_evidence: Rep. by the Repealing and Amending Act, 1930 (VIII of 1930), s. 3 and Sch. II.
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment which may extend to six months or fine extending to five hundred rupees for each elephant concerned
metadata.one_line: This Act prohibits killing or capturing wild elephants without a license and sets penalties for violations.
metadata.summary: The Elephants' Preservation Act, 1879 was enacted to provide for the preservation of wild elephants. It prohibits any person from killing, injuring, or capturing wild elephants unless in defense, when they are harming property or infrastructure, or under a specific license. The Provincial Government is empowered to declare main roads and canals and make rules regarding licenses, fees, and conditions. Penalties include fines up to five hundred rupees per elephant and imprisonment for repeat offenders.

metadata.short_title: The Emigration Ordinance, 1979
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to repeal and, with certain modifications, re‑enact the Emigration Act, 1922
repeals: Emigration Act, 1922
establishes: Bureau of Emigration and Overseas Employment
Director-General, Bureau of Emigration and Overseas Employment
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance regulates emigration from Pakistan, establishes the Bureau of Emigration, and repeals the 1922 Act.
metadata.summary: The Emigration Ordinance, 1979 was promulgated to repeal and re-enact the Emigration Act, 1922 with modifications. It establishes the Director-General and the Bureau of Emigration and Overseas Employment to regulate emigration and protect the interests of Pakistani citizens working abroad. The document defines key terms such as 'emigrant' and 'dependent', grants powers to appoint Protectors of Emigrants and Labour Attaches, and outlines offences related to fraudulent induction or false representation regarding government authority.

metadata.short_title: The Employees Cost of Living (Relief) Act, 1974
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for payment of a cost of living allowance to employees and for matters ancillary thereto.
repeals: The Employees Cost of Living (Relief) Act, 1973
metadata.max_penalty: simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to two thousand rupees, or with both
metadata.one_line: This Act mandates employers to pay a cost of living allowance to employees with wages below a certain threshold.
metadata.summary: The Employees Cost of Living (Relief) Act, 1974 provides for the payment of a cost of living allowance to employees whose wages do not exceed a specified limit. It defines key terms such as 'employee', 'employer', and 'undertaking' to determine eligibility and scope. The Act specifies the rates for the allowance, the timing of payments, and establishes penalties for non-compliance. It also includes provisions regarding the recovery of allowances and savings of certain rights.

metadata.short_title: The Employees' Old-Age Benefits Act, 1976
metadata.long_title: An Act to repeal and re-enact the law relating of old-Age benefits for the persons employed in industrial, commercial and other organizations.
repeals: law relating to old-age benefits for the persons employed in industrial, commercial and other organizations
metadata.one_line: This Act establishes a system of old-age benefits, contributions, and pensions for employees in industrial and commercial organizations.
metadata.summary: The Employees' Old-Age Benefits Act, 1976 repeals and re-enacts laws regarding old-age benefits for persons employed in industrial, commercial, and other organizations. It mandates compulsory insurance for establishments employing a certain number of persons and establishes a Board of Trustees to manage the Employee's Old-Age Benefits Fund. The Act outlines contribution rates, recovery mechanisms for unpaid contributions, and provides for various benefits including old-age pension, invalidity pension, and survivor's pension.

metadata.short_title: The Employees' Social Insurance Ordinance, 1962
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to introduce a scheme of social insurance for providing benefits to certain employees or their dependants in the event of sickness, maternity, employment injury or death, and for matters ancillary thereto
repeals: Workmen's Compensation Act, 1923 (VIII of 1923)
Employer's Liability Act, 1938 (XXIV of 1938)
Mines Maternity Benefit Act, 1941 (XIX of 1941)
metadata.one_line: Establishes a social insurance scheme for employees providing benefits for sickness, maternity, injury, and death.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance introduces a social insurance scheme to provide financial and medical benefits to employees and their dependants in cases of sickness, maternity, employment injury, or death. It establishes the Employees' Social Insurance Institution, governed by a Governing Body and supported by Medical Advisory Councils, to manage contributions, funds, and benefit distribution. The law supersedes earlier enactments like the Workmen's Compensation Act, 1923, and sets out specific rates for benefits based on wage classes.

metadata.short_title: The Employers' Liability Act, 1938
metadata.long_title: An Act to declare that certain defences shall not be raised in suits for damages in Pakistan in respect of injuries sustained by workmen.
metadata.one_line: This Act prevents employers from raising certain defences in suits for damages regarding injuries to workmen.
metadata.summary: The Employers' Liability Act, 1938 declares that specific defences cannot be raised in lawsuits for damages concerning injuries sustained by workmen. It defines 'workman' and 'employer' broadly to cover various types of service contracts and employment relationships. The Act bars the defence of common employment in cases involving employer negligence, unsafe machinery, or obedience to negligent orders, unless the risk was fully explained and voluntarily undertaken by the workman.

metadata.short_title: The Employment (Record of Services) Act, 1951
metadata.long_title: An Act to make provision for compulsory maintenance of the record of service of persons in certain classes of employment in certain areas.
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Provincial Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, appoints
metadata.max_penalty: fifty rupees for an employer; five rupees for an employee
metadata.one_line: This Act mandates the compulsory maintenance of service books for specific classes of employment across Pakistan.
metadata.summary: The Employment (Record of Services) Act, 1951 establishes a legal framework for maintaining official records of service for employees in specified sectors. It requires employers to produce and maintain service books for their employees, detailing identification, employment periods, wages, and conduct. The Act empowers the Labour Commissioner to inspect these records and imposes penalties on employers or employees who fail to comply with the provisions.

metadata.short_title: The Employment of Children Act, 1991
metadata.long_title: An Act to prohibit the employment of children in certain occupations and to regulate the conditions of work of children
repeals: The Employment of Children Act, 1938
establishes: National Committee on the Rights of the Child
metadata.one_line: Prohibits child employment in hazardous occupations and regulates working conditions for children across Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Act prohibits the employment of children in specific hazardous occupations and processes listed in its Schedule. It also regulates the hours, periods, and safety conditions under which children may work in establishments not covered by the prohibition. The Federal Government is empowered to add occupations or processes to the Schedule via notification and constitutes a National Committee on the Rights of the Child to advise on these additions.

metadata.short_title: The Enemy Agents Ordinance, 1943
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the trial and punishment of enemy agents and persons committing certain offences with intent to aid the enemy.
metadata.max_penalty: death
metadata.one_line: Provides for the trial and punishment of enemy agents and those aiding the enemy with special judges.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance was promulgated to address an emergency by establishing a legal framework for trying and punishing enemy agents. It defines 'enemy' as any state at war with Pakistan and 'enemy agent' as someone working for such a state. The law empowers the Federal Government to appoint Special Judges with jurisdiction throughout Pakistan to try these specific offences, which carry the penalty of death. Additionally, it restricts access to court records and prohibits the unauthorized disclosure of information regarding proceedings under this Ordinance.

name: Enemy Property (Continuance of Emergency Provisions) Ordinance, 1969

metadata.short_title: The Enemy Property (Continuance of Emergency Provisions) Ordinance, 1969
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the continuance of certain provisions of the Defence of Pakistan Rules relating to the control of trading with enemy and control of enemy firms, and the administration of the property belonging to them.
metadata.commencement: on the day on which the Defence of Pakistan Ordinance, 1965 (XXIII of 1965), ceases to have effect under clause (7) of Article 30 of the Constitution
repeals: Defence of Pakistan Ordinance, 1965 (XXIII of 1965)
metadata.one_line: Continues emergency provisions regarding enemy property and trading controls after the Defence of Pakistan Ordinance, 1965 lapses.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance continues specific provisions of the Defence of Pakistan Rules concerning trading with enemies and controlling enemy firms. It applies to all citizens and persons in government service throughout Pakistan. The law ensures that orders made under these rules remain valid even if inconsistent with other enactments, while protecting officials acting in good faith from legal proceedings.

name: Enemy Property (Continuance of Emergency Provisions) Ordinance, 1977

metadata.short_title: The Enemy Property (Continuance of Emergency Provisions) Ordinance, 1977
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the continuance of certain provisions of the Defence of Pakistan Rules relating to the control of trading with enemy and control of enemy firms, and the administration of the property belonging to them;
metadata.commencement: at once (deemed to have taken effect on 1977-09-15)
metadata.one_line: Continues emergency provisions regarding enemy trading and property administration in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance continues specific provisions of the Defence of Pakistan Rules concerning the control of trading with enemies and the management of their property. It applies to all citizens and persons in government service throughout Pakistan, taking effect immediately upon promulgation. The document empowers the Federal Government to delegate duties to subordinate officers or provincial authorities while protecting actions taken in good faith under these rules from legal challenge.

metadata.short_title: The Enforcement of Shari'ah Act, 1991
metadata.long_title: An Act for the enforcement of the Shari'ah
establishes: Commission for Islamization of education and economy
metadata.one_line: This Act establishes Shari'ah as the supreme law and mandates its enforcement across education, economy, and social life in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: The Enforcement of Shari'ah Act, 1991 declares Shari'ah as the supreme law of Pakistan and mandates all citizens to observe it. It requires courts to interpret laws consistent with Islamic principles and establishes commissions to Islamize education and the economy. The Act also safeguards non-Muslim rights, ensures women's constitutional rights remain unaffected, and validates existing financial obligations until an alternative economic system is introduced.

name: Enforcement of Women's Property Rights Act, 2020

metadata.short_title: The Enforcement of Women's Property Rights Act, 2020
metadata.long_title: An Act to protect and secure the rights of ownership of women in the property
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Islamabad Capital Territory
establishes: Ombudsman (under section 7 of the Protection against Harassment of Women at the Workplace Act, 2010)
metadata.one_line: This Act empowers the Ombudsman to protect women's property rights and restore possession or title within Islamabad Capital Territory.
metadata.summary: The Enforcement of Women's Property Rights Act, 2020 is designed to protect and secure the ownership and possession rights of women in properties. It establishes a mechanism where women deprived of their property can file complaints with the Ombudsman if no court proceedings are pending. The Ombudsman has the authority to conduct summary enquiries, direct the restoration of possession or title, recover lost rent, and refer complex cases to civil courts for detailed adjudication.

name: Epidemic Diseases Act, 1897 (Repeal by W.P. Act. XXXVi of 1958))

metadata.short_title: The Epidemic Diseases Act, 1897
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the better prevention of the spread of Dangerous Epidemic Disease.
metadata.status_evidence: This Act has been repealed in its application to the Province of West Pakistan by West Pakistan Act 36 of 1958.
metadata.max_penalty: punishable under section 188 of the Pakistan Penal Code (XLV of 1860)
metadata.one_line: Provides powers to provincial and federal governments to prevent the spread of dangerous epidemic diseases.
metadata.summary: This Act empowers Provincial and Federal Governments to take special measures and prescribe regulations when an outbreak of a dangerous epidemic disease is suspected. It allows for the inspection of travelers, segregation of infected persons, and detention of ships or vessels arriving at ports. The Act also provides legal protection to persons acting in good faith under its provisions and imposes penalties on those who disobey regulations made under it.

metadata.short_title: The Equity Participation Fund (Repeal) Act, 2016
metadata.long_title: An Act to repeal the Equity Participation Fund Ordinance, 1970
repeals: Equity Participation Fund Ordinance, 1970
metadata.status_evidence: An Act to repeal the Equity Participation Fund Ordinance, 1970
metadata.one_line: This Act repeals the Equity Participation Fund Ordinance, 1970 effective immediately.
metadata.summary: The Equity Participation Fund (Repeal) Act, 2016 is a federal law enacted by Parliament to repeal the Equity Participation Fund Ordinance, 1970. It came into force at once upon enactment on May 9, 2016. The Act contains provisions allowing the Federal Government to issue notifications to resolve any difficulties arising from the repeal within one year.

metadata.short_title: The Essential Personnel (Registration) Ordinance, 1948
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the compulsory registration of Essential Personnel at Employment Exchanges.
metadata.administering_body: Government of Pakistan (Ministry of Labour implied by context of Employment Exchanges)
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance mandates the compulsory registration of essential personnel at Employment Exchanges.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance provides for the compulsory registration of essential personnel at Employment Exchanges set up by the Government. It defines essential personnel and employment exchanges, outlines the liability to register for individuals aged 18 to 60, and details the process for obtaining registration certificates. The text also specifies penalties for non-compliance and procedures for applications submitted personally or by post.

metadata.short_title: The Esso Undertakings (Vesting) Act, 1976
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for vesting in the Federal Government of certain undertakings of Esso Eastern Inc. in Pakistan.
metadata.one_line: This Act vests Esso Eastern Inc.'s Pakistani petroleum undertakings in the Federal Government.
metadata.summary: The Esso Undertakings (Vesting) Act, 1976 provides for the vesting of certain business assets and liabilities of Esso Eastern Inc. in Pakistan into the Federal Government. It defines 'Esso undertakings' to include petroleum products, lubricants, and chemical products but excludes natural gas and crude oil businesses. The Act establishes a government company to hold these vested interests and outlines provisions for employee pensions, tax liabilities, and contracts.

name: Establishment of Special Court (Overseas Pakistanis Property) Act, 2024

metadata.short_title: The Establishment of Special Court (Overseas Pakistanis Property) Act, 2024
metadata.long_title: An Act to establish special courts for adjudication of petitions in respect of immovable properties of overseas Pakistanis
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Islamabad Capital Territory
metadata.one_line: Establishes special courts in Islamabad to adjudicate petitions regarding immovable properties of overseas Pakistanis.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes special courts within the Islamabad Capital Territory to exclusively handle disputes involving the immovable properties of overseas Pakistanis. It defines 'Overseas Pakistani' based on passport or identity card status and residence abroad for over 182 days. The Act provides mechanisms for e-filing, outlines the appointment and tenure of judges, and grants special courts powers similar to district judges under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.

name: Establishment of the Federal Bank for Cooperatives and Regulation of Cooperative Banking (Repeal) Act, 2018 (Act No_XXVI of 2018)

metadata.short_title: The Establishment of the Federal Bank for Cooperatives and Regulation of Cooperative Banking (Repeal) Act, 2018
metadata.long_title: An Act to repeal the Establishment of the Federal Bank for Cooperatives and Regulation of Cooperative Banking Act, 1977
repeals: The Establishment of the Federal Bank for Cooperatives and Regulation of Cooperative Banking Act, 1977 (IX of 1977)
metadata.status_evidence: An Act to repeal the Establishment of the Federal Bank for Cooperatives and Regulation of Cooperative Banking Act, 1977
metadata.one_line: Repeals the 1977 Act establishing the Federal Bank for Cooperatives and regulating cooperative banking.
metadata.summary: This Act serves to repeal the Establishment of the Federal Bank for Cooperatives and Regulation of Cooperative Banking Act, 1977. It was enacted by Parliament on May 18, 2018, and came into force immediately upon enactment. The primary mechanism is a direct repeal of the earlier legislation governing the Federal Bank for Cooperatives.

name: Establishment of the Federal Bank for Cooperatives and Regulation of cooperative Banking Act, 1977(Repeal by Act XXVi of 2018 s.2)

metadata.short_title: The Establishment of the Federal Bank for Cooperatives and Regulation of Cooperative Banking Act, 1977
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of a Federal Bank for Cooperatives and regulation of Cooperative Banking.
amends: The Establishment of the Federal Bank for Cooperatives and Regulation of Cooperative Banking Ordinance, 1976 (XL of 1976)
repeals: The Establishment of the Federal Bank for Cooperatives and Regulation of Cooperative Banking Ordinance, 1976 (XL of 1976)
metadata.status_evidence: [Repeal by Act XXVi of 2018 s.2]
metadata.one_line: Establishes a Federal Bank for Cooperatives and regulates cooperative banking across Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Federal Bank for Cooperatives to regulate cooperative banking in Pakistan. It defines the bank's structure, including its Board, Managing Director, and officers, while granting powers to inspect banks, manage liquid assets, and impose conditions on borrowing. The Act also outlines tax exemptions for the bank and repeals a previous 1976 Ordinance.

name: Establishment of the Office of Federal Tax Ombudsman Ordinance, 2000

metadata.short_title: The Establishment of the Office of Federal Tax Ombudsman Ordinance, 2000
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the appointment of the Federal Tax Ombudsman
establishes: Office of the Federal Tax Ombudsman
metadata.max_penalty: Power to punish for contempt (Section 16)
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Federal Tax Ombudsman to investigate maladministration in federal tax laws.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Office of the Federal Tax Ombudsman to diagnose, investigate, and redress injustices caused by maladministration in the administration of federal tax laws. It defines maladministration broadly to include arbitrary decisions, delays, inefficiency, and corrupt motives. The Ordinance grants the Ombudsman powers to enter premises, summon witnesses, punish for contempt, and recommend remedies, while also defining the tenure, remuneration, and immunity of the office holder.

name: Establishment of the Office of Wafaqi Mohtasib (Ombudsman) Order, 1983

metadata.short_title: The Establishment of the Office of Wafaqi Mohtasib (Ombudsman) Order, 1983
metadata.long_title: An Order to provide for the appointment of the Wafaqi Mohtasib (Ombudsman) to diagnose, investigate, redress and rectify any injustice done to a person through mala administration.
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Office of Wafaqi Mohtasib to investigate maladministration in federal agencies.
metadata.summary: This Order establishes the Office of the Wafaqi Mohtasib (Ombudsman) to diagnose, investigate, and rectify injustices caused by maladministration within federal government agencies. The Mohtasib is appointed by the President for a four-year term and possesses powers to enter premises, punish for contempt, and make recommendations. The Order defines maladministration broadly to include arbitrary decisions, negligence, and corruption, while granting the Mohtasib immunity from legal jurisdiction.

metadata.short_title: Esta-Code
metadata.one_line: A consolidated manual of administrative and establishment rules for federal civil servants in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: Esta-Code (Edition-2021) is a compilation of administrative and establishment manuals prepared by the Pakistan Public Administration Research Centre. It consolidates various rules, regulations, and instructions issued by concerned authorities regarding the Civil Services structure, recruitment, appointments, transfers, promotions, discipline, and retirement. The document excludes obsolete or redundant instructions and aims to provide up-to-date information for informed decision-making within the Federal Government.

name: Evacuee Property and Displaced Persons Laws (Repeal) Act, 1975

metadata.short_title: The Evacuee Property and Displaced Persons Laws (Repeal) Act, 1975
metadata.long_title: An Act to repeal certain laws relating to evacuee property and the rehabilitation of displaced persons
repeals: Registration of Claims (Displaced Persons) Act, 1956
Pakistan Rehabilitation Act, 1956
Pakistan (Administration of Evacuee Property) Act, 1957
Displaced Persons (Compensation and Rehabilitation) Act, 1958
Displaced Persons (Land Settlement) Act, 1958
Scrutiny of Claims (Evacuee Property) Regulation, 1961
Price of Evacuee Property and Public Dues (Recovery) Regulation, 1971
metadata.one_line: Repeals specific laws regarding evacuee property and displaced persons rehabilitation, transferring jurisdiction to provincial authorities.
metadata.summary: This Act repeals several existing laws related to evacuee property and the rehabilitation of displaced persons. Upon repeal, pending proceedings are transferred to officers notified by the Provincial Government, with final orders executed by the Board of Revenue. The Act also mandates the transfer of available urban and rural properties to the Provincial Government for disposal, subject to specific conditions regarding agricultural land and subsistence holdings.

name: Evacuee Trust Properties (Management and Disposal) Act, 1975

metadata.short_title: The Evacuee Trust Properties (Management and Disposal) Act, 1975
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the management and disposal of evacuee properties attached to charitable, religious or educational trusts or institutions.
metadata.commencement: deemed to have taken effect on the first day of July, 1974
metadata.one_line: This Act provides for the management and disposal of evacuee trust properties attached to charitable, religious or educational trusts.
metadata.summary: The Evacuee Trust Properties (Management and Disposal) Act, 1975 establishes the Evacuee Trust Property Board to manage and dispose of evacuee properties linked to charitable, religious, or educational institutions. The Board is a body corporate with powers to acquire, hold, and dispose of property, and it must maintain records and submit annual budgets to the Federal Government. The Act defines key terms such as 'evacuee trust property' and outlines the constitution, functions, and removal conditions for the Board's members.

name: Ex-Employees of the Former Government of East Pakistan (Appointment to Federal Posts) Ordinance, 1983.

metadata.short_title: The Ex-Employees of the Former Government of East Pakistan (Appointment to Federal Posts) Ordinance, 1983
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the appointment of former employees of the Government of East Pakistan to posts under the Federal Government.
metadata.commencement: at once; deemed to have taken effect on the sixteenth day of December, 1971
metadata.one_line: Provides for the appointment of former East Pakistan government employees to federal posts with recognition of seniority and pension.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance facilitates the appointment of former employees of the Government of East Pakistan to existing or supernumerary posts under the Federal Government. It ensures that their service rendered before migration counts towards seniority and pension eligibility in the Federation. The provisions apply to individuals who migrated or were repatriated between December 16, 1971, and December 31, 1974.

name: Ex-Government Servants (Employment with Foreign Governments) (Prohibition) Act, 1966

metadata.short_title: The Ex-Government Servants (Employment with Foreign Governments) (Prohibition) Act, 1966
metadata.long_title: An Act to prohibit ex-Government servants from seeking or taking up employment with a foreign Government or foreign agency
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to seven years, or with fine which may extend to fifty thousand rupees, or with forfeiture of property
metadata.one_line: Prohibits ex-government servants from seeking foreign employment without Federal Government permission.
metadata.summary: This Act prohibits former government servants from seeking or accepting employment with foreign governments or agencies to protect national security. It applies to the whole of Pakistan and requires written permission from the Federal Government before such employment can be undertaken. The law also restricts those already in foreign service at the time of enactment from continuing after three months without permission, prescribing severe penalties including imprisonment and fines for violations.

metadata.short_title: The Excise (Spirits) Act, 1863
metadata.long_title: An Act to make special provision for the levy of the Excise-duty payable on Spirits used exclusively in Arts and Manufactures or in Chemistry.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of Pakistan (extended by Ord. 21 of 1960)
repeals: section 11, Act III of 1852
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment not exceeding six calendar months and penalty not exceeding one thousand rupees
key_definitions: spirits used exclusively in Arts and Manufactures or in Chemistry
metadata.one_line: This Act levies excise duty on spirits used for arts, manufactures, or chemistry after rendering them unfit for consumption.
metadata.summary: The Excise (Spirits) Act, 1863 provides for the levy of excise duty on spirits intended exclusively for arts, manufactures, or chemistry. It mandates that such spirits must be permanently rendered unfit for human consumption before removal from a licensed distillery. The Act prescribes rules for ascertaining this unfitness, sets penalties for breaches including fines and imprisonment, and allows for the confiscation of liquor and vehicles involved in offences.

name: Excise Duty on Minerals (Labour Welfare) Act, 1967

metadata.short_title: The Excise Duty on Minerals (Labour Welfare) Act, 1967
metadata.long_title: An Act to impose a duty of excise on certain minerals for financing measures for promoting the welfare of labour employed in the mining industry.
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Federal Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, appoint
repeals: Coal Mines Labour Welfare Fund Act, 1947
establishes: Mines Labour Housing and General Welfare Fund
metadata.one_line: Imposes excise duty on minerals to fund labour welfare, housing, and medical measures in the mining industry.
metadata.summary: This Act imposes an excise duty on specific minerals dispatched from mines to finance the welfare of mining labour. The proceeds are credited to a dedicated Fund with separate accounts for housing and general welfare. The Act establishes two boards, the Mines Labour Housing Board and the Miners Welfare Board, to administer these funds and oversee measures such as housing construction, public health improvements, and dispensary services. It also repeals the Coal Mines Labour Welfare Fund Act, 1947, transferring its assets and liabilities to the new framework.

name: Exclusive Fishery Zone (Regulation of Fishing) Act, 1975

metadata.short_title: Exclusive Fishery Zone (Regulation of Fishing) Act, 1975
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the regulation of fishing within the exclusive fishery zone of Pakistan.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of Pakistan and to waters within the zone
metadata.max_penalty: rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to five years, or with fine which may extend to ten million rupees, or with both
metadata.one_line: Regulates fishing in Pakistan's exclusive fishery zone through licensing, prohibitions on harmful methods, and penalties.
metadata.summary: This Act regulates fishing activities within the Exclusive Fishery Zone of Pakistan to ensure sustainable practices. It prohibits fishing without a license issued by the licencing authority and bans dangerous methods like dynamiting and poisoning. The Federal Government has the power to declare closed seasons or prohibited areas via notification. Offenders face rigorous imprisonment up to five years or fines up to ten million rupees, along with potential forfeiture of catch and gear.

name: Execution of the Punishment of Whipping Ordinance, 1979

metadata.short_title: The Execution of the Punishment of Whipping Ordinance, 1979
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to make provision relating to the execution of the punishment of whipping.
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance regulates the execution of whipping punishments across Pakistan, including medical checks and procedural rules.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance provides specific provisions for executing the punishment of whipping under laws in force at the time. It mandates medical examinations to ensure safety, specifies whip construction standards, and outlines conditions such as weather, age, and pregnancy that may postpone execution. The Ordinance applies to the whole of Pakistan but allows Provincial Governments to make rules for implementation.

metadata.short_title: Exit from Pakistan (Control) Ordinance, 1981
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the control of exit of certain persons from Pakistan.
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to five years
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance empowers the Federal Government to prohibit persons from exiting Pakistan and prescribes punishment for contravention.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance provides the legal framework for controlling the exit of certain persons from Pakistan. It grants the Federal Government the power to issue orders prohibiting specific individuals or classes of persons from leaving the country, even if they possess valid travel documents. The text outlines procedures for reviewing such orders and establishes criminal penalties, including imprisonment up to five years, for anyone who contravenes, attempts to contravene, or abets a contravention of these exit prohibitions.

metadata.short_title: The Explosive Substances Act, 1908
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the law relating to explosive substances
metadata.max_penalty: death or imprisonment for life
metadata.one_line: This Act amends the law relating to explosive substances and defines offenses regarding their use, possession, and causing explosions.
metadata.summary: The Explosive Substances Act, 1908 further amends the law concerning explosive substances. It defines what constitutes an 'explosive substance' and includes materials for making them or apparatus used to cause explosions. The Act prescribes punishments for causing explosions likely to endanger life or property, attempting such acts, possessing explosives under suspicious circumstances, and being an abettor to these offenses. It also establishes restrictions on the trial of offenses against this Act, requiring consent from the Provincial Government.

metadata.short_title: The Explosives Act, 1884
metadata.long_title: An Act to regulate the manufacture, possession, use, sale, transport and importation of Explosives.
metadata.commencement: on such day as the Federal Government, by notification in the official Gazette, appoints
metadata.max_penalty: half a million rupees
metadata.one_line: Regulates the manufacture, possession, use, sale, transport and importation of explosives in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Act regulates the manufacture, possession, use, sale, transport, and importation of explosives. It defines various types of explosives and related terms such as illegal activities and deliberate explosions. The Act empowers the Federal Government to make rules regarding licensing and prohibits actions by certain persons or young individuals. It also outlines procedures for inquiries into accidents and penalties for violations.

name: Export Control on Goods, Technologies, Material and Equipment related to nuclear and Biological Weapons and their Delivery Systems Act, 2004

metadata.short_title: Export Control on Goods, Technologies, Material and Equipment related to Nuclear and Biological Weapons and their Delivery Systems Act, 2004
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for export control on goods, technologies, material and equipment related to nuclear and biological weapons and their delivery systems;
