establishes: Government Authority to administer export controls
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to fourteen years, or fine not exceeding five million rupees, or both
metadata.one_line: This Act establishes federal export controls on goods and technologies related to nuclear and biological weapons.
metadata.summary: The Export Control on Goods, Technologies, Material and Equipment related to Nuclear and Biological Weapons and their Delivery Systems Act, 2004 provides for strict export controls over items related to nuclear and biological weapons. It applies to citizens, foreign nationals in Pakistan, and Pakistani-registered transport wherever they are. The Federal Government is authorized to make rules, delegate administration, establish an oversight board, and designate enforcement agencies. The Act defines key terms such as 'export', 'technology', and 'biological weapon' and prescribes severe penalties including up to fourteen years imprisonment for violations.

metadata.short_title: The Export Development Fund Act, 1999
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of export development fund
repeals: Government of Pakistan, Ministry of Commerce, Resolution S.R.O. No. 843(I)/92, dated the 1st September, 1992
establishes: Board of Administrators of Export Development Fund
metadata.administering_body: Federal Government (via the Board of Administrators)
metadata.one_line: Establishes an Export Development Fund to strengthen export infrastructure and promote exports through a dedicated Board.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Export Development Fund to strengthen and develop infrastructure for promoting exports. The Fund is administered by a Board of Administrators appointed by the Federal Government, comprising private sector exporters and government representatives. Money from the Fund is utilized for establishing training institutes, subsidizing delegations, supporting trade offices abroad, conducting research, and other export promotion activities approved by the Board.

metadata.short_title: Export Processing Zones Authority Ordinance, 1980
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to establish an Export Processing Zones Authority
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Federal Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, specify
establishes: Board of the Export Processing Zones Authority
key_definitions: Export Processing Zone developer and operator
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Export Processing Zones Authority to plan, develop, and manage export processing zones in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Export Processing Zones Authority as a body corporate responsible for planning, developing, and managing export processing zones. It defines the composition of the Board, outlines the powers to establish private and public participated zones, and provides mechanisms for land acquisition and financial management. The Authority is empowered to prepare master plans, sanction industries, and make rules or regulations with Federal Government approval.

metadata.short_title: The Export Import Bank of Pakistan Act, 2022
metadata.long_title: An Act to establish the Export-Import Bank of Pakistan for the promotion of international trade and to provide for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto
metadata.commencement: at once, save for sections 35 and 36 which shall come into force on the date of the notification issued by the Federal Government or the respective Provincial Governments
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Export-Import Bank of Pakistan to promote international trade through financing and insurance.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Export-Import Bank of Pakistan as the official export credit agency of the country. The Bank is empowered to provide trade financing, trade credit insurance, equity participation, and other trade services to support international trade. It outlines the Bank's capital structure, management by a Board of Directors, regulatory oversight by the State Bank of Pakistan, and procedures for accounts, audit, and liquidation.

metadata.short_title: The Extradition Act, 1972
metadata.long_title: An Act to consolidate and amend the law relating to the extradition of fugitive offenders.
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Federal Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, appoint
subjects: offences at sea or in air
metadata.one_line: This Act consolidates and amends the law regarding the extradition of fugitive offenders to and from treaty and non-treaty states.
metadata.summary: The Extradition Act, 1972 consolidates and amends laws concerning the extradition of fugitive offenders. It applies to the whole of Pakistan and covers procedures for surrendering offenders to treaty and non-treaty states, including magisterial enquiries and conditions for discharge. The Act defines key terms like 'extradition offence' and 'fugitive offender', lists specific extraditable offences in the Schedule, and empowers the Federal Government to make rules and amend the Schedule.

metadata.short_title: The Eye Surgery (Restriction) Ordinance, 1960
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to prevent surgery on the eye by persons other than registered medical practitioners
metadata.max_penalty: seven years imprisonment and fine
metadata.one_line: Restricts eye surgery to registered medical practitioners and prescribes penalties for violations.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance prevents non-registered persons from performing eye surgery in Pakistan. It defines terms like 'eye surgery' and types of blindness, establishing that only registered medical practitioners can perform such operations. Violations result in imprisonment and fines, with heavier penalties if the act causes partial or complete blindness.

metadata.short_title: The Factories Act, 1934
metadata.long_title: An Act to consolidate and amend the law regulating labour in factories.
metadata.one_line: Consolidates and amends laws regulating labour conditions, safety, and welfare in factories across Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Act consolidates and amends the law regulating labour in factories. It defines key terms such as child, adolescent, and adult, and sets out provisions for health, safety, working hours, and welfare facilities. The Act empowers inspectors to enforce regulations and imposes penalties for contraventions.

metadata.short_title: The Fatal Accidents Act, 1855
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide compensation to families for loss occasioned by the death of a person caused by actionable wrong.
metadata.territorial_extent: all the Provinces and the Capital of the Federation, except the Scheduled Districts (with specific declarations for Sind and Punjab Scheduled Districts)
key_definitions: child (includes son, daughter, grandson, granddaughter, step-son, step-daughter)
metadata.one_line: Provides compensation to families for loss caused by the death of a person due to wrongful acts.
metadata.summary: This Act allows families to sue for damages when a person dies due to a wrongful act that would have entitled them to damages if the person had not died. It limits suits to one per subject matter but allows claims for estate losses to be added. The recovered amount is divided among the deceased's wife, husband, parents, and children after deducting costs.

name: Federal Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education Act, 1975

metadata.short_title: The Federal Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education Act, 1975
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of a Federal Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of Pakistan (including Federal Capital, FATA, states not forming part of a Province, institutions abroad)
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Federal Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, appoint
subjects: Federal Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education
establishes: Federal Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education
metadata.one_line: This Act establishes the Federal Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education and defines its powers, composition, and functions.
metadata.summary: This Act provides for the establishment of the Federal Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education as a body corporate. It outlines the Board's jurisdiction over institutions in specific territories and abroad, details its composition including ex-officio and elected members, and grants it powers to make regulations regarding examinations, admissions, and affiliation. The Act also covers administrative aspects such as officers, annual audits, provident funds, and the Federal Government's power to supersede the Board.

name: Federal Board of Revenue Act, 2007 (extracted from Finance Act, 2007)

metadata.short_title: The Federal Board of Revenue Act, 2007
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of Federal Board of Revenue and for matters connected therewith or ancillary thereto
metadata.commencement: at once for this section; on such date as the Federal Government may notify for remaining provisions
repeals: Central Board of Revenue Act, 1924 (IV of 1924)
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Federal Board of Revenue, repeals the Central Board of Revenue Act, 1924, and defines its powers and functions.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Federal Board of Revenue to enhance tax collection capacity through modern techniques and a motivated workforce. It reorganizes the Central Board of Revenue into the Federal Board of Revenue with defined membership, powers, and human resource policies. The Act grants the Board authority to make rules and regulations, manage its budget, and maintain a data bank while repealing the previous 1924 Act.

name: Federal Constitutional Court Judges (Leave, Pension and Privileges) Order, 2025

metadata.short_title: The Federal Constitutional Court Judges (Leave, Pension and Privileges) Order, 2025
metadata.one_line: This Order regulates leave, pension, and privileges for Judges of the Federal Constitutional Court.
metadata.summary: This Order determines the privileges, allowances, rights regarding leave absence, and pension for every Judge of the Federal Constitutional Court. It establishes rules for various types of leave, leave accounts, salary rates during leave, and entitlements upon retirement including specific facilities for retired judges and their widows. The document also defines key terms related to service and appointments within the context of the Constitution.

metadata.short_title: The Federal Court(Repeal) Act, 2014
metadata.long_title: An Act to repeal the Federal Court Act, 1937
repeals: The Federal Court Act, 1937 (XXV of 1937)
metadata.one_line: This Act repeals the Federal Court Act, 1937 and comes into force immediately.
metadata.summary: The Federal Court(Repeal) Act, 2014 is a short legislative instrument enacted by Parliament to repeal the Federal Court Act, 1937. It contains no substantive provisions other than the repeal of the earlier Act and its immediate commencement. The document serves to remove the 1937 legislation from the statute book.

name: Federal Employees Benevolent Fund and Group Insurance Act,1969

metadata.short_title: The Federal Employees Benevolent Fund and Group Insurance Act, 1969
metadata.long_title: An Act to establish a benevolent fund for the common benefit of the employees of the [Federal Government] and certain autonomous bodies and to provide for their group insurance.
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Federal Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, appoint
metadata.one_line: Establishes a benevolent fund and group insurance scheme for federal employees and autonomous bodies.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Federal Employees Benevolent Fund to provide financial assistance to federal employees and members of certain autonomous bodies. It also sets up a Board of Trustees to manage the fund and provides for group insurance coverage for these employees. The legislation defines eligible employees, their families, subscription rates, and the conditions under which benevolent grants are paid upon death or other incidents.

name: Federal Excise Act, 2005 (Same as on the official website of FBR dated 30-06-2026)

metadata.short_title: The Federal Excise Act, 2005
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the levy, collection and payment of duties of excise on goods and services and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
repeals: The Federal Excise Act, 1957
establishes: Tax Fraud Investigation Wing Inland Revenue
metadata.one_line: This Act establishes the framework for levying, collecting, and paying excise duties on goods and services in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: The Federal Excise Act, 2005 provides the legal framework for the imposition, collection, and payment of federal excise duties on specified goods and services. It outlines procedures for filing returns, registration, exemptions, and the recovery of unpaid duties. The Act also defines various offences related to non-compliance, establishes penalties, and sets out mechanisms for adjudication, appeals, and searches.

name: Federal Government Employees Housing Authority Act, 2020.

metadata.short_title: The Federal Government Employees Housing Authority Act, 2020
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for establishment of Federal Government Employees Housing Authority
metadata.max_penalty: fine to the Authority which may be fixed in the regulations for each category of violation
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Federal Government Employees Housing Authority to plan and develop housing schemes for federal employees.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Federal Government Employees Housing Authority to plan and develop housing schemes for serving and retired Federal Government employees. The Authority is a body corporate with powers to acquire land, regulate schemes, and provide public services in specified areas. It includes provisions for the Executive Board's composition, asset transfer from the Foundation, tax exemptions, and legal immunities for its officials.

name: Federal Government Lands and Buildings (Recovery of Possession) Ordinance, 1965

metadata.short_title: The Federal Government Lands and Buildings (Recovery of Possession) Ordinance, 1965
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the speedy recovery of possession of Central Government lands and buildings.
metadata.one_line: Provides for the speedy recovery of possession of Central Government lands and buildings from lessees, licensees, and unauthorized occupants.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance empowers authorized officers to evict outgoing lessees and licensees who fail to vacate Federal Government land or buildings upon the expiry or determination of their lease/license. It also allows for the eviction of unauthorized occupants and the demolition of structures erected by those in possession without authority. The document further provides mechanisms for recovering costs of demolition, arrears of rent, and obtaining police assistance, while barring civil courts from interfering with these recovery proceedings.

metadata.short_title: The Federal Investigation Agency Act, 1974
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the constitution of a Federal Investigation Agency for the investigation of certain offences committed in connection with matters concerning the Federal Government, and for matters connected therewith
repeals: The Pakistan Special Police Establishment Ordinance, 1948 (VIII of 1948)
the Special Police and Provincial Police (Amalgamation) Order, 1962 (P. O. No. I of 1962)
metadata.max_penalty: rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both
metadata.one_line: Constitutes the Federal Investigation Agency to investigate specific federal offences with powers equivalent to provincial police.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) to investigate offences connected to matters concerning the Federal Government. It grants members of the Agency powers similar to Provincial Police officers, including arrest and seizure of property, throughout Pakistan. The Act also provides for the transfer of personnel from the Special Police Establishment upon its repeal and outlines the superintendence by the Federal Government and administration by the Director-General.

metadata.short_title: Federal Judicial Academy Act, 1997
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of the Federal Judicial Academy
establishes: Board of Governors of the Academy
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Federal Judicial Academy to train judicial officers and court personnel.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Federal Judicial Academy as a body corporate with its headquarters in Islamabad. The Academy aims to provide orientation, training, and education for judges, magistrates, law officers, and court personnel while holding conferences and publishing research. A Board of Governors is created to supervise the Academy's affairs, approve budgets, and manage staff appointments and funds.

name: Federal Medical Teaching Institutes Act, 2021 (Repealed by Act No.I of 2023)

metadata.short_title: The Federal Medical Teaching Institutes Act, 2021
metadata.long_title: An Act to re-organize the Federal medical teaching institute and teaching hospitals thereof
repeals: The Federal Medical Teaching Institutes Act, 2023
metadata.status_evidence: [Repealed by Act No.I of 2023]
establishes: medical teaching institution as autonomous body
metadata.one_line: Re-organizes Federal medical teaching institutes and hospitals as autonomous bodies with a Board of Governors.
metadata.summary: This Act re-organizes Federally owned medical teaching institutes and their affiliated teaching hospitals in Pakistan to provide autonomy. It establishes a Board of Governors comprising private sector members to administer the institutions, define their functions, and manage affairs. The Act defines key terms related to faculties, employees, and healthcare services while empowering the Government to make rules and regulations for its implementation.

name: Federal Ministers and Ministers of State (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) Act, 1975

metadata.short_title: The Federal Ministers and Ministers of State (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) Act, 1975
metadata.long_title: An Act to determine the salaries, allowances and privileges of the Federal Ministers and Ministers of State
metadata.one_line: This Act determines the salaries, allowances, and privileges for Federal Ministers and Ministers of State.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the framework for determining the salaries, allowances, and privileges applicable to Federal Ministers and Ministers of State. It details specific entitlements including monthly salary equivalents, equipment allowances, sumptuary allowances, official residence usage, transport provisions, and medical facilities. The legislation also outlines rules regarding travelling allowances, leave, personal staff, provident funds, and compensation for air accidents involving ministers.

metadata.short_title: The Federal Ombudsmen Institutional Reforms Act, 2013
metadata.long_title: An Act to make institutional reforms for standardizing and harmonizing the laws relating to Federal Ombudsmen institution and the matters ancillary or akin thereto;
metadata.one_line: This Act standardizes Federal Ombudsmen laws, grants administrative autonomy, and defines their powers and tenure.
metadata.summary: The Federal Ombudsmen Institutional Reforms Act, 2013 aims to standardize and harmonize laws regarding Federal Ombudsmen institutions. It grants them administrative and financial autonomy while defining their tenure, removal processes, and specific powers such as granting temporary injunctions and punishing contempt. The Act applies to the whole of Pakistan and comes into force immediately.

metadata.short_title: The Federal Prosecution Service, Act, 2023
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for establishment of federal prosecution service
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of Islamabad Capital Territory
repeals: provisions of law authorizing the prosecution function undertaken by agencies notified under section 2(b)
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Federal Criminal Prosecution Service and defines the powers, functions, and appointment of federal prosecutors.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Federal Criminal Prosecution Service to institute and conduct criminal cases initiated by the Islamabad Capital Territory police or Federal agencies. It outlines the qualifications for appointing the Federal Prosecutor General, the administrative structure of the service, and the specific duties and powers of prosecutors. The Act also provides for a code of conduct, indemnity for prosecutors acting in good faith, and grants the Government power to make rules necessary for its implementation.

name: Federal Public Service Commission (Validation of Rules) Act, 2021

metadata.short_title: The Federal Public Service Commission (Validation of Rules) Act, 2021
metadata.long_title: An Act to validate the rules for regulating the competitive examination conducted by the Federal Public Service Commission
metadata.one_line: Validates rules regulating competitive examinations conducted by the Federal Public Service Commission in 2016 and 2017.
metadata.summary: This Act validates the rules issued by the Federal Public Service Commission for conducting competitive examinations in 2016 and 2017. It deems these rules, along with their amendments, to have been validly made from the date of their notification. Furthermore, any examinations held, acts done, notifications issued, or proceedings taken under these validated rules are deemed to have been validly conducted despite any defects in approval.

metadata.short_title: The Federal Public Service Commission Ordinance, 1977
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to repeal and, with certain modifications, re-enact the Federal Public Service Commission Act, 1973.
amends: The Federal Public Service Commission Act, 1973
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance re-enacts the Federal Public Service Commission Act, 1973 with modifications to regulate the Commission's composition and functions.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance was promulgated by the President to repeal and modify the Federal Public Service Commission Act, 1973. It establishes the Federal Public Service Commission and defines its composition, term of office for members, and eligibility criteria. The document outlines the Commission's primary functions, which include conducting recruitment examinations for federal services and advising the President on recruitment principles. It also details procedures for the appointment of the Chairman, the oath of office, and the submission of annual reports to the National Assembly and Senate.

name: Federal Supervision of Curricula Text-books and Maintenance of Standards of Education Act, 1976

metadata.short_title: The Federal Supervision of Curricula, Text books and Maintenance of Standards of Education Act, 1976
metadata.long_title: An Act to make provision for Federal supervision of curricula text books and maintenance of standards of education.
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year and guilty of gross misconduct
metadata.one_line: Establishes federal supervision over school curricula, textbooks, and education standards across Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Act provides for Federal supervision of curricula and textbooks to promote national cohesion and social harmony. It establishes a Competent Authority appointed by the Federal Government to prepare study schemes, approve textbooks, and direct amendments or deletions in educational materials. The Act extends to the whole of Pakistan and comes into force immediately, with penalties including imprisonment for non-compliance.

metadata.short_title: The Federal Universities Ordinance, 2002
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to constitute and restructure Universities set up by the Federal Government
metadata.commencement: on such dates as may be specified by the Government through notifications in the official Gazette
repeals: Acts, Ordinances or other legislative instruments constituting the universities listed in the Schedule
establishes: University bodies (Chancellor, Senate, Syndicate, Academic Council)
metadata.one_line: An Ordinance to constitute and restructure universities set up by the Federal Government in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance provides for the constitution and restructuring of universities established by the Federal Government. It grants these institutions academic, financial, and administrative autonomy while improving governance and management. The law applies to specific universities listed in the Schedule and allows for the creation of new universities through government notification.

name: Federal Urdu University of Arts, Sciences and Technology, Islamabad Ordinance, 2002

metadata.short_title: The Federal Urdu University of Arts, Sciences and Technology, Islamabad Ordinance, 2002
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for Establishment of Federal Urdu University of Arts, Sciences and Technology, Islamabad
establishes: Federal Urdu University of Arts, Sciences and Technology, Islamabad
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Federal Urdu University of Arts, Sciences and Technology, Islamabad and its governing bodies.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Federal Urdu University of Arts, Sciences and Technology, Islamabad, incorporating existing colleges in Karachi. It defines the university's structure, including the Chancellor, Senate, Syndicate, and Academic Council, and outlines their powers and functions. The document also provides for the creation of a University Fund, the making of Statutes, Regulations, and Rules, and includes general provisions regarding jurisdiction, indemnity, and emergency powers exercised by the President.

metadata.short_title: The Federal Ziauddin University Act, 2024
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of Federal Ziauddin University at Islamabad.
establishes: Board of Advanced Studies and Research
metadata.one_line: Establishes Federal Ziauddin University in Islamabad with academic autonomy and non-profit status.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Federal Ziauddin University at Islamabad as a body corporate on a non-profit basis. It grants the university academic, financial, and administrative autonomy while ensuring it remains open to all persons regardless of sex, religion, race, or creed. The legislation defines the university's structure, including its Patron, Chancellor, Rector, Vice Chancellor, and various governing bodies like the Academic Council and Governing Body. It also outlines the powers to confer degrees, manage funds, and establish faculties across health sciences, engineering, law, and other disciplines within the Islamabad Territory.

metadata.short_title: The Fee-Charging Employment Agencies (Regulation) Act, 1976
metadata.long_title: An Act to regulate the working of fee-charging and other employment agencies conducted with a view to profit for placement of workers within Pakistan.
metadata.commencement: on such dates as the Federal Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, specify
metadata.one_line: Regulates fee-charging employment agencies in Pakistan through licensing, prohibition of unlicensed operation, and penalties.
metadata.summary: This Act regulates the working of fee-charging and other profit-oriented employment agencies for placing workers within Pakistan. It prohibits acting as a fee-charging agency without a licence issued by the competent authority appointed by the Federal Government. The Act defines key terms like 'employment agency' and 'fee-charging employment agency', outlines the process for issuing, renewing, cancelling, or suspending licences, and establishes offences and penalties for contravention. It also provides for the making of rules to carry out the Act's purposes and grants indemnity to persons acting in good faith under the Act.

metadata.short_title: The Ferries Act, 1878
metadata.long_title: An Act to regulate Ferries
metadata.territorial_extent: the Punjab and the North-West Frontier Province
metadata.commencement: on such date as the appropriate Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, fix
repeals: Regulation VI of 1891 in Punjab
metadata.one_line: Regulates public and private ferries, tolls, management, and penalties in Punjab and NWFP.
metadata.summary: This Act regulates ferries in certain provinces, specifically the Punjab and North-West Frontier Province. It empowers the appropriate government to declare, establish, and discontinue public ferries while defining their limits and courses. The legislation outlines provisions for tolls, compensation claims, management by municipalities or local bodies, and penalties for breaches of rules or unauthorized operations.

metadata.short_title: Finance Ordinance, 2001
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to give effect to the financial proposals of the Federal Government for the year beginning on the first day of July, 2001, and to amend certain laws for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
metadata.commencement: at once except section 3 (from 2001-07-01) and section 5 (on such date as the Federal Government may notify)
metadata.one_line: Amends various laws to implement financial proposals and adjust excise, sales, and income taxes for the fiscal year starting July 2001.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance was promulgated by the President to give effect to the Federal Government's financial proposals for the fiscal year beginning July 1, 2001. It amends the Central Excises Act, 1944, and the Petroleum Products (Development Surcharge) Ordinance, 1961, among others, to adjust tax rates and definitions. The document also updates income tax provisions regarding National Savings Schemes and omits certain sections of the Khushhali Bank Ordinance, 2000.

metadata.short_title: The Financial Institutions (Recovery of Finances) Ordinance, 2001
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to repeal, and, with certain modifications, re-enact, the Banking Companies (Recovery of Loans, Advances, Credits and finances), Act, 1997
repeals: The Banking Companies (Recovery of Loans, Advances, Credits and Finances) Act, 1997
metadata.one_line: Repeals and re-enacts the 1997 Banking Recovery Act to establish Banking Courts for recovering finances from financial institutions.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance repeals and modifies the Banking Companies (Recovery of Loans, Advances, Credits and Finances) Act, 1997. It establishes special Banking Courts to handle suits for the recovery of written-off finances and other debts owed by customers to financial institutions. The document defines 'financial institution' broadly to include banks, leasing companies, and investment entities, while excluding the State Bank of Pakistan. It grants financial institutions the power to sell mortgaged properties without court intervention under specific conditions and restricts the transfer of assets during legal proceedings.

metadata.short_title: The Financial Institutions (Secured Transactions) Act, 2016
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the creation of security interests over movable property and to establish a secured transactions registry
metadata.commencement: upon issuance of the notification by the Commission under sub section (2) of section 19
metadata.one_line: This Act establishes a registry for securing movable property transactions and defines rules for creating, perfecting, and enforcing security interests.
metadata.summary: The Financial Institutions (Secured Transactions) Act, 2016 provides a legal framework for creating security interests over movable property to secure obligations owed by customers to financial institutions. It establishes a specialized Secured Transactions Registry managed by a Commission to record and manage these interests. The Act outlines procedures for perfection, priority rules among competing claims, enforcement modes, and includes transitional provisions for existing security interests.

name: Fiscal Responsibility and Debt Limitation Act, 2005

metadata.short_title: The Fiscal Responsibility and Debt Limitation Act, 2005
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for reduction of Federal fiscal deficit and ratio of public debt to gross domestic product to a prudent level by effective public debt management
metadata.one_line: This Act establishes principles for reducing federal fiscal deficit and public debt to prudent levels through effective management.
metadata.summary: The Fiscal Responsibility and Debt Limitation Act, 2005 aims to reduce the Federal fiscal deficit and the ratio of public debt to GDP to prudent levels. It mandates the Federal Government to pursue specific fiscal and debt management principles, including limiting deficits and reducing total public debt within set timelines. The Act requires the publication of economic, fiscal, and debt policy statements before the National Assembly and establishes a Debt Management Office to oversee these functions.

metadata.short_title: The Fisheries Act, 1897
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for certain matters relating to Fisheries in Pakistan.
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to two months, or with fine which may extend to two hundred rupees
metadata.one_line: This Act regulates fisheries in Pakistan, prohibiting destruction of fish by explosives or poison and empowering provincial governments to make protective rules.
metadata.summary: The Fisheries Act, 1897 provides for matters relating to fisheries throughout Pakistan. It defines key terms such as 'fish', 'fixed engine', and 'private water'. The Act prohibits the use of explosives or poisons to catch or destroy fish and outlines penalties for such offenses. It also empowers Provincial Governments to make rules protecting fish in selected waters and regulating fishing methods, subject to certain conditions.

name: Flour Milling Control and Development (Repeal) Ordinance, 1977

metadata.short_title: The Flour Milling Control and Development (Repeal) Ordinance, 1977
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to repeal the Flour Milling Control and Development Act, 1976 (LVII of 1976)
repeals: The Flour Milling Control and Development Act, 1976 (LVII of 1976)
metadata.max_penalty: rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance repeals the Flour Milling Control and Development Act, 1976, and provides for the return of establishments and employee continuance.
metadata.summary: The document is an Ordinance promulgated by the President to repeal the Flour Milling Control and Development Act, 1976. It mandates the return of establishments acquired under the repealed Act to their previous management within a specified period. The Ordinance ensures the continuance in service of employees, provides for compensation calculations, and allows the Corporation to continue until wound up by the Provincial Government.

metadata.short_title: The Flying Clubs (Appointment of Administrators) Ordinance, 1978
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the appointment of Administrators of Flying Clubs.
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both
metadata.one_line: Provides for the appointment of Administrators to manage Flying Clubs when the Committee cannot function properly.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance empowers the Federal Government to appoint an Administrator to manage a Flying Club if the existing Committee is unable to function. The Administrator assumes full management powers, including auditing accounts and initiating legal proceedings, while receiving remuneration directed by the Federal Government. The Ordinance overrides other laws regarding club management and provides indemnity for officials acting in good faith under its provisions.

metadata.short_title: The Foreign Assets (Declaration and Repatriation) Act, 2018
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for declaration and repatriation of assets and income held outside Pakistan
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term not exceeding one year or with both
key_definitions: cost of acquisition of the mortgaged asset
metadata.one_line: This Act provides for the declaration and repatriation of foreign assets held by Pakistani citizens.
metadata.summary: The Foreign Assets (Declaration and Repatriation) Act, 2018 addresses the non-reporting of assets held outside Pakistan. It applies to all Pakistani citizens except holders of public office, their spouses, and dependent children, requiring them to declare such assets and pay applicable taxes. The Act mandates the repatriation of these funds, outlines specific tax rates for different asset types, and ensures confidentiality while overriding other conflicting laws.

name: Foreign Cultural Associations (Regulation of Functioning) Act, 1975

metadata.short_title: The Foreign Cultural Associations (Regulation of Functioning) Act, 1975
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the regulation of the functioning of foreign cultural associations
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine which may extend to ten thousand rupees, or with both
metadata.one_line: This Act regulates the formation, functioning, registration, and dissolution of foreign cultural associations in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: The Act provides for the regulation of foreign cultural associations operating within Pakistan. It mandates that such associations must be registered by the Federal Government and prohibits them from engaging in activities prejudicial to Pakistan's ideology or security. The legislation outlines specific responsibilities regarding financial accounts, restrictions on government servants joining these bodies, and penalties for contravention of its provisions.

metadata.short_title: The Foreign Currency Accounts (Protection) Ordinance, 2001
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for protection to foreign currency accounts and for matters connected therewith or ancillary thereto
metadata.administering_body: Federal Government / State Bank of Pakistan
metadata.one_line: Provides protection for foreign currency account holders and empowers the Federal Government to make related rules.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance provides legal protection to individuals holding foreign currency accounts, ensuring they can operate, sell, withdraw, or transfer funds without restriction. It grants indemnity to the Federal Government and authorized persons acting in good faith under this law. The provisions override conflicting sections of existing laws like the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act, 1947, while adding protection alongside the Protection of Economic Reforms Act, 1992.

metadata.short_title: The Foreign Exchange (Prevention of Payments) Act, 1972
metadata.long_title: An Act to enable the Federal Government to prohibit certain payments.
metadata.commencement: at once and deemed to have taken effect on the 10th day of March, 1972
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years and fine
metadata.one_line: Enables the Federal Government to prohibit certain payments and direct the State Bank to stop them.
metadata.summary: This Act empowers the Federal Government to prohibit specific payments related to foreign exchange repatriation. It authorizes the State Bank of Pakistan to direct authorized dealers or other persons to deposit amounts with the bank within a specified time. The Act provides indemnity to the government and banks for actions taken in good faith under it, outlines penalties for contravention including imprisonment up to three years and fines, and grants power to make rules.

metadata.short_title: The Foreign Exchange (Temporary Restrictions) Act, 1998
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for dealings in foreign exchange
repeals: The Foreign Exchange (Temporary Restrictions) Ordinance, 1998 (VII of 1998)
metadata.one_line: Imposes temporary restrictions on foreign exchange dealings and suspends withdrawal rights pending Federal Government rules.
metadata.summary: This Act provides for temporary restrictions on dealings in foreign exchange to stabilize the economy. It suspends the right to withdraw, transfer, or take out foreign exchange held as of May 28, 1998, without prior permission from the State Bank of Pakistan. The Federal Government is empowered to make rules regarding repayment, profit payments, and classifying citizens based on residence status. Certain protections under the Protection of Economic Reforms Act, 1992 remain unaffected, and the previous Ordinance on this subject is repealed.

metadata.short_title: The Foreign Exchange Regulation Act, 1947
metadata.long_title: An Act to regulate certain payments, dealings in foreign exchange and securities and the import and export of currency and bullion.
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Federal Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, appoint
metadata.administering_body: Federal Government / State Bank of Pakistan
metadata.one_line: Regulates payments, foreign exchange dealings, securities, and currency/bullion import/export in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Act regulates payments, dealings in foreign exchange and securities, and the import and export of currency and bullion. It defines key terms such as 'foreign exchange', 'authorised dealer', and 'currency'. The Federal Government and State Bank of Pakistan are empowered to give directions, make rules, and impose penalties for contraventions.

metadata.short_title: The Foreign Investment (Promotion and Protection) Act, 2022
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for promotion and protection of certain qualified foreign investments and for matters incidental thereto
metadata.one_line: Promotes and protects qualified foreign investments in Pakistan through incentives, tax stability, and banking protections.
metadata.summary: This Act aims to attract large-scale foreign investment into Pakistan by providing sustainable economic growth and improving the investment climate. It offers direct and indirect tax incentives, facilitates the transfer and repatriation of funds, and protects these benefits from withdrawal or modification. The legislation applies to qualified investments across the whole of Pakistan, with specific provisions for the Reko Diq Project in Balochistan, and establishes an Investment Ombudsman to handle disputes.

name: Foreign Private Investment (Promotion and Protection) Act, 1976

metadata.short_title: The Foreign Private Investment (Promotion and Protection) Act, 1976
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the promotion and protection of foreign private investment in Pakistan.
metadata.one_line: This Act promotes and protects foreign private investment in Pakistan through tax concessions, repatriation facilities, and equal treatment.
metadata.summary: The Foreign Private Investment (Promotion and Protection) Act, 1976 provides for the promotion and protection of foreign private investment in Pakistan. It applies to industrial undertakings established with Federal Government approval after September 1, 1954, ensuring repatriation of profits and capital, tax concessions, and equal treatment with domestic investments. The Act also facilitates remittances by foreign employees and protects approved agreements from being affected by government takeover or acquisition.

metadata.short_title: The Foreigners Act, 1946
metadata.long_title: An Act to confer upon the Federal Government certain powers in respect of foreigners.
repeals: The Alien Registration Authority (Composition and Functions) Order, 2001
metadata.one_line: An Act empowering the Federal Government to regulate the entry, presence, and departure of foreigners in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Act confers specific powers upon the Federal Government regarding the management of foreigners entering, residing in, or departing from Pakistan. It grants authority to make orders restricting movement, imposing conditions on residence, and regulating activities. The legislation also establishes penalties for contraventions, provisions for deportation, and mechanisms for determining nationality.

metadata.short_title: The Forest Act, 1927
metadata.long_title: An Act to consolidate the law relating to forests, the transit of forest produce and the duty leviable on timber and other forest-produce
metadata.territorial_extent: Sind, the Punjab and the North-West Frontier Province (except the District of Hazara); extendable to other parts by Provincial Government notification
repeals: consolidated law relating to forests
metadata.one_line: Consolidates laws regarding forest management, timber transit duties, and related penalties in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Act consolidates the legal framework for managing reserved, village, and protected forests within specific provinces. It establishes powers for Provincial Governments to reserve forests, regulate timber transit, and impose duties on forest produce. The legislation also outlines procedures for handling cattle trespass, defining various forest-related terms, and prescribing penalties for contraventions.

metadata.short_title: The Foundation University Ordinance, 2002
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the establishment of a Foundation University at Islamabad and for matters ancillary thereto or connected therewith
establishes: Board of Advanced Studies and Research
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Foundation University at Islamabad and defines its structure, powers, and governing bodies.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Foundation University at Islamabad as a body corporate with perpetual succession. It outlines the composition of the university's authorities, including the Patron, Chancellor, President, Rector, and Board of Governors. The document grants the university powers to provide instruction, conduct research, and manage its own finances and discipline through specific committees.

name: Freedom of Information Ordinance, 2002(Repealed by Act XXXIV of 2017))

metadata.short_title: The Freedom of Information Ordinance, 2002
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for transparency and freedom of information
metadata.status_evidence: [Repealed by Act XXXIV of 2017]
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term not exceeding two years, or with fine, or with both
metadata.one_line: Provides for transparency and freedom of information to ensure citizens have improved access to public records.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance ensures that citizens of Pakistan have improved access to public records, making the Federal Government more accountable. It mandates that no requester shall be denied access to official records except under specific exemptions listed in the text. The Ordinance establishes procedures for filing complaints with the Mohtasib or Federal Tax Ombudsman if information is wrongfully denied or unduly delayed.

metadata.short_title: The Frontier Corps Ordinance, 1959
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to consolidate and amend the law relating to the regulation of the Frontier Corps Units
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of Pakistan (specifically members wherever they may be)
metadata.max_penalty: dismissal from service and imprisonment (specific terms not fully detailed in excerpts)
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance consolidates and amends laws regulating the Frontier Corps, defining its structure, powers, and offences.
metadata.summary: The Frontier Corps Ordinance, 1959 was promulgated by the President to consolidate and amend laws regarding the regulation of Frontier Corps units. It establishes the constitution, appointment of officers, and duties of members serving in the Frontier Corps under the Federal Government. The document outlines powers for maintaining the force, defines various terms related to service and custody, and prescribes offences and punishments for members, including summary trials and collective fines.

name: Funds Vesting in the President (Transfer) Act, 1973

metadata.short_title: The Funds Vesting in the President (Transfer) Act, 1973
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the administration of certain Funds vesting in the President and for matters connected therewith
metadata.one_line: This Act vests specified funds in the Federal Government and outlines their utilization purposes.
metadata.summary: The Funds Vesting in the President (Transfer) Act, 1973 provides for the administration of certain funds that vest in the President. It transfers these funds, along with their income and profits, to the Federal Government. The Act specifies four particular funds: the President's Relief Fund, the President's Palestine and Arab Relief Fund, the Tazeenul Quran Fund, and the Presidents' Welfare Fund. These funds are to be utilized for their original purposes or similar ones as circumstances permit.

metadata.short_title: The Futures Market Act, 2016
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the regulation of futures market and matters connected therewith and incidental thereto
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Federal Government may appoint by notification in the official Gazette
repeals: The Securities and Exchange Ordinance, 1969 (XVII of 1969)
metadata.one_line: This Act regulates the futures market in Pakistan, licensing exchanges and clearing houses while prohibiting insider trading and market abuse.
metadata.summary: The Futures Market Act, 2016 establishes a regulatory framework for futures markets in Pakistan by licensing futures exchanges and clearing houses. It empowers the Commission to supervise regulated activities, enforce conduct standards, and investigate market abuses such as insider trading and manipulation. The Act also outlines disciplinary procedures, penalties for offences, and transitional provisions repealing the previous Securities and Exchange Ordinance, 1969.

metadata.short_title: The Gas (Theft Control and Recovery) Act, 2016
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for prosecution of cases of gas theft and other offences relating to gas and to provide a procedure for recovery of amounts due
metadata.one_line: This Act establishes Gas Utility Courts to prosecute gas theft and recover outstanding amounts due to utility companies.
metadata.summary: The Gas (Theft Control and Recovery) Act, 2016 provides a legal framework for prosecuting cases of gas theft and other related offences. It establishes specialized Gas Utility Courts with exclusive jurisdiction over these matters to ensure expeditious recovery of dues, fines, and penalties owed to Gas Utility Companies. The Act defines various terms related to gas infrastructure and consumers, outlines procedures for complaints and suits, and grants powers to disconnect supply or impose additional fines in lieu of consumed gas.

metadata.short_title: The Gas Infrastructure Development Cess Act, 2015
metadata.long_title: An Act to levy and collect the Gas Infrastructure Development Cess
repeals: The Gas Infrastructure Development Cess Act, 2011 (XXI of 2011)
metadata.one_line: This Act levies and collects a cess on natural gas consumers for infrastructure development projects.
metadata.summary: The Gas Infrastructure Development Cess Act, 2015 provides for the levy, collection, and utilization of a cess on natural gas. It applies to gas consumers excluding the domestic sector and specific industrial categories like fertilizer fuel stock. The collected funds are utilized for major pipeline projects such as the Iran Pakistan Pipeline Project and TAPI. The Federal Government is responsible for billing, collection, and utilizing the cess, while also having the power to make rules and amend schedules.

metadata.short_title: The General Clauses Act, 1897
metadata.long_title: An Act to consolidate and extend the General Clauses Acts, 1868 and 1887.
repeals: General Clauses Act, 1868
General Clauses Act, 1887
metadata.one_line: Consolidates and extends previous General Clauses Acts to define terms and rules for construction of Pakistani laws.
metadata.summary: This Act consolidates and extends the General Clauses Acts of 1868 and 1887 to provide general definitions and rules for interpreting all Pakistan laws. It establishes standard meanings for terms like 'Act', 'Abet', and 'Affidavit' applicable across Central Acts and Regulations. The legislation also outlines procedures for the coming into operation, repeal, revival, and computation of time within legal enactments.

metadata.short_title: The General Statistics (Reorganization) Act, 2011
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for reorganization of statistical system in Pakistan through the merger of certain organizations and to provide for establishment of the Pakistan Bureau of Statistics for producing reliable, authentic, timely and transparent data compatible with the needs of the economy and socio economic development requirements of the nation and for matter connected therewith and incidental thereto
repeals: The General Statistics Act, 1975 (LXIX of 1975)
the Agricultural Census Act, 1958 (XLI of 1958)
the Census Ordinance, 1959 (X of 1959)
metadata.one_line: This Act reorganizes Pakistan's statistical system by establishing the Pakistan Bureau of Statistics and repealing previous census acts.
metadata.summary: The General Statistics (Reorganization) Act, 2011 establishes the Pakistan Bureau of Statistics to produce reliable data for national economic development. It merges existing organizations like the Federal Bureau of Statistics and Population Census Organization into the new Bureau. The Act defines the structure of the Governing Council, appoints a Chief Statistician, and outlines procedures for conducting censuses and collecting statistical data across the whole of Pakistan.

metadata.short_title: The Geneva Convention Implementing Act, 1936
metadata.long_title: An Act to implement Article 28 of the Geneva Convention of the 27th day of July, 1929.
metadata.max_penalty: fine which may extend to fifty rupees
metadata.one_line: Implements Article 28 of the 1929 Geneva Convention by prohibiting unauthorized use of Red Cross emblems in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Act implements obligations under the 1929 Geneva Convention regarding the protection of wounded and sick soldiers. It prohibits any person from using specific emblems like 'Red Cross', 'Red Crescent', or imitations thereof without entitlement, except for authorized medical vehicles with written permission. The law also bans the use of the Swiss white cross on red ground emblem in trade or business. Contraventions are punishable by a fine up to fifty rupees and require prior sanction from the Federal Government for prosecution.

metadata.short_title: The Geographical Indications (Registration and Protection) Act, 2020
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for registration and effective protection of geographical indications
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Federal Government may by notification in the Official Gazette appoint
repeals: Clause (xix) of section 2 of the Trade Marks Ordinance, 2001 (XIX of 2001)
metadata.one_line: Provides for the registration and protection of geographical indications in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes a legal framework for the registration and protection of geographical indications (GIs) for goods originating in specific territories or regions. It creates a Geographical Indications Registry headed by a Registrar to manage applications, examinations, and the register itself. The legislation outlines procedures for registration, rights conferred upon registrants, mechanisms for infringement proceedings before IP Tribunals, and penalties for false application of GIs.

name: Ghurki Institute of Science and Technology Act, 2026

metadata.short_title: The Ghurki Institute of Science and Technology Act, 2026
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of the Ghurki Institute of Science and Technology
establishes: Ghurki Institute of Science and Technology
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Ghurki Institute of Science and Technology as a private sector body corporate with academic autonomy.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Ghurki Institute of Science and Technology as a body corporate in the private sector. It grants the Institute perpetual succession, the power to hold property, and full academic, financial, and administrative autonomy. The Act defines the structure of the Institute, including its Patron, Chancellor, Rector, and various authorities like the Board of Governors and Academic Council.

metadata.short_title: The Glanders and Farcy Act, 1899
metadata.long_title: An Act to consolidate and amend the law relating to Glanders and Farcy.
repeals: enactments mentioned in the Schedule
establishes: Veterinary Practitioners appointed by Provincial Government
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to one month, or with fine which may extend to fifty rupees, or with both
metadata.one_line: Consolidates and amends laws regarding glanders and farcy in horses, including inspection, seizure, and destruction protocols.
metadata.summary: This Act consolidates and amends the law relating to glanders and farcy among horses. It empowers the Provincial Government to appoint Inspectors and Veterinary Practitioners to examine seized horses. If a horse is found diseased, it must be destroyed or treated as prescribed, while premises are disinfected. The Act also provides for penalties for non-compliance and allows the Provincial Government to make rules to carry out its purposes.

name: Global Climate-Change Impact Studies Centre Act, 2013

metadata.short_title: The Global Climate-Change Impact Studies Centre Act, 2013
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for establishment of Global Climate-Change Impact Studies Centre
metadata.administering_body: Federal Government (via Ministry dealing with climate change)
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Global Climate-Change Impact Studies Centre to conduct scientific research on climate change impacts.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Global Climate-Change Impact Studies Centre (GCISC) as a body corporate to undertake scientific investigations into climate change. The Centre is tasked with studying impacts on sectors like water, agriculture, and health, while collaborating with international organizations. It creates a Board of Governors for management and grants the Federal Government authority to issue policy directives.

metadata.short_title: The Government Buildings Act, 1899
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the exemption from the operation of municipal building laws of certain buildings and lands which are the property, or in the occupation, of the Government and situate within the limits of a municipality.
metadata.one_line: Exempts certain government-owned buildings within municipalities from local building laws.
metadata.summary: This Act provides for the exemption of specific government buildings and lands from municipal building laws. It applies to properties owned or occupied by the Government situated within municipal limits. The legislation outlines procedures for raising objections regarding the erection or alteration of such buildings and grants inspection powers to municipal authorities with Provincial Government permission.

metadata.short_title: The Government Grants Act, 1895
metadata.long_title: An Act to explain the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, so far as relates to grants from the [Government], and to remove certain doubts as to the powers of the [Government] in relation to such grants.
metadata.one_line: Explains the Transfer of Property Act regarding government land grants and removes doubts on government powers.
metadata.summary: This Act clarifies how the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 applies to land grants made by the Government. It states that the 1882 Act does not apply to any grant or transfer of land made by or on behalf of the Government. All conditions and limitations in such government grants remain valid according to their tenor, regardless of other laws.

name: Government Management of Private Estates Act, 1892

metadata.short_title: The Government Management of Private Estates Act, 1892
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the levy of a rate on private estates under the management of the Government to meet the cost of supervision and management.
repeals: the original sub-section (2) of section 2 as amended by the Burma Laws Act, 1898
the Federal Laws (Revision and Declaration) Act, 1951
metadata.status_evidence: [Repeal.] Rep.by the Repealing and Amending Act, 1914 (X of 1914), s.3 and Schedule II.
metadata.one_line: This Act empowers the Provincial Government to levy rates on private estates under government management to cover supervision costs.
metadata.summary: This Act provides for the levy of a rate on private estates managed by the Government to cover the cost of supervision and management. It defines key terms such as 'immoveable property' and 'gross income', and grants the Provincial Government the power to vary or remit rates in special cases. The Act also exempts government establishments from court jurisdiction regarding cost decisions and validates past rate levies.

metadata.short_title: The Government Savings Banks Act, 1873
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the law relating to Government Savings Banks
repeals: The Savings Banks Act, 1863 (26 and 27 Vict., c. 87)
metadata.one_line: This Act amends the law relating to Government Savings Banks and regulates payments of deposits for deceased, minors, lunatics, and married women.
metadata.summary: The Government Savings Banks Act, 1873 amends the law regarding Government Savings Banks in Pakistan. It provides specific provisions for the payment of deposits belonging to deceased persons, minors, lunatics, and married women, including rules on nominations and discharges upon receipt. The Act also empowers the Federal Government to prescribe rules regulating certificates and payments under various sections.

metadata.short_title: The Government Tenants (North-West Frontier) Act, 1893
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the grant of Special Tenancies in Government lands in the North-West Frontier.
metadata.one_line: Provides for the grant of special tenancies in government lands in the North-West Frontier and regulates tenant rights.
metadata.summary: This Act facilitates the granting of special tenancies in government-owned lands located in the North-West Frontier. It establishes a system for issuing statements of tenancy conditions, maintaining registers of these tenancies, and recording entries signed by both the tenant and the Deputy Commissioner. The legislation outlines restrictions on transferring or selling tenant rights without specific consent from the Financial Commissioner and allows sums due to be recovered as land revenue arrears.

metadata.short_title: The Government Trading Taxation Act, 1926
metadata.long_title: An Act to determine the liability of certain Governments to taxation in [Pakistan] in respect of trading operations.
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Federal Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, appoint
key_definitions: Government of a Province of Pakistan
metadata.one_line: Determines the tax liability of Provincial Governments on trading operations carried on outside their respective provinces.
metadata.summary: This Act determines the tax liability of Provincial Governments in Pakistan regarding trading operations. It stipulates that when a trade or business is carried on by a Provincial Government outside its own province, it is liable to taxation under the Income Tax Ordinance, 1979 as if it were a company. The text includes numerous footnotes indicating amendments and adaptations made by various Federal Orders and Acts between 1937 and 1981.

metadata.short_title: The Guardians and Wards Act, 1890
metadata.long_title: An Act to consolidate and amend the law relating to Guardian and Ward.
repeals: THE SCHEDULE
metadata.one_line: Consolidates and amends the law relating to guardianship of minors and management of their property.
metadata.summary: This Act consolidates and amends laws regarding the appointment, duties, and liabilities of guardians for minors. It defines terms like 'minor' and 'guardian', outlines court procedures for appointing guardians, and regulates the management of a ward's property. The Act also covers the removal of guardians, their remuneration, and the powers of Collectors acting as guardians.

metadata.short_title: The Gun and Country Club Act, 2023
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment, administration and management of the affairs of the Gun and Country Club in Islamabad.
metadata.administering_body: Federal Government (via the Secretary of the division concerned)
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Gun and Country Club in Islamabad and provides for its administration, management, and governance.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Gun and Country Club in Islamabad as a body corporate with perpetual succession. It defines the roles of the Patron-in-Chief (Prime Minister), Administrator, and Management Committee, outlining their powers and functions regarding club affairs, finances, and employment. The legislation also empowers the Federal Government to make rules for external matters and the Management Committee to make regulations for internal matters.

metadata.short_title: The Gwadar Port Authority Ordinance, 2002
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the establishment of an Authority within the limits of Gwadar Port for making arrangements for the planning, construction, operation, management and maintenance of Gwadar Deep Water Port at Gwadar, hereinafter referred to as Gwadar Port, and associated facilities and industries and for matters incidental thereto
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Port area
metadata.max_penalty: ten million rupees
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Gwadar Port Authority to manage, plan, and maintain the Gwadar Deep Water Port.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Gwadar Port Authority to oversee the planning, construction, operation, management, and maintenance of the Gwadar Deep Water Port. It defines the Authority's powers regarding tolls, land acquisition, pollution control, and financial management through a dedicated fund. The document also outlines the composition of the Board, appointment of officers, and provisions for the dissolution of the Authority by the Federal Government.

metadata.short_title: The Gwadur (Application of Central Laws) Ordinance, 1960
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance for applying to Gwadur all Central laws which are or may hereafter be in force in the Mekran District in the Kalat Division of the Province of West Pakistan.
metadata.territorial_extent: Gwadur (ceded territory), Mekran District in the Kalat Division of the Province of West Pakistan
repeals: any law or legal instrument having the force of law in Gwadur (Gwadur law) in force immediately before the eighth day of September, 1958
metadata.one_line: Applies all Central laws in force in Mekran District to the ceded territory of Gwadur as of September 8, 1958.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance applies all Federal Acts, Orders, and notifications in force in the Mekran District of West Pakistan to the territory of Gwadur. It deems these laws to have been in force in Gwadur since September 8, 1958, while repealing corresponding local Gwadur laws. The text ensures that past actions, rights, liabilities, and legal proceedings under the repealed local laws remain valid and unaffected by this application of Federal law.

metadata.short_title: The Hackney-carriage Act, 1879
metadata.long_title: An Act for the regulation and control of hackney-carriages in certain Municipalities and Cantonments.
repeals: Section 4
metadata.max_penalty: fine which may extend to fifty rupees; imprisonment for a term which may extend to one month
metadata.one_line: Regulates and controls hackney-carriages in specific municipalities and cantonments through rules on licensing, fares, and penalties.
metadata.summary: This Act provides for the regulation and control of hackney-carriages in certain municipalities and cantonments. It empowers municipal committees to make rules regarding licenses, animal conditions, fare limits, and carriage standards. The Act also establishes mechanisms for resolving fare disputes between hirers and drivers through Magistrates and defines penalties for rule breaches.

metadata.short_title: The Hajj and Umrah (Regulation) Act, 2024
metadata.long_title: An Act for regulating and managing the Hajj and Umrah
metadata.administering_body: division concerned (Secretary of the division concerned)
metadata.one_line: This Act regulates and manages Hajj and Umrah activities, licensing organizers, and managing funds in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: The Act provides a comprehensive framework for regulating Hajj and Umrah activities, including policy formulation, licensing of organizers, and quota management. It establishes committees for complaint disposal and appeals, defines terms related to pilgrims and service providers, and outlines procedures for fund management and audit. The legislation also grants powers to the Federal Government and division concerned to make rules and regulations, impose penalties for violations, and recover arrears.

metadata.short_title: The Health Services Academy (Restructuring) Act, 2018
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for restructuring of health services academy as a degree awarding institute
repeals: Health Services Academy Ordinance, 2002 (LXII of 2002)
establishes: Health Services Academy (restructured as a degree awarding institute)
metadata.one_line: Restructures the Health Services Academy into an autonomous degree-awarding institute with new governance structures.
metadata.summary: This Act restructures the Health Services Academy, established under the 2002 Ordinance, into a degree-awarding institute to enhance higher education quality. It grants the academy autonomy while improving governance and management through the creation of a corporate body with perpetual succession. The legislation defines various authorities including the Senate, Syndicate, and Academic Council, and outlines procedures for appointing officers and teachers.

metadata.short_title: Health Services Academy Ordinance, 2002
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the establishment of Health Services Academy
metadata.one_line: Establishes the autonomous Health Services Academy Islamabad for health sciences training and research.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Health Services Academy Islamabad as an autonomous body with perpetual succession. It empowers the Academy to provide instruction in health sciences, conduct research, affiliate institutions, and award degrees in collaboration with Quaid-i-Azam University. The Academy manages its own funds derived from grants, fees, and investments while operating under the supervision of a Board of Governors and the Ministry of Health.

metadata.short_title: Heavy Industries Taxila Board Act, 1997
metadata.long_title: An Act to establish a Heavy Industries Taxila Board and to provide for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Heavy Industries Taxila Board to manage factories for defence and civilian needs.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Heavy Industries Taxila Board consisting of a Chairman and five members appointed by the Federal Government. The Board is empowered to manage, organize, and reorganize heavy industries and manufacturing factories under its control. Its principal functions include meeting defence requirements during war and peace while utilizing commercial potential for civilian needs. The Board operates under the directions of the Federal Government regarding national interest and policy questions.

metadata.short_title: The High Treason (Punishment) Act, 1973
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the punishment of persons found guilty of acts of abrogation or subversion of a Constitution or of high treason
metadata.max_penalty: death or imprisonment for life
metadata.one_line: Provides punishment including death or life imprisonment for high treason and subversion of the Constitution.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes penalties for individuals found guilty of abrogating or subverting a Constitution in force since March 23, 1956, or committing high treason. It prescribes punishments of death or life imprisonment for such offenses. The procedure requires a written complaint authorized by the Federal Government before any court can take cognizance of these specific offenses.

metadata.short_title: The Higher Education Commission Ordinance, 2002
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the establishment of the Higher Education Commission
repeals: The University Grants Commission Act, 1974 (XXIII of 1974)
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Higher Education Commission to promote higher education and research, repealing the UGC Act 1974.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Higher Education Commission (HEC) as a body corporate with perpetual succession to oversee higher education and research in Pakistan. It defines the composition of the Commission, including members from international eminence, provincial governments, and the private sector, under the supervision of the Prime Minister or Chief Executive. The document repeals the University Grants Commission Act, 1974, transferring all assets, liabilities, and personnel from the UGC to the new Commission effective immediately upon commencement.

metadata.short_title: The Hindu Disposition of Property Act, 1916
metadata.long_title: An Act to remove certain existing disabilities in respect of the power of disposition of property by Hindus for the benefit of persons not in existence at the date of such disposition.
metadata.one_line: Removes disabilities preventing Hindus from making property dispositions for beneficiaries not yet born.
metadata.summary: This Act allows Hindus to make dispositions of property (via transfer inter vivos or will) for the benefit of persons not in existence at the time of the disposition. It applies limitations and conditions regarding such transfers based on the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 and specific sections of the Indian Succession Act, 1925. The Act also provides a mechanism for the Provincial Government to extend its provisions to the Khoja community via notification.

metadata.short_title: The Hindu Gains of Learning Act, 1930
metadata.long_title: An Act to remove doubt as to the rights of a member of a Hindu undivided family in property acquired by him by means of his learning.
metadata.one_line: This Act clarifies that property acquired by a Hindu family member through their own learning is their separate property.
metadata.summary: The Hindu Gains of Learning Act, 1930 removes doubts regarding the rights of members of a Hindu undivided family to property acquired through their own learning. It establishes that such gains are the exclusive and separate property of the acquirer, regardless of whether the learning was imparted by family members or aided by joint funds. The Act also defines key terms like 'acquirer', 'gains of learning', and 'learning' to ensure uniform application across the country.

metadata.short_title: The Hindu Inheritance (Removal of Disabilities) Act, 1928
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Hindu Law relating to exclusion from inheritance of certain classes of heirs, and to remove certain doubts.
metadata.one_line: Removes disabilities preventing persons with defects from inheriting under Hindu law.
metadata.summary: This Act amends Hindu law to prevent the exclusion of heirs from inheritance or joint-family property solely due to disease, deformity, or physical or mental defects. It applies to all persons governed by Hindu law except those following the Daya-bhaga School and excludes persons who have been lunatics or idiots since birth. The legislation also preserves rights accrued before its commencement and does not confer new rights regarding religious offices or charitable trusts.

metadata.short_title: The Hindu Marriage Act, 2017
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for solemnization of marriages by Hindu families and for matters ancillary and incidental thereto
metadata.territorial_extent: the Islamabad Capital Territory and the Provinces of Balochistan, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Punjab
metadata.max_penalty: six months imprisonment or fine up to one hundred thousand rupees or both
metadata.one_line: Provides for solemnization and registration of Hindu marriages in specified provinces and the ICT.
metadata.summary: This Act consolidates laws regarding the solemnization of marriages by Hindu families in Balochistan, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Punjab, and the Islamabad Capital Territory. It establishes conditions for valid marriage, procedures for registration via appointed registrars, and remedies for void or voidable marriages. The Act also outlines penalties for bigamy and false statements during registration.

metadata.short_title: The Hindu Marriage Disabilities Removal Act, 1946
metadata.long_title: An Act to remove certain disabilities and doubts under Hindu Law in respect of marriages between Hindus.
metadata.one_line: Removes disabilities under Hindu Law regarding marriages between persons of the same gotra, pravara, or caste sub-divisions.
metadata.summary: This Act removes specific disabilities and doubts under Hindu Law concerning the validity of marriages between Hindus. It declares that a marriage is not invalid solely because the parties belong to the same gotra or pravara, or different sub-divisions of the same caste. The Act applies to the whole of Pakistan and was extended to various princely states and leased areas through subsequent orders.

name: Hindu Married Women's Right to Separate Residence and Maintenance Act, 1946

metadata.short_title: The Hindu Married Women's Right to Separate Residence and Maintenance Act, 1946
metadata.long_title: An Act to give Hindu married women a right to separate residence and maintenance under certain circumstances.
metadata.one_line: This Act grants Hindu married women the right to separate residence and maintenance from their husbands under specific circumstances.
metadata.summary: This legislation provides Hindu married women with the legal right to claim separate residence and financial maintenance from their husbands. The grounds for such a claim include the husband suffering from a loathsome disease, committing cruelty, deserting the wife, marrying again, converting to another religion, or keeping a concubine. When determining the amount of maintenance, courts must consider the social standing of the parties and the husband's financial means.

metadata.short_title: The Hindu Widows' Re-marriage Act, 1856
metadata.long_title: An Act to remove all legal obstacles to the marriage of Hindu Widows.
