metadata.territorial_extent: all the Provinces and the Capital of the Federation, except the Scheduled Districts (with specific extensions to certain districts in Sind and N.W.F.P. via later acts)
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for any term not exceeding one year or to fine or to both
metadata.one_line: Legalizes the re-marriage of Hindu widows and adjusts their inheritance and guardianship rights upon remarriage.
metadata.summary: This Act removes legal obstacles preventing Hindu widows from contracting a second valid marriage. It stipulates that a widow's rights in her deceased husband's property cease upon remarriage, transferring succession to his next heirs. The law also addresses the guardianship of children born from such marriages and sets conditions for consent required for minor versus major widows.

name: Hindu Women s Rights to Property Act, 1937

metadata.short_title: The Hindu Women's Rights to Property Act, 1937
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Hindu Law governing Hindu Women's Rights to Property.
metadata.one_line: Amends Hindu Law to grant widows specific shares in the property of a deceased husband who died intestate.
metadata.summary: This Act amends Hindu Law to provide better property rights for women. It applies when a Hindu dies intestate leaving a widow, granting her a share equivalent to that of a son under specific schools of law. The Act defines 'dying intestate' regarding testamentary dispositions and clarifies the nature of the interest devolving on a widow as a limited estate with partition rights.

name: House Building Finance Corporation (Repeal) Act, 2018 (Act No_XXV of 2018)

metadata.short_title: The House Building Finance Corporation (Repeal) Act, 2018
metadata.long_title: An Act to repeal the House Building Finance Corporation Act, 1952
repeals: The House Building Finance Corporation Act, 1952
metadata.one_line: This Act repeals the House Building Finance Corporation Act, 1952 and comes into force immediately.
metadata.summary: The document is a short Federal Act enacted by Parliament to repeal the existing House Building Finance Corporation Act, 1952. It was passed on May 18, 2018, and came into force at once upon enactment. The primary mechanism of this legislation is the total supersession of the 1952 Act, effectively ending its legal operation.

name: House Building Finance Corporation Act, 1952(Repeal by act XXV of 2018,s.2)

metadata.short_title: The House Building Finance Corporation Act, 1952
metadata.long_title: An Act to establish a House Building Finance Corporation.
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Federal Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, appoint
repeals: Act XVIII of 1891
metadata.one_line: Establishes the House Building Finance Corporation to provide financial facilities for housing construction and purchase.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the House Building Finance Corporation as a body corporate with perpetual succession. The Corporation is empowered to raise funds, make investments, and provide loans for the construction, reconstruction, repair, and purchase of houses. It outlines the constitution of the Board of Directors, management structure, and powers regarding business transactions and enforcement of claims.

name: Hyderabad Institute for Technology and Management Sciences Act, 2021

metadata.short_title: The Hyderabad Institute for Technology and Management Sciences Act, 2021
metadata.long_title: An act to provide for the establishment of Hyderabad Institute for Technology and Management Sciences as a degree awarding institute
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, appoint
establishes: Hyderabad Institute for Technology and Management Sciences
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Hyderabad Institute for Technology and Management Sciences as a degree awarding institution with academic autonomy.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Hyderabad Institute for Technology and Management Sciences as a degree awarding institution located in Hyderabad. It grants the institute perpetual succession, the power to hold property, and full academic, financial, and administrative autonomy. The Act defines various authorities including the Board of Governors, Academic Council, and committees responsible for finance, planning, and student discipline.

name: Hydrocarbon Development Institute of Pakistan Act,2006

metadata.short_title: The Hydrocarbon Development Institute of Pakistan Act, 2006
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of the Hydrocarbon Development Institute of Pakistan
repeals: The Government of Pakistan, Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Resources Resolution No. DP(1l)/82, dated the 26th July, 1984
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Hydrocarbon Development Institute of Pakistan for hydrocarbon research, development, and quality control.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Hydrocarbon Development Institute of Pakistan as a body corporate to conduct scientific research and development in the hydrocarbon sector. The Institute is headed by a Board of Governors and a Director-General, with headquarters in Islamabad. Its functions include formulating national policies, undertaking basic studies, promoting optimum exploitation of resources, controlling environmental pollution, and providing consultancy services. The Act also provides for the transfer of assets, contracts, and employees from the former Institute to the new entity.

name: Hydrogenated Vegetable Oil Industry (Control and Development) Act, 1973

metadata.short_title: The Hydrogenated Vegetable Oil Industry (Control and Development) Act, 1973
metadata.long_title: An Act to regulate the operation and future development of the hydrogenated vegetable oil industry.
metadata.one_line: This Act regulates the hydrogenated vegetable oil industry, allowing the Federal Government to take over management and acquire shares.
metadata.summary: The Hydrogenated Vegetable Oil Industry (Control and Development) Act, 1973 was enacted to regulate the operation and future development of the hydrogenated vegetable oil industry. It empowers the Federal Government to take over the management or acquire shares in establishments within this industry while safeguarding small investors. The Act establishes a Board of Management, outlines functions regarding funds and officers, and provides principles for calculating compensation upon acquisition.

metadata.short_title: The Ibadat International University Islamabad Act, 2021
metadata.long_title: An Act for the Establishment of Ibadat International University, Islamabad
metadata.one_line: Establishes Ibadat International University, Islamabad as a private sector institution in the whole of Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Ibadat International University, Islamabad, as an entity operating in the private sector. It defines the university's structure, including its Patron, Chairman, Board of Governors, and various academic and administrative authorities. The legislation outlines the powers of these bodies, provisions for statutes and regulations, employment terms for officers and teachers, and mechanisms for appeals and indemnity.

name: ICT (Tax on Services) Ordinance, 2001 (Same as on the official website of FBR dated 30-06-2025)

metadata.short_title: Islamabad Capital Territory (Tax on Services) Ordinance, 2001
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for levy of sales tax on services rendered or provided in the Islamabad Capital Territory and for matters ancillary thereto or connected therewith
metadata.one_line: Imposes sales tax on services rendered in the Islamabad Capital Territory with specific rates and exemptions.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance provides for the levy of sales tax on services rendered or provided within the Islamabad Capital Territory. It establishes a tax regime mirroring the Sales Tax Act, 1990, specifying rates for various service categories and conditions regarding input tax adjustments. The document also outlines provisions for exporting services at zero percent and allows for the creation of a negative list of exempt services.

name: ICT Rights of Persons with Disability Act, 2020

metadata.short_title: The ICT Rights of Persons with Disability Act, 2020
metadata.long_title: An Act to promote, protect and effectively ensure the rights and inclusion of persons with disabilities in the communities in line with the Islamic Injunctions and provisions of the Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan to advance efforts for recognition of their respect and dignity in the society;
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Islamabad Capital Territory (ICT)
repeals: The Disabled Persons (Employment and Rehabilitation) Ordinance, 1981 (XL of 1981)
establishes: Council on Rights of Persons with Disabilities
metadata.administering_body: The Council on Rights of Persons with Disabilities
metadata.one_line: This Act promotes and protects the rights, inclusion, and dignity of persons with disabilities in Islamabad Capital Territory.
metadata.summary: The ICT Rights of Persons with Disability Act, 2020 establishes a legal framework to ensure equality, non-discrimination, and full participation for persons with disabilities within the Islamabad Capital Territory. It creates the Council on Rights of Persons with Disabilities to oversee rehabilitation, registration, and advocacy efforts while mandating government support in education, employment, and health services. The Act also provides for special disability courts, insurance coverage, and repeals the earlier Disabled Persons (Employment and Rehabilitation) Ordinance, 1981 within its territorial scope.

metadata.short_title: The Identification of Prisoners Act, 1920
metadata.long_title: An Act to authorise the taking of measurements and photographs of convicts and others.
metadata.one_line: Authorizes taking measurements and photographs of convicts and arrested persons for identification purposes.
metadata.summary: This Act authorizes the taking of measurements and photographs of convicted persons and those arrested for serious offences. It defines key terms such as 'measurements' to include finger and foot-print impressions, and outlines the powers of police officers and magistrates to order these procedures. The Act also provides for the destruction of records upon acquittal and establishes that resistance to these measures is an offence.

metadata.short_title: The Illegal Dispossession Act, 2005
metadata.long_title: An Act to curb the activities of the property grabbers
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment which may extend to ten years and with fine
metadata.one_line: An Act to curb property grabbers by preventing illegal dispossession of immovable property and providing for eviction and compensation.
metadata.summary: This Act aims to protect lawful owners and occupiers from illegal or forcible dispossession by property grabbers. It defines key terms such as 'owner', 'occupier', and 'Property' (immovable property) and prohibits entering property without lawful authority with the intention of dispossession. The Act establishes procedures for investigation, trial within sixty days, attachment of property, and interim eviction orders. It prescribes severe penalties, including up to ten years imprisonment, and provides for compensation to victims.

metadata.short_title: The Import of Goods (Development Surcharge) Ordinance, 1984
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the levy and collection of a development surcharge on certain goods imported through the Karachi customs-port.
metadata.commencement: on such day as the Federal Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, appoint
metadata.one_line: Levies a development surcharge on specific goods imported through Karachi to reimburse the Karachi Port Trust.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance provides for the levy and collection of a development surcharge on goods imported through the Karachi customs-port. The proceeds are intended to reimburse the Karachi Port Trust for expenditures incurred on constructing the Jinnah Bridge over China Creek. The surcharge applies at a rate of three rupees and fifty paisa per ton, excluding foodgrains, fertilizers, and petroleum products. Collection procedures follow the Customs Act, 1969.

name: Import of Goods (Price Equalization Surcharge) Act, 1967

metadata.short_title: The Import of Goods (Price Equalization Surcharge) Act, 1967
metadata.long_title: An Act to levy an additional duty for equalization of prices of certain imported goods.
metadata.max_penalty: punishable under section 5 of the Imports and Exports (Control) Act, 1950
metadata.one_line: This Act levies an additional duty on specified imported goods to equalize their prices.
metadata.summary: The Import of Goods (Price Equalization Surcharge) Act, 1967 imposes an additional duty on certain imported goods whose landed cost is lower than the highest rate declared for a specific shipping period. The Federal Government determines the highest landed cost and declares it via notification in the official Gazette. The Act empowers the Federal Government to make rules regarding the collection, repayment, and delivery of goods subject to the surcharge, as well as to amend the Schedule listing specified goods.

metadata.short_title: Imports and Exports (Control) Act, 1950
metadata.long_title: An Act to continue powers to prohibit or control imports and exports.
repeals: Imports and Exports (Control) Act, 1947
metadata.one_line: Continues federal powers to prohibit, restrict, or control imports and exports via orders and licences.
metadata.summary: This Act empowers the Federal Government to continue and exercise powers to prohibit or control imports and exports into and out of Pakistan. It allows for the issuance of licences by the Chief Controller and provides for the creation of a Revolving Fund to support these operations. The Act also outlines penalties for offences and specifies that cognizance of such offences can be taken by specific customs officers or the Chief Controller.

name: Income Tax Ordinance, 2001 (Same as on the official website of FBR dated 31-06-2026)

metadata.short_title: Income Tax Ordinance, 2001
metadata.long_title: An Act to consolidate the law relating to income-tax.
metadata.one_line: Consolidates the law relating to income-tax in Pakistan, defining charge, computation, and exemptions.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance consolidates the law relating to income-tax in Pakistan. It establishes the charge of tax on various heads of income including salary, property, business, capital gains, and other sources. The document outlines rules for computing taxable income, deductions allowed, tax credits, and provisions for minimum tax and exemptions for specific categories like SMEs and foreign-source income.

metadata.short_title: The Indecent Advertisements Prohibition Act, 1963
metadata.long_title: An Act to prohibit indecent Advertisements
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both
key_definitions: taking any part in the publication of any advertisement
metadata.one_line: This Act prohibits the publication and display of indecent advertisements throughout Pakistan.
metadata.summary: The Indecent Advertisements Prohibition Act, 1963 was enacted to prohibit indecent advertisements in Pakistan. It defines what constitutes an advertisement and indecent content, prohibiting persons from publishing or displaying such material. The Act prescribes penalties for contravention, including imprisonment and fines, and provides for the confiscation of documents containing indecent advertisements.

metadata.short_title: The Indus River System Authority Act, 1992
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of the Indus River System Authority
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Indus River System Authority to regulate and monitor water distribution in accordance with the Water Accord.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Indus River System Authority as a body corporate to regulate and monitor the distribution of water sources in the Indus River system. The Authority consists of five members nominated by the Provinces and the Federal Government, with specific duties to coordinate activities and review river operation patterns based on the Water Accord. It provides for the Authority's constitution, financing through an 'Authority Fund', audit procedures, and the power to make rules and regulations.

name: Industrial and Commercial Employment (Standing Orders) Ordinance, 1968

metadata.short_title: Industrial and Commercial Employment (Standing Orders) Ordinance, 1968
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend and consolidate the law relating to industrial employment in the Province of West Pakistan.
amends: Industrial and Commercial Employment (Standing Orders) Ordinance, 1960
repeals: Industrial and Commercial Employment (Standing Orders) Ordinance, 1960
metadata.max_penalty: fine which may extend to one hundred rupees (or double punishment for repeat offences)
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance consolidates laws on industrial employment and sets standing orders for workmen in West Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends and consolidates the law relating to industrial employment in the Province of West Pakistan. It applies to industrial or commercial establishments employing twenty or more workmen, excluding government establishments. The document defines key terms such as 'workman' and 'employer', establishes standing orders regarding classification, wages, leave, and termination, and outlines penalties for contravention.

name: Industrial Development Bank of Pakistan (Reorganization and Conversion) Act, 2011

metadata.short_title: The Industrial Development Bank of Pakistan (Reorganization and Conversion) Act, 2011
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the reorganization and conversion of the Industrial Development Bank of Pakistan into a public limited company
repeals: Industrial Development Bank of Pakistan Ordinance, 1961 (XXXI of 1961)
metadata.one_line: This Act reorganizes IDBP into a public limited company, transfers its assets/liabilities, and repeals the 1961 Ordinance.
metadata.summary: This Act provides for the conversion of the Industrial Development Bank of Pakistan (IDBP) into a public limited company known as the Industrial Development Bank Limited. It mandates the transfer of all assets, liabilities, contracts, and proceedings from IDBP to the new Company and deems the Company to be a banking company pending license approval. The Act also validates actions taken prior to its commencement and repeals the Industrial Development Bank of Pakistan Ordinance, 1961.

name: Industrial Development Bank of Pakistan Ordinance, 1961(Repeal by ord.XXXViii of 2009,s.14(w.e.f 17-09-2007 upto 25-03-2010))

metadata.short_title: The Industrial Development Bank of Pakistan Ordinance, 1961
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to establish an Industrial Development Bank
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Federal Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, direct
repeals: Pakistan Industrial Finance Corporation Act, 1949
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Industrial Development Bank of Pakistan to provide credit facilities to industrial concerns.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Industrial Development Bank of Pakistan to replace the Pakistan Industrial Finance Corporation. It provides for making credit facilities available expeditiously to industrial concerns in Pakistan and matters connected therewith. The document defines key terms, outlines the bank's structure including its Board and officers, and details its powers regarding loans, borrowing, and business transactions.

name: Industrial Relations Act, 2008 (Repealed by Act X of 2012)

metadata.short_title: Industrial Relations Act, 2008
metadata.long_title: An Act to consolidated and rationalize the law relating to formation of trade unions, and improvement of relations between employers and workman.
repeals: Industrial Relations Ordinance 2002 (XCI of 2002)
metadata.max_penalty: fine or imprisonment (specific amounts not stated in excerpts)
metadata.one_line: Consolidates and rationalizes laws on trade unions, industrial relations, dispute resolution, and strikes in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Act consolidates and rationalizes the law regarding the formation of trade unions and the regulation of relations between employers and workmen. It establishes mechanisms for collective bargaining, defines unfair labour practices, and sets out procedures for resolving industrial disputes through conciliation, arbitration, and Labour Courts. The Act also regulates strikes and lock-outs, particularly in public utility services, and provides penalties for contraventions.

metadata.short_title: Industrial Relations Act, 2012
metadata.long_title: An Act to consolidate and rationalize the law relating to formation of trade unions, and improvement of relations between employers and workmen in the Islamabad Capital Territory and in trans-provincial establishments and industry
repeals: Industrial Relations Ordinance, 2002
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for two years or more or fine
metadata.one_line: Consolidates and rationalizes laws regarding trade unions, collective bargaining, industrial disputes, and strikes in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Act consolidates and rationalizes the law relating to the formation of trade unions and the improvement of relations between employers and workmen. It applies to all persons employed in establishments in the Islamabad Capital Territory or carrying on business in more than one province, excluding specific government and defense services. The legislation establishes mechanisms for collective bargaining, dispute settlement through conciliation and arbitration, and regulates strikes and lock-outs while creating penalties for unfair labour practices.

name: Industrial Relations Ordinance, 2002 (Repealed by Act No IV of 2008)

metadata.short_title: Industrial Relations Ordinance, 2002
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend, consolidate and rationalize the law relating to formation of trade unions, regulation and improvement of relations between employers and workmen and avoidance and settlement of any differences or disputes arising between them.
repeals: Industrial Relations Ordinance, 1969

It establishes mechanisms for collective bargaining, conciliation, arbitration, and adjudication of industrial disputes through Labour Courts and the National Industrial Relations Commission. The Ordinance defines public utility services, outlines rights and duties of employers and workers, and prescribes penalties for unfair labour practices and illegal strikes or lock-outs.

metadata.short_title: The Industrial Statistics Act, 1942
metadata.long_title: An Act to facilitate the collection of statistics of certain kinds relating to industries
metadata.commencement: on such date as the appropriate Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, appoint

metadata.administering_body: the appropriate Government (Federal Government for industries under Federal control; Provincial Government for other industries)
metadata.one_line: This Act facilitates the collection of industrial statistics and establishes a statistics authority with powers to call for returns.
metadata.summary: The Industrial Statistics Act, 1942 provides a legal framework for collecting statistics relating to factories and labour welfare conditions. It empowers the appropriate Government to appoint a statistics authority responsible for issuing notices and accessing records to gather this data. The Act includes strict provisions restricting the publication of individual returns without consent and imposes penalties for refusing to furnish information or providing false data.

metadata.short_title: The Injured Persons (Medical Aid) Act, 2004
metadata.long_title: An Act to make provisions for medical aid and treatment of injured persons
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment up to two years or fine not less than ten thousand rupees or both
metadata.administering_body: Federal Government or a Provincial Government
metadata.one_line: This Act ensures immediate medical aid for injured persons without delay, police interference, or waiting for relative consent.
metadata.summary: The Injured Persons (Medical Aid) Act, 2004 provides for the immediate medical treatment of injured persons regardless of pending medico-legal formalities. It prohibits police interference during treatment, allows emergency operations without relative consent, and mandates that injured persons not be taken to police stations before receiving care. The Act empowers governments to notify hospitals capable of handling emergencies and establishes penalties for violations.

metadata.short_title: The Inland Mechanically Propelled Vessels Act, 1917
metadata.long_title: An act to consolidate the enactments relating to [Mechanically Propelled Vessels].
repeals: SCHEDULE II
metadata.max_penalty: fine not exceeding one thousand rupees
metadata.one_line: Consolidates laws regulating mechanically propelled vessels, surveys, certificates, and penalties in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Act consolidates legislation regarding mechanically propelled vessels operating on inland waters. It establishes requirements for survey certificates, competency licenses for masters and engineers, and regulations for the carriage of passengers and dangerous goods. The Act empowers Provincial Governments to make rules, appoint surveyors, and impose penalties for non-compliance.

metadata.short_title: The Insolvency (Karachi Division) Act, 1909
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the law of Insolvency in [the Karachi Division]
metadata.one_line: Amends the law relating to insolvency proceedings specifically for the Karachi Division.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the law of insolvency applicable to the Karachi Division. It establishes the constitution and powers of courts, procedures for adjudication and discharge of insolvents, administration of property by official assignees, and rules regarding proof of debts and distribution of dividends. The Act also covers penalties for undischarged insolvents obtaining credit and provisions for small insolvencies.

metadata.short_title: The Inspection Agencies (Registration and Regulation) Ordinance, 1981
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to control and regulate the business in relation to pre-shipment inspection of goods exported out of or imported into, Pakistan.
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Federal Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, appoint
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance regulates pre-shipment inspection businesses and establishes an Authority and Council for registration.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance controls and regulates the business of pre-shipment inspection for goods exported from or imported into Pakistan. It establishes an Authority to register inspection companies and a Council to provide technical assistance. The law prohibits unregistered firms from conducting inspections and sets penalties for violations, while empowering the Federal Government to make rules and appoint officials.

name: Institute For Art and Culture Act, 2018

metadata.short_title: The Institute for Art and Culture Act, 2018
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of Institute for Art and Culture and to provide for matters connected therewith and ancillary thereto
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Institute for Art and Culture as a body corporate with academic autonomy under the Federal Government.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Institute for Art and Culture as a body corporate with perpetual succession and administrative autonomy. It defines the composition of the Institute, including the Patron, Chancellor, Senate, and Vice-Chancellor, and outlines their respective powers and functions. The Act also provides for the creation of various authorities, such as the Academic Council and Syndicate, to manage academic and administrative affairs.

name: Institute of Management, Sciences and Technology Act, 2026

metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Institute of Management, Sciences and Technology as a body corporate in the private sector. The Institute is located principally in Okara but can set up campuses elsewhere after evaluation by the Higher Education Commission. It grants the Institute academic, financial, and administrative autonomy subject to Board approval for certain activities.

name: Institute Of Science And Technology Bahawalpur Act, 2018

metadata.short_title: The Institute of Science and Technology Bahawalpur Act, 2018
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of Institute of Science and Technology, Bahawalpur as the degree awarding institute

subjects: Institute of Science and Technology Bahawalpur
establishes: Institute of Science and Technology, Bahawalpur
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Institute of Science and Technology Bahawalpur as a degree awarding institution with autonomous powers.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Institute of Science and Technology, Bahawalpur as a degree awarding institution located in Bahawalpur. It grants the Institute academic, financial, and administrative autonomy while defining its internal structure, including the Chancellor, Board of Governors, Academic Council, and various committees. The Act also provides for the making of Statutes, Regulations, and Rules to govern the Institute's operations.

metadata.short_title: The Institute of Space Technology Act, 2010
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of the Institute of Space Technology and for matters connected therewith for ancillary thereto
metadata.commencement: at once; deemed to have taken effect on the 5th day of June, 2007
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Institute of Space Technology as a degree awarding body with academic autonomy.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Institute of Space Technology in Islamabad as a degree awarding institute with perpetual succession and a common seal. It grants the Institute academic, financial, and administrative autonomy, including the power to employ staff on prescribed terms. The Act defines various authorities such as the Senate, Syndicate, and Academic Council, outlines their powers and functions, and provides for an Institute Fund subject to audits.

name: Intellectual Property Organization of Pakistan Act, 2012

metadata.short_title: The Intellectual Property Organization of Pakistan Act, 2012
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of Intellectual Property Organization of Pakistan
metadata.commencement: 2012-08-28, except sections 15 to 19 which shall come into force on such date as the Federal Government may appoint by notification
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Intellectual Property Organization of Pakistan to manage intellectual property rights comprehensively.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Intellectual Property Organization of Pakistan as an autonomous body with perpetual succession. It creates a Policy Board comprising members from the public and private sectors, as well as provincial representatives. The Act integrates various intellectual property offices and empowers the organization to advocate for IP rights, establish tribunals, and enforce laws related to trademarks, patents, and copyrights across the whole of Pakistan.

metadata.short_title: Inter-Boards Coordination Commission Act, 2023
metadata.long_title: An Act to re-constitute the Inter-Boards Committee of Chairmen as Inter-Boards Coordination Commission
repeals: Resolution No.F.l0-ll/86-CF.I dated the 30th day of June 1987
metadata.one_line: Re-constitutes the Inter-Boards Committee as the Inter-Boards Coordination Commission to standardize examinations and manage qualifications.
metadata.summary: This Act re-constitutes and re-structures the existing Inter-Boards Committee of Chairmen into the Inter-Boards Coordination Commission (IBCC). The IBCC serves as a body corporate responsible for standardizing examinations, assessing equivalence of local and foreign qualifications, and promoting curricular activities across secondary and higher secondary levels. It establishes a Board of Governors and an executive director to oversee administrative functions, while also regulating foreign examination boards operating in the country.

metadata.short_title: The Inter-Governmental Commercial Transactions Act, 2022
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for a mechanism to carry out a commercial transaction under an inter-governmental framework agreement to promote, attract and encourage foreign states to have economic and business relations with the Islamic Republic of Pakistan.
establishes: Cabinet Committee on Inter-Governmental Commercial Transactions
metadata.one_line: Provides a legal framework for commercial transactions under inter-governmental agreements with foreign states.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes a mechanism to facilitate economic and business relations between Pakistan and foreign states through inter-governmental framework agreements. It empowers the Federal Government to enter into such agreements and constitutes a Cabinet Committee to oversee negotiations, approve transactions, and recommend regulatory relaxations. The Act grants broad powers to execute commercial transactions including sales, investments, and joint ventures while providing indemnity for procedural lapses unless done in bad faith.

metadata.short_title: The Interest Act, 1839
metadata.long_title: An Act concerning the allowance of Interest in certain Cases
metadata.territorial_extent: the territories under the Government of the East India Company
key_definitions: debts or sums certain payable at a certain time
metadata.one_line: Empowers courts to allow interest on debts payable by written instrument or upon written demand.
metadata.summary: This Act extends provisions regarding the allowance of interest to territories under the Government of the East India Company. It empowers courts to allow interest to creditors on debts payable at a certain time, provided the rate does not exceed the current market rate. Interest is allowed from the date the debt was payable if based on a written instrument, or from the date of a written demand for payment otherwise. The Act includes provisions regarding its extent in various provinces and scheduled districts.

name: International Court of Justice (Review and Re-consideration) Act, 2021

metadata.short_title: The International Court of Justice (Review and Re-consideration) Act, 2021
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the right of review and re-consideration in giving effect to the judgement of the International Court of Justice
key_definitions: Secretary, Ministry of Law and Justice
metadata.one_line: Provides for review and re-consideration by High Courts regarding military court orders affecting foreign nationals under the Vienna Convention.
metadata.summary: This Act grants foreign nationals the right to seek review and re-consideration in High Courts concerning orders from military courts that affect their consular rights under the Vienna Convention. It allows petitions to be filed by the foreign national, their representative, or a consular officer within sixty days of the relevant order. The High Court examines whether denial of consular access caused prejudice to the right of defence, evidence, and fair trial principles.

metadata.short_title: The International Development Association Ordinance, 1960
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to give effect to an international agreement for the establishment and operation of an International Development Association and for purposes connected therewith.

metadata.one_line: This Ordinance gives effect to an international agreement for the International Development Association and grants it immunities.
metadata.summary: The document provides for Pakistan's participation in the International Development Association by giving force of law to specific provisions of their Agreement. It designates the State Bank of Pakistan as the depository for the Association's assets and mandates that payments be made from the Federal Consolidated Fund. The Ordinance also grants the Association, its assets, and its officers various immunities from legal process, seizure, and taxation.

metadata.short_title: The International Finance Corporation Act, 1956
metadata.long_title: An Act to give effect to an international agreement for the establishment and operation of an International Finance Corporation and for purposes connected therewith.

metadata.summary: The Act provides for Pakistan's participation in the International Finance Corporation based on an international agreement approved by the Executive Directors of the Bank. It designates the State Bank of Pakistan as the depository for the Corporation's assets and mandates that certain provisions of the Agreement have the force of law in Pakistan. The legislation outlines financial provisions regarding payments from the Federal Consolidated Fund or Revenues of the Federal Government and grants the Corporation specific immunities, privileges, and tax exemptions within Pakistani territories.

name: International Institute of Science, Arts and Technology Act, 2022

metadata.summary: This Act establishes the International Institute of Science, Arts and Technology as a body corporate with perpetual succession. It grants the Institute academic, financial, and administrative autonomy while defining its structure, including the Patron, Chancellor, Board of Governors, Syndicate, and Academic Council. The Act outlines the powers and functions of these authorities, provisions for teaching and examinations, and mechanisms for making Statutes, Regulations, and Rules.

metadata.short_title: The International Islamic University Ordinance, 1985

metadata.summary: This Ordinance was promulgated by the President to reconstitute and reorganize the existing Islamic University into an autonomous International Islamic University. It establishes the university's structure, including its officers, authorities like the Board of Governors and Academic Council, and various institutes focused on Islamic learning and research. The document repeals the previous 1980 Ordinance while saving past actions and liabilities, and it creates a trust to support the university's objectives.

name: International Monetary Fund (IMF) and Bank Act , 1950

metadata.commencement: on such date as the Federal Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, appoint

metadata.one_line: This Act implements agreements with the International Monetary Fund and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development.
metadata.summary: The Act provides for the payment of subscriptions and charges to the International Monetary Fund and the International Bank by the Federal Government. It designates the State Bank of Pakistan as the depository for currency holdings related to these international bodies. The legislation also grants specific immunities, privileges, and tax exemptions to the institutions and their officers, while empowering the government to call for necessary information.

metadata.short_title: The Investigation for Fair Trial Act, 2013
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for investigation for collection of evidence by means of modern techniques and devices to prevent and effectively deal with scheduled offences and to regulate the powers of the law enforcement and intelligence agencies and for matters connected therewith or ancillary thereto
metadata.one_line: Regulates powers of law enforcement and intelligence agencies regarding modern investigative techniques like surveillance and interception.
metadata.summary: This Act provides a legal framework for collecting evidence using modern techniques such as covert surveillance, wiretapping, and communication interception. It regulates the powers of law enforcement and intelligence agencies to prevent arbitrary use of authority while ensuring fair trial procedures. The legislation applies to all citizens within or outside Pakistan and establishes mechanisms for judicial oversight, including the issuance of warrants by High Court Judges and the maintenance of records.

metadata.short_title: The Investment Corporation of Pakistan Ordinance, 1966
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to establish an Investment Corporation in Pakistan
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Investment Corporation of Pakistan to encourage investments and develop the capital market.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Investment Corporation of Pakistan (ICP) to encourage and broaden the base of investments while developing the capital market in Pakistan. It defines the Corporation as a body corporate with perpetual succession, outlining its powers to acquire property, sue, and be sued. The document details the structure of the Board, qualifications for directors, share capital management, borrowing powers, and auditing requirements. It also grants the Federal Government authority to make rules and regulations regarding the Corporation's conduct and operations.

metadata.short_title: The Iqbal Academy Ordinance, 1962

metadata.summary: The Iqbal Academy Ordinance, 1962 repeals and modifies the Iqbal Academy Act, 1951 to bring greater efficiency to the Academy's administration. It establishes the Iqbal Academy as a body corporate with perpetual succession, defining its composition, aims, and objects which include promoting the study of Iqbal's works and publishing related materials. The Ordinance outlines the structure of the Governing Body and Executive Committee, details funding sources including government grants, and sets out provisions for staff appointment, audit, and penalties for unauthorized use of the Academy's name.

metadata.short_title: The Islamabad (Preservation of Landscape) Ordinance, 1966
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the preservation of landscape in Islamabad

metadata.summary: This Ordinance provides for the preservation of landscape within the Islamabad Capital Territory. It prohibits any person from removing, destroying, damaging, or altering anything that affects a landscape, except with permission from the Authority. The law establishes penalties including imprisonment up to six months or fines up to five thousand rupees, and grants specific powers to officers of the Authority for enforcement, evidence collection, and requisitioning police assistance.

name: Islamabad Capital Territory (Prohibition of Plastic Book Covers) Act, 2026

metadata.short_title: The Islamabad Capital Territory (Prohibition of Plastic Book Covers) Act, 2026

metadata.summary: This Act prohibits sellers from distributing books encased in single-use plastic covers within the Islamabad Capital Territory to safeguard the environment. It provides exemptions for biodegradable materials, reusable covers, archival items, and integral book components. Sellers found guilty of violations face fines up to fifty thousand rupees for a first offence and one hundred thousand rupees for subsequent offences.

name: Islamabad Capital Territory Agricultural Produce Markets Ordinance, 2002

metadata.summary: This Ordinance regulates the purchase and sale of agricultural products within the Islamabad Capital Territory. The document defines various terms related to agriculture and dealers, outlines the constitution and duties of these committees, and provides powers to make rules and bye-laws governing trade conditions.

name: Islamabad Capital Territory Charities Registration, regulation and Facilitation Act, 2021

The legislation also empowers the authority to impose administrative fines for vexatious complaints and repeals the previous Ordinance regarding voluntary social welfare agencies in this territory.

name: Islamabad Capital Territory Child Marriage Restraint Act, 2025

It establishes strict penalties for adults marrying children, parents facilitating such unions, and acts of child abuse or trafficking related to marriage. The Act also empowers courts to issue injunctions to prevent impending child marriages and mandates the registration of valid marriages with verified identity documents.

name: Islamabad Capital Territory Child Protection Act, 2018

metadata.summary: The Islamabad Capital Territory Child Protection Act, 2018 establishes a legal framework to protect children from violence, neglect, and exploitation within the Islamabad Capital Territory. It creates the Child Protection Advisory Board and various institutions responsible for assessing child needs and creating care plans. The Act defines specific terms regarding child abuse and exploitation, restricts parental custody in risk situations, and sets up a fund for child care purposes.

name: Islamabad Capital Territory Domestic Workers Act, 2022

metadata.summary: This Act regulates the employment of domestic workers within the Islamabad Capital Territory to safeguard their safety and dignity. It establishes specific rights including minimum wages, maternity benefits, leave, and accommodation, while strictly prohibiting child labour under sixteen years of age. The legislation creates a Governing Body and Dispute Resolution Committees to handle conflicts between employers and workers, and outlines penalties for violations such as employing children or failing to pay minimum wages.

name: Islamabad Capital Territory Food Safety Act, 2021

The Act prescribes offences for selling unsafe or substandard food, failing to comply with regulations, and obstructing officers, along with corresponding penalties and compensation mechanisms.

name: Islamabad Capital Territory Local Government (Amendment) Ordinance, 2026

name: Islamabad Capital Territory Local Government Act, 2015

metadata.territorial_extent: the Islamabad Capital Territory except any area excluded by the Government, by notification

name: Islamabad Capital Territory Private Education Institution (Registration and Regulation) Act, 2013

name: Islamabad Capital Territory Prohibition of Corporal Punishment Act, 2021

name: Islamabad Capital Territory Prohibition of Interest of Private Loans Act, 2023

name: Islamabad Capital Territory Senior Citizens Act, 2021

metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes a legal framework to ensure the security of property and persons within shops, business, and industrial establishments in the Islamabad Capital Territory. It empowers the Federal Government to issue orders regulating security measures and defines various types of establishments, including banks and offices. The document prescribes penalties for contravening these orders, including imprisonment or fines.

metadata.short_title: The Islamabad Capital Territory Trust Act, 2020
metadata.long_title: An Act to define and amend the law relating to trusts
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Islamabad Capital Territory
repeals: The Trust Act, 1882 (II of 1882)
metadata.administering_body: Chief Commissioner of Islamabad Capital Territory
metadata.one_line: Defines and amends law relating to trusts within Islamabad Capital Territory, repealing the Trust Act, 1882.
metadata.summary: This Act defines and amends the law relating to trusts registered within the territorial limits of the Islamabad Capital Territory. It addresses the need for effective administration and financial monitoring that the previous Trust Act, 1882 did not provide. The legislation outlines the creation, registration, administration, duties, liabilities, and rights of trustees and beneficiaries, while also establishing rules regarding the extinction of trusts and obligations in their nature.

name: Islamabad Capital Territory Waqf Properties Act, 2020

metadata.short_title: The Islamabad Capital Territory Waqf Properties Act, 2020
metadata.long_title: An Act for proper management and administration of waqf properties
repeals: The Auqaf (Federal Control) Act, 1976
metadata.max_penalty: twenty-five million rupees
metadata.one_line: This Act establishes the framework for managing waqf properties in Islamabad and repeals the Auqaf (Federal Control) Act, 1976.
metadata.summary: The Islamabad Capital Territory Waqf Properties Act, 2020 provides for the proper management, supervision, and administration of waqf properties within the territorial limits of the Islamabad Capital Territory. It establishes a Chief Administrator of Auqaf appointed by the Chief Commissioner, along with deputy administrators and managers to handle day-to-day operations. The Act outlines procedures for registration, leasing, eviction of wrongfully possessed persons, and financial reporting, while repealing the previous Auqaf (Federal Control) Act, 1976.

metadata.short_title: The Islamabad Club (Administration) Ordinance, 1978
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the proper administration of the affairs of the Islamabad Club.
metadata.commencement: on such day as the Federal Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, appoint
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance provides for the administration of the Islamabad Club by an Administrator and Managing Committee appointed by the Federal Government.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance was promulgated to ensure the proper administration of the Islamabad Club, which serves officers of the Federal Government and diplomatic corps. It establishes an Administrator appointed by the Federal Government and a Managing Committee comprising service members, club members, and a diplomatic representative. Upon commencement, the original company is dissolved, and all its assets, liabilities, and functions vest in the Administrator.

metadata.short_title: Islamabad Consumers Protection Act, 1995
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for promotion and protection of the interest of consumers
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment up to two years or fine up to forty thousand rupees or both
metadata.one_line: This Act promotes and protects consumer interests in Islamabad by establishing a Council, defining unfair practices, and setting penalties.
metadata.summary: The Islamabad Consumers Protection Act, 1995 establishes the Consumers' Protection Council and an Authority (Court of Sessions) to protect consumer rights within the Islamabad Capital Territory. It defines key terms such as 'consumer' and 'unfair trade practice,' prohibiting false advertisements and misleading representations. The Act outlines procedures for complaints, powers for special magistrates to try cases summarily, penalties for infringements including imprisonment and fines, and provisions for compensation and confiscation of goods.

name: Islamabad Healthcare Regulation Act, 2018 (Act No_ XXIII of 2018)

metadata.short_title: The Islamabad Healthcare Regulation Act, 2018
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for establishment of the Islamabad Healthcare Regulatory Authority
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Islamabad Capital Territory
metadata.max_penalty: ten hundred thousand Rupees
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Islamabad Healthcare Regulatory Authority to regulate healthcare services, licensing, and quality standards in Islamabad.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Islamabad Healthcare Regulatory Authority to ensure quality healthcare services for residents of the Islamabad Capital Territory. It creates a Board and Registration Board to oversee licensing, set standards, conduct inspections, and collect fees from healthcare establishments. The legislation also defines various medical terms, outlines penalties for non-compliance, and grants overriding effect to its provisions over inconsistent laws.

metadata.short_title: The Islamabad High Court Act, 2010
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for establishment of a High Court for Islamabad Capital Territory
amends: Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898 (Act V of 1898)
Province of West Pakistan (Dissolution) Order, 1970 (P.O.1 of 1970)
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Islamabad High Court for the Islamabad Capital Territory and adapts existing laws.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes a High Court for the Islamabad Capital Territory in pursuance of Article 175 of the Constitution. It defines the composition of the court, its jurisdiction over the territory, and the transfer of pending proceedings from the Lahore High Court. The Act also provides for the adaptation of existing laws regarding practice, procedure, and subordinate judiciary to apply mutatis mutandis to the new court.

name: Islamabad Nature Conservation and Wildlife Management Act, 2024

metadata.short_title: The Islamabad Nature Conservation and Wildlife Management Act, 2024
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the protection, preservation, conservation, and management of Nature in the Islamabad Capital Territory
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of Islamabad Capital Territory
repeals: The Islamabad Wildlife (Protection, Preservation, Conservation and Management) Ordinance (LXX of 1979)
establishes: Nature Conservation and Wildlife Management Board
metadata.administering_body: Ministry of Climate Change and Environmental Coordination
metadata.one_line: This Act protects, preserves, conserves, and manages nature in the Islamabad Capital Territory by establishing a Board and setting penalties.
metadata.summary: The Islamabad Nature Conservation and Wildlife Management Act, 2024 establishes a framework for the protection and management of nature within the Islamabad Capital Territory. It creates a dedicated Board to oversee conservation efforts and defines various protected species and areas. The Act repeals the previous 1979 Ordinance and imposes significant penalties for offences related to wildlife hunting, trading, and habitat destruction.

name: Islamabad Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act, 2020.

metadata.short_title: The Islamabad Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act, 2020
metadata.long_title: An Act to establish the Real Estate Regulatory Authority for regulation and promotion of the real estate sector and for matters connected therewith
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Real Estate Regulatory Authority and Appellate Tribunal to regulate the real estate sector in Islamabad.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Real Estate Regulatory Authority (RERA) and the Real Estate Appellate Tribunal to regulate and promote the real estate sector. It mandates the registration of real estate projects and developers, defines the functions of agents and allottees, and provides mechanisms for dispute resolution. The Act also outlines penalties for non-compliance and grants powers to the Federal Government to supersede the Authority if necessary.

name: Islamabad Real Estate Agents and Motor Vehicles Dealers (Regulation of Business) Ordinance, 1984

metadata.short_title: The Islamabad Real Estate Agents and Motor Vehicles Dealers (Regulation of Business) Ordinance, 1984
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to regulate the business of real estate agents and motor vehicles dealers in the Islamabad Capital Territory.
metadata.max_penalty: six months imprisonment or fine up to five thousand rupees or both
metadata.administering_body: District Excise and Taxation Officer, Islamabad or any other officer authorised by the Federal Government
metadata.one_line: Regulates business of real estate agents and motor vehicle dealers in Islamabad requiring registration.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance regulates the business of real estate agents and motor vehicles dealers within the Islamabad Capital Territory. It mandates that no person shall engage in this business without registering with the designated authority and holding a valid certificate. The document establishes procedures for initial registration, renewal, fixation of commission rates, and imposes penalties for operating without registration or breaching conditions.

metadata.short_title: The Islamabad Rent Restriction Ordinance, 2001
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to regulate the relations between the landlords and tenants of rented premises in the Islamabad Capital Territory
metadata.territorial_extent: such urban area of Islamabad Capital Territory as the Federal Government may specify
repeals: The West Pakistan Urban Rent Restriction Ordinance, 1959 (W.P. Ord.VI of 1959), to the extent of the Islamabad Capital Territory
metadata.max_penalty: fine which may extend to five thousand rupees; compensation not less than five thousand rupees or more than ten thousand rupees for abuse of process
metadata.one_line: Regulates landlord-tenant relations in Islamabad, defines fair rent, and establishes a Mediation Council.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance regulates the relationship between landlords and tenants of rented premises within specified urban areas of the Islamabad Capital Territory. It establishes a Controller of Rents to determine fair rent and creates a Mediation Council for dispute resolution. The law sets rules for tenancy agreements, rent increases, eviction procedures, and penalties for contravention, while repealing the West Pakistan Urban Rent Restriction Ordinance, 1959 to the extent it applies to Islamabad.

name: Islamabad Subordinate Judiciary Service Tribunal Act, 2016

metadata.short_title: the Islamabad Subordinate Judiciary Service Tribunal Act, 2016
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of the Islamabad Subordinate Judiciary Service Tribunal and for matters connected therewith or ancillary thereto
metadata.one_line: Establishes a tribunal for the subordinate judiciary of Islamabad to handle service terms, conditions, and disciplinary matters.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Islamabad Subordinate Judiciary Service Tribunal to adjudicate matters regarding the terms and conditions of service for members of the subordinate judiciary under the administrative control of the Islamabad High Court. The Tribunal has exclusive jurisdiction over these issues, including disciplinary matters, and consists of judges nominated by the Chief Justice of the Islamabad High Court. It provides mechanisms for appeals against departmental orders, reviews of final orders, and defines the powers of the Tribunal to function as a civil court.

name: Islamabad Transfusion of Safe Blood Ordinance, 2002

metadata.short_title: Islamabad Transfusion of Safe Blood Ordinance, 2002
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to regulate transfusion of safe blood and blood products in the Islamabad Capital Territory and to provide for matters connected therewith and incidental thereto.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Islamabad Capital Territory
metadata.one_line: Regulates safe blood transfusion, establishes an Authority, and sets bio-safety standards for blood banks in Islamabad.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance regulates the transfusion of safe and healthy blood products free from viruses and infective agents within the Islamabad Capital Territory. It establishes the Islamabad Blood Transfusion Authority to register blood banks, issue licenses, and ensure adherence to national safety standards. The document defines 'safe blood' as being free from HIV, Hepatitis B and C, malaria, and syphilis, while prescribing strict bio-safety measures for laboratories.

name: Islamabad University of Health Sciences and Emerging Technologies, Islamabad Act, 2024

metadata.short_title: The Islamabad University of Health Sciences and Emerging Technologies, Islamabad Act, 2024
metadata.long_title: An Act for the establishment of Islamabad University of Health Sciences and Emerging Technologies
establishes: Islamabad University of Health Sciences and Emerging Technologies (IUHT)
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Islamabad University of Health Sciences and Emerging Technologies with full autonomy in Islamabad.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Islamabad University of Health Sciences and Emerging Technologies (IUHT) as a body corporate within the Islamabad Capital Territory. It grants the university academic, financial, and administrative autonomy while requiring compliance with constitutional provisions. The Act defines the structure of the Board of Governors, Academic Council, and various committees responsible for finance, discipline, and planning.

name: Islamabad Wildlife (Protection, Preservation, Conservation and Management) Ordinance, 1979 (Repealed by Act no. XVI of 2024 section 41 (w.e.f 27-08-2024))

metadata.short_title: The Islamabad Wildlife (Protection, Preservation, Conservation and Management) Ordinance, 1979
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the protection, preservation, conservation and management of wildlife and setting up of a National Park in the Islamabad Capital Territory.
metadata.status_evidence: [Repealed by Act no. XVI of 2024 section 41 (w.e.f 27-08-2024)]
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance protects wildlife in Islamabad, establishes a National Park, and regulates hunting and trade.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance was promulgated to protect, preserve, conserve, and manage wildlife within the Islamabad Capital Territory. It establishes a Wildlife Management Board and designates areas as National Parks, Sanctuaries, and Game Reserves. The law prohibits hunting and capturing of wild animals without authorization, restricts specific hunting methods and weapons, and regulates the import, export, and trade of wild animals and trophies.

name: Islambad Capital Territory Local Government Elections Ordinance, 2002

metadata.short_title: The Islamabad Capital Territory Local Government Elections (Amendment) Ordinance, 2002
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Islamabad Capital Territory Local Government Elections Ordinance, 2002.
amends: The Islamabad Capital Territory Local Government Elections Ordinance, 2002
metadata.one_line: Amends the 2002 Elections Ordinance to update candidate qualifications and election dates.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Islamabad Capital Territory Local Government Elections Ordinance, 2002. It substitutes a clause requiring candidates for Nazim or Naib Nazim positions to hold at least a bachelor's degree. Additionally, it changes the figure '2004' to '2005' in section 18 regarding election timelines. The Ordinance was promulgated by the President under emergency powers on October 2, 2002.

metadata.short_title: The Islamic Development Bank Ordinance, 1978
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to implement the international agreement for the establishment and operation of the Islamic Development Bank and for matters connected therewith.
metadata.commencement: at once and deemed to have taken effect on the twenty-third day of April, 1975
establishes: Islamic Development Bank (as an international institution in Pakistan)
metadata.one_line: Implements the international agreement for the Islamic Development Bank and grants it immunities in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance implements the international agreement establishing the Islamic Development Bank (IDB) and outlines Pakistan's obligations as a member. It designates the State Bank of Pakistan as the depository for the Bank's assets and grants the IDB specific legal status, immunities, exemptions from taxation, and privileges regarding its personnel and communications. The Federal Government is empowered to make rules and amend the schedule conforming to changes in the international agreement.

name: Jammu and Kashmir (Administration of property) Ordinance, 1961

metadata.short_title: The Jammu and Kashmir (Administration of Property) Ordinance, 1961
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to vest in the Central Government certain immovable properties which vested in the State of Jammu and Kashmir on the fifteenth day of August, 1947, and to provide for matters connected therewith.
establishes: Administrator of State Properties of Jammu and Kashmir
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance vests Jammu and Kashmir properties in the Federal Government and establishes an Administrator to manage them.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance was promulgated by the President to vest immovable properties located in Pakistan, which previously belonged to the State of Jammu and Kashmir, into the ownership of the Federal Government. It empowers the Federal Government to manage, sell, or lease these properties and establishes an Administrator with specific powers to take possession, evict unauthorized occupants, and handle disputes. The Ordinance also provides for the constitution of a Management Committee to advise the government and outlines procedures for appeals and revisions regarding administrative orders.

metadata.short_title: The Judicial Officers' Protection Act, 1850
metadata.long_title: An Act for the protection of Judicial Officers
metadata.territorial_extent: all the Provinces and the Capital of the Federation except the Scheduled Districts; Baluchistan; specific Scheduled Districts (Sind, Hazara, Peshawar, Kohat, Bannu, Dera Ismail Khan, Dera Ghazi Khan) with exceptions
metadata.one_line: Protects judicial officers from civil suits for acts done in good faith while discharging judicial duties.
metadata.summary: This Act provides protection to Judges, Magistrates, Justices of the Peace, Collectors, and other persons acting judicially against civil liability. It states that such officers shall not be sued in any Civil Court for acts done or ordered in the discharge of their judicial duty if done in good faith and with a belief in their jurisdiction. The Act also protects officers executing lawful warrants or orders issued by these judicial officers.

metadata.short_title: The Jute (Repeal) Ordinance, 1983
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to repeal the Jute Ordinance, 1962.
repeals: The Jute Ordinance, 1962 (LXXIV of 1962)
metadata.status_evidence: An Ordinance to repeal the Jute Ordinance, 1962.
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance repeals the Jute Ordinance, 1962 effective immediately.
metadata.summary: The Jute (Repeal) Ordinance, 1983 was promulgated by the President to repeal the existing Jute Ordinance, 1962. It came into force immediately upon promulgation on December 22, 1983. The document serves solely to remove the earlier legislation from the statute book.

metadata.short_title: The Juvenile Justice System Act, 2018
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for criminal justice system for juveniles
repeals: The Juvenile Justice System Ordinance, 2000 (XXII of 2000)
metadata.one_line: Establishes a criminal justice system for juveniles including courts, committees, and rehabilitation centers.
metadata.summary: This Act provides a comprehensive criminal justice system specifically designed for juveniles in Pakistan. It establishes Juvenile Courts and Juvenile Justice Committees to handle cases involving children under eighteen years of age. The legislation outlines procedures for arrest, bail, investigation, and trial, emphasizing diversion processes and social reintegration over formal judicial proceedings where possible. It also sets standards for observation homes and rehabilitation centers, ensuring legal assistance is provided at state expense.

name: Kalam Bibi International Women Institute Bannu Act, 2023

metadata.short_title: The Kalam Bibi International Women Institute Bannu Act, 2023
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of the Kalam Bibi International Women Institute Bannu
establishes: Kalam Bibi International Women Institute Bannu
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Kalam Bibi International Women Institute Bannu by upgrading the Women Campus of University of Bannu.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Kalam Bibi International Women Institute Bannu as a body corporate by reconstituting the existing Women Campus of the University of Bannu. It defines the institute's structure, including its authorities such as the Senate and Syndicate, and outlines their powers and functions. The legislation also provides for the transfer of employees and properties from the former campus to the new institute, along with legal indemnity for officials acting in good faith.

name: Karachi Electric Supply Corporation (Removal from Service) Ordinance, 1999

metadata.short_title: The Karachi Electric Supply Corporation (Removal from Service) Ordinance, 1999
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for removal from service of the Karachi Electric Supply Corporation
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance empowers the Karachi Electric Supply Corporation to retire or remove employees from service without assigning reasons.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance provides for the removal of persons from the service of the Karachi Electric Supply Corporation. It allows the Corporation to retire any employee without assigning a reason or to remove an employee after giving them notice and an opportunity to show cause. Additionally, it mandates that retired employees receive additional pay for three months beyond their standard retiring benefits.

metadata.short_title: The Karachi Electricity Control Act, 1952
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the continuance of powers to control the production, distribution, use and consumption of electrical energy.
metadata.commencement: immediately on the expiry of the Sind Electricity Control Act, 1947
repeals: Sind Electricity Control Act, 1947 (Sind Act III of 1947)
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months or with fine or with both
metadata.one_line: This Act continues powers to control electrical energy production and distribution in Karachi Division, repealing the 1947 Act.
metadata.summary: The Karachi Electricity Control Act, 1952 provides for the continuance of powers to control the production, distribution, use, and consumption of electrical energy in the Karachi Division. It allows the Provincial Government to regulate rates, levy surcharges, and issue licenses or permits through orders. The Act also establishes penalties for contravention of such orders and repeals the Sind Electricity Control Act, 1947 within the Capital of the Federation.

name: Karachi Essential Articles (Price Control and Antl-Hoarding) Act, 1953

metadata.short_title: The Karachi Essential Articles (Price Control and Anti-Hoarding) Act, 1953
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for regulating the possession, distribution, sale and prices of certain essential articles in the [Karachi Division].
repeals: The Karachi Essential Articles (Price Control and Anti-Hoarding) Ordinance, 1953
metadata.max_penalty: deemed to have committed the offence of hoarding or dealing in the black market under section 3 of the Hoarding and Black Market Act, 1948
metadata.one_line: Regulates possession, distribution, sale, and prices of essential articles in Karachi to prevent hoarding.
metadata.summary: This Act regulates the possession, distribution, sale, and pricing of specific essential articles within the Karachi Division. It empowers the Commissioner to fix maximum prices, require price marking, control quantities possessed by traders, and issue trading licenses. The legislation prohibits sales above fixed prices and establishes penalties for contraventions, which are treated as offences under the Hoarding and Black Market Act, 1948.

metadata.short_title: The Karachi Hotels and Lodging-houses (Control) Act, 1950
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for special measures for control of rates chargeable in hotels and lodging-houses in Karachi, for the reservation of accommodation therein and for ancillary matters.
metadata.one_line: This Act controls rates and accommodation in Karachi hotels, appoints controllers, and sets penalties for violations.
metadata.summary: The Karachi Hotels and Lodging-houses (Control) Act, 1950 establishes a regulatory framework specifically for hotels and lodging-houses in the Karachi Division. It empowers the Provincial Government to appoint Controllers who are responsible for registering establishments, classifying them by standard, and fixing fair rates for board, lodging, and services. The Act also mandates the reservation of accommodation at the Controller's instance and outlines penalties for charging excessive rates or failing to comply with registration and display requirements.

metadata.short_title: The Karachi Port Security Force Ordinance, 2002
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the constitution and regulation of the Karachi Port Security Force
metadata.territorial_extent: the Ports limits of Karachi Port
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance establishes the Karachi Port Security Force to maintain law and order, safety, and investigate offences within Karachi Port limits.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance provides for the constitution, regulation, and administration of the Karachi Port Security Force. It defines the force's functions, which include maintaining law and order, regulating access to the port area, preventing pollution and hazards, and investigating offences connected with port affairs. The document also outlines the appointment of officers, specific offences punishable under the Ordinance, and the jurisdiction of appointed Magistrates.

metadata.short_title: The Karachi Port Trust Act, 1886
metadata.long_title: An Act to constitute a Board of Trustees for the Port of Karachi and to define their powers and duties.
establishes: Board of Trustees for the Port of Karachi
metadata.one_line: Constitutes a Board of Trustees for the Port of Karachi and defines their powers regarding property, works, tolls, and borrowing.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes a Board of Trustees to manage the Port of Karachi. It outlines the constitution, duties, and disqualifications of trustees, as well as the Board's powers over property, wharves, and shipping. The legislation also covers financial matters including borrowing powers, sinking funds, and the collection of tolls and charges.

metadata.short_title: The Karachi Rent Restriction Act, 1953
metadata.long_title: An Act to make certain provisions regarding accommodation, whether residential or non-residential furnished or unfurnished, in the Karachi Division.
repeals: The Sind Rent Restriction Act, 1947 (Sind Act X of 1947)
The Sind Rent Restriction (Amendment) Act, 1952 (XXXVII of 1952)
The Karachi Rent Restriction Ordinance, 1953 (Ord I of 1953)
metadata.one_line: This Act regulates accommodation in Karachi Division by fixing fair rents and restricting tenant eviction.
metadata.summary: The Karachi Rent Restriction Act, 1953 provides provisions regarding residential and non-residential accommodation in the Karachi Division. It establishes a Rent Controller to fix fair rents based on historical rates or construction costs and restricts rent increases and evictions. The Act defines terms such as 'fair rent' and 'landlord', outlines procedures for applications, and repeals previous enactments applicable to the Capital of the Federation.

metadata.short_title: The Kazis Act, 1880
metadata.long_title: An Act for the appointment of persons to the office of Kazi
repeals: Act No. XI of 1864
metadata.status_evidence: This Act has been repealed to the extent of Islamabad Capital Territory see Ordinance No. 27 of 1981, s. 4 and 3rd Sch.
metadata.one_line: Empowers Provincial Governments to appoint Kazis for local areas and defines their limited non-judicial role.
metadata.summary: This Act empowers the Provincial Government to appoint persons to the office of Kazi in any local area where Muslims desire such appointments. It clarifies that these appointments do not confer judicial or administrative powers nor make the presence of a Kazi mandatory for marriage ceremonies. The Act also provides mechanisms for suspending or removing Kazis and their deputies, and allows the government to extend the Act's application via notification.

name: King Hamad University of Nursing and Associated Medical Sciences Act, 2025

metadata.short_title: The King Hamad University of Nursing and Associated Medical Sciences Act, 2025
metadata.long_title: An Act to establish the King Hamad University of Nursing and Associated Medical Sciences
establishes: King Hamad University of Nursing and Associated Medical Sciences
metadata.one_line: Establishes the King Hamad University of Nursing and Associated Medical Sciences with defined authorities and functions.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the King Hamad University of Nursing and Associated Medical Sciences to enhance higher education in nursing and associated medical sciences. It defines the university's purposes, powers, and structure, including its Senate, Syndicate, and Academic Council. The legislation also outlines provisions for affiliating institutions, managing the university fund, and regulating internal committees for finance and discipline.

metadata.short_title: The Korangi Fisheries Harbour Authority Ordinance, 1982
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the establishment of Korangi Fisheries Hourbour Authority.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Korangi Fisheries Harbour
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Korangi Fisheries Harbour Authority to manage and maintain the harbour within Port Qasim limits.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Korangi Fisheries Harbour Authority as a body corporate to plan, construct, operate, and maintain the Korangi Fisheries Harbour. The Authority is managed by a Board consisting of members appointed by the Federal Government and representing the Government of Sindh. It grants powers for fisheries resource exploitation, financial management, and imposes penalties for offences related to rates and property damage.

metadata.short_title: The Lac Cess Act, 1930
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the levy and collection of a cess on lac and refuse lac exported from Pakistan.
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Federal Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, appoint
repeals: The Repealing Act 1938 (I of 1938)
metadata.one_line: This Act provides for the levy and collection of a cess on lac and refuse lac exported from Pakistan.
metadata.summary: The Lac Cess Act, 1930 establishes a customs duty known as 'lac cess' on all lac and refuse lac exported from Pakistan. The cess is levied at specific rates per maund or such other rate as the Federal Government may prescribe by notification. The Act empowers the Federal Government to make rules for carrying out its purposes, which must be published in the official Gazette.

metadata.short_title: The Land Acquisition (Mines) Act, 1885
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for cases in which Mines or Minerals are situate under land which it is desired to acquire under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole or any specified part of the territory under its administration
repeals: The Land Acquisition (Mines) Act, 1885
metadata.status_evidence: [Repealed. Rep. by the Repealing and Amending Act, 1937 (XX of 1937), s. 3 and Schedule II.]
metadata.one_line: Provides for the acquisition of land containing mines and regulates mining operations on acquired land.
metadata.summary: This Act addresses cases where mines or minerals are located under land intended for acquisition. It allows the Provincial Government to declare that specific mines are not needed, thereby preventing their vesting in the government while acquiring the surface land.
