The legislation outlines procedures for giving notice before working mines, inspecting mine operations, and paying compensation for injuries to mines or restrictions on mining activities. It also defines terms like 'local authority' and 'Company' and stipulates that the Act applies alongside the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.

metadata.short_title: The Land Acquisition Act, 1894
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the law for the acquisition of land for public purposes and for Companies.
repeals: section 2 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894
metadata.one_line: Amends the law for acquiring land for public purposes and companies, defining procedures for compensation and possession.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the legal framework for acquiring land needed for public purposes and for companies. It establishes procedures for preliminary investigations, declarations of necessity, and the determination of compensation by Collectors or Courts. The Act grants powers to Provincial Governments and officers to take possession of land, handle objections, and make rules for enforcement.

metadata.short_title: The Land Control (Karachi Division) Act, 1952
metadata.long_title: An Act to make provision for the prevention of unauthorised occupation of certain lands in the Karachi Division and unauthorised building thereon, and for eviction therefrom
repeals: The Land Control (Capital of the Federation) Ordinance, 1952
metadata.one_line: Prevents unauthorised occupation and building in Karachi Division, grants permissions, and enables eviction.
metadata.summary: This Act provides for the prevention of unauthorised occupation of lands and unauthorised building within the Karachi Division. It empowers an Authorised Officer to grant or refuse permission for construction, remove unauthorised buildings, and evict occupiers. The Act also establishes penalties for offences, defines key terms like 'controlled area' and 'unauthorised building', and repeals a previous Ordinance.

metadata.short_title: The Land Improvement Loans Act, 1883
metadata.long_title: An Act to consolidate and amend the law relating to loans of money by the Government for agricultural improvements.
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Provincial Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, appoint
repeals: The Land Improvement Act, 1871
Act XXI of 1876
metadata.one_line: Consolidates and amends laws regarding government loans for agricultural improvements like irrigation and drainage.
metadata.summary: This Act consolidates and amends the law relating to government loans for agricultural improvements. It defines 'Collector' and specifies that loans can be granted for works adding to land value, such as wells, tanks, drainage, or reclamation. The Act outlines procedures for loan applications, repayment periods, and exemptions from stamp duty and land revenue assessment increases.

metadata.short_title: The Land Reforms Act, 1977
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for further land reforms
metadata.max_penalty: rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to seven years or with forfeiture of his immovable property or with both
metadata.one_line: This Act establishes limits on land ownership and possession to ensure equitable distribution of wealth across Pakistan.
metadata.summary: The Land Reforms Act, 1977 provides for further land reforms by restricting individual land holdings to specific acreage limits based on irrigation status. It outlines procedures for obtaining declarations, vesting excess land in the Government, and compensating owners or tenants for surrendered lands. The Act also establishes Federal and Provincial Land Commissions with powers to review cases and set up organizations, while defining offences related to non-compliance with its provisions.

name: Land Reforms Regulation (Validation of Orders) Ordinance, 1978

metadata.short_title: The Land Reforms Regulation (Validation of Orders) Ordinance, 1978
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to validate certain orders passed by the Chairman or a Member of the Federal Land Commission
metadata.one_line: Validates orders passed by the Federal Land Commission before this Ordinance commenced.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance validates certain orders previously passed by the Chairman or a Member of the Federal Land Commission. It applies to all such orders issued before the commencement of this law that were purportedly made under the authority conferred by paragraph 29 of the Land Reforms Regulation, 1972. The validation is deemed to have always been in effect, notwithstanding any contrary court order or decision.

metadata.short_title: The Lansdowne Bridge Act, 1892
metadata.long_title: An Act to remove doubts as to the levy and collection of tolls upon the Lansdowne Bridge over the Indus at Sukkur in Sind, and for other purposes.
metadata.one_line: Removes doubts about levying tolls on the Lansdowne Bridge over the Indus at Sukkur.
metadata.summary: This Act clarifies the authority to levy and collect tolls on the Lansdowne Bridge, which was built and repaired by the Federal Government. It validates past toll collections made under previous repealed acts and extends these provisions to other public roads or bridges funded by the Federal or Provincial Governments that lack adequate alternative toll arrangements.

name: Law and Justice Commission of Pakistan Ordinance, 1979

metadata.short_title: The Law and Justice Commission of Pakistan Ordinance, 1979
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to establish a Law and Justice Commission of Pakistan for a systematic development and reform of the laws and to provide for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto
establishes: Law and Justice Commission of Pakistan
metadata.administering_body: Law and Justice Commission of Pakistan
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Law and Justice Commission of Pakistan to reform laws, improve court administration, and promote access to justice.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Law and Justice Commission of Pakistan with the Chief Justice of Pakistan as its Chairman. The Commission is tasked with studying existing statutes, recommending reforms for modernization, codifying laws, and removing anomalies or obsolete provisions. It also functions to improve legal education, coordinate between the judiciary and executive, and manage a specific fund for access to justice initiatives.

metadata.short_title: The Law Commission Ordinance, 1979
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to establish a [Law and Justice Commission of Pakistan] for a systematic development and reform of the laws and to provide for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto
establishes: Law and Justice Commission of Pakistan
metadata.administering_body: Federal Government (via Ministry of Law, Justice and Human Rights)
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Law and Justice Commission of Pakistan to reform laws, improve administration of justice, and codify statutes.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Law and Justice Commission of Pakistan with a composition including the Chief Justice of Pakistan and other judicial officers. The Commission is tasked with studying existing laws, recommending reforms for modernization, simplifying procedures, and ensuring access to justice. It also manages a specific fund for legal aid and human rights activities while having the power to make rules and constitute committees.

metadata.short_title: The Law Reforms Ordinance, 1972
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend certain laws for the purpose of giving effect to certain recommendations of the Law Reforms Commission, 1967—70 and to achieve uniformity in national interest.
amends: Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898 (Act V of 1898)
metadata.one_line: Amends various laws including the Code of Criminal Procedure to implement Law Reforms Commission recommendations.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends certain existing Acts and Ordinances to give effect to recommendations made by the Law Reforms Commission between 1967 and 1970. It establishes new rights of appeal to High Courts in specific civil cases and modifies the computation of limitation periods for such appeals. The document also updates provisions regarding the powers of various classes of Magistrates under the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898.

metadata.short_title: The Law Reports Act, 1875
metadata.long_title: An Act for the improvement of Law Reports.
metadata.commencement: on such day as the Federal Government notifies in this behalf in the official Gazette
repeals: Act II of 1875
metadata.max_penalty: fine which may extend to one lac rupees or in default of payment of fine with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months
metadata.one_line: This Act regulates the publication of law reports and certifies judicial decisions for authority.
metadata.summary: The Law Reports Act, 1875 was enacted to improve the quality and authority of published law reports in Pakistan. It restricts courts from treating unauthorized reports as binding authority and requires specific certifications for judgments based on principles of law or first impressions. The Act also imposes penalties for publishing unapproved judgments and defines the jurisdiction for trying related offences.

metadata.short_title: The Laws Local Extent Act, 1874
metadata.long_title: An Act for declaring the local extent of certain Enactments, and for other purposes
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of Pakistan, except the Scheduled Districts
repeals: Repealing Act, 1876 (XII of 1876)
metadata.one_line: Declares the local extent of certain Acts passed by the Governor General and defines Scheduled Districts.
metadata.summary: This Act declares the local extent of specific enactments passed by the Governor General of India. It states that acts listed in the First Schedule are in force throughout Pakistan, excluding Scheduled Districts. The Act also preserves the power of Federal and Provincial Governments to extend these acts and includes provisions for savings regarding repealed or omitted sections.

metadata.short_title: The Lawyers Welfare and Protection Act, 2023
metadata.long_title: An Act to make provision and make laws in respect of welfare and protection of advocates
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to five years or fine which may extend to two hundred thousand rupees or with both
metadata.one_line: This Act provides welfare and protection for advocates, defines offences against them, and mandates specific facilities.
metadata.summary: The Lawyers Welfare and Protection Act, 2023 establishes a legal framework to protect advocates from violence and harassment. It defines various acts of violence, including coercion and assault, and prescribes severe penalties including imprisonment up to five years for repeat offenders. The Act also mandates welfare measures such as legal advisory roles for large entities, health facilities equivalent to gazetted officers, financial support from institutions, and a specific package for families of advocates killed in terrorism-related incidents.

name: Legal Aid and Justice Authority Act, 2020

metadata.short_title: The Legal Aid and Justice Authority Act, 2020
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of a Legal Aid and Justice Authority
metadata.commencement: on such date or dates as the Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, appoint
repeals: The Women in Distress and Detention Fund Act, 1996 (XV of 1996)
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Legal Aid and Justice Authority to provide legal and financial assistance for access to justice in criminal cases.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Legal Aid and Justice Authority to provide legal, financial, and other assistance for access to justice to poor and vulnerable segments of society in criminal cases. The Authority is managed by a Board of Governors comprising federal ministers, legislators, and officials from various ministries. It creates a panel of advocates and volunteers to offer pro bono services and manages a dedicated fund for these purposes.

metadata.short_title: The Legal Practitioners (Fees) Act, 1926
metadata.long_title: An Act to define in certain cases the rights of legal practitioners to sue for their fees and their liabilities to be sued in respect of negligence in the discharge of their professional duties.
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Federal Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, appoint
metadata.one_line: Defines rights of legal practitioners to sue for fees and their liability for negligence in professional duties.
metadata.summary: This Act defines the rights of legal practitioners to institute proceedings for recovering fees under an agreement or computed according to prevailing law. It also clarifies that legal practitioners are not exempt from being sued for losses or injuries caused by negligence in conducting their professional duties. The Act applies to the whole of Pakistan and came into force on a date appointed by the Federal Government via official Gazette notification.

name: Legal Practitioners and Bar Councils Act, 1973

metadata.short_title: The Legal Practitioners and Bar Councils Act, 1973
metadata.long_title: An Act to repeal and, with certain modifications, re-enact the law relating to legal practitioners and bar councils.
repeals: the law relating to legal practitioners and bar councils
metadata.one_line: This Act establishes bar councils and regulates the enrolment, rights, conduct, and disciplinary procedures of advocates in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: The Legal Practitioners and Bar Councils Act, 1973 repeals and re-enacts previous laws regarding legal practitioners. It provides for the constitution of the Pakistan Bar Council and Provincial Bar Councils, including their composition and functions. The Act details the enrolment process for advocates, their rights to practice, and the disciplinary mechanisms available to maintain professional standards.

metadata.short_title: The Legal Representatives' Suits Act, 1855
metadata.long_title: An Act to enable Executors, Administrators or Representatives to sue and be sued for certain wrongs
metadata.territorial_extent: all the Provinces and the Capital of the Federation, except the Scheduled Districts (with specific extensions to certain districts in Sind and N.W.F.P. as per notifications)
metadata.one_line: Enables executors and administrators to sue or be sued for wrongs committed by the deceased within one year of death.
metadata.summary: This Act allows executors, administrators, or representatives of a deceased person to maintain actions for wrongs committed during the deceased's lifetime that caused pecuniary loss to their estate. It also permits actions against such representatives for wrongs committed by the deceased within one year before their death. The Act ensures that the death of either party does not abate the suit, allowing it to continue against or by the representatives, though they may raise a defense of lack of assets.

metadata.short_title: The Legal Tender (Inscribed Notes) Ordinance, 1977
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide that certain bank notes shall cease to be legal tender
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance declares that bank notes bearing political, religious, or commercial messages cease to be legal tender.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance provides for the cessation of certain bank notes from being legal tender. It applies to the whole of Pakistan and comes into force immediately. Bank notes bearing written, stamped, embossed, or inscribed words intended to convey political, religious, or commercial messages are affected. The State Bank of Pakistan is authorized to stop receiving or exchanging these specific notes after a date specified by Federal Government notification.

metadata.short_title: The Lepers Act, 1898
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the segregation and medical treatment of pauper lepers and the control of lepers following certain callings.
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Provincial Government declares it applicable thereto
metadata.max_penalty: fine which may extend to twenty rupees
metadata.one_line: This Act provides for the segregation, medical treatment, and control of pauper lepers in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: The Lepers Act, 1898 was enacted to segregate and provide medical treatment for pauper lepers while controlling those following certain callings. It empowers Provincial Governments to appoint leper asylums and constitute Boards to manage them. The Act outlines procedures for the arrest, examination, and detention of pauper lepers by police officers and Inspectors, as well as penalties for employing lepers in prohibited trades.

name: Letters of Administration and Succession Certificates Act, 2020

metadata.short_title: The Letters of Administration and Succession Certificates Act, 2020
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for an efficacious and speedy mechanism for issuance of Letters of Administration and Succession Certificates
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of Islamabad Capital Territory
metadata.commencement: on such dates as the Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, appoint
metadata.one_line: Establishes a mechanism for issuing succession certificates via NADRA to curb fraud in Islamabad Capital Territory.
metadata.summary: This Act provides an efficacious and speedy mechanism for the issuance of Letters of Administration and Succession Certificates aimed at curtailing fraud and forgery. It establishes a Succession Facilitation Unit within the National Database and Registration Authority (NADRA) to process applications from legal heirs regarding immovable or movable property. The Act outlines specific procedures including public notice publication, bio-metric verification, and the handling of factual controversies by referring cases to appropriate forums under existing laws.

metadata.short_title: The Life Insurance (Nationalisation) Order, 1972
metadata.long_title: An Order to provide for the nationalisation of life insurance business in Pakistan.
metadata.one_line: This Order nationalises life insurance business in Pakistan by vesting it in the Federal Government and establishing the Life Insurance Corporation.
metadata.summary: The Life Insurance (Nationalisation) Order, 1972 provides for the nationalisation of life insurance business in Pakistan. It vests the management of all insurers transacting life insurance business in the Federal Government as from March 19, 1972. The Order establishes the Life Insurance Corporation to transact life insurance business and transfers existing assets, liabilities, and employees to the Corporation. It outlines the functions of the Corporation, its finance and audit mechanisms, and provisions for compensation to insurers whose business is nationalised.

metadata.short_title: The Lighthouse Act, 1927
metadata.long_title: An Act to consolidate and amend the law relating to the provision, maintenance and control of lighthouses by the Government in Pakistan.
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Federal Government may, by notification in the official Gazette appoint
repeals: Repealed by the Repealing Act, 1938 (I of 1938), s. 2 and Sch.
metadata.max_penalty: Penalty for evading payment of light dues (specific amount not stated in excerpts)
metadata.one_line: This Act consolidates and amends laws regarding the provision, maintenance, control, and dues of lighthouses in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: The Lighthouse Act, 1927 consolidates and amends laws concerning the provision, maintenance, and control of lighthouses by the Government. It vests management of general lighthouses in the Federal Government while regulating local lighthouses through provincial authorities or local bodies. The Act establishes mechanisms for levying and collecting light dues, defining tonnage, and recovering unpaid amounts, including penalties for evasion. It creates advisory committees to advise on erection, alteration, and costs related to lighthouses, and empowers the Federal Government to make rules for their administration.

metadata.short_title: The Limitation (Emergency and War Conditions) Act, 1965
metadata.long_title: An Act to extend the period of limitation in certain cases
metadata.one_line: Extends limitation periods for suits and acts involving displaced persons or those detained in enemy territory due to war.
metadata.summary: This Act extends the period of limitation for instituting suits, appeals, applications, or performing acts when affected by war or armed hostilities. It applies to persons displaced from areas declared as affected or detained in enemy territory, allowing them six months after such conditions cease to act within the prescribed limits. The Act overrides existing limitation laws during these specific emergency circumstances and defines terms like 'affected area' and 'enemy subject'.

metadata.short_title: The Limitation Act, 1908
metadata.long_title: An Act to consolidate and amend the law for the Limitation of Suits, and for other purposes.
metadata.commencement: Section 31 and this section at once; the rest on 1909-01-01
repeals: THE SECOND SCHEDULE
THE THIRD SCHEDULE
metadata.one_line: Consolidates and amends the law regarding limitation periods for suits, appeals, applications, and acquisition of property by possession.
metadata.summary: This Act consolidates and amends laws concerning the limitation of suits, appeals, and applications to courts. It establishes specific time limits within which legal actions must be instituted or preferred, otherwise they are subject to dismissal. The Act also provides rules for acquiring ownership of easements and other property through possession, defines key legal terms such as 'suit' and 'easement', and outlines exceptions where the limitation period may be extended or excluded.

metadata.short_title: The Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2017
metadata.long_title: An Act to make provisions for the incorporation, regulation and winding up of limited liability partnerships as body corporate and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto
establishes: Commission (Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan)
metadata.max_penalty: fine which may extend to one million rupees and with a further fine which may extend to ten thousand rupees for every day after the first day after which the default continues
metadata.administering_body: Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan
metadata.one_line: This Act provides for the incorporation, regulation, and winding up of limited liability partnerships in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: The Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2017 establishes a legal framework for the formation and regulation of limited liability partnerships (LLPs) as body corporates. It covers preliminary matters such as definitions and short titles, outlines the nature of LLPs including separate legal personality and partner liabilities, and details procedures for registration, financial disclosures, and conversion from firms or private companies. The Act also prescribes penalties for non-compliance, offences by LLPs, and mechanisms for winding up and dissolution.

name: Listed Companies (Substantial Acquisition of Voting Shares and Takes-Overs) Ordinance, 2002

metadata.short_title: The Listed Companies (Substantial Acquisition of Voting Shares and Takeovers) Ordinance, 2002
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for substantial acquisition of voting shares and takeovers of listed companies and for matters ancillary thereto or connected therewith
metadata.max_penalty: fine extending to thirty million rupees for contravention; further fine of one hundred thousand rupees per day for continuing contravention
metadata.administering_body: Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan
metadata.one_line: Regulates substantial acquisition of voting shares and takeovers of listed companies in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes a transparent system for the substantial acquisition of voting shares and takeovers of listed companies to ensure fair treatment for all investors. It defines key terms such as 'acquirer' and 'control', outlines obligations for public announcements and offers, and grants powers to the Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan to make rules and regulations. The provisions apply to the whole of Pakistan and override other laws regarding these matters.

metadata.short_title: The Literacy Ordinance, 1985
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to encourage Literacy
metadata.territorial_extent: the Islamabad Capital territory and also applies to the establishments and institutions under the control of the Federal Government throughout Pakistan
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Federal Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, appoint
metadata.administering_body: Federal Ministry of Education or Federal Directorate of Education
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance restricts passports, driving/arms licences and federal employment to literate persons.
metadata.summary: The Literacy Ordinance, 1985 was promulgated by the President to encourage literacy in Pakistan. It applies to the Islamabad Capital Territory and Federal Government establishments throughout the country. The law mandates that passports (except Hajj), driving licences, arms licences, and federal employment are restricted to literate persons only.

name: Loans for Agricultural, Commercial and Industrial Purposes Act, 1973

metadata.short_title: The Loans for Agricultural, Commercial and Industrial Purposes Act, 1973
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for credit facilities for persons engaged in agriculture, commerce and industry.
metadata.one_line: Provides credit facilities for agriculture, commerce, and industry using land as security via pass books.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes a legal framework for providing credit facilities to persons engaged in agriculture, commerce, and industry. It allows banks to grant loans secured by land using a specific 'pass book' authenticated by Revenue Officers. The Act overrides conflicting laws and details the process for creating charges on land and recovering defaults through revenue authorities.

metadata.short_title: The Local Authorities Loans Act, 1914
metadata.long_title: An Act to consolidate and amend the law relating to the grant of loans to Local Authorities
repeals: The enactments listed in Schedule II
metadata.one_line: Consolidates law on loans for local authorities regarding borrowing powers, funds, and repayment conditions.
metadata.summary: This Act consolidates and amends the law concerning the grant of loans to local authorities. It defines 'local authority' and 'funds', outlines specific purposes for borrowing such as works, relief during famine, and epidemic prevention, and sets limits on loan amounts. The Act empowers the appropriate Government to make rules regarding the nature of funds, inquiries, and enforcement of conditions. It also specifies that contracts made otherwise than under this Act after its passing shall be void.

name: Local Authorities Pensions and Gratuities Act, 1919

metadata.short_title: The Local Authorities Pensions and Gratuities Act, 1919
metadata.long_title: An Act to extend the powers of local authorities in regard to the granting of pensions and gratuities.
metadata.one_line: Extends powers of local authorities to grant pensions and gratuities to officers wounded or incapacitated in service.
metadata.summary: This Act empowers local authorities to grant extraordinary pensions and gratuities to officers who were wounded or incapacitated since August 4, 1914, while serving the State. It also provides benefits to the widows and children of such officers who died due to injuries or illness incurred during service. The Act applies to the whole of Pakistan and distinguishes between cantonment/port authorities (Federal Government) and other local authorities (Provincial Government).

metadata.short_title: The Maintenance Orders Enforcement Act, 1921
metadata.long_title: An Act to facilitate the enforcement of Maintenance Orders made in other Countries and vice versa.
metadata.one_line: Facilitates enforcement and transmission of maintenance orders between Pakistan and reciprocating territories.
metadata.summary: This Act facilitates the mutual enforcement of maintenance orders between Pakistan and other countries. It establishes procedures for registering foreign orders transmitted by proper authorities, transmitting Pakistani orders to reciprocating territories, and making provisional provincial maintenance orders against residents of reciprocating countries. The Act defines key terms like 'maintenance order' and 'reciprocating territory', empowers the Federal Government to make rules, and allows courts to receive depositions from foreign jurisdictions as evidence.

metadata.short_title: The Majority Act, 1875
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Law respecting the age of majority
metadata.commencement: on the expiration of three months from the passing thereof
metadata.one_line: This Act amends the law regarding the age of majority for persons domiciled in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: The Majority Act, 1875 amends the legal framework concerning the age of majority for individuals domiciled in Pakistan. It establishes that minors with appointed guardians or under Court of Wards jurisdiction attain majority at twenty-one years, while others do so at eighteen. The Act specifies how age is computed and includes savings clauses regarding marriage, dower, divorce, adoption, and religious rites.

metadata.short_title: The Malaria Eradication Board (Repeal) Act, 1975
metadata.long_title: An Act to repeal the Malaria Eradication Board Ordinance, 1961
repeals: The Malaria Eradication Board Ordinance, 1961 (XVIII of 1961)
metadata.one_line: Repeals the Malaria Eradication Board Ordinance, 1961 and transfers its assets and liabilities to the Federal Government.
metadata.summary: This Act repeals the Malaria Eradication Board Ordinance, 1961. Upon repeal, all officers and employees of the Board are transferred to the Federal Government. Additionally, all rights, properties, assets, debts, and liabilities of the Board vest in the Federal Government, and any legal proceedings against the Board are deemed to be against the Federal Government.

name: Managed Cement Establishments (Payment to Corporation) Ordinance, 1979

metadata.short_title: The Managed Cement Establishments (Payment to Corporation) Ordinance, 1979
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the payment of certain amount by managed cement establishments to the State Cement Corporation of Pakistan.
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance mandates managed cement establishments to pay amounts to the State Cement Corporation and establishes a development fund.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance requires managed cement establishments to make payments to the State Cement Corporation of Pakistan for each metric ton of cement produced and sold after March 24, 1976. The proceeds are credited to the Cement Development Fund, which is administered by the Corporation for industry development schemes or subsidies. The Federal Government has the power to fix payment amounts via notification and to make rules regarding payment methods and fund maintenance.

name: Manoeuvres, Field Firing and Artillery Practice Act, 1938

metadata.short_title: The Manoeuvres, Field Firing and Artillery Practice Act, 1938
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide facilities for Military manoeuvres and for field firing and artillery practice
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to three months, or with fine which may extend to five thousand rupees, or with both
metadata.one_line: This Act provides facilities for military manoeuvres and field firing while regulating compensation and offences.
metadata.summary: The Manoeuvres, Field Firing and Artillery Practice Act, 1938 authorizes the Federal Government to conduct military exercises and artillery practice across specified areas. It outlines powers for encampment and resource use, mandates compensation for damages caused to persons or property, and establishes procedures for assessing claims. The Act also defines offences related to contravention of its provisions and empowers the Federal Government to make rules for its implementation.

metadata.short_title: The Marine Insurance Act, 2018
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the regulation of the business of marine insurance and matters connected therewith and incidental thereto
repeals: Sections 130A and 135A of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882
metadata.max_penalty: five million rupees (plus one hundred thousand rupees per day for continuing contravention)
metadata.one_line: Regulates marine insurance business in Pakistan, defining terms, policies, losses, and liabilities.
metadata.summary: This Act regulates the business of marine insurance throughout Pakistan. It defines key terms such as 'marine insurance', 'maritime perils', and 'ship', and establishes rules for insurable interest, disclosure, and policy construction. The legislation covers various types of losses including total loss, partial loss, salvage charges, and general average contributions. It also outlines the rights of insurers regarding subrogation and contribution, while repealing specific sections of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882.

metadata.short_title: The Maritime Security Agency Act, 1994
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for constitution and regulation of the [Pakistan] Maritime Security Agency.
metadata.territorial_extent: all officers and members of the [Pakistan] staff of the [Pakistan] Maritime Security Agency wherever they may be
metadata.one_line: This Act constitutes and regulates the Maritime Security Agency to safeguard Pakistan's maritime interests.
metadata.summary: The Maritime Security Agency Act, 1994 establishes the Pakistan Maritime Security Agency to regulate maritime activities and protect national maritime interests. The agency is headed by a Director General appointed from the Pakistan Navy and consists of various directors for operations, administration, technical affairs, budget, and legal matters. The Act outlines the constitution, staff appointments, oath of allegiance, powers of search and arrest, and exemptions from port charges for agency vessels.

name: Marketing Of Petroleum Products (Federal Control) (Repeal) Ordinance, 2002

metadata.short_title: Marketing of Petroleum Products (Federal Control) (Repeal) Ordinance, 2002
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to repeal the Marketing of Petroleum Products (Federal Control) Act, 1974
metadata.commencement: at once except sections 3 to 7 which shall come into force upon the occurrence of the effective date
repeals: Marketing of Petroleum Products (Federal Control) Act, 1974
Order issued pursuant to section 5 of the Act for the take over of the management of PSO contained in statutory notification S. R. O. No. 100(I)/77 dated 31st January 1977
metadata.one_line: Repeals the Marketing of Petroleum Products (Federal Control) Act, 1974 to facilitate private sector development and privatisation of PSO.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance repeals the Marketing of Petroleum Products (Federal Control) Act, 1974, reflecting a shift from federal control to private sector development in the oil marketing sector. It applies to the whole of Pakistan and specifically addresses the transition of Pakistan State Oil Company Limited (PSO) from a managed company to a standard corporate entity under the Companies Ordinance, 1984. The document outlines the automatic reconstitution of PSO's Board of Management into a Board of Directors, the cessation of federal management powers, and provisions for holding director elections within twelve months. It also includes savings clauses protecting contracts and employees from the repeal's effects while ensuring liability protection for former board members.

name: Marriage Functions (Prohibition of Ostentatious Displays and Wasteful Expenses) Ordinance, 2000

metadata.short_title: The Marriage Functions (Prohibition of Ostentatious Displays and Wasteful Expenses) Ordinance, 2000
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance whereas it is expedient to provide for the prohibition of ostentatious displays and wasteful expenses on marriages and ceremonies related thereto;
metadata.max_penalty: simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to one month or with fine not less than one hundred thousand rupees and not more than five hundred thousand rupees or with both
metadata.one_line: Prohibits ostentatious displays like fireworks and restricts wasteful expenses at marriage functions across Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance prohibits ostentatious displays such as lighting decorations, exploding crackers, or displaying fireworks during marriage ceremonies. It also restricts the serving of meals to one dish plus soft drinks in public venues like hotels and restaurants, while allowing family members to eat within their own homes. The law creates offences for contravention, punishable by imprisonment up to one month or a fine between 100,000 and 500,000 rupees, and designates specific officers appointed by the Federal or Provincial Government to file complaints for cognizance.

metadata.short_title: The Marriages Validation Act, 1892
metadata.long_title: An Act to validate certain marriages solemnized under Part VI of the Christian Marriage Act, 1872.
repeals: The Marriages Validation Act, 1892 (except as to Straits Settlements)
metadata.status_evidence: Rep. by the Repealing and Amending Act, 1914 (10 of 1914).
metadata.one_line: Validates certain irregular marriages between Native Christians and non-Native Christians solemnized under the Christian Marriage Act, 1872.
metadata.summary: This Act validates marriages solemnized under Part VI of the Christian Marriage Act, 1872, where one party was a Native Christian and the other was not. It declares these marriages valid in law as if both parties were Native Christians, provided they were solemnized in good faith and neither party had contracted a valid marriage prior to this Act's commencement. The Act also validates related records and certificates for such marriages.

metadata.short_title: The Married Women's Property Act, 1874
metadata.long_title: An Act to explain and amend the law relating to certain married women, and for other purposes.
repeals: Married Women's Property Act, 1870
metadata.one_line: Defines married women's wages and earnings as separate property and limits husbands' liability for wives' debts.
metadata.summary: This Act explains and amends the law regarding the property rights of certain married women. It declares that a married woman's wages, earnings, savings, and investments acquired after the Act's passing are her separate property. The legislation also addresses insurance policies taken out by or for the benefit of wives and limits a husband's liability for his wife's debts contracted before marriage.

metadata.short_title: The Martial Law Regulation No. 60 (Repeal) Act, 1989
metadata.long_title: An Act to repeal Martial Law Regulation No. 60
metadata.one_line: This Act repeals Martial Law Regulation No. 60 regarding educational institutions in Islamabad.
metadata.summary: The document is a short Act enacted to repeal Martial Law Regulation No. 60. The specific regulation being repealed concerns educational institutions located within the Islamabad Capital Territory. The Act comes into force immediately upon enactment.

metadata.short_title: The Maternity and Paternity Leave Act, 2023
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the facility of maternity and paternity leave to the employees of public and private establishments under administrative control of the Federal Government
metadata.territorial_extent: all public and private establishments under administrative control of the Federal Government wherever they may be
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment up to six months or a fine up to one hundred thousand rupees or both
metadata.one_line: Provides maternity and paternity leave rights for employees of Federal Government-controlled public and private establishments.
metadata.summary: This Act grants paid maternity leave to female employees and paternity leave to male employees working in public or private establishments under the administrative control of the Federal Government. Maternity leave entitlements vary based on birth order, ranging from 180 days for the first birth down to 90 days for the third birth, while paternity leave is capped at thirty days. The Act establishes specific definitions for key terms like 'employee' and 'establishment' and prescribes offences with penalties for non-compliance.

metadata.short_title: The Measures of Length Act, 1889
metadata.long_title: An Act to declare the imperial standard yard for the United Kingdom to be the legal standard measure of length in Pakistan.
metadata.commencement: on such day as the Federal Government may appoint
repeals: Regulation XII of 1827 of the Bombay Code
metadata.one_line: Declares the imperial standard yard for the UK as the legal standard measure of length in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Act declares the imperial standard yard for the United Kingdom to be the legal standard measure of length in Pakistan. It defines the standard foot and inch based on the standard yard and establishes presumptions regarding the accuracy of certified measures. The Act allows public inspection of these certified measures and mandates that specific authorities keep copies of the standard measures.

metadata.short_title: The Medical and Dental Degrees Ordinance, 1982
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to repeal and, with certain modifications, re-enact the Medical Degrees Act, 1916
repeals: The Medical Degrees Act, 1916 (VII of 1916)
metadata.max_penalty: rigorous imprisonment for a term not less than one year or more than five years and fine up to fifty thousand rupees
metadata.administering_body: Medical and Dental Council of Pakistan
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance repeals the 1916 Act and regulates the conferment of medical and dental degrees in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: The Medical and Dental Degrees Ordinance, 1982 was promulgated to repeal and modify the Medical Degrees Act, 1916. It restricts the right to confer medical and dental degrees to specific authorities listed in the Schedule or authorized by the Federal or Provincial Governments. The Ordinance prohibits unauthorized conferment of degrees and imposes penalties for falsely assuming medical titles or practicing without qualification.

metadata.short_title: The Medical Colleges (Governing Bodies) Ordinance, 1961
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the constitution of Governing Bodies for Medical Colleges in Pakistan.
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance provides for the constitution and powers of Governing Bodies for Medical Colleges in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes Governing Bodies to administer and manage Medical Colleges across Pakistan. It defines the composition of these bodies, including members appointed by the Provincial Government and representatives from institutions specified by the government. The text outlines the powers of the Governing Body, the structure of various committees like the Executive and Finance committees, and provisions regarding the College Fund and financial management.

metadata.short_title: The Medical Officers (Regularization of Appointments) Act, 1992
metadata.long_title: An act to provide for the regularization of the appointment of certain medical officers appointed on adhoc basis
amends: Federal Public Service Commission Ordinance, 1977 (XLV of 1977)
metadata.one_line: This Act regularizes adhoc appointments of certain medical officers in the Federal Government with effect from its commencement.
metadata.summary: The Medical Officers (Regularization of Appointments) Act, 1992 provides for the regularization of appointments of medical officers who were appointed on an adhoc basis before October 12, 1988. It applies to those appointed in institutions under the Health Division and as RMOs in the National Institute of Cardiovascular Diseases. The Act stipulates that such officers shall be deemed to have been appointed on a regular basis upon an order by the Federal Government, subject to verification of character, antecedents, domicile, qualifications, experience, and age limits.

metadata.short_title: The Medical Qualifications (Information) Ordinance, 1960
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the furnishing of certain information by persons qualified in certain branches of medicine.
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to one month, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both
metadata.administering_body: Director-General (Director of Health Services of the Province)
metadata.one_line: Requires persons in specific medical branches residing in Pakistan to furnish qualification and personal information to the Director-General.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance mandates that all persons residing in Pakistan with qualifications in specified medical branches must provide certain information to the Director-General. The required details include personal particulars, educational and professional qualifications, and occupational records. Compliance is required within one month of the Ordinance's promulgation or an individual's first qualification, subject to extensions by the Director-General. Failure to furnish this information without sufficient cause is punishable by imprisonment up to one month, a fine up to one thousand rupees, or both.

metadata.short_title: The Medical Tribunal Act, 2020
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the setting up of special judicial tribunal to efficiently and expeditiously hear and decide disputes arising out of matters pertaining to the medical and health sectors
repeals: The Medical Tribunal Ordinance, 2019
metadata.one_line: Establishes a special judicial tribunal to hear disputes in the medical and health sectors efficiently.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes a special judicial tribunal known as the Medical Tribunal to handle disputes in the medical and health sectors. The Tribunal consists of a Chairman appointed by the Prime Minister and members including jurists and technical experts. It has jurisdiction over offences and appeals arising from various medical sector laws, such as the Pakistan Nursing Council Act and the Pharmacy Act. Appeals against the Tribunal's final orders can be made to the Supreme Court of Pakistan within thirty days.

name: Members of Majlis-e-Shoora (Parliament) Immunities and Privileges Act, 2023

metadata.short_title: The Members of Majlis-e-Shoora (Parliament) Immunities and Privileges Act, 2023
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the members of Majlis-e-Shoora (Parliament) immunities and privileges
metadata.one_line: Provides immunities and privileges for members of the National Assembly and Senate regarding arrest, detention, and legal process.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes specific immunities and privileges for members of the Majlis-e-Shoora (Parliament) to ensure their participation in parliamentary proceedings. It regulates procedures related to preventive detention, arrest, registration of cases against members, and the service of legal processes within parliamentary precincts. The legislation mandates immediate intimation to the Chairman or Speaker regarding arrests, detentions, or summons involving members and grants exemptions from arrest during critical voting periods.

name: Members of Parliament (Salaries and Allowances) Act, 1974

metadata.short_title: The Members of Parliament (Salaries and Allowances) Act, 1974
metadata.long_title: An Act to consolidate and amend the law relating to salaries and allowances of members of Parliament and to provide for certain privileges of the Leaders of the House and the Leaders of the Opposition in the two Houses of Parliament.
metadata.one_line: This Act consolidates and amends laws regarding salaries, allowances, and privileges for Members of Parliament.
metadata.summary: The Members of Parliament (Salaries and Allowances) Act, 1974 consolidates and amends the law relating to the salaries and allowances of members of Parliament. It provides specific rates for daily allowance, conveyance allowance, travelling allowance, housing allowance, telephone facilities, and sumptuary allowance. The Act also defines key terms such as 'House', 'session', and 'Leader of the House' and outlines provisions for travel vouchers and air tickets that do not lapse at the end of a financial year.

name: Members of Parliament and Provincial Assemblies (Exemption of Advisers from Disqualification) Act, 1976

metadata.short_title: The Members of Parliament and Provincial Assemblies (Exemption of Advisers from Disqualification) Act, 1976
metadata.long_title: An Act to declare the holders of the office of Adviser to the Governor not to be disqualified from being elected or chosen as, and from being a member of Parliament or a Provincial Assembly.
metadata.commencement: at once; deemed to have taken effect on 1975-12-31
metadata.one_line: Exempts Advisers to Governors from disqualification when Federal Government assumes provincial functions.
metadata.summary: This Act declares that holders of the office of Adviser to the Governor are not disqualified from being elected or chosen as members of Parliament or Provincial Assemblies. The exemption applies specifically during periods when an Order under Article 232(2)(c) is in force, allowing the Federal Government to assume provincial functions, or when a Proclamation under Article 234 is in force. The Act came into force immediately but was deemed effective from December 31, 1975.

name: Members of the Election Commission (Salary, Allowances, Perks and Privileges) Act, 2016

metadata.short_title: The Members of the Election Commission (Salary, Allowances, Perks and Privileges) Act, 2016
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for salary, allowances and privileges of the members of the Election Commission of Pakistan.
metadata.commencement: at once and deemed to have taken effect on and from the 13th June, 2011
metadata.one_line: This Act provides salary, allowances, perks, privileges, provident fund, and leave terms for members of the Election Commission.
metadata.summary: The Act establishes the financial benefits and privileges for members of the Election Commission of Pakistan. It grants them the same salary, allowances, perks, and privileges as a High Court Judge. Additionally, it outlines provisions for joining the General Provident Fund and specific leave entitlements granted by the President.

name: Members Of The National Assembly (Exemption From Preventive Detention And Personal Appearance) Ordinance, 1963

metadata.short_title: The Members of the National Assembly (Exemption from Preventive Detention and Personal Appearance) Ordinance, 1963
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for certain privileges of the Members of the National Assembly of Pakistan.
metadata.one_line: Provides exemptions from preventive detention and personal appearance for National Assembly members during sessions.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance grants specific privileges to Members of the National Assembly of Pakistan regarding their legal status. It exempts them from preventive detention under any law and relieves them from being required to appear personally in Civil, Revenue Courts, or before Election Tribunals during a session and for fourteen days before and after. The provisions also restrict Civil and Revenue Courts from proceeding with matters involving a Member as a party unless the Member waives their privilege in writing.

metadata.short_title: The Mental Health Ordinance, 2001
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to consolidate and amend the law relating to the mentally disordered persons with respect to their care and treatment, the management of their property and other related matters
repeals: The Lunacy Act, 1912 (IV of 1912)
metadata.max_penalty: Penalty for making false statement (Section 52)
metadata.one_line: Consolidates and amends laws regarding care, treatment, and property management for mentally disordered persons in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance consolidates and amends the law relating to the care and treatment of mentally disordered persons. It establishes a Federal Mental Health Authority and regulates admission, detention, and discharge procedures in psychiatric facilities. The document also provides for the management of property, guardianship appointments, and protection of human rights for such persons.

metadata.short_title: The Merchandise Marks Act, 1889
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Law relating to Fraudulent Marks on Merchandise.
repeals: sections 478 to 489 of the Indian Penal Code
Sea Customs Act, 1878 (amendments)
metadata.one_line: Amends law on fraudulent marks, defines false trade descriptions, and sets penalties for applying them to goods.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the law regarding fraudulent marks on merchandise by defining terms like 'trade description' and 'false trade description'. It applies to the whole of Pakistan and comes into force on April 1, 1889. The legislation outlines provisions for stamping piece-goods manufactured in Pakistan, rules for sampling goods to determine their character, and penalties for applying false descriptions or selling goods with such descriptions.

metadata.short_title: The Mesne Profits and Improvements Act, 1855
metadata.long_title: An Act relating to mesne profits and to improvements made by holders under defective titles
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of Pakistan (except the Scheduled Districts)
repeals: s. 1 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 (4 of 1882), in places to which it extends
metadata.one_line: Limits liability for mesne profits and secures compensation to bona fide holders who made improvements under defective titles.
metadata.summary: This Act limits the liability for mesne profits and secures the value of improvements made by bona fide holders under defective titles. It protects persons who erected buildings or made improvements believing they held an absolute estate, even if later evicted by someone with a better title. The holder is entitled to the estimated value of the improvement at the time of eviction or the option to purchase the land interest.

metadata.short_title: The Metal Tokens Act, 1889
metadata.long_title: An Act for the Protection of Coinage and other purposes
repeals: section 98, Act X of 1882
section 28 of the Indian Penal Code
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both
metadata.one_line: Prohibits private making of metal pieces for money and amends penal code sections regarding coinage.
metadata.summary: This Act prohibits private persons from making or possessing metal pieces intended for use as money. It establishes penalties for unlawful making, issue, or possession of such pieces and extends these prohibitions to local authorities and railways. The Act also amends specific sections of the Indian Penal Code and applies certain provisions to the importation of metal pieces.

metadata.short_title: The Microfinance Institutions Ordinance, 2001
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to regulate the establishment, business and operations of microfinance institutions.
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one hundred thousand rupees, or with both
metadata.one_line: Regulates the establishment, business, and operations of microfinance institutions in Pakistan to protect depositors.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance regulates the establishment, business, and operations of microfinance institutions to promote poverty alleviation and social welfare. It applies to the whole of Pakistan and establishes a Depositors' Protection Fund managed by the State Bank of Pakistan. The law defines key terms such as 'microfinance institution', 'deposit', and 'depositor', while imposing restrictions on establishment and licensing requirements. It also outlines penalties for false information and grants the State Bank powers regarding inspection, investigation, and removal of directors.

name: Military College of Engineering, Risalpur (Degree) Ordinance, 1962

metadata.short_title: The Military College of Engineering, Risalpur (Degree) Ordinance, 1962
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to grant a charter to the Military College of Engineering, Risalpur.
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance grants a charter to the Military College of Engineering, Risalpur to award Bachelor of Civil Engineering degrees.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance grants a charter to the Military College of Engineering, Risalpur, enabling it to award the Degree of Bachelor of Civil Engineering. It establishes the constitution and powers of the College, including the Controlling Authority (Engineer-in-Chief), the Commandant, and the Academic Board. The document outlines the College's functions such as providing instruction, holding examinations, and managing student welfare, while empowering the Federal Government to make rules and regulations.

metadata.short_title: The Mines Act, 1923
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend and consolidate the law relating to the regulation and inspection of mines
repeals: Regulation XII of 1887
metadata.one_line: This Act regulates and inspects mines, defines roles for owners and managers, and sets safety and employment standards.
metadata.summary: The Mines Act, 1923 consolidates laws regarding the regulation and inspection of mines in Pakistan. It establishes Mining Boards and Committees to oversee operations and defines the duties of owners, agents, and managers. The Act covers health and safety provisions, limits on working hours for various groups including women and children, leave entitlements, and penalties for contraventions.

metadata.short_title: The Mines Maternity Benefit Act, 1941
metadata.long_title: An Act to regulate the employment of women in mines for a certain period before and after childbirth and to provide for payment of maternity benefit to them.
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Federal Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, appoint
metadata.max_penalty: fine which may extend to fifty rupees (for rules contravention) or one hundred rupees (for section 16 contravention); specific penalty amounts for the Act itself are not explicitly detailed in the provided excerpts other than those for subordinate rules and section 16
metadata.administering_body: Federal Government (via Provincial Government for rules)
metadata.one_line: Regulates women's employment in mines around childbirth and provides maternity benefits.
metadata.summary: This Act regulates the employment of women in mines during pregnancy and after childbirth, prohibiting work for a specific period following delivery. It grants women the right to leave of absence before and after delivery and entitles them to maternity benefits if they meet continuous employment conditions. The Act also protects women from dismissal during their authorized absence due to confinement and empowers Provincial Governments to make rules and exempt certain mines.

name: Minimum Wages for Unskilled Workers Ordinance, 1969.

metadata.short_title: The Minimum Wages for Unskilled Workers Ordinance, 1969
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to fix the minimum rates of wages for unskilled workers employed in certain commercial and industrial establishment in Pakistan.
metadata.max_penalty: simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to two thousand rupees, or with both
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance fixes minimum wages for unskilled workers in commercial and industrial establishments across Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes minimum wage rates for unskilled workers employed in specific commercial and industrial establishments throughout Pakistan. It defines key terms such as 'employer', 'wages', and 'industrial area', while specifying deductions allowed for housing and transport provided by the employer. The document also outlines penalties for employers who fail to comply with these wage requirements and restricts cognizance of offences to complaints made by aggrieved workers or authorized officers.

metadata.short_title: The Minimum Wages Ordinance, 1961
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the regulation of minimum rates of wages for workers employed in certain industrial undertakings.
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months or fine not exceeding five hundred rupees
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance regulates minimum wages for workers in certain industrial undertakings and establishes Boards to recommend rates.
metadata.summary: The Minimum Wages Ordinance, 1961 provides for the regulation of minimum rates of wages for workers employed in specific industrial undertakings. It empowers Provincial Governments to establish Minimum Wages Boards consisting of representatives from employers, workers, and independent members to recommend wage rates. The Ordinance defines key terms such as 'worker', 'employer', and 'industry', prohibits paying wages below the declared minimum rate, and outlines offences and penalties for contravention.

name: Modaraba Companies and Modaraba (Floatation and Control) Ordinance, 1980

metadata.short_title: The Modaraba Companies and Modaraba (Floatation and Control) Ordinance, 1980
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for matters relating to registration of modaraba companies and the floatation, management and regulation of modarabas.
metadata.max_penalty: fine which may extend to one hundred thousand rupees; continuing contravention punishable with a further fine of one thousand rupees per day
metadata.administering_body: Federal Government (via Registrar appointed by notification)
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance regulates the registration, floatation, management, and winding up of modaraba companies in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: The Modaraba Companies and Modaraba (Floatation and Control) Ordinance, 1980 provides a legal framework for the registration and operation of modaraba companies. It defines eligibility criteria for registration, outlines the business operations and conditions applicable to modarabas, and establishes a Tribunal for winding up proceedings. The Ordinance also empowers the Federal Government to appoint a Registrar and make rules to regulate accounts, audits, and fees.

metadata.short_title: The Motion Pictures Ordinance, 1979
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the censorship of films and the regulation of exhibition of films by means of cinematographs
repeals: The Cinematograph Act, 1918 (II of 1918)
The Censorship of Films Act, 1963 (XVIII of 1963)
metadata.one_line: Establishes a Board to certify films for public exhibition and regulates cinematograph screenings across Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance provides for the censorship of films and the regulation of their exhibition by means of cinematographs. It establishes a Board constituted by the Federal Government to examine, certify, or refuse certification of films based on specific principles such as national security and morality. The document outlines procedures for licensing exhibition places, handling appeals, and imposing penalties for unauthorized screenings, while repealing earlier acts on film censorship.

metadata.short_title: The Motor Vehicles Act, 1939
metadata.long_title: An Act to consolidate and amend the law relating to motor vehicles.
repeals: Chapters I to VI
Chapters IX, X (except section 125)
Schedules I to XI
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment which may extend to three months, or with fine which may extend to five hundred rupees, or with both
metadata.one_line: Consolidates and amends the law relating to motor vehicles, including insurance requirements and offences.
metadata.summary: This Act consolidates and amends the law regarding motor vehicles in Pakistan. It establishes a framework for third-party insurance, requiring policies to cover liability for death or bodily injury. The Act empowers the Federal Government to make rules on traveling passes, vehicle entry conditions, and insurance certificates. It also defines offences related to driving uninsured vehicles and outlines penalties.

metadata.short_title: The Multi-unit Co-operative Societies Act, 1942
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the incorporation, regulation and winding up of co-operative societies with objects not confined to one Province.
metadata.max_penalty: fine which may extend to fifty rupees
metadata.one_line: Provides for the incorporation, regulation and winding up of co-operative societies operating across multiple provinces.
metadata.summary: This Act regulates co-operative societies whose objects are not confined to a single province. It applies to societies incorporated before or after its commencement under various provincial laws. The Act establishes a Central Registrar with powers over these multi-unit societies and outlines procedures for registering branches in different provinces, including requirements to submit bye-laws and returns.

metadata.short_title: The Municipal Taxation Act, 1881
metadata.long_title: An Act to give power to prohibit the levy of municipal taxes in certain cases.
metadata.one_line: Empowers Federal and Provincial Governments to prohibit municipal taxes on military, naval, air-force personnel and the governments themselves.
metadata.summary: This Act empowers the Federal and Provincial Governments to prohibit the levy of municipal taxes in specific cases. It applies to taxes payable by persons in military, naval, or air-force service compelled by duty to reside within a municipality, as well as taxes payable by the Provincial Government itself. When such prohibitions are in force, the respective governments become liable to pay the amounts that would otherwise have been collected from these persons or entities.

metadata.short_title: The Muslim Family Laws Ordinance, 1961
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to give effect to certain recommendations of the Commission on Marriage and Family Laws
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Federal Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, appoint
repeals: Arbitration Act, 1940 (X of 1940)
Code of Civil Procedure 1908 (Act V of 1908)
metadata.max_penalty: simple imprisonment which may extend to one month, or with fine which may extent to two hundred rupees, or with both
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance regulates Muslim marriages, divorce, maintenance, and succession in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: The Muslim Family Laws Ordinance, 1961 was promulgated to implement recommendations from the Commission on Marriage and Family Laws. It establishes an Arbitration Council to handle disputes regarding polygamy and maintenance, while also defining rules for marriage registration, dower, and succession rights. The Ordinance overrides existing laws and customs to ensure uniform application across Pakistan.

metadata.short_title: The Mussalman Wakf Act, 1923
metadata.long_title: An Act to make provision for the better management of wakf property and for ensuring the keeping and publication of proper accounts in respect of such properties.
establishes: Court (District Judge or designated subordinate Court)
metadata.max_penalty: two thousand rupees
metadata.one_line: This Act regulates the management of wakf property, requires account keeping by mutwallis, and establishes court oversight.
metadata.summary: The Mussalman Wakf Act, 1923 provides for the better management of wakf property and ensures proper accounts are kept and published. It mandates that mutwallis furnish detailed particulars regarding wakf property, income, and expenses to a designated Court within six months of the Act's commencement or creation of the wakf. The Act empowers Provincial Governments to make rules for its implementation and allows for exemptions for specific sections of the Muslim community.

metadata.short_title: The Mussalman Wakf Validating Act, 1913
metadata.long_title: An Act to declare the rights of Mussalmans to make settlements of property by way of 'wakf' in favour of their families, children and descendants.
metadata.one_line: Validates wakfs created by Muslims for family support and charitable purposes.
metadata.summary: This Act declares the rights of Muslims to create wakfs (endowments) in favor of their families, children, and descendants. It removes doubts regarding the validity of such settlements even if the ultimate benefit is reserved for the poor or other religious purposes after the extinction of the family line. The legislation also saves local and sectarian customs from being affected by its provisions.

metadata.short_title: The Mutual Legal Assistance (Criminal Matters) Act, 2020
metadata.long_title: An Act to enact a law for mutual legal assistance in criminal matters
repeals: provisions relating to mutual legal assistance in criminal matters contained in the Customs Act, 1969 (IV of 1969)
metadata.administering_body: Ministry of Interior, Government of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan
metadata.one_line: Enacts a law for mutual legal assistance in criminal matters between Pakistan and foreign countries.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes a framework for mutual legal assistance in criminal matters between Pakistan and other countries. It defines key terms such as 'central authority', 'information system', and 'proceeds of crime'. The Act outlines procedures for transmitting information, executing requests for evidence gathering, freezing or seizing assets, and handling foreign confiscation orders. It also specifies that assistance shall not be refused on grounds of bank secrecy or fiscal matters.

metadata.short_title: My University Islamabad Act, 2013
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of MY University, Islamabad and for matters connected with and ancillary thereto
metadata.territorial_extent: Pakistan (including abroad as determined by the Board)
metadata.administering_body: Federal Government (via the Board of Governors)
metadata.one_line: Establishes MY University Islamabad with academic autonomy and defines its authorities, officers, and functions.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes MY University Islamabad as a body corporate with perpetual succession and academic, financial, and administrative autonomy. It defines the university's structure, including the Patron, Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, Board of Governors, Executive Committee, and Academic Council. The Act outlines the powers to establish campuses locally and abroad, make statutes and regulations, and manage the University Fund.

metadata.short_title: The National Accountability Ordinance, 1999
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the setting up of a National Accountability Bureau so as to eradicate corruption and corrupt practices and hold accountable all those persons accused of such practices and matters ancillary thereto
metadata.commencement: at once and shall be deemed to have come into force from the 1st day of January, 1985
metadata.max_penalty: Rigorous imprisonment for fourteen years or life imprisonment
metadata.one_line: Establishes the National Accountability Bureau to eradicate corruption and hold accountable persons accused of corrupt practices.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the National Accountability Bureau (NAB) to detect, investigate, and prosecute cases involving corruption and corrupt practices. It applies to all persons in Pakistan, including public servants, with specific exceptions for taxation matters and certain procedural lapses. The law empowers NAB to freeze properties, seek international legal assistance, and imposes severe penalties, including up to fourteen years of rigorous imprisonment or life imprisonment, for offenses such as misuse of authority and fraud.

name: National Agri-trade and Food Safety Authority Act, 2026

metadata.short_title: The National Agri-trade and Food Safety Authority Act, 2026
metadata.long_title: An Act to establish the National Agri-trade and Food Safety Authority.
repeals: the Pakistan Plant Quarantine Act, 1976 (LXXV of 1976)
the Pakistan Animal Quarantine (Import and Export of Animals and Animal Products) Ordinance, 1
establishes: National Agri-trade and Food Safety Authority (NAFSA)
metadata.one_line: Establishes a federal authority to regulate agrochemicals, food safety, and facilitate international trade while repealing previous quarantine laws.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the National Agri-trade and Food Safety Authority (NAFSA) to regulate the quality of agricultural produce, plants, animals, and related products for domestic use and international trade. It mandates compliance with sanitary and phytosanitary (SPS) measures and quality standards to facilitate competitive inter-provincial and international trade. The Act creates various committees including a Board of Governors, Scientific Committee, and Appellate Committee, while also defining key terms such as 'adulterated pesticide' and 'agricultural product'. Furthermore, it repeals existing laws like the Pakistan Plant Quarantine Act, 1976, and abolishes the Animal Quarantine Department and Department of Plant Protection, transferring their functions and assets to the new Authority.

name: National and Provincial Assemblies (Elections to Reserved Seats) Act, 1976

metadata.short_title: The National and Provincial Assemblies (Elections to Reserved Seats) Act, 1976
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the conduct of elections to the reserved seats in the National Assembly and the Provincial Assemblies.
repeals: The National and Provincial Assemblies (Elections to Reserved Seats) Act, 1976
metadata.status_evidence: This Act has been repealed in its application to the election to which the Representation of the People Act, 1976 (85 of 1976) applies, see Act No. 85 of 1976, s. 109.
metadata.one_line: Provides for the conduct of elections to reserved seats in National and Provincial Assemblies, including disputes and offences.
metadata.summary: This Act regulates elections to reserved seats in the National Assembly and Provincial Assemblies. It establishes procedures for election petitions, defines corrupt practices and illegal activities, and sets out disqualifications for candidates. The Election Commission is empowered to ensure fair conduct of elections and adjudicate disputes through appointed Tribunals.

name: National Anti-Money Laundering and Counter Financing of Terrorism Authority Act, 2023

metadata.short_title: The National Anti-Money Laundering and Counter Financing of Terrorism Authority Act, 2023
metadata.long_title: An Act to establish National Anti-Money Laundering and Counter Financing of Terrorism Authority in Pakistan
repeals: Prime Minister's Office Order No 3021/M/SPM/2019 dated 2nd August, 2019
Notification No. 4-1/2019-Min-I dated 30-12-2019
establishes: National Anti-Money Laundering and Counter Financing of Terrorism Authority
metadata.one_line: Establishes a federal authority to combat money laundering and terrorism financing across Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the National Anti-Money Laundering and Counter Financing of Terrorism Authority in Pakistan to unify state response against money laundering and terrorism financing. The Authority is a body corporate with headquarters in Islamabad, comprising members from various ministries, financial institutions, and law enforcement agencies. It possesses administrative and financial powers to coordinate international efforts, implement government policy, and make rules and regulations necessary for its functions.

metadata.short_title: The National Archives Act, 1993
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the custody and preservation of public records of Pakistan and archival materials of historical and national significance to Pakistan
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to three months, or with fine, or with both
metadata.administering_body: Department of the Government of Pakistan designated as the National Archives of Pakistan
metadata.one_line: This Act establishes the National Archives to preserve public records and regulates their transfer, access, and destruction.
metadata.summary: The National Archives Act, 1993 provides for the custody and preservation of public records and archival materials of historical significance in Pakistan. It establishes the National Archives department and an Advisory Board to manage these records. The Act outlines procedures for transferring non-current records, surrendering records on demand, and granting public access after a specified period, while also defining penalties for contravention.

metadata.short_title: National Assembly Secretariat Employees Act, 2018
metadata.long_title: An Act to regulate the recruitment and the conditions of service of persons appointed in the National Assembly Secretariat
metadata.territorial_extent: all employees in the National Assembly Secretariat wherever they may be
repeals: National Assembly Secretariat (Recruitment and Conditions of Service) Rules, 1973
metadata.one_line: Regulates recruitment and service conditions for National Assembly Secretariat employees.
metadata.summary: This Act regulates the recruitment and conditions of service for persons appointed in the National Assembly Secretariat. It defines key terms such as 'civil servant', 'deputation', and 'pay', and establishes the structure and strength limits of the Secretariat. The Act provides for appointments, promotions, and the making of rules by the Speaker with the concurrence of the Finance Committee. It also repeals the previous 1973 Rules while validating past actions taken under them.

metadata.short_title: The National Bank of Pakistan Ordinance, 1949
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to constitute a National Bank of Pakistan.
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance constitutes the National Bank of Pakistan and defines its establishment, capital, management, and business.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance was promulgated to constitute the National Bank of Pakistan to extend banking facilities and provide credit for agriculture. It establishes the Bank as a body corporate with perpetual succession, defining its share capital and the liability of shareholders. The document outlines the structure of the Central Board and Local Boards, their powers to transact business, manage staff, and make bye-laws for the efficient conduct of the Bank's affairs.

metadata.short_title: The National Book Foundation Act, 1972
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of a Foundation for making books available at moderate prices.
metadata.administering_body: Federal Government (via Ministry of Education and Provincial Coordination)
metadata.one_line: Establishes the National Book Foundation to make books available at moderate prices through a Board of Governors.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the National Book Foundation as a body corporate to make books available at moderate prices. The Foundation is managed by a Board of Governors comprising government officials, provincial representatives, and eminent educationists.
