Its functions include receiving grants, publishing and importing books, encouraging writers, and promoting literacy across Pakistan.

name: National College of Arts Institute Act, 2021

metadata.short_title: The National College of Arts Institute Act, 2021
metadata.long_title: An Act to reconstitute National College of Arts
repeals: National College of Arts Ordinance, 1985 (XXVIII of 1985)
establishes: National College of Arts (reconstituted body corporate)
metadata.one_line: This Act reconstitutes the National College of Arts as a body corporate with academic and administrative autonomy.
metadata.summary: The National College of Arts Institute Act, 2021 reconstitutes the National College of Arts, Lahore, as a body corporate with perpetual succession. It grants the College academic, financial, and administrative autonomy, including the power to employ officers and hold property. The Act establishes various authorities such as the Board of Governors, Academic Council, and Syndicate, while repealing the previous Ordinance from 1985.

metadata.short_title: The National College of Arts Ordinance, 1985
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to confer on the National College of Arts, Lahore, the power to award degrees.
establishes: National College of Arts (as a body corporate)
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance confers degree-awarding powers on the National College of Arts, Lahore, and establishes its governance structure.
metadata.summary: The National College of Arts Ordinance, 1985 was promulgated by the President to grant the National College of Arts in Lahore the authority to award degrees. It establishes the College as a body corporate with perpetual succession and defines its purpose to provide instruction, training, research, and service in arts and allied disciplines at various levels. The Ordinance outlines the composition and functions of the Board of Governors, the Controlling Authority (Federal Minister for Education), and committees responsible for finance, planning, and staff selection. It also mandates that degrees cannot be granted without passing examinations in Islamic and Pakistan Studies.

metadata.short_title: The National Command Authority Act, 2010
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the constitution and establishment of National Command Authority
metadata.commencement: at once and shall be deemed to have taken effect on the 13th December, 2007
metadata.one_line: Establishes the National Command Authority to control nuclear and space technologies in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the National Command Authority (NCA) to provide complete command and control over research, development, production, and use of nuclear and space technologies. The Authority is headed by the Prime Minister as Chairman and includes other senior ministers and military chiefs. It grants the NCA powers to supervise strategic organizations, manage budgets, classify employees based on security needs, and take measures regarding employee movement and privacy for national security.

name: National Commission For Human Development Ordinance, 2002

metadata.short_title: The National Commission for Human Development Ordinance, 2002
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the establishment of National Commission for Human Development
metadata.one_line: Establishes the National Commission for Human Development to promote social sector development through collaboration with NGOs and government departments.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the National Commission for Human Development as a body corporate to implement social sector programmes. The Commission works in collaboration with philanthropists, Government line departments, and non-Governmental Organizations to support primary education, literacy, income-generating activities, and basic health care. It comprises a Chairman appointed by the President and five Members, ensuring provincial representation and gender equality. The Commission functions autonomously under the Cabinet Division, formulates policies, manages projects, and maintains accounts while receiving assistance from executive authorities across the Federation and Provinces.

name: National Commission for Human Rights Act, 2012

metadata.short_title: The National Commission for Human Rights Act, 2012
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of a National Human Rights Commission
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of Pakistan except Chapter V which shall extend to the Islamabad Capital Territory
metadata.one_line: Establishes the National Commission for Human Rights to promote and protect human rights in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the National Commission for Human Rights (NCHR) to promote and protect human rights as guaranteed by the Constitution and international instruments. The Commission consists of a Chairperson, members from each province and minority communities, and is headed by a Secretary appointed by the Commission itself. It has powers to conduct inquiries into complaints, establish Human Rights Courts, and make rules for its functioning, with provisions for financial independence and indemnity for its members.

name: National Commission for Minorities Rights Act, 2025

metadata.short_title: The National Commission for Minorities Rights Act, 2025
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for constitution of a National Commission for Minorities Rights
metadata.one_line: Establishes a National Commission for Minorities Rights to safeguard and promote the rights of minorities in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the National Commission for Minorities Rights to safeguard and promote the social, economic, political, and legal rights of minorities as defined under Article 260 of the Constitution. The Commission consists of a Chairperson, minority members nominated by Provincial Governments and the Chief Commissioner of Islamabad Capital Territory, and representatives from other national commissions. It is empowered to inquire into complaints, provide advice, manage its own fund, and make rules and regulations for its administration.

name: National Commission on the Rights of Child Act, 2017

metadata.short_title: The National Commission on the Rights of Child Act, 2017
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for constitution of a National Commission on the rights of child and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto
establishes: National Commission on the Rights of Child
metadata.administering_body: Federal Government (via Prime Minister and Division concerned)
metadata.one_line: Establishes the National Commission on the Rights of Child to protect child rights across Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the National Commission on the Rights of Child to exercise powers and perform functions related to child rights in accordance with international obligations. The Commission consists of a Chairperson, ex-officio members from various divisions, provincial representatives, and children, appointed by the Prime Minister. It provides for the constitution of the Commission, its secretariat in Islamabad, funding, accounts, audit procedures, and the power to make rules.

name: National Commission on the Status of Women Act, 2012

metadata.short_title: National Commission on the Status of Women Act, 2012
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the setting up of National Commission on the status of Women
repeals: National Commission on the Status of Women Ordinance, 2000 (XXVI of 2000)
establishes: National Commission on the Status of Women (NCSW)
metadata.one_line: Establishes the National Commission on the Status of Women to promote women's rights and repeals the 2000 Ordinance.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the National Commission on the Status of Women (NCSW) to promote social, economic, political, and legal rights of women in Pakistan. The Commission consists of a Chairperson, members from provinces and territories, ex-officio representatives, and a Secretary, with headquarters in Islamabad. It empowers the Commission to review federal laws affecting women, conduct research, and make recommendations for gender equality, while also defining its functions, financial control, and indemnity provisions.

metadata.short_title: The National Counter Terrorism Authority Act, 2013
metadata.long_title: An Act to establish National Counter Terrorism Authority in Pakistan
metadata.one_line: Establishes the National Counter Terrorism Authority to coordinate state response against terrorism and extremism.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the National Counter Terrorism Authority (NaCTA) as a body corporate to unify the state's response to terrorism and extremism. The Authority is tasked with collecting intelligence, formulating national strategies, developing action plans, and coordinating with international entities. It comprises a Board of Governors including federal secretaries and provincial representatives, along with an Executive Committee and appointed coordinators. The Federal Government retains power to issue binding directives on policy matters.

name: National Database and Registration Authority Ordinance (NADRA), 2000

metadata.short_title: The National Database and Registration Authority Ordinance, 2000
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the establishment of the National Database and Registration Authority so as to facilitate the registration of all persons and the establishment and maintenance of multipurpose databases, data warehouses, networking, interfacing of databases and related facilities
repeals: The National Registration Act, 1973 (LVI of 1973)
metadata.one_line: Establishes NADRA to manage national databases and issue identity cards across Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the National Database and Registration Authority (NADRA) to facilitate the registration of all persons in Pakistan. It provides for the creation of multipurpose databases, data warehouses, and networking systems to improve governance and reduce corruption. The Authority is empowered to issue various identity cards, including National Identity Cards and Alien Registration Cards, while managing funds and accounts separately from the Federal Consolidated Fund.

metadata.short_title: The National Defence University Act, 2011
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of the National DEFENCE University at Islamabad
metadata.commencement: at once; deemed to have taken effect on the 5th day of June, 2007
repeals: Government of Pakistan's Resolution, u.o No NDC/102/I/A, dated the 16th March 1971
metadata.one_line: Establishes the National Defence University at Islamabad and repeals the 1971 Resolution.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the National Defence University (NDU) as a body corporate with its principal seat in Islamabad. It defines the university's structure, including the Chancellor, Senate, Syndicate, and Academic Council, and outlines their powers and functions. The Act also provides for the establishment of a university fund, audit procedures, and rules regarding the appointment of teachers and officers. Additionally, it repeals the Government of Pakistan Resolution No. NDC/102/I/A dated 16th March 1971 and incorporates its assets and liabilities into the new university.

metadata.short_title: The National Development Volunteer Programme (Repeal) Ordinance, 1980
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to repeal the National Development Volunteer Programme Act, 1973
metadata.commencement: at once; deemed to have taken effect on the first day of June, 1980
repeals: The National Development Volunteer Programme Act, 1973 (XLIX of 1973)
metadata.status_evidence: An Ordinance to repeal the National Development Volunteer Programme Act, 1973
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance repeals the National Development Volunteer Programme Act, 1973 effective June 1, 1980.
metadata.summary: This Federal Ordinance was promulgated by the President on July 21, 1980, to immediately repeal the National Development Volunteer Programme Act, 1973. The text states that circumstances rendered immediate action necessary under the Proclamation of July 5, 1977. Although enacted in July, the Ordinance is deemed to have taken effect retroactively from June 1, 1980.

metadata.short_title: The National Disaster Management Act, 2010
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of a National Disaster Management System for Pakistan
metadata.administering_body: Ministry or Division of the Federal Government having administrative control of disaster management
metadata.one_line: Establishes a national disaster management system including commissions, authorities, and response forces across Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes a comprehensive National Disaster Management System for Pakistan to handle natural and man-made disasters. It creates structures at federal, provincial, and district levels, including the National Disaster Management Commission and Authority. The legislation defines key terms like 'disaster' and outlines powers for relief, rehabilitation, and emergency procurement while providing immunity for officials acting in good faith.

metadata.short_title: National Education Foundation Ordinance, 2002
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to establish the National Education Foundation for the purpose of carrying out the objectives of this Ordinance.
metadata.territorial_extent: the territories of Federal administered Areas as defined in section 2(i)
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Federal Government may notify in the official Gazette
repeals: National Education Foundation established under Notification S.R.O. No. 487(I)/97, dated 26-06-1997
metadata.one_line: Establishes the National Education Foundation to promote quality education in Federal Administered Areas through public-private partnerships.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the National Education Foundation as a body corporate to promote quality and gender-sensitive education in Federal Administered Areas. The Foundation operates through a Board of Governors and utilizes grants and loans to support private schools and NGOs, focusing on disadvantaged communities. It defines specific terms related to beneficiaries, teachers, and educational institutions, and repeals an earlier foundation established in 1997.

name: National Energy Efficiency and Conservation Act, 2016

metadata.short_title: The National Energy Efficiency and Conservation Act, 2016
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of institutions and enunciation of mechanisms and procedures so as to provide for effective conservation and efficient use of energy
repeals: The Federal Government's Resolution No. S.R.O. 4(KE)186, dated the 23rd December, 1986
subjects: National Energy Efficiency and Conservation Board
National Energy Efficiency and Conservation Authority
establishes: National Energy Efficiency and Conservation Board
National Energy Efficiency and Conservation Authority
metadata.max_penalty: fine
metadata.one_line: Establishes institutions to ensure effective conservation and efficient use of energy across Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the National Energy Efficiency and Conservation Board and Authority to manage energy conservation mechanisms. It defines key terms related to energy sectors, audits, and efficiency standards applicable nationwide. The Federal Government is empowered to issue energy saving certificates and specify energy values, while Provincial Governments assist in enforcement. The Act also dissolves ENERCON, transferring its assets and liabilities to the new Authority.

metadata.short_title: The National Excellence Institute Act, 2025
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of National Excellence Institute and for matters connected therewith and ancillary thereto
metadata.one_line: Establishes the National Excellence Institute as a body corporate with academic, financial and administrative autonomy.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the National Excellence Institute as a body corporate with perpetual succession. It grants the Institute academic, financial, and administrative autonomy, subject to the Higher Education Commission Act, 2002. The Act defines various authorities including the Board of Governors, Syndicate, and Academic Council, and provides for the making of Statutes, Regulations, and Rules. It also establishes an Institute Fund and includes provisions for indemnity for officers acting in good faith.

metadata.short_title: The National Forensics Agency Act, 2024
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for establishment of a National Forensics Agency
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment which may extend to one year or with fine which may extend to one hundred thousand Rupees or with both
metadata.one_line: Establishes the National Forensics Agency to conduct forensic examinations and render expert opinions for courts and authorities.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the National Forensics Agency as an independent body corporate with financial and administrative autonomy. The Agency is tasked with conducting conventional and digital forensics examinations, rendering expert opinions to courts and tribunals, and assisting in civil, criminal, corporate, and public matters. It defines various terms related to forensics, AI, and personnel, outlines the functions of its Board and Director General, and provides for the transfer of existing staff from the NFA Project to the new Agency.

name: National Fund for Cultural Heritage Act, 1994

metadata.short_title: The National Fund for Cultural Heritage Act, 1994
metadata.long_title: An Act to establish the National fund for Culture Heritage for conservation and preservation of Pakistan's national heritage and its proper maintenance and matters connected therewith or incidental thereto
repeals: The National Fund for Cultural Heritage Ordinance, 1994 (V of 1994)
metadata.administering_body: Ministry of Minorities, Culture, Sports, Tourism and Youth Affairs
metadata.one_line: Establishes the National Fund for Cultural Heritage to conserve Pakistan's national heritage through a Board of Governors.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the National Fund for Cultural Heritage to promote the conservation and preservation of Pakistan's national heritage. The Fund is financed by government grants, international aid, private contributions, and income from properties. It is managed by a Board of Governors comprising federal ministers, secretaries, and eminent professionals. The Act also provides tax exemptions for donations and repeals the previous Ordinance V of 1994.

metadata.short_title: The National Guards Act, 1973
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the constitution and discipline of the National Guards.
repeals: Mujahid Force Ordinance, 1965 (XXII of 1965)
establishes: Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education (as 'Board')
metadata.one_line: This Act provides for the constitution, discipline, and control of the Mujahid Force and Janbaz Force within the National Guards.
metadata.summary: The National Guards Act, 1973 establishes the legal framework for the constitution and discipline of the National Guards in Pakistan. It creates two primary forces: the Mujahid Force and the Janbaz Force, defining their personnel, enrolment, training, and discharge procedures. The Act applies to the whole of Pakistan and incorporates provisions from the Pakistan Army Act, 1952, while repealing the earlier Mujahid Force Ordinance, 1965.

metadata.short_title: The National Highway Authority Act, 1991
metadata.long_title: An Act to establish a National Highway Authority for planning, development, operation and maintenance of National Highways and strategic roads and to provide for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto
metadata.one_line: Establishes the National Highway Authority to plan, develop, operate and maintain national highways and strategic roads.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the National Highway Authority as a body corporate responsible for planning, development, operation, and maintenance of National Highways and strategic roads. The Authority is governed by a Council and an Executive Board, with its headquarters located in Islamabad. It provides for the appointment of officers, recruitment conditions, financial management including an Annual statement of accounts, and powers to acquire land and enter premises for highway construction.

metadata.short_title: The National Highways Safety Ordinance, 2000
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for safe driving on the national highways and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto
metadata.one_line: Provides for safe driving on national highways, defines terms, sets penalties for violations, and regulates vehicle registration.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance aims to ensure safe driving on national highways by defining key terms related to vehicles and drivers. It establishes rules for licensing, vehicle registration, and the cancellation of licenses or registration due to violations. The document also outlines specific offences with corresponding fines, ranging from Rs.150 to Rs.1000, covering issues like careless driving, improper parking, and interference with emergency vehicles.

metadata.short_title: The National Information Technology Board Act, 2022
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for establishment of National Information Technology Board
repeals: Ministry of Information Technology and Telecommunication's Notification No. 6(13)/2004-Dev, dated the 11th August, 2014
Cabinet Division's Office Memorandum No.4-1/2021-Min-I dated Islamabad, the 27th May, 2021
metadata.one_line: Establishes the National Information Technology Board to manage e-governance software applications across Federal Ministries and Divisions.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the National Information Technology Board (NITB) to facilitate e-governance across Pakistan. The Board will provide advisory services, consultancies, and software applications to Federal Ministries, Divisions, and autonomous bodies. Its primary goal is to focus on cross-cutting e-governance initiatives that can be replicated for better government-to-government and government-to-citizen services.

name: National Institute of Cardiovascular Diseases (Administration) Ordinance, 1979

metadata.short_title: The National Institute of Cardiovascular Diseases (Administration) Ordinance, 1979
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the proper administration of the affairs of the National Institute of Cardiovascular Diseases, Karachi.
establishes: National Institute of Cardiovascular Diseases (as a body corporate)
metadata.administering_body: Federal Government (via Ministry of Health, Social Welfare and Population)
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance establishes the National Institute of Cardiovascular Diseases as a body corporate and provides for its administration.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance provides for the proper administration of the National Institute of Cardiovascular Diseases in Karachi. It incorporates the Institute as a body corporate with perpetual succession and vests its powers in a Governing Body consisting of federal ministers, government officials, and nominated members. The document outlines the Institute's functions, including treatment, research, training, and international cooperation, while also regulating the terms of service for employees and officers.

metadata.short_title: The National Institute of Electronics Ordinance, 1979
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the establishment of a National Institute of Electronics.
metadata.one_line: Establishes the National Institute of Electronics to conduct research, development, and training in electronics across Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the National Institute of Electronics as a body corporate headquartered in Islamabad. The Institute is tasked with designing electronic components, conducting research, providing advanced training, and fostering international cooperation in the field of electronics. It operates under the directives of the Federal Government while being exempt from certain provisions of the Industrial Relations Ordinance, 1969.

name: National Institute of Folk and Traditional Heritage (Lok Virsa), Ordinance, 2002

metadata.short_title: The National Institute of Folk and Traditional Heritage (Lok Virsa) Ordinance, 2002
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for reconstitution of the National Institute of Folk and Traditional Heritage (Lok Virsa) to effectively preserve indigenous cultural heritage to project true identity of Pakistan
repeals: Government of Pakistan's Resolution No. F.10-11/82-Admn; dated the 19th June, 1983
establishes: National Institute of Folk and Traditional Heritage (Lok Virsa)
metadata.one_line: Reconstitutes the National Institute of Folk and Traditional Heritage to preserve indigenous cultural heritage.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance reconstitutes the National Institute of Folk and Traditional Heritage (Lok Virsa) as a body corporate with perpetual succession. It empowers the Institute to conduct research, preserve folklore, establish museums, and promote Pakistan's cultural identity through various programs and partnerships. The Federal Government retains the power to issue binding policy directives, while the Board of Governors oversees the Institute's affairs. Upon commencement, all previous assets and liabilities related to the Institute transfer to this new entity.

name: National Institute of Health (NIH) Ordinance, 1980 (Repealed by ACT No. XIII OF 2021 section 33 (w.e.f 29-07-2021))

metadata.short_title: The National Institute of Health Ordinance, 1980
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the establishment of the National Institute of Health.
repeals: National Health Laboratories
metadata.status_evidence: [Repealed by ACT No. XIII OF 2021 section 33 (w.e.f 29-07-2021)]
subjects: Transfer of employees from National Health Laboratories
metadata.one_line: Establishes the National Institute of Health as a body corporate for research, training, and disease control.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the National Institute of Health (NIH) as a body corporate with perpetual succession to conduct research on communicable diseases, produce vaccines, and train medical personnel. It defines the functions of the NIH, including advising the Federal Government on disease control and collaborating with international organizations like the WHO. The document also dissolves the existing National Health Laboratories and transfers their assets and employees to the new Institute, while empowering the Federal Government to make rules and regulations for its administration.

metadata.short_title: The National Institute of Health (Re-organization) Act, 2021
metadata.long_title: An Act to re-organize and create the National Institute of Health
repeals: The National Institute of Health Ordinance, 1980 (Ordinance XLIII of 1980)
The Pakistan Health Research Council Act, 2016 (XII of 2016)
establishes: center for environmental and occupational health
metadata.one_line: This Act re-organizes and establishes the National Institute of Health as an autonomous body to manage health research and disease control.
metadata.summary: The National Institute of Health (Re-organization) Act, 2021 creates an autonomous body corporate called the National Institute of Health (NIH). It establishes various institutes and centers for disease control, health research, and biological products under the NIH's authority. The Act also sets up a Board of Governors, defines financial management structures, and repeals previous legislation governing the National Institute of Health Ordinance, 1980 and the Pakistan Health Research Council Act, 2016.

metadata.short_title: The National Institute of Oceanography Act, 2007
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for establishment of the National Institute of Oceanography
metadata.one_line: Establishes the National Institute of Oceanography to conduct marine research and coordinate oceanographic activities in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the National Institute of Oceanography as a body corporate with perpetual succession. The Institute is tasked with conducting multi-disciplinary research, training programs, and maintaining a national data center for oceanographic information. It is managed by a Board of Governors comprising representatives from various government ministries, scientific institutions, and the armed forces. The Act also provides for tax exemptions and the power to make rules.

metadata.short_title: The National Institute of Technology Act, 2025
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for establishment of the National Institute of Technology in the private sector and for matters ancillary thereto
metadata.one_line: Establishes the National Institute of Technology as a private sector body corporate with perpetual succession.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the National Institute of Technology (NIT) as a body corporate in the private sector, with its principal seat at Lahore. It defines the institute's structure, including the Patron, Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, and various authorities like the Board of Governors and Academic Council. The Act outlines the powers and functions of these bodies, provisions for statutes and regulations, and the management of the Institute Fund.

metadata.short_title: The National Insurance Corporation (Reorganization) Ordinance, 2000
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for conversion of the National Insurance Corporation into a public limited company
repeals: National Insurance Corporation Act, 1976
metadata.one_line: Converts the National Insurance Corporation into a public limited company and repeals the 1976 Act.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance provides for the conversion of the National Insurance Corporation into a public limited company known as the National Insurance Company Limited. It vests all property, rights, and liabilities of the Corporation into the new Company and transfers eligible employees to the Company on existing terms. The legislation also grants an exemption from registration fees and allows the Company to operate without immediate registration under the Insurance Ordinance 2000 for one year.

name: National Insurance Corporation Act, 1976(Repeal by ord.37 of 200,s.9(when notified))

metadata.short_title: The National Insurance Corporation Act, 1976
metadata.long_title: An Act to establish a National Insurance Corporation.
metadata.status_evidence: [Repeal.] Omitted by the Federal Laws (Revision and Declaration) Ordinance, 1981 (XXVII of 1981), s. 3 and Sch., II.
metadata.one_line: Establishes the National Insurance Corporation to insure public property and manage related functions.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the National Insurance Corporation as a body corporate with perpetual succession. It provides for the corporation's capital, management by a Board of Directors appointed by the Federal Government, and its primary function of insuring public property. The Act also outlines powers to make rules and regulations, audit requirements, and provisions for the transfer of existing employees' services.

metadata.short_title: The National Investment (Unit) Trust Ordinance, 1965
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for certain matters relating to the National Investment (Unit) Trust and for matters connected therewith
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance regulates the National Investment (Unit) Trust, defining its units as transferable property and securities.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance provides for matters relating to the National Investment (Unit) Trust. It defines key terms such as the Management Company and Trustee, and establishes that Units are transferable movable property and approved securities. The Federal Government is empowered to authorize Bearer Certificates and make necessary rules.

metadata.short_title: The National Judicial (Policy Making) Committee Ordinance, 2002
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for National Judicial (Policy Making) Committee
metadata.administering_body: Law and Justice Commission of Pakistan
metadata.one_line: Establishes the National Judicial (Policy Making) Committee to coordinate judicial policy within the Court system.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the National Judicial (Policy Making) Committee, headed by the Chief Justice of Pakistan. The Committee is tasked with coordinating and harmonizing judicial policy, improving the administration of justice, and setting performance standards for judicial officers. It also handles finances provided by the Law and Justice Commission and publishes annual reports to the President.

metadata.short_title: The National Logistics Corporation Act, 2023
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of National Logistics Corporation
repeals: Planning and Development Division's Notification No. 2(2) Admn.1/70, dated the 9th November, 1979
Cabinet Division's Notification No.120/19/78-Min, dated the 12th August, 1978
establishes: Board of the National Logistics Corporation
metadata.one_line: Establishes the National Logistics Corporation to manage multi-modal logistics and infrastructure development across Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the National Logistics Corporation as a body corporate with perpetual succession to manage multi-modal logistics networks and infrastructure development. The Corporation functions under government policy guidelines, headed by a Director General, and includes powers to acquire property, sue, and engage in commercial activities both within and outside Pakistan. It also provides for the transfer of assets, rights, and employees from the former National Logistics Board and Cell to the new Corporation, while repealing specific earlier notifications.

name: National Metrology Institute of Pakistan Act, 2022

metadata.short_title: The National Metrology Institute of Pakistan Act, 2022
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of National Metrology Institute of Pakistan
repeals: Weights and Measures (International System) Act, 1967
any other law for the time being in force to the extent of the matters covered under this Act
metadata.one_line: Establishes the National Metrology Institute of Pakistan as an apex body for a unified national measurement system.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the National Metrology Institute of Pakistan (NMIP) as an apex body to implement a unified national measurement system. It defines the functions, management structure, and powers of the Institute, including its Board of Governors and Director-General. The Act also provides for the transfer of assets and liabilities from the former NPSL and repeals previous laws on weights and measures.

name: National Press Trust (Appointment of Chairman) Act, 1972

metadata.short_title: The National Press Trust (Appointment of Chairman) Act, 1972
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for appointment of the Chairman of the National Press Trust.
metadata.one_line: Provides for the appointment, tenure, and resignation of the Chairman of the National Press Trust.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the legal framework for appointing a Chairman to the National Press Trust. It grants the President the authority to appoint an individual of eminence, repute, and integrity to the role. The Act also outlines the Chairman's tenure at the pleasure of the President, their remuneration from the Trust Fund, and the procedure for resignation.

name: National Rahmatul-Lil-Aalameen Wa Khatamun Nabiyyin Authority Act, 2022

metadata.short_title: The National Rahmatul-Lil-Aalameen Wa Khatamun Nabiyyin Authority Act, 2022
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of National Rahmatul-Lil-Aalameen Wa Khatamun Nabiyyin Authority
subjects: National Rahmatul-Lil-Aalameen Wa Khatamun Nabiyyin Authority
establishes: National Rahmatul-Lil-Aalameen Wa Khatamun Nabiyyin Authority
metadata.one_line: Establishes the National Rahmatul-Lil-Aalameen Wa Khatamun Nabiyyin Authority to promote Seerat research and guide the youth.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the National Rahmatul-Lil-Aalameen Wa Khatamun Nabiyyin Authority to promote research on the Seerat of Prophet Muhammad and address contemporary social challenges. The Authority comprises a Chairperson, eight members, and an Advisory Board appointed by the Prime Minister. It grants the Authority powers to make rules and regulations, enjoy tax exemptions, and submit annual reports to Parliament.

name: National School of Public Policy Ordinance, 2002

metadata.short_title: The National School of Public Policy Ordinance, 2002
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the establishment of the National School of Public Policy and for matters ancillary therewith and connected thereto
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Federal Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, appoint
metadata.one_line: Establishes the National School of Public Policy in Islamabad to provide higher education, training, and research in public policy.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the National School of Public Policy as a body corporate headquartered in Islamabad. The School is empowered to conduct instruction, research, and training in various disciplines related to public administration and policy. It includes provisions for the composition of its Board of Governors, management of funds, and the merger of existing training organizations into the new entity.

metadata.short_title: The National Security Council Act, 2004
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of National Security Council
repeals: The National Security Council Order, 2001 (Chief Executive's Order No. 5 of 2001)
metadata.one_line: Establishes the National Security Council as a forum for consultation on national security matters and repeals the 2001 Order.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the National Security Council to serve as a forum for consultation on matters of national security, including sovereignty, integrity, defence, and crisis management. The Council is chaired by the President and includes key figures such as the Prime Minister, Chief Ministers, and Chiefs of Staff Committees. It formulates recommendations to the President and Government and can refer proposals of national importance to Parliament.

metadata.short_title: The National Skills University Islamabad Act, 2018
metadata.long_title: An Act to upgrade the status of National Institute of Science and Technical Education, Islamabad into National Skills University
repeals: Notification No.F.4-1/2004-F&A dated the December 29, 2004
metadata.one_line: This Act upgrades the National Institute of Science and Technical Education to the National Skills University Islamabad.
metadata.summary: The National Skills University Islamabad Act, 2018 upgrades the National Institute of Science and Technical Education, Islamabad to the status of a university. It establishes the university as a body corporate with its main campus in Islamabad and defines various authorities including the Senate, Syndicate, and Academic Council. The Act outlines the powers, purposes, and structure of the university, including provisions for staff appointments, student discipline, financial management, and the establishment of additional campuses.

metadata.short_title: The National Sports Trust (Repeal) Ordinance, 1980
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to repeal the National Sports Trust Act, 1972
repeals: The National Sports Trust Act, 1972
metadata.status_evidence: An Ordinance to repeal the National Sports Trust Act, 1972

metadata.summary: This Ordinance was promulgated by the President to immediately repeal the National Sports Trust Act, 1972. Upon repeal, all rights, properties, assets, debts, liabilities, and obligations of the National Sports Trust are transferred to the Pakistan Sports Board. Additionally, any contracts, legal proceedings, and functions previously performed by the Trust are deemed to have been made by or performed by the Board.

metadata.short_title: The National Tariff Commission Act, 2015
metadata.long_title: An Act to reform and repeal the National Tariff Commission Act, 1990
repeals: National Tariff Commission Act, 1990 (VI of 1990)
metadata.one_line: This Act reforms the National Tariff Commission, repeals the 1990 Act, and defines its functions regarding tariffs and trade remedies.
metadata.summary: The National Tariff Commission Act, 2015 was enacted to reform and repeal the National Tariff Commission Act, 1990. It establishes the National Tariff Commission as a body corporate with specific qualifications for members and outlines its functions to advise the Federal Government on tariff measures and trade remedies. The Act provides timelines for investigations, defines key terms like 'Trade Remedy Laws', and includes provisions for penalties and indemnity.

metadata.short_title: National Textile University Ordinance, 2002
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to set-up a National Textile University
metadata.one_line: Establishes the National Textile University as a body corporate for textile education and research.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the National Textile University at the national level to provide education and research facilities in textile technology. The University is constituted as a fully autonomous body corporate with perpetual succession, comprising various councils, committees, and staff members. It grants the University powers to determine courses, award degrees, conduct research, and manage its own funds and administration.

metadata.short_title: The National Training Ordinance, 1980

metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the National Training Board and Provincial Training Boards to regulate and promote vocational training. It defines key terms such as 'establishment' and 'industry', outlines the composition and functions of these boards, and provides for their funding and administration. The document also sets out penalties for non-compliance with board directives and empowers the boards to make regulations.

name: National University of Computer and Emerging Sciences Ordinance, 2000

metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the establishment of a National University of Computer and Emerging Sciences

metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the National University of Computer and Emerging Sciences as a body corporate to provide quality education in computer and emerging sciences. It defines the university's structure, including the Patron, Chancellor, Rector, Board of Trustees, and Board of Governors. The document outlines the powers for teaching, research, examinations, and faculty appointments, while also setting up committees for finance and planning.

name: National University of Medical Sciences Act, 2015

metadata.short_title: The National University of Medical Sciences Act, 2015
metadata.long_title: An Act to establish the National University of Medical Sciences
metadata.one_line: Establishes the National University of Medical Sciences and defines its structure, powers, and functions.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the National University of Medical Sciences to provide medical education and research facilities. It outlines the university's purposes, powers, and functions while ensuring it remains open to all classes and creeds. The legislation details the composition of governing bodies such as the Board of Governors, Syndicate, and Academic Council, along with provisions for staff appointments, student welfare, and examination conduct.

name: National University of Modern Languages Ordinance, 2000

metadata.short_title: The National University of Modern Languages Ordinance, 2000
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the establishment of the National University of Modern Languages at Islamabad

metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the National University of Modern Languages (NUML) at Islamabad as a fully autonomous body corporate. It empowers the University to determine courses, conduct examinations, award degrees, and pursue research in modern languages. The document also transfers assets, liabilities, and staff from the former National Institute of Modern Languages to the new University upon its commencement.

metadata.short_title: The National University of Pakistan Act, 2023
metadata.long_title: An Act to establish the national University of Pakistan
metadata.one_line: Establishes the National University of Pakistan and defines its structure, authorities, and functions.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the National University of Pakistan and provides for its establishment, powers, and functions. It outlines the composition and roles of various authorities including the Board, Syndicate, and Academic Council. The Act also details financial provisions, staff appointment procedures, and the framework for making statutes, regulations, and rules.

name: National University of Science and Technology Act (NUST) , 1997

repeals: The National University of Sciences and Technology Ordinance, 1996 (No.CI of 1996)
subjects: National University of Sciences and Technology
establishes: National University of Sciences and Technology
metadata.one_line: Establishes the National University of Sciences and Technology at Islamabad with autonomous powers for education and research.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the National University of Sciences and Technology (NUST) as a body corporate with perpetual succession. It grants the University autonomy to govern its academic and administrative functions, including determining courses, selecting students, awarding degrees, and conducting research. The Act defines the structure of the University, including the Chancellor, Board of Governors, and various councils, while repealing the previous 1996 Ordinance.

name: National Vocational and Technical Training Commission (NAVTTC) Act, 2011

metadata.short_title: The National Vocational and Technical Training Commission Act, 2011
metadata.long_title: An Act to Provide for regulation, coordination and policy direction for vocational and Technical Training
repeals: Cabinet Division's Notification No.4-16/2005-Min-I, dated the 30th December, 2005
National Training Ordinance, 1980 (IX of 1980)
establishes: National Vocational and Technical Training Commission
metadata.one_line: Establishes the National Vocational and Technical Training Commission to regulate and coordinate vocational and technical training in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes an autonomous organization called the National Vocational and Technical Training Commission to provide regulation, coordination, and policy direction for vocational and technical training. The Commission is a body corporate with its headquarters at Islamabad and is administratively attached to the Prime Minister's Secretariat. It consists of a Board comprising government secretaries, private sector representatives, and other members appointed by the Federal Government. The Act also repeals previous notifications and ordinances related to national training bodies and transfers their assets and staff to the new Commission.

name: National Zakat Foundation (Merger in Bait-ul-Mal) Ordinance, 2001

metadata.short_title: The National Zakat Foundation (Merger in the Bait-ul-Mal) Ordinance, 2001
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for merger of the National Zakat Foundation in the Bait-ul-Mal

metadata.summary: This Ordinance provides for the merger of the National Zakat Foundation into the Bait-ul-Mal. It vests all assets, properties, rights, and liabilities of the Foundation in the Bait-ul-Mal effective March 31, 2001. The document also details the transfer of employees to the Bait-ul-Mal or their termination with compensation, while ensuring pending legal proceedings continue against the merged entity.

metadata.short_title: The Natural Gas (Development Surcharge) Ordinance, 1967
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the levy and collection of a development surcharge on natural gas and for matters connected therewith.
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance levies a development surcharge on natural gas sales and sets maximum prices and penalties for violations.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance provides for the levy and collection of a development surcharge on natural gas sold by specified companies. It defines key terms such as 'fixed sale price' and 'differential margin', allows for income tax deductions on the surcharge paid, and sets maximum prices that companies cannot exceed. The document establishes offences for selling natural gas above the fixed price, punishable by imprisonment up to three years or fines, and grants the Federal Government powers to make rules and amend the schedule.

metadata.short_title: Natural Gas Regulatory Authority Ordinance, 2000
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the establishment of Natural Gas Regulatory Authority
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Natural Gas Regulatory Authority to regulate natural gas transportation and distribution in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Natural Gas Regulatory Authority to foster competition and improve efficiency in natural gas services. It applies to the whole of Pakistan and regulates activities including transmission, distribution, sale, and purification of natural gas. The Authority determines tariffs and prices, subject to review by the Federal Government, while defining key terms related to consumers, licensees, and existing companies.

metadata.short_title: The Naturalization Act, 1926
metadata.long_title: An Act to consolidate and amend the law relating to the naturalization in [Pakistan] of aliens resident therein.
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Federal Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, appoint
repeals: Indian Naturalization Act, 1852
metadata.one_line: Consolidates and amends the law regarding the naturalization of aliens resident in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Act consolidates and amends laws concerning the naturalization of aliens residing in Pakistan. It outlines the qualifications for granting a certificate of naturalization, including residency requirements and good character. The Act details the application process, the oath of allegiance required, and provisions for the revocation of certificates.

metadata.short_title: The Naval Armament Act, 1923
metadata.long_title: An Act to give effect in [Pakistan] to the Treaty for the Limitation of Naval Armament.
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Federal Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, appoint

metadata.one_line: Regulates the building and equipping of vessels of war in Pakistan to comply with naval armament treaties.
metadata.summary: This Act gives effect to the Treaty for the Limitation of Naval Armament signed in London in 1936. It restricts the building, altering, arming, or equipping of vessels of war without a licence granted by the Federal Government. The Act outlines procedures for seizing ships built in contravention of its provisions, defines offences and penalties, and establishes the authority of courts and officers to enforce these restrictions throughout Pakistan.

name: Naya Pakistan Housing and Development Authority Act (NPHDA), 2020

metadata.short_title: The Naya Pakistan Housing and Development Authority Act, 2020

metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Naya Pakistan Housing and Development Authority (NPHDA) to provide housing and facilitate real estate development. It grants the Authority powers to plan, construct, and manage various infrastructure projects on a profit or non-profit basis. The legislation also outlines the Authority's functions, administrative structure, financial provisions, and specific offences related to unauthorized construction or land use.

metadata.short_title: The Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881
metadata.long_title: An Act to define and amend the law relating to Promissory Notes, Bills of Exchange and Cheques
repeals: enactments listed in the Schedule
metadata.one_line: Defines and amends the law relating to promissory notes, bills of exchange, and cheques in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Act defines and amends the legal framework governing promissory notes, bills of exchange, and cheques. It establishes rules regarding their creation, negotiation, presentment for payment or acceptance, and discharge from liability. The legislation also covers procedures for dishonour, protest, noting, and the appointment of notaries public, applying to instruments made within or outside Pakistan.

name:

metadata.summary: This Ordinance provides for the transfer of the Network Analyser Study Centre, located in Lahore, from the Federal Government to the Pakistan Water and Power Development Authority (WAPDA). It details the financial terms of the asset transfer, stipulating that land ownership remains with the Federal Government while equipment costs are paid by WAPDA. The Ordinance also governs the transfer of existing civil servants employed at the Centre, allowing them to become employees of WAPDA or opt for termination with compensation.

name: New Energy Vehicles Adoption Levy Act, 2025

metadata.one_line: Imposes a levy on internal combustion engine vehicles to promote the adoption of new energy vehicles across Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Act imposes a levy on internal combustion engine motor vehicles manufactured or imported in Pakistan to encourage the adoption of new energy vehicles. The levy is collected similarly to import duties and sales tax, with proceeds used for promoting new energy vehicle adoption as determined by the Federal Government. It defines key terms such as 'new energy motor vehicle' and provides exemptions for diplomatic missions and export-only vehicles.

metadata.short_title: The Newspaper Employees (Conditions of Service) Act, 1973
metadata.long_title: An Act to repeal and, with certain amendments, re enact the Working Journalists (Conditions of Service) Ordinance, 1960
repeals: The Working Journalists (Conditions of Service) Ordinance, 1960
establishes: Board of Trustees for Provident Fund
metadata.one_line: This Act regulates the conditions of service, wages, leave, and termination for newspaper employees across Pakistan.
metadata.summary: The Newspaper Employees (Conditions of Service) Act, 1973 repeals and re-enacts the Working Journalists (Conditions of Service) Ordinance, 1960 with amendments. It applies to all newspaper establishments in Pakistan and covers conditions such as appointment orders, termination notice periods, provident fund contributions, working hours, leave entitlements, and wage fixation by a Board. The Act also establishes a Tribunal for disputes and grants rule-making powers to the Federal Government.

metadata.short_title: The Newsprint Control Ordinance, 1971
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for regulating the keeping, storage, distribution, disposal, acquisition and use of newsprint.

metadata.one_line: Regulates the keeping, storage, distribution, disposal, acquisition and use of newsprint in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance regulates the entire lifecycle of newsprint, including its storage, distribution, and usage for newspapers and other publications. It establishes a system where the Federal Government must grant prior permission for using newsprint after commencement, approves specific dealers, and fixes maximum prices for sales. The law requires importers and holders to declare their stock within seven days and maintain detailed records of all transactions related to newsprint.

name: NFC Institute of Engineering and Technology Multan Act, 2012

metadata.short_title: The NFC Institute of Engineering and Technology Multan Act, 2012
metadata.long_title: An Act to establish NFC Institute of Engineering and Technology Multan with degree awarding status to enhance the quality of higher education in the country and for matters connected therewith or ancillary thereto

metadata.summary: This Act establishes the NFC Institute of Engineering and Technology Multan to enhance higher education quality in Pakistan. It creates a governance structure including a Chancellor, Senate, Academic Council, and Syndicate to manage the institute's academic and administrative functions. The legislation also provides for the merger of existing entities into the new institute and repeals previous incorporation certificates.

name: Nippon Institute of Advanced Sciences Act, 2026

metadata.short_title: The Nippon Institute of Advanced Sciences Act, 2026
metadata.long_title: An Act to establish the Nippon Institute of Advanced Sciences
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Nippon Institute of Advanced Sciences with full academic and administrative autonomy.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Nippon Institute of Advanced Sciences in Sheikhupura as a body corporate with perpetual succession. It grants the Institute academic, financial, and administrative autonomy, allowing it to employ staff and manage property independently. The Act defines the structure of governing bodies including the Board of Governors, Syndicate, and Academic Council, outlining their powers and functions regarding teaching, research, and examinations.

name: Non-Performing Assets and Rehabilitation of Industrial Undertaking (Legal Proceedings) Ordinance, 2000

metadata.short_title: The Non-Performing Assets and Rehabilitation of Industrial Undertakings (Legal Proceedings) Ordinance, 2000
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for expeditious legal remedies for matters relating to non-performing assets and recovery of the outstanding amounts payable to banks and financial institutions to make them attractive for privatization and to promote the revitalization of nation's economy and rehabilitation and restructuring of industrial undertakings
metadata.one_line: Provides expeditious legal remedies for non-performing assets and recovery of amounts payable to banks and financial institutions.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes a framework for expeditious legal remedies regarding non-performing assets held by banks and financial institutions. It aims to recover outstanding amounts, make these assets attractive for privatization, and promote the revitalization of the national economy through restructuring and rehabilitation. The document grants exclusive civil and criminal jurisdiction to High Courts over claims and proceedings related to these assets, including provisions for appeals and asset sales.

metadata.short_title: The North-West Frontier Constabulary Act, 1915

metadata.summary: This Act provides for the regulation of the Frontier Constabulary within the North-West Frontier. It establishes the force under the Federal Government, defines the roles of Commandants and subordinate officers, and outlines their powers, duties, and punishments. The Act also covers matters such as pay, allowances, collective fines, and the application of criminal powers beyond the frontier limits.

metadata.short_title: The Notaries Ordinance, 1961

metadata.summary: This Ordinance provides for and regulates the profession of notaries in Pakistan. It establishes the power to appoint notaries, maintain registers, issue certificates of practice, and define the specific functions of notaries. The Ordinance also outlines penalties for falsely representing oneself as a notary and provisions for reciprocal arrangements with foreign countries.

metadata.short_title: The Oaths Act, 1873
metadata.long_title: An Act to consolidate the law relating to Judicial Oaths, and for other purposes.
repeals: law relating to official oaths, affirmations and declarations
metadata.status_evidence: Section 2: Rep. by the Repealing Act, 1873 (XII of 1873).
metadata.one_line: Consolidates laws regarding judicial oaths, affirmations, and the persons authorized to administer them.
metadata.summary: This Act consolidates the law relating to judicial oaths and affirmations while repealing previous laws on official oaths. It specifies which courts and persons are authorized to administer oaths, defines who must take them (witnesses, interpreters, jurors), and provides forms for Muslim and non-Muslim witnesses. The Act also ensures that proceedings are not invalidated by the omission of an oath or irregularities in its administration.

metadata.short_title: The Obstructions in Fairways Act, 1881
metadata.long_title: An Act to empower the Government to remove or destroy obstructions in fairways, and to prevent the creation of such obstructions.
metadata.one_line: Empowers the Federal Government to remove obstructions in fairways and regulate their creation.
metadata.summary: This Act empowers the Federal Government to remove or destroy obstructions, such as sunken vessels or fishing-stakes, that endanger navigation in fairways leading to ports. It provides for the recovery of expenses incurred in removal, the sale of unclaimed items, and compensation for lawful obstructions removed under the Act. The Federal Government is also authorized to make rules prohibiting the placement of obstructions.

name: Off the Grid (Captive Power Plants) Levy Act, 2025

metadata.short_title: The Off The Grid (Captive Power Plants) Levy Act, 2025
metadata.long_title: An Act to impose an off the grid levy on natural gas based captive power plants
metadata.one_line: Imposes a levy on natural gas consumption by captive power plants to fund reductions in electricity tariffs.
metadata.summary: This Act imposes an off-the-grid levy on captive power plants consuming natural gas or RLNG. The collected funds are utilized by the Federal Government to reduce power generation tariffs for all consumer categories. The levy rate is calculated based on the difference between industrial power tariffs and self-generation costs, with specific increases scheduled through 2026.

name: Offence of Qazf (Enforcement of Hadd) Ordinance, 1979

metadata.short_title: The Offence of Qazf (Enforcement of Hadd) Ordinance, 1979
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to bring in conformity with the injunctions of Islam the law relating to the offence of qazf
metadata.max_penalty: hadd (amputation)
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance enforces Islamic hadd punishment for false accusations of zina (qazf) across Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance modifies existing laws to align the offence of qazf with Islamic injunctions found in the Quran and Sunnah. It defines qazf as making a false imputation of zina against a person, particularly when done with intent to harm their reputation. The law prescribes hadd punishment for such offences committed against muhsan individuals and outlines strict proof requirements involving Muslim witnesses or confessions. It also specifies procedural aspects, including the requirement for a Muslim presiding officer and the application of the Code of Criminal Procedure.

name: Offence of Zina (Enforcement of Hudood) Ordinance,1979

metadata.short_title: The Offence of Zina (Enforcement of Hudood) Ordinance, 1979
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to bring in conformity with the Injunctions of Islam the law relating to the offence of zina.
repeals: Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898 (section 561)
metadata.max_penalty: stoning to death or whipping of one hundred stripes
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance enforces Islamic law regarding the offence of zina and prescribes punishments including stoning or whipping.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance modifies existing laws to align them with Islamic injunctions found in the Holy Quran and Sunnah concerning the offence of zina. It defines specific terms such as 'adult', 'hadd', and 'Muhsan' and establishes strict evidentiary requirements, including the need for four male witnesses or a confession, for imposing severe punishments like stoning or whipping. The Ordinance applies to the whole of Pakistan and mandates that trials be conducted by Courts of Session presided over by Muslim officers.

name: Offences Against Property (Enforcement of Hudood) Ordinance, 1979

metadata.short_title: The Offences Against Property (Enforcement of Hudood) Ordinance, 1979
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to bring in conformity with the injunctions of Islam the law relating to certain offences against property.
metadata.max_penalty: death or imprisonment for life
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance enforces Islamic hudood punishments for theft and haraabah across Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance modifies existing laws to align property offence penalties with Islamic injunctions from the Quran and Sunnah. It defines specific terms like 'Hirz' (property custody) and 'nisab' (value threshold) to distinguish between theft liable to 'hadd' (fixed punishment) and 'tazir' (discretionary punishment). The law applies to the whole of Pakistan, requires presiding officers to be Muslim unless the accused is not, and repeals conflicting provisions in other laws.

name: Offences in Respect of Banks (Special Courts) Ordinance, 1984

metadata.short_title: The Offences in Respect of Banks (Special Courts) Ordinance, 1984
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for speedy trial of certain offences committed in respect of banks and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of Pakistan and also applies to the business of a bank transacted outside Pakistan
metadata.one_line: Establishes special courts for the speedy trial of offences committed in respect of banks.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance provides for the establishment of Special Courts to ensure the speedy trial of specific offences committed against banks. It defines key terms such as 'bank' and 'scheduled offence', outlines the procedure for transferring pending cases to these special courts, and grants them specific powers including restrictions on the accused leaving Pakistan. The Ordinance also includes provisions for indemnity for persons acting in good faith under it and states that its provisions override other laws.

metadata.short_title: The Official Secrets Act, 1923
metadata.long_title: An Act to consolidate and amend the law in Pakistan relating to official secrets.
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both

metadata.summary: This Act consolidates and amends the law in Pakistan regarding official secrets. It defines various terms such as documents, intelligence agencies, and prohibited places, while establishing offences for actions prejudicial to public order or state safety. The legislation outlines penalties including imprisonment and fines, and provides powers for search warrants and restricting public access to trials.

metadata.short_title: The Official Trustees Act, 1913

The Act outlines the fees payable to the trustee, the audit process for their accounts, and the rules governing their administration of trust property across the whole of Pakistan.

name: Oil and Gas Development Corporation (Re-Organization) Ordinance, 2001

name: Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Amendment) Ordinance, 2026

name: Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (OGRA) Ordinance , 2002
