name: Organization of the Islamic Conference (Immunities and Privileges) Act, 1977

metadata.short_title: The Organization of the Islamic Conference (Immunities and Privileges) Act, 1977
metadata.long_title: An Act to give effect in Pakistan to the Agreement on Immunities and Privileges of the Organization of the Islamic Conference.
metadata.one_line: This Act gives effect in Pakistan to the Agreement on Immunities and Privileges of the Organization of the Islamic Conference.
metadata.summary: The Act provides legal capacity, immunities, and privileges to the Organization of the Islamic Conference and its representatives within Pakistan. It grants exemptions from taxes, customs duties, and legal processes for the organization's property and assets, while ensuring inviolability of premises and archives. The legislation also facilitates official communications, travel, and dispute settlement mechanisms consistent with the international agreement.

name: PAF Air War College Institute Act, 2021

metadata.short_title: The PAF Air War College Institute Act, 2021
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for re-organization of the Pakistan Air Force Air War College as a degree awarding institute
metadata.one_line: Re-organizes the PAF Air War College into a premier degree awarding institute for defence and security studies.
metadata.summary: This Act re-organizes the Pakistan Air Force Air War College into a premier degree awarding institute focused on defence and security studies. It establishes a corporate body comprising a Patron, Chancellor, Senate, President, and various academic authorities like the Academic Council and Syndicate. The legislation defines the powers, functions, and composition of these bodies while providing for the institute's fund, audit, and transitory provisions to manage pending cases from previous affiliations.

name: Pakistan (Army and Air Force) Reserves Act, 1950

metadata.short_title: The Pakistan (Army and Air Force) Reserves Act, 1950
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the constitution and discipline of the Pakistan Army and Air Force Reserves.
repeals: law relating to the government and discipline of the Pakistan Army and Air Force Reserves
metadata.one_line: This Act provides for the constitution and discipline of Pakistan Army and Air Force Reserves.
metadata.summary: The Pakistan (Army and Air Force) Reserves Act, 1950 consolidates and amends laws regarding the government and discipline of military reserves. It defines categories of reservists, outlines their liability to service within and outside Pakistan, and empowers the Federal Government to make rules and regulations concerning training, pay, and appointments. The Act also specifies that reservists are subject to specific Army and Air Force Acts for disciplinary purposes.

metadata.short_title: The Pakistan (Exchange of Prisoners) Ordinance, 1948
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to implement an agreement with India regarding the exchange of certain classes of prisoners between Pakistan and India.
metadata.territorial_extent: the Punjab, the North-West Frontier and Baluchistan (extendable to other parts of Pakistan by notification)
metadata.commencement: at once in the Punjab, the North-west Frontier and Baluchistan; on such date as the Government of the Province concerned may specify for any other part
metadata.one_line: An Ordinance to implement an agreement with India regarding the exchange of certain classes of prisoners.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance implements an agreement between Pakistan and India for the exchange of specific classes of prisoners. It grants Provincial Governments the power to order the removal and transfer of prisoners to India, while avoiding the jurisdiction of Pakistani courts over these individuals during transit. The document also outlines procedures for repatriating prisoners, including custody arrangements, bail provisions, and the reconstruction of missing warrants. It defines key terms such as 'transferable prisoner' and 'repatriated prisoner' and empowers the government to make rules regarding communication channels and specifications.

metadata.short_title: The Pakistan Academy of Letters' Act, 2013
metadata.long_title: An Act to establish the Pakistan Academy of Letters
repeals: The Ministry of Education's Resolution No. 8-18/75/Cb, dated the 7th July, 1976
metadata.one_line: This Act establishes the Pakistan Academy of Letters as an autonomous body to promote Pakistani language and literature.
metadata.summary: The Pakistan Academy of Letters' Act, 2013 establishes the Pakistan Academy of Letters as a corporate autonomous body with its main office in Islamabad. The Act creates a Board of Governors comprising representatives from various ministries, provinces, and linguistic communities to oversee the Academy's policies and functions. It provides for the establishment of funds, appointment of employees, audit procedures, and repeals a previous resolution regarding the Academy.

metadata.short_title: The Pakistan Aeronautical Complex Board Ordinance, 2000
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to establish the Pakistan Aeronautical Complex Board Kamra and to provide for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Pakistan Aeronautical Complex Board Kamra to manage and reorganize factories for national defence needs.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Pakistan Aeronautical Complex Board Kamra to manage, organize, and run existing factories on sound commercial lines. The Board is empowered to administer factory affairs, determine employee service terms, and meet defence requirements during war and peace. It operates under the directions of the Federal Government regarding national interest and policy.

metadata.short_title: The Pakistan Agricultural Research Council Ordinance, 1981
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for constituting and re-organizing the Pakistan Agricultural Research Council.
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance establishes the Pakistan Agricultural Research Council and defines its functions, management, and finance.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance provides for the constitution and re-organization of the Pakistan Agricultural Research Council. It establishes the Council as a body corporate with powers to undertake agricultural research, arrange training, and manage funds. The document outlines the structure of the Board of Governors, the functions of the Executive Committee, and financial provisions including borrowing power and tax exemptions.

metadata.short_title: The Pakistan Air Force Act, 1953
metadata.long_title: An Act to consolidate the law relating to the Pakistan Air Force.
metadata.max_penalty: death
metadata.one_line: Consolidates laws relating to the Pakistan Air Force, defining service conditions, offences, punishments, and courts-martial procedures.
metadata.summary: This Act consolidates the law relating to the Pakistan Air Force, establishing its structure, personnel rules, and disciplinary framework. It defines various ranks and roles, outlines conditions of service including tenure and termination, and lists numerous military offences with corresponding punishments. The Act also provides for the constitution and powers of different types of courts-martial and grants the Federal Government power to make regulations.

metadata.short_title: The Pakistan Air Safety Investigation Act, 2023
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for better investigation of accidents and other incidents arising out of navigation of aircrafts and for matters connected therewith and ancillary thereto
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of Pakistan and also apply to citizens of Pakistan wherever they may be; aircraft registered in Pakistan wherever they may be; aircraft registered outside Pakistan but for the time being in or over Pakistan; persons on such aircraft; and aircraft operated by a person who is not a citizen of Pakistan but has his principal place of business or residence in Pakistan
repeals: section 7 of the Civil Aviation Ordinance, 1960 (Ordinance XXXII of 1960) and the rules made thereunder in relation to the subject matter of this Act
metadata.one_line: This Act establishes the Bureau of Aircraft Safety Investigations to investigate accidents and incidents involving aircraft in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: The Pakistan Air Safety Investigation Act, 2023 provides a legal framework for investigating accidents and incidents involving aircraft within Pakistan. It establishes the Bureau of Aircraft Safety Investigations and defines its powers, duties, and functions regarding evidence preservation, investigation reports, and international cooperation. The Act also outlines various offences related to obstructing investigations or withholding information, along with provisions for an Air Safety Fund and indemnity for officials.

metadata.short_title: The Pakistan Airports Authority Act, 2023
metadata.long_title: An Act to establish the Pakistan Airports Authority for better administration, operation and development of airports and air transport services in Pakistan.
metadata.commencement: at once on the expiry of one hundred and eighty days from the date of notification if no date is appointed, otherwise on such date as the Federal Government may notify
repeals: Civil Aviation Ordinance, 1960 (XXXII of 1960)
Pakistan Civil Aviation Authority Ordinance, 1982 (XXX of 1982)
establishes: Board of the Pakistan Airports Authority
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Pakistan Airports Authority to administer, operate, and develop airports and air transport services in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Pakistan Airports Authority for the administration, operation, and development of airports and air transport services. It defines the Authority's structure, including its Board, Executive Committee, and Director General, and outlines its functions and powers. The Act also covers financial provisions, offences and penalties related to airport operations, and repeals previous aviation ordinances.

name: Pakistan Animal Quarantine (Import and Export of Animals and Animal Products) Ordinance, 1979

metadata.short_title: The Pakistan Animal Quarantine (Import and Export of Animals and Animal Products) Ordinance, 1979
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to regulate the import, export and quarantine of animals and animal products
repeals: section 15 of the Pakistan Animal Quarantine (Import and Export of Animals and Animal Products) Ordinance, 1979
metadata.one_line: Regulates the import, export, and quarantine of animals and animal products to prevent disease spread.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance regulates the import, export, and quarantine of animals and animal products in Pakistan to prevent the introduction or spread of diseases. It empowers the Federal Government to issue notifications prohibiting or restricting trade based on health risks and designates specific points of entry and exit. The Quarantine Officer is authorized to inspect, detain, test, and manage animals and products in quarantine facilities.

name: Pakistan Armed Forces Nursing Service Act, 1952

metadata.short_title: The Pakistan Armed Forces Nursing Service Act, 1952
metadata.long_title: An Act to constitute a force to be called the [Pakistan Armed Forces Nursing Service] and to provide for its discipline.
metadata.one_line: Constitutes the Pakistan Armed Forces Nursing Service and provides for its discipline and organization.
metadata.summary: This Act constitutes a force designated as the Pakistan Armed Forces Nursing Service, which is part of the Armed Forces of Pakistan. It establishes that all members must hold commissioned rank and are appointed by the Federal Government via notification in the official Gazette. The Act applies to members wherever they may be and provides for rules and regulations regarding their organization, pay, duties, discipline, training, and leave.

metadata.short_title: The Pakistan Arms Ordinance, 1965
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to consolidate and amend the law relating to the sale, transport; bearing or possession of arms, ammunition or military stores
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of Pakistan except the Tribal Areas
repeals: The Arms Act 1878 (XI of 1878), as in force in the Province of West Pakistan, together with all enactments amending or modifying the same, except the provisions thereof relating to manufacture (including conversion), export or import of arms, ammunition and military stores
metadata.one_line: Consolidates and amends laws regarding the sale, transport, bearing, and possession of arms and ammunition in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance consolidates and amends the law relating to the sale, transport, bearing, or possession of arms, ammunition, or military stores. It prohibits unlicensed sale, repair, transport, and possession of arms while establishing a licensing framework for public servants and members of non-regular forces. The document defines key terms such as 'arms', 'ammunition', and 'cannon' broadly to include various weapons and explosives, and outlines penalties for breaches of these provisions.

metadata.short_title: The Pakistan Army Act, 1952
metadata.long_title: An Act to consolidate the law relating to the Pakistan Army.
establishes: Chief of the Army Staff concurrently the Chief of the Defense Forces
Commander of the National Strategic Command
metadata.max_penalty: death
metadata.one_line: Consolidates laws relating to the Pakistan Army, covering enrolment, discipline, offences, courts martial, and pay.
metadata.summary: This Act consolidates the law relating to the Pakistan Army. It defines who is subject to the Act, outlines procedures for appointment, enrolment, and termination of service, and details punishments and offences. The Act establishes various types of courts martial and provisions for provost marshals, while also regulating pay, allowances, and the powers of commanding officers.

metadata.short_title: The Pakistan Atomic Energy Commission Ordinance, 1965
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the establishment of an Atomic Energy Commission.
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Pakistan Atomic Energy Commission to promote peaceful uses of atomic energy.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Pakistan Atomic Energy Commission (PAEC) as a body corporate with perpetual succession. It empowers the Commission to acquire property, sue and be sued, and manage funds for the promotion of peaceful atomic energy uses and international obligations. The text defines key terms such as 'Atomic energy' and 'special nuclear material', outlines the composition of the Commission appointed by the Federal Government, and provides powers to make rules and regulations. It also facilitates the transfer of assets, liabilities, and employees from the dissolved Pakistan Atomic Energy Council to the new Commission.

metadata.short_title: The Pakistan Bait-ul-Mal Act, 1991
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for establishment of a Bait ul Mal
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Bait ul Mal fund and Board to provide financial assistance to destitute widows, orphans, and needy persons.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes a welfare fund known as Bait ul Mal to be administered by a specifically constituted Board. The fund is financed through tax receipts, government grants, voluntary donations, and asset sales to assist destitute widows, orphans, invalids, and other needy individuals. The Board manages the administration of the fund, maintains accounts subject to audit, and utilizes resources for rehabilitation, education, medical treatment, and self-employment schemes.

name: Pakistan Banking (Prevention of Default and Evasion of labilities) Ordinance, 1947

metadata.short_title: The Pakistan Banking (Prevention of Default and Evasion of Liabilities) Ordinance, 1947
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for prevention of loss to people in Pakistan from the withholding of payments of cheques and delivery of things held in safe custody by banks acting under directions issued by a Government or authority outside Pakistan.
metadata.status_evidence: Omitted by A.O., 1961, Art. 2 and Sch., (with effect from the 23rd March, 1956).
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment which may extend to three years or with fine or with both
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance prevents Pakistani banks from complying with external government instructions to stop cheque payments or withhold assets.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance was enacted to prevent banking concerns in Pakistan from defaulting on their commitments due to external pressure. It prohibits banks from acting on instructions from foreign governments regarding cheque payments, deposit deliveries, or other banking business without prior approval from the Federal Government. The document grants the Federal Government powers to demand explanations, inspect bank books, search premises, prohibit asset removal, and seize assets to cover liabilities arising from wrongful withholding of payments.

name: Pakistan Banking and Finance Services Commission Act, 1992

metadata.short_title: The Pakistan Banking and Finance Services Commission Act, 1992
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of a Banking and Finance Services Commission
establishes: Pakistan Banking and Finance Services Commission
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Pakistan Banking and Finance Services Commission to regulate recruitment in financial institutions.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Pakistan Banking and Finance Services Commission to ensure a sound basis for recruiting officers in financial institutions. The Commission conducts competitive examinations, interviews, and tests for various grades within these institutions while advising the Federal Government on recruitment qualifications. It also manages its own funds, appoints necessary officers, and submits annual reports to the President.

metadata.short_title: The Pakistan Boy Scouts Association Ordinance, 1959
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to incorporate the Pakistan Boy Scouts Association and to provide for certain matters connected therewith.
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Federal Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, appoint
subjects: Exclusive rights to titles and uniforms
metadata.max_penalty: fine
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance incorporates the Pakistan Boy Scouts Association and grants it exclusive rights to titles and uniforms.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance incorporates the Pakistan Boy Scouts Association as a body corporate with perpetual succession. It grants the Association exclusive rights to use specific emblems, badges, uniforms, and titles containing the word 'Scouts'. The Ordinance also establishes penalties for contravention of these exclusive rights and allows the Federal Government to prescribe rules regarding the Association's constitution.

metadata.short_title: The Pakistan Broadcasting Corporation Act, 1973
metadata.long_title: An Act to establish a Pakistan Broadcasting Corporation
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Pakistan Broadcasting Corporation as a body corporate with perpetual succession.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Pakistan Broadcasting Corporation to ensure effective operation and growth of broadcasting as a public service medium. It creates a Board of Directors comprising independent members, government nominees, and representatives from various divisions to manage the corporation's administration and programs. The Act outlines the corporation's financial powers, including budget approval, borrowing authority, and audit requirements, while also providing for the transfer of assets and liabilities from Radio Pakistan.

metadata.short_title: The Pakistan Citizenship Act, 1951
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for Pakistan citizenship
metadata.max_penalty: punishable under section 177 of the Pakistan Penal Code (Act XLV of 1860)
metadata.one_line: This Act provides for the acquisition, deprivation, and regulation of Pakistan citizenship.
metadata.summary: The Pakistan Citizenship Act, 1951 establishes the legal framework for determining who is a citizen of Pakistan. It defines citizenship based on birth, descent, migration, naturalisation, and incorporation of territory, while also regulating dual nationality and the status of married women. The Act outlines procedures for registration, certificates of domicile, and penalties for making false statements to obtain citizenship.

metadata.short_title: The Pakistan Civil Aviation Act, 2023
metadata.long_title: An Act to consolidate and amend the law for better regulation and control of civil aviation and to confer certain duties and powers on the Authority of the service
repeals: Ordinance XXXII of 1960
Ordinance XXX of 1982
metadata.max_penalty: Upto Rupees ten million and rupees five hundred thousand for each day if the violation continues after imposition of penalty
metadata.one_line: This Act consolidates and amends laws regulating civil aviation, establishing the Authority and setting penalties for offences.
metadata.summary: The Pakistan Civil Aviation Act, 2023 consolidates and amends existing laws to regulate and control civil aviation in Pakistan. It establishes the Pakistan Civil Aviation Authority, defines its functions and powers, and sets out requirements for aircraft registration, air service licences, and airport operations. The Act also outlines offences related to aviation safety and security, along with corresponding administrative penalties.

metadata.short_title: The Pakistan Civil Aviation Authority Ordinance, 1982
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to establish a Civil Aviation Authority
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Civil Aviation Authority to regulate civil aviation activities and develop air transport infrastructure in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Civil Aviation Authority as a body corporate to regulate and control civil aviation activities in Pakistan. It empowers the Authority to manage airports, provide air traffic services, and develop infrastructure for safe and efficient air transport. The Federal Government retains policy-making power and can issue binding directives to the Authority.

metadata.short_title: The Pakistan Climate Change Act, 2017
metadata.long_title: An Act to meet Pakistan's obligations under international conventions relating to climate change and address the effects of climate change.
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Pakistan Climate Change Council, Authority and Fund to address climate change effects.
metadata.summary: This Act fulfills Pakistan's international obligations regarding climate change by establishing a comprehensive framework for adaptation and mitigation. It creates the Pakistan Climate Change Council chaired by the Prime Minister, the Pakistan Climate Change Authority to manage funds and projects, and the Pakistan Climate Change Fund. The legislation defines key terms like 'climate change' and 'greenhouse gas', empowers the Authority to sanction financial assistance, and ensures the Act overrides inconsistent laws.

metadata.short_title: The Pakistan Coast Guards Act, 1973
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the constitution and regulation of the Pakistan Coast Guards.
metadata.territorial_extent: all members of the Pakistan Coast Guards wherever they may be serving
establishes: Deputy Director General, Pakistan Coast Guards
metadata.one_line: This Act constitutes and regulates the Pakistan Coast Guards to prevent smuggling, illegal immigration, and enhance coastal security.
metadata.summary: The Pakistan Coast Guards Act, 1973 provides for the constitution, regulation, and administration of the Pakistan Coast Guards Force. It empowers the Federal Government to establish the force with specific functions including preventing smuggling, stopping illegal immigration, countering enemy infiltration, and supplementing national defence. The Act outlines the appointment of officers and staff, their pay and privileges, disciplinary measures under the Pakistan Army Act, 1952, and the form of affirmation required for members.

metadata.short_title: The Pakistan Coinage Act
metadata.long_title: An Act to consolidate and amend the law relating to Coinage and the Mint.
repeals: The Schedule
metadata.one_line: Consolidates and amends laws relating to coinage, mints, legal tender, and counterfeit coins in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Act consolidates and amends the law regarding coinage and mints within Pakistan. It defines terms related to coin alteration, establishes the power of the Federal Government to create or abolish mints, and specifies denominations and designs for coins. The legislation also outlines procedures for handling diminished, defaced, or counterfeit coins and bars suits against officials acting in good faith under the Act.

name: Pakistan College of Physicians and Surgeons Ordinance, I962

metadata.short_title: Pakistan College of Physicians and Surgeons Ordinance, 1962
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to establish a College of Physicians and Surgeons in Pakistan.
establishes: Pakistan College of Physicians and Surgeons
metadata.administering_body: Federal Government (initial appointments) and the Council of the College
metadata.one_line: Establishes a corporate body to promote specialist medical practice, post-graduate training, and research in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Pakistan College of Physicians and Surgeons as a body corporate with perpetual succession. It defines the composition of the College through Fellows appointed by the Federal Government or elected/appointed by the Council. The College's functions include promoting specialist practice, arranging post-graduate training, conducting examinations, and facilitating research. A Council is constituted to manage affairs, comprising members appointed by the Federal Government and provincial governments, with powers to appoint officers, hold exams, and make rules.

name: Pakistan Commissions of Inquiry Act, 1956(Repeal by act iX of 2017 s.19)

metadata.short_title: The Pakistan Commissions of Inquiry Act, 1956
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the appointment of Commissions of Inquiry and for vesting such Commissions with certain powers.
repeals: Ordinance XXIV of 1955
metadata.one_line: Provides for the appointment and powers of Commissions of Inquiry into matters of public importance.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the framework for appointing Commissions of Inquiry to investigate definite matters of public importance. It vests these commissions with the powers of a Civil Court, including summoning witnesses, receiving evidence, and punishing contempt. The Federal Government is empowered to appoint single or multi-member commissions and can extend the Act's provisions to other inquiring authorities.

metadata.short_title: The Pakistan Commissions of Inquiry Act, 2017
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for constitution of Commissions of Inquiry and to provide for matters connected therewith and ancillary thereto
repeals: The Pakistan Commissions of Inquiry Act, 1956 (VI of 1956)
metadata.one_line: This Act provides for the constitution, powers, and procedure of Commissions of Inquiry constituted by the Federal Government.
metadata.summary: The Pakistan Commissions of Inquiry Act, 2017 establishes the framework for constituting Commissions of Inquiry into matters of public importance by the Federal Government. It grants these commissions extensive powers similar to civil courts, including summoning witnesses, seizing documents, ordering police investigations, and punishing contempt. The Act mandates that final reports be made public within thirty days unless the Commission recommends otherwise in the public interest.

name: Pakistan Council for Science and Technology Act, 2017

metadata.short_title: The Pakistan Council for Science and Technology Act, 2017
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for establishment of the Pakistan Council for Science and Technology
repeals: Ministry of Science and Technology's Resolution notified vide No. 3(5)/82-NSC, dated the 16th June, 1987
establishes: Pakistan Council for Science and Technology
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Pakistan Council for Science and Technology to advise on national science, technology, and innovation policies.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Pakistan Council for Science and Technology as a body corporate to advise the Federal Government on science and technology policies. The Council is tasked with policy research, identifying priority areas for development, and promoting collaboration between academia, industry, and international organizations. It includes provisions for the composition of its Board of Governors, management structure, financial regulations, and the transfer of assets and personnel from a previously dissolved council.

name: Pakistan Council of Architects and Town Planners Ordinance, 1983

metadata.short_title: The Pakistan Council of Architects and Town Planners Ordinance, 1983
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to make provisions for the regulation of architectural and town planning professions.
establishes: Pakistan Council of Architects and Town Planners
key_definitions: architectural and town planning public organisation
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance regulates architectural and town planning professions by constituting a Council to oversee registration and conduct.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Pakistan Council of Architects and Town Planners to regulate the architectural and town planning professions in Pakistan. It defines the composition of the Council, including a Chairman and Vice Chairmen nominated by the Federal Government, and outlines the process for registering architects and town planners who hold specified qualifications. The document also empowers the Council to frame bye-laws and a Code of Professional Conduct, recognize foreign qualifications, and impose penalties for infractions.

name: Pakistan Council of Research in Water Resources Act, 2007

metadata.short_title: The Pakistan Council of Research in Water Resources Act, 2007
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for establishment of the Pakistan Council of Research in Water Resources
repeals: Ordinance XCI of 2002
establishes: Pakistan Council of Research in Water Resources
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Pakistan Council of Research in Water Resources to conduct and promote water resources research across Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Pakistan Council of Research in Water Resources as a body corporate with perpetual succession. The Council is tasked with conducting, coordinating, and promoting research on all aspects of water resources, including irrigation, drainage, flood control, and drinking water supply. It also functions to design conservation technologies, maintain a national database, and advise the government on water policy. The Act empowers the Federal Government to make rules for the Council's administration and specifies that the Council shall not be liable for income tax.

name: Pakistan Council of Scientific and Industrial Research Act, 1973

metadata.short_title: The Pakistan Council of Scientific and Industrial Research Act, 1973
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of a Pakistan Council of Scientific and Industrial Research.
establishes: Pakistan Council of Scientific and Industrial Research
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Pakistan Council of Scientific and Industrial Research to promote technological research and development.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Pakistan Council of Scientific and Industrial Research as a body corporate with perpetual succession. The Council is tasked with setting up and managing technological research institutes, coordinating research work, and promoting overall technological development in Pakistan. It defines the composition of the Council, including members from the Federal Government, industries, and scientific sectors, and outlines their terms of office and functions.

metadata.short_title: The Pakistan Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958
metadata.long_title: An Act to repeal and re-enact, with certain amendments, the Pakistan Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1948.
amends: The Pakistan Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1948
repeals: The Pakistan Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1948
metadata.one_line: This Act repeals and re-enacts the 1948 Amendment to establish Special Judges for speedy trials of corruption and other offences.
metadata.summary: The Pakistan Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 repeals and re-enacts the 1948 Act with amendments to provide for the speedy trial and effective punishment of specific offences. It establishes Special Judges appointed by the appropriate Government to try cases within designated territorial limits. The Act defines key terms such as 'appropriate Government' and 'public servant', outlines the jurisdiction of Special Judges, and specifies that certain offences under the Pakistan Penal Code and Prevention of Corruption Act are triable exclusively by these judges.

metadata.short_title: The Pakistan Currency Act, 1950
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the issue and putting into circulation of Government of Pakistan one-rupee notes
repeals: Pakistan Currency Ordinance, 1948 (XIII of 1948)
metadata.one_line: Provides for the issue and circulation of Government of Pakistan one-rupee notes as legal tender.
metadata.summary: This Act authorizes the Federal Government to issue and circulate one-rupee notes which serve as legal tender in Pakistan. It extends to the whole of Pakistan and applies provisions regarding counterfeiting from the Pakistan Penal Code to these notes. The Act also defines a 'Pakistan one-rupee note' as any such note issued by the Government of Pakistan.

name: Pakistan Electronic Media Regulatory Authority Ordinance (PEMRA), 2002

metadata.short_title: The Pakistan Electronic Media Regulatory Authority Ordinance, 2002
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to regulate electronic media in Pakistan
metadata.one_line: Establishes PEMRA to regulate electronic media, issue licenses, and ensure accountability in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Pakistan Electronic Media Regulatory Authority (PEMRA) to regulate electronic media in Pakistan. It aims to improve information standards, enlarge media choices for the public, facilitate grassroots devolution of power, and ensure transparency and good governance. The Authority is empowered to issue broadcast licenses, manage complaints through councils, impose fines, and make rules regarding media operations and ownership concentration.

metadata.short_title: The Pakistan Engineering Council Act, 1975
metadata.long_title: An Act to make provision for the regulation of the engineering profession and for that purpose to constitute an Engineering Council
metadata.one_line: This Act regulates the engineering profession in Pakistan by constituting an Engineering Council to set standards and license engineers.
metadata.summary: The Pakistan Engineering Council Act, 1975 establishes the Pakistan Engineering Council to regulate the engineering profession across the country. The Council is empowered to accredit engineering qualifications and institutions, grant temporary licenses, and maintain a register of professional engineers. It also sets up governing bodies like the Governing Body and Management Committee to oversee operations, enforce professional ethics, and conduct inquiries into complaints against engineers.

metadata.short_title: The Pakistan Environmental Protection Act, 1997
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the protection, conservation, rehabilitation and improvement of the environment, for the prevention and control of pollution, and promotion of sustainable development
repeals: Pakistan Environmental Protection Ordinance, 1983 (XXXVII of 1983)
metadata.one_line: This Act establishes the Pakistan Environmental Protection Council and Agency to protect the environment, control pollution, and promote sustainable development.
metadata.summary: The Pakistan Environmental Protection Act, 1997 provides a legal framework for the protection, conservation, and rehabilitation of the environment. It establishes the Pakistan Environmental Protection Council and the Federal Agency, along with Provincial Agencies, to enforce regulations on pollution, hazardous waste, and emissions. The Act defines key environmental terms, sets up tribunals for dispute resolution, and repeals the earlier 1983 Ordinance while saving existing rules and appointments.

metadata.short_title: The Pakistan Essential Services (Maintenance) Act, 1952
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the maintenance of certain essential services
metadata.territorial_extent: Pakistan (with specific extensions to Baluchistan and other areas mentioned in footnotes)
repeals: Ordinance XI of 1941
metadata.max_penalty: punishment provided for the offence (specific amount not stated in excerpts)
metadata.one_line: This Act maintains essential services by regulating employment, restricting movement, and defining offences for the Federal Government.
metadata.summary: The Pakistan Essential Services (Maintenance) Act, 1952 provides for the maintenance of certain essential services under the Federal Government. It applies to employments declared essential for national security or community life, allowing the government to order personnel to remain in specified areas and regulate wages. The Act defines offences related to disobedience, abandonment of employment, or unauthorized departure from designated areas, prescribing penalties and restricting legal proceedings against those acting in good faith under the Act.

name: Pakistan Fish Inspection and Quality Control Act, 1997

metadata.short_title: The Pakistan Fish Inspection and Quality Control Act, 1997
metadata.long_title: An Act to regulate quality and promote export of fish and fishery products from Pakistan
metadata.one_line: This Act regulates the quality and export of fish products in Pakistan through registration and inspection.
metadata.summary: The Pakistan Fish Inspection and Quality Control Act, 1997 was enacted to regulate quality standards and promote the export of fish and fishery products from Pakistan. It establishes an Inspection Committee comprising representatives from the Export Promotion Bureau, Marine Fisheries Department, and trade associations to oversee industry fitness and handle appeals. The Act mandates registration for all fish processing plants and exporters, grants inspection powers to Fishery Officers authorized by the Federal Government, and sets penalties for exporting substandard or unwholesome products.

metadata.short_title: The Pakistan General Cosmetics Act, 2023
metadata.long_title: An Act to regulate the quality, standard, labeling, packing, manufacturing, storage, distribution and sales of general cosmetics
metadata.one_line: This Act establishes the Pakistan General Cosmetics Regulatory Authority to regulate cosmetics quality, standards, and sales across Pakistan.
metadata.summary: The Pakistan General Cosmetics Act, 2023 regulates the quality, standard, labeling, packing, manufacturing, storage, distribution, and sales of general cosmetics in Pakistan. It establishes the Pakistan General Cosmetics Regulatory Authority as an autonomous body under the Ministry of Science and Technology to oversee these functions. The Act defines key terms such as 'general cosmetic', 'counterfeit cosmetic', and 'substandard cosmetics', outlines the composition of the Authority, and provides for offences, penalties, and the maintenance of accounts.

metadata.short_title: The Pakistan Girl Guides Association Ordinance, 1960
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to incorporate the Pakistan Girl Guides Association and to provide for certain matters connected therewith

It grants the Association exclusive rights to use specific emblems, badges, uniforms, and titles related to 'Guides'. The document also establishes penalties for contravention of these exclusive rights and allows the Federal Government to prescribe rules regarding the Association's constitution.

metadata.one_line: Establishes the Pakistan Global Institute as a body corporate with academic autonomy and defines its governance structure.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Pakistan Global Institute as a body corporate with perpetual succession and academic, financial, and administrative autonomy. It outlines the composition of the Institute, including the Patron, Chancellor, Senate, and Vice-Chancellor, and grants powers to prescribe courses, hold examinations, and award degrees. The legislation also details the governance framework through various committees and bodies, while providing for staff welfare, benefits, and mechanisms for appeals and indemnity.

metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of Pakistan, for purposes of imports and exports, trade and commerce with foreign countries and inter provincial trade and commerce in all such articles and processes which are described or represented as being Halal; Islamabad Capital Territory, for all other purposes envisaged under this Act.

metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Pakistan Halal Authority as a body corporate to promote trade and commerce in Halal articles and processes. The Authority is responsible for setting standards, issuing certificates, and regulating the use of Halal logos and marks. It applies to imports, exports, and inter-provincial trade involving Halal products across Pakistan.

metadata.summary: The Pakistan Health Research Council Act, 2016 provides for the reconstitution and reorganization of the Pakistan Medical Research Council into the Pakistan Health Research Council. It grants the Council administrative and financial autonomy to promote health research across various fields including allopathy and traditional medicine. The Act establishes a Board, Executive Committee, and other committees to oversee functions, manage funds through endowments and grants, and facilitate research capacity development.

metadata.summary: The Pakistan Hotels and Restaurants Act, 1976 provides measures to control and regulate service standards and amenities for tourists in hotels and restaurants. It establishes a Controller and an Advisory Committee to oversee registration, classification, fair rates, and medical facilities. The Act applies to the whole of Pakistan and repeals the earlier Ordinance from 1976.

metadata.summary: This Ordinance provides for the immediate dissolution of the Pakistan Industrial Development Corporation. It mandates the transfer of the Corporation's business, projects, properties, and shares to a newly formed Company or its subsidiary. The document ensures the continuity of employee services, legal proceedings, and provident fund rights during and after the transition.

metadata.summary: The Act provides for the transfer of certain projects and companies owned by the West Pakistan Industrial Development Corporation to specified corporations. It defines key terms such as 'project', 'managed company', and 'corporation' to facilitate this transfer. The legislation overrides other laws and grants indemnity to the Federal Government and involved entities for actions taken in good faith under the Act.

metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Pakistan Institute for Parliamentary Services as a body corporate with perpetual succession. The Institute is tasked with maintaining data, conducting research on laws, providing technical assistance and training to Parliamentarians, and managing internship programs. It is governed by a Board of Governors comprising members from the Senate, National Assembly, and Provincial Assemblies, along with the Federal Minister for Parliamentary Affairs.

It establishes the Institute as a body corporate with perpetual succession, enabling it to acquire property, admit students, conduct examinations, and confer academic distinctions. The document outlines the powers of the Board of Governors, the roles of various officers including the Chancellor and Rector, and provisions regarding research, budgeting, and indemnity for officers acting in good faith.

It grants the Institute academic, financial, and administrative autonomy while establishing its governing authorities, including the Senate, Syndicate, and Academic Council. The legislation also outlines the management of the Institute Fund, provisions for staff appointments from government or other institutions, and legal indemnity for officials acting in good faith.

It dissolves the existing Council and vests all powers, assets, and liabilities in a newly appointed Administrator. The Federal Government is authorized to appoint an Administrator and a Managing Committee to aid in the Institute's management, while also retaining the power to make rules for its implementation.

It vests all property, rights, and liabilities of the Corporation into the new Company while ensuring existing employee terms and pension benefits are maintained. The legislation also mandates the cessation of listing for old shares and their transfer to the new entity on stock exchanges.

It outlines the Corporation's share capital, management structure including the Board of Directors and Executive Committee, and its powers to transact insurance and reinsurance business. The Act also details provisions for investment of funds, accounts, audits, and penalties for wrong statements or wrongful use of the Corporation's name.

metadata.summary: This Ordinance was promulgated by the President to repeal the Pakistan International Airlines Corporation (Conversion) Act, 2016. It was issued because the Senate and National Assembly were not in session, necessitating immediate action under Article 89 of the Constitution. The repeal is subject to a saving clause that deems all actions, orders, and rights acquired under the repealed Act to remain valid and in force.

metadata.summary: This Act converts the Pakistan International Airlines Corporation into a public limited company effective from its promulgation date. It provides for the automatic transfer of all assets and liabilities without conveyance or registration, while ensuring existing contracts remain valid. The Federal Government is empowered to waive taxes and fees, and the Act repeals the previous 1956 legislation governing the corporation.

Its primary function is to acquire the undertaking of Orient Airways Limited and provide safe, efficient, and coordinated air-transport services. The Corporation is administered by a Board of Directors appointed under the supervision of the Federal Government, which retains power to issue binding policy directives.

metadata.short_title: The Pakistan Junior Cadet Corps Act, 1953
metadata.long_title: An Act to constitute a Junior Cadet Corps

metadata.summary: The Pakistan Junior Cadet Corps Act, 1953 establishes a force designated as the Junior Cadet Corps under the control of the Federal Government. It provides for the constitution of units in boys' schools, the enrollment of physically fit students above thirteen years of age, and the appointment of officers from school staff. The Act outlines military training requirements, discipline enforcement by school headmasters, and provisions regarding allowances and the termination of officer commissions.

metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Pakistan Land Port Authority to administer an integrated system for cross-border movement of goods and passengers at land ports. It provides a framework for declaring land ports, regulating their operations, ensuring security, and coordinating with government agencies for trade facilitation. The Authority is empowered to make rules, levy fees, manage assets, and adjudicate disputes related to land port operations.

The document also details audit arrangements, compensation terms for transferred interests, and provisions ensuring employees continue in service.

metadata.summary: The Pakistan Maritime Zones Act, 2023 consolidates and amends the law relating to the territorial sea and maritime zones of Pakistan. It defines various maritime zones including internal waters, contiguous zone, exclusive economic zone, and continental shelf, while establishing rights of innocent passage for foreign ships. The Act also addresses pollution prevention, piracy, jurisdiction over foreign ships, and repeals the previous Territorial Waters and Maritime Zones Act, 1976.

The Academy is empowered to make regulations with the approval of the Federal Government to carry out the Ordinance's purposes.

metadata.short_title: The Pakistan Navy (Extension of Service) Act, 1950
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the retention in service of certain persons enrolled for service in the Pakistan Navy.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of Pakistan (with specific extensions to Baluchistan and associated areas noted in the text)
metadata.one_line: Provides for the retention in service of certain persons enrolled for service in the Pakistan Navy after their term expires.
metadata.summary: This Act allows for the extension of service for members of the Pakistan Navy whose original term has expired. It authorizes them to continue serving until discharged by the Officer Commanding the Pakistan Navy, with a maximum extension period of five years. The Act applies to the whole of Pakistan but includes specific provisions for its application in Baluchistan, the Federated Areas, Leased Areas, the Baluchistan States Union, and Khairpur State.

metadata.short_title: The Pakistan Navy Ordinance, 1961
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to consolidate and amend the law relating to the government and discipline of the Pakistan Navy.
repeals: The Schedule
metadata.one_line: An Ordinance consolidating and amending laws regarding the government and discipline of the Pakistan Navy.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance consolidates and amends the law relating to the government and discipline of the Pakistan Navy. It defines persons subject to the ordinance, outlines conditions of service, lists various offences including mutiny and desertion, establishes courts-martial for trials, and prescribes punishments and penalties. The document also includes provisions for the appointment of the Chief of the Naval Staff and rules regarding the execution of sentences.

metadata.short_title: The Pakistan Nuclear Regulatory Authority Ordinance, 2001
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the establishment of the Pakistan Nuclear Regulatory Authority for regulation of nuclear safety and radiation protection in Pakistan and the extent of civil liability for nuclear damage resulting from any nuclear incident
repeals: The Pakistan Nuclear Safety and Radiation Protection Ordinance, 1984
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Pakistan Nuclear Regulatory Authority to regulate nuclear safety and radiation protection in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Pakistan Nuclear Regulatory Authority as the competent national authority for regulating nuclear safety and radiation protection. It defines the Authority's functions, powers, and composition, including provisions for licensing, civil liability limits, and financial guarantees. The document also dissolves previous regulatory bodies like the PNRB and DNSRP, transferring their assets and liabilities to the new Authority.

name: Pakistan Nursing and Midwifery Council Act, 2026

metadata.short_title: The Pakistan Nursing and Midwifery Council Act, 2026
metadata.long_title: An Act to consolidate the laws relating to registration, licensing, and training of nurses, nurse practitioners, midwives, midwifery associates, and nurse auxiliaries
repeals: The Pakistan Nursing Council Act, 1973 (Act No. XXVI of 1973)
Pakistan Nursing and Midwifery Council Ordinance, 2025
establishes: Provincial and Regional Nursing and Midwifery Board
metadata.max_penalty: Imprisonment for two years or a fine up to one million rupees, or both; fines up to ten million rupees for institutions; suspension or cancellation of registration/license.
metadata.administering_body: Federal Government, through the Division concerned
metadata.one_line: This Act consolidates laws regarding the registration, licensing, and training of nursing and midwifery professionals in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: The Pakistan Nursing and Midwifery Council Act, 2026 consolidates existing laws to regulate the registration, licensing, and training of nurses, nurse practitioners, midwives, and related personnel. It establishes the Pakistan Nursing and Midwifery Council along with provincial boards to oversee standards, recognition of institutions, and maintenance of registers. The Act outlines offences, penalties for unregistered practice, and mechanisms for digital identification and data management.

name: Pakistan Nursing Council Act (PNC), 1973 (Repealed by Act No. XXXVII of 2026, s. 53 (w.e.f 04-06-2026))

metadata.short_title: The Pakistan Nursing Council Act, 1973
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend and consolidate the laws relating to registration and training of nurses, midwives and health visitors.
repeals: Pakistan Nursing Council Act, 1952 (LIX of 1952)
metadata.status_evidence: [Repealed by Act No. XXXVII of 2026, s. 53 (w.e.f 04-06-2026)]
metadata.administering_body: Ministry of National Health Services, Regulation & Coordination
metadata.one_line: This Act establishes the Pakistan Nursing and Midwifery Council to regulate nursing registration, training, and practice nationwide.
metadata.summary: The Pakistan Nursing Council Act, 1973 consolidates laws regarding the registration and training of nurses, midwives, and health visitors in Pakistan. It establishes the Pakistan Nursing and Midwifery Council (PN&MC) as the regulatory body responsible for maintaining registers, recognizing qualifications, and regulating professional practice. The Act defines various nursing roles, sets standards for educational courses, and empowers the Council to make regulations and rules necessary for its functions.

metadata.short_title: The Pakistan Ordnance Factories Board Ordinance, 1961
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the constitution of a Pakistan Ordnance Factories Board and for investing it with certain powers and functions of the Central Government in relation to the ordnance factories.
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance establishes the Pakistan Ordnance Factories Board and grants it powers to manage ordnance factories.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance provides for the constitution of the Pakistan Ordnance Factories Board to manage and administer ordnance factories. It invests the Board with specific powers previously held by the Central Government, including determining employment terms, appointing staff, and managing technical projects. The Board operates under the directions of the Federal Government regarding national interest and defence requirements.

metadata.short_title: The Pakistan Ordnance Factories Board Ordinance, 1961
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the constitution of a Pakistan Ordnance Factories Board and for investing it with certain powers and functions of the Central Government in relation to the ordnance factories.
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance establishes the Pakistan Ordnance Factories Board and invests it with powers to manage ordnance factories.
metadata.summary: The document provides for the constitution of the Pakistan Ordnance Factories Board to manage and administer ordnance factories. It invests the Board with specific powers previously held by the Central Government regarding recruitment, discipline, and operations within these factories. The Board is guided by the Federal Government on policy matters involving national interest and defence requirements.

metadata.short_title: The Pakistan Penal Code
metadata.long_title: An Act to consolidate the law relating to offences.
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for life or death
metadata.one_line: Consolidates laws relating to offences, punishments, and general exceptions in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Act consolidates the law relating to offences committed within Pakistan and extends it to extra-territorial offences. It defines key terms such as 'person', 'offence', and 'dishonestly', outlines various punishments including imprisonment and fines, and establishes general exceptions like private defence and acts done by a person of unsound mind. The Code covers a wide range of crimes from unlawful assembly to rape and kidnapping.

metadata.short_title: The Pakistan Plant Quarantine Act, 1976
metadata.long_title: An Act to give effect in Pakistan to the International Plant Protection Convention, 1951.
metadata.status_evidence: [Repealed by Act I of 2019]
metadata.repealed_by: The Federal Laws (Revision and Declaration) Ordinance, 1981 (XXVII of 1981), s. 3 and Sen., II
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to two thousand rupees, or with both
metadata.one_line: This Act gives effect to the International Plant Protection Convention, 1951, regulating plant imports and pests.
metadata.summary: The Pakistan Plant Quarantine Act, 1976 was enacted to implement the International Plant Protection Convention, 1951 within Pakistan. It empowers the Federal Government to prohibit or regulate the import of articles likely to cause infection or carry pests through official notifications. The Act defines key terms such as 'crop', 'pest', and 'import', establishes penalties for contravention, and delegates certain powers to Provincial Governments regarding intra-provincial transportation.

name: Pakistan Postal Services Management Board Ordinance, 2002

metadata.short_title: The Pakistan Postal Services Management Board Ordinance, 2002
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the establishment of the Pakistan Postal Services Management Board and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Pakistan Postal Services Management Board to manage the Pakistan Post Office Department.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Pakistan Postal Services Management Board as a body corporate to manage the Pakistan Post Office Department. It defines the composition of the Board, including independent members and ex-officio representatives from the Federal Government and the Post Office Department. The Board is empowered to set postal tariffs, prepare budgets, conduct audits, and make rules and regulations, subject to the directives of the Federal Government and the State-Owned Enterprises Act.

metadata.short_title: The Pakistan Railways Police Act, 1977
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the constitution and regulation of the Pakistan Railways Police
metadata.one_line: This Act provides for the constitution, regulation, and functions of the Pakistan Railways Police.
metadata.summary: The Pakistan Railways Police Act, 1977 establishes the Pakistan Railways Police force under the control of the Federal Government. It outlines the police's functions, including preventing loss to railway property, ensuring passenger safety, maintaining law and order on railways, and investigating offences related to railways. The Act defines key terms such as 'officer', 'member', and 'Railway', and grants powers to officers for search, arrest, and maintenance of order. It also provides for the appointment of magistrates, public prosecutors, and rules regarding the transfer of provincial railway police forces.

metadata.short_title: The Pakistan Rangers Ordinance, 1959
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to constitute a force called the Pakistan Rangers for the protection of and maintenance of order in the border areas
metadata.territorial_extent: the Provinces of the Punjab and Sind
repeals: The West Pakistan Border Police Act, 1958
the Sind Rangers Force Act, 1943
metadata.max_penalty: transportation for life or rigorous imprisonment for seven years
metadata.one_line: Constitutes the Pakistan Rangers force for border protection and order maintenance, repealing earlier border police acts.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Pakistan Rangers to protect border areas and maintain order. It vests control in the Federal Government while allowing provincial consultation for rules. The law defines various ranks and duties, outlines offences with severe penalties, and repeals previous legislation regarding border police forces.

metadata.short_title: The Pakistan Red Crescent Society Act
metadata.long_title: An Act to constitute a [Pakistan] Red Crescent Society
repeals: Pakistan Red Cross Society Order, 1947
metadata.status_evidence: Section 1(1): 'Repealed.'; Footnote 6: 'Rep. by the Federal Laws (Revision and Declaration) Act No. XXVI of 1951, s. 3 and Sch. II.'; Footnote 2: 'repealed by Ordinance No. XXVII of 1981, s.2, Schedule I.'
metadata.repealed_by: Federal Laws (Revision and Declaration) Act No. XXVI of 1951
metadata.administering_body: Managing Body of the Pakistan Red Crescent Society
metadata.one_line: This Act constitutes the Pakistan Red Crescent Society to administer funds for medical aid and relief, though it is now repealed.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Pakistan Red Crescent Society to manage public monies and gifts for medical aid to the sick and wounded. It incorporates a body corporate with perpetual succession and defines the constitution of its Managing Body and Branch Committees across Pakistan. The Act outlines specific purposes for fund application, including war relief, tuberculosis care, and child welfare, though the entire legislation has been repealed by subsequent laws.

name: Pakistan Refugees Rehabilitation Finance Corporation (Dissolution) Ordinance, 1980

metadata.short_title: The Pakistan Refugees Rehabilitation Finance Corporation (Dissolution) Ordinance, 1980
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the dissolution of the Pakistan Refugees Rehabilitation Finance Corporation.
repeals: Pakistan Refugees Rehabilitation Finance Corporation Ordinance, 1959 (II of 1960)
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance dissolves the Pakistan Refugees Rehabilitation Finance Corporation and transfers its assets and liabilities.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance provides for the immediate dissolution of the Pakistan Refugees Rehabilitation Finance Corporation. It authorizes the Federal Government to transfer the Corporation's undertakings, properties, officers, and employees to another body or authority by order. Upon dissolution, the original 1959 Ordinance is repealed, and all debts and legal proceedings are deemed to belong to the successor authority.

metadata.short_title: The Pakistan Science Foundation Act, 1973
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of the Pakistan Science Foundation.
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Pakistan Science Foundation to promote and finance scientific activities relevant to socio-economic needs.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Pakistan Science Foundation as a body corporate with perpetual succession. The Foundation functions as a financing agency for scientific research, technological development, and the establishment of science centers and museums. It is managed by a Board of Trustees comprising whole-time and part-time members appointed or nominated by the President and the National Science Council. The Foundation receives funds from grants, donations, and income, maintains accounts audited by chartered accountants, and submits annual reports to the Federal Government and the National Assembly.

metadata.short_title: The Pakistan Single Window Act, 2021
metadata.long_title: An Act to make provisions for the establishment of Pakistan single window
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Federal Government may, by a notification in the official Gazette, appoint
metadata.one_line: Establishes an autonomous body to simplify cross-border trade processes and facilitate international trade in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Pakistan Single Window, an autonomous body designed to simplify cross-border trade processes and reduce business costs. It creates a single point for submitting trade data to enable synchronized processing and harmonization of documents required for regulatory control. The Act defines various terms related to electronic transactions, risk management systems, and the roles of the Governing Council, lead agency, and operating entity.

metadata.short_title: The Pakistan Sovereign Wealth Fund Act, 2023
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for establishment of Pakistan Sovereign Wealth Fund
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Pakistan Sovereign Wealth Fund to manage federal assets for sustainable economic development.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Pakistan Sovereign Wealth Fund, owned and controlled by the Federal Government, to maximize asset value for future generations. The Fund has perpetual succession and financial independence, with a Board and Supervisory Council overseeing its operations. It manages transferred government assets, including shares in state-owned enterprises, through investment strategies approved by the Supervisory Council.

name: Pakistan Space and Upper Atmosphere Research Commission Ordinance, 1981

metadata.short_title: The Pakistan Space and Upper Atmosphere Research Commission Ordinance, 1981
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the establishment of a Space Research Council and the Pakistan Space and Upper Atmosphere Research Commission.
establishes: Pakistan Space and Upper Atmosphere Research Commission (SUPARCO)
metadata.administering_body: Federal Government (through DCC of NCA, with SPD as secretariat)
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Pakistan Space and Upper Atmosphere Research Commission to promote peaceful uses of space.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Pakistan Space and Upper Atmosphere Research Commission (SUPARCO) and a Space Research Council. It empowers the Commission to advance research in space science, enhance indigenous capabilities, and promote the peaceful applications of space technology for socio-economic development. The Federal Government exercises control over the Commission through the Development Control Committee of the National Command Authority (DCC), while the Strategic Plans Division coordinates tasking and financial/administrative matters.

name: Pakistan Standards and Quality Control Authority Act, 1996

metadata.short_title: Pakistan Standards and Quality Control Authority Act, 1996
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of Pakistan Standards and Quality Control Authority
repeals: Pakistan Standards Institution (Certification Marks) Ordinance, 1961
establishes: Pakistan Standards and Quality Control Authority
metadata.administering_body: Pakistan Standards and Quality Control Authority
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Pakistan Standards and Quality Control Authority to regulate standards, quality control, and certification marks across Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Pakistan Standards and Quality Control Authority as a body corporate to provide standardization and quality control services. It defines key terms related to articles, products, testing, and metrology while granting the Authority powers to prohibit improper use of marks and restrict exports. The Act also dissolves previous organizations like the Pakistan Standards Institution and transfers their assets and liabilities to the new Authority.

metadata.short_title: The Pakistan Study Centres Act, 1976
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of Pakistan Study Centres in the Universities for the study of languages, literature, social structure, customs, attitudes and motivation, of the people of various regions of Pakistan.
establishes: National Institute of Pakistan Studies, University of Islamabad
Board of Governors for each Centre
key_definitions: Institute (National Institute of Pakistan Studies, University of Islamabad)
metadata.one_line: Establishes Pakistan Study Centres in universities to study regional languages, literature, and social structures.
metadata.summary: This Act provides for the establishment of Pakistan Study Centres within universities across Pakistan. It defines the functions of these centres, which include studying regional cultures, establishing degree programs, and promoting research. The Act also establishes a Board of Governors for each centre to manage its affairs and appoints a Director as the executive head. Additionally, it creates a National Institute of Pakistan Studies at the University of Islamabad and outlines provisions for funding, auditing, and rule-making.

metadata.short_title: The Pakistan Telecommunication (Re-organisation) Act, 1996
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for re-organisation of telecommunication system in Pakistan by establishing the Pakistan Telecommunication Authority, the Frequency Allocation Board, National Telecommunication Corporation and the Pakistan Telecommunication Employees Trust, regulation of telecommunication industry, transfer of telecommunication services to private sector and for matter connected therewith or incidental thereto
repeals: The Pakistan Telecommunication Corporation Act, 1991 (XVII of 1991)
The Pakistan Telecommunication (Re-Organization) Ordinance, 1996 (LXXVII of 1996)
Ministry of Communications, Government of Pakistan, Notifications numbering 5(4)/95-PTC, dated the 7th August, 1995
metadata.one_line: This Act reorganizes Pakistan's telecommunication system by establishing new regulatory bodies and transferring services to the private sector.
metadata.summary: The Pakistan Telecommunication (Re-organisation) Act, 1996 provides for the re-organization of the telecommunication system in Pakistan. It establishes key institutions including the Pakistan Telecommunication Authority, Frequency Allocation Board, National Telecommunication Corporation, and the Pakistan Telecommunication Employees Trust. The Act regulates the telecommunication industry, facilitates the transfer of services to the private sector, and repeals previous conflicting laws and ordinances.

metadata.short_title: The Pakistan Territorial Force Act, 1950
metadata.long_title: An Act to constitute a Pakistan Territorial Force.
metadata.status_evidence: 20. [Repeal.] Rep. by the Repealing and Amending Ordinance, 1965 (10 of 1965), s. 2 and 1st Sch.
metadata.one_line: This Act constitutes the Pakistan Territorial Force, defining its structure, enrolment, service liability, and administration.
metadata.summary: The Pakistan Territorial Force Act, 1950 establishes a force to be raised and maintained by the Federal Government. It outlines the constitution of units, classes of officers, enrolment procedures for citizens or domiciliaries in Pakistan, and the duration of service not exceeding six years. The Act also provides for rules and regulations regarding training, remuneration, discipline, and exemptions from local taxation for enrolled personnel.

metadata.short_title: The Pakistan Tobacco Board Ordinance, 1968
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the establishment of Tobacco Board for the promotion of the cultivation, manufacture and export of tobacco and tobacco products.
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Pakistan Tobacco Board to promote tobacco cultivation, manufacture, and export.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Pakistan Tobacco Board to promote the cultivation, manufacture, and export of tobacco. It defines the Board's constitution, functions, and control mechanisms under the Federal Government. The legislation also sets out powers regarding price fixation, cess levies, and penalties for contraventions.

metadata.short_title: The Pakistan Tourist Guides Act, 1976
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the regulation and control of the profession of tourist guides
metadata.max_penalty: fine which may extend to five hundred rupees
metadata.one_line: This Act regulates and controls the profession of tourist guides in Pakistan through licensing and a code of conduct.
metadata.summary: The Pakistan Tourist Guides Act, 1976 establishes a regulatory framework for tourist guides across the whole of Pakistan. It creates the Tourist Guide Regulatory Committee to advise the Federal Government and assist in preparing codes of conduct. The Act mandates licensing for all tourist guides, sets service charge limits, and prescribes penalties for unlicensed practice or code violations.

name: Pakistan Trade Control of Wiled Fauna and Flora Act, 2012

metadata.short_title: The Pakistan Trade Control of Wild Fauna and Flora Act, 2012
metadata.long_title: An Act to give effect to the United Nations Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild/Fauna and flora
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Federal Government may by notification in the official Gazette, appoint
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than one year or more than two years or with fine which shall not be less than 0.500 million rupees or more than 1.000 million rupees
metadata.one_line: This Act regulates the export, import, and re-export of wild fauna and flora specimens in Pakistan to implement international conventions.
metadata.summary: The Pakistan Trade Control of Wild Fauna and Flora Act, 2012 gives effect to the United Nations Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora. It prohibits the export, re-export, and import of specimens listed in the Convention's Appendices unless specific permits are obtained from designated authorities. The Act establishes a Management Authority and a Scientific Authority to oversee trade conditions, ensure species survival, and maintain records of all transactions.

metadata.short_title: The Pakistan Veterinary Medical Council Act, 1996
metadata.long_title: An act to constitute the Veterinary Medical Council in Pakistan.
metadata.one_line: This Act constitutes the Pakistan Veterinary Medical Council to regulate veterinary practice and recognize qualifications.
metadata.summary: The Pakistan Veterinary Medical Council Act, 1996 establishes a body corporate known as the Pakistan Veterinary Medical Council. The Council is responsible for regulating the registration, practice, and conduct of veterinarians in Pakistan while establishing uniform standards for veterinary medicine and surgery. It defines recognized qualifications from Pakistani institutions and abroad, maintains a public register of practitioners, and prescribes penalties for fraudulent representation or unauthorized use of unregistered qualifications.

name: Pakistan Water and Power Development Authority Act, 1958

metadata.short_title: The Pakistan Water and Power Development Authority Act, 1958
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the unified and co-ordinated development of the water and power resources of Pakistan.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of Pakistan, except the Districts of Karachi
repeals: The West Pakistan Water and Power Development Authority Ordinance, 1958 (West Pakistan Ordinance No. VIII of 1958)
establishes: Pakistan Water and Power Development Authority
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Pakistan Water and Power Development Authority to unify water and power resource development.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Pakistan Water and Power Development Authority as a body corporate to coordinate the development of water and power resources. The Authority is granted powers to control water resources, operate power houses and grids, and frame schemes for execution. It outlines the constitution of the Authority, including the appointment of a Chairman and Members, their remuneration, and conditions of service. The Act also covers financial provisions, including the maintenance of accounts, audit by the Auditor-General, and the sale of power at fixed rates.

metadata.short_title: The Parsi Marriage and Divorce Act, 1936
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the law relating to marriage and divorce among Parsis.
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Federal Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, appoint
metadata.max_penalty: penalties provided in sections 494 and 495 of the Pakistan Penal Code for bigamy; simple imprisonment up to one year or fine for failing to register certificate
metadata.one_line: This Act amends the law relating to marriage and divorce among Parsis in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: The Parsi Marriage and Divorce Act, 1936 amends the legal framework governing marriage and divorce specifically for Parsis. It establishes special matrimonial courts, defines requisites for valid marriages including age limits and consent, and outlines procedures for divorce, alimony, and child custody. The Act also prescribes penalties for bigamy and false certificates while defining prohibited degrees of relationship.

metadata.short_title: The Partition Act, 1893
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Law relating to Partition
metadata.one_line: Amends the law relating to partition by empowering courts to order sales instead of division in specific cases.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the law regarding partition suits, specifically allowing courts to order a sale of property and distribution of proceeds if division is not reasonably possible. It outlines procedures for shareholders to buy out others at valuation, rules for reserved bidding, and provisions for representing parties under disability. The Act applies to pending suits instituted before its commencement where no final partition scheme has been approved.

metadata.short_title: The Partnership Act, 1932
metadata.long_title: An Act to define and amend the law relating to partnership
metadata.commencement: 1932-10-01 (except section 69 which comes into force on 1933-10-01)
repeals: section 55 of the Partnership Act, 1890
metadata.one_line: This Act defines partnership law, outlines partner rights and liabilities, and establishes firm registration procedures.
metadata.summary: The Partnership Act, 1932 defines the legal nature of partnerships, the rights and duties of partners, and the liability of firms to third parties. It covers the formation, management, dissolution, and winding up of firms, as well as the registration process and associated fees. The Act applies to the whole of Pakistan and incorporates provisions from the Contract Act, 1872 where not inconsistent.

metadata.short_title: The Passports Act, 1974
metadata.long_title: An Act to regulate departure from and entry into Pakistan and visit to foreign countries of the citizen of Pakistan.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of Pakistan and also applies to all citizens of Pakistan, wherever they may be
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year (for section 3 contravention) or three years (for document offences), or fine, or both; rigorous imprisonment not less than six months and fine not less than one thousand rupees for trafficking in passports
metadata.one_line: Regulates departure from, entry into Pakistan, and visits to foreign countries by Pakistani citizens.
metadata.summary: This Act regulates the departure from and entry into Pakistan, as well as visits to foreign countries by citizens of Pakistan.
