It prohibits leaving the country without a valid passport issued by or under the authority of the Federal Government and sets out penalties for contravention. The Act empowers police officers and Customs officials to arrest suspects, seize documents, and cancel passports, while also allowing the Federal Government to make rules and delegate powers.

metadata.short_title: The Patents Ordinance, 2000
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend and consolidate the law relating to patents in order to give effect in Pakistan to the provisions of the International Convention on Trade Related Intellectual Property Rights, 1994, in accordance with its objectives and principles.
repeals: Patents and Designs Act, 1911 (Act II of 1911)
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance consolidates patent law to align with TRIPS and establishes the Patent Office and related procedures.
metadata.summary: The Patents Ordinance, 2000 amends and consolidates the law relating to patents in Pakistan. It aims to give effect to the International Convention on Trade Related Intellectual Property Rights, 1994. The document establishes the Patent Office, defines patentability criteria such as novelty and inventive step, and outlines procedures for applications, examinations, and infringement proceedings. It also provides for compulsory licences, penalties for offences, and the regulation of patent agents.

metadata.short_title: The Pay-As-You-Earn Scheme Act, 1973
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for introducing a scheme for the import of machinery and equipment on credit for establishing certain industrial units and enterprises
metadata.one_line: Provides for a scheme to import machinery on credit using export earnings from industrial units.
metadata.summary: This Act introduces a scheme allowing the import of machinery and equipment on credit for specific industrial units and enterprises. The cost of such imports must be met from the export earnings of the importing unit. The Federal Government is empowered to prepare the scheme and make rules for its administration, including penalties for failing to repatriate foreign exchange.

metadata.short_title: The Payment of Wages Act, 1936
metadata.long_title: An Act to regulate the payment of wages to certain classes of persons employed in industry.
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Federal Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, appoint
metadata.max_penalty: fine which may extend to two hundred rupees
metadata.one_line: Regulates payment of wages, permissible deductions, and penalties for employers in factories, industrial establishments, and railways.
metadata.summary: This Act regulates the payment of wages to persons employed in industry, including factories, industrial establishments, commercial establishments, and railways. It defines key terms such as 'wages' and 'industrial establishment', sets rules for wage periods and times of payment, and specifies allowable deductions from wages. The Act also establishes the powers of inspectors, procedures for claims arising from unpaid wages or malicious deductions, and penalties for offences under the Act.

name: Payment Systems and Electronic Fund Transfers Act, 2007

metadata.short_title: The Payment Systems and Electronic Fund Transfers Act, 2007
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide regulatory framework for payment systems and electronic fund transfers
metadata.max_penalty: one million rupees fine; suspension or revocation of license
metadata.one_line: This Act regulates payment systems and electronic fund transfers in Pakistan to protect consumers and define liabilities.
metadata.summary: The Payment Systems and Electronic Fund Transfers Act, 2007 establishes a regulatory framework for payment systems and electronic fund transfers within Pakistan. It defines key terms such as 'Consumer', 'Financial Institution', and 'Designated Payment System' while empowering the State Bank to supervise these operations. The Act outlines the rights and liabilities of various parties involved in electronic transactions, including provisions for complaint resolution, penalties for non-compliance, and immunity for acts done in good faith by the State Bank.

name: Peaceful Assembly and Public Order Act, 2024

metadata.short_title: The Peaceful Assembly and Public Order Act, 2024
metadata.long_title: An Act to regulate the holding of public assemblies at certain places in Islamabad Capital Territory and to provide for matters ancillary thereto
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term that may extend to ten years
metadata.one_line: Regulates public assemblies in Islamabad, requiring permits and defining penalties for unlawful gatherings.
metadata.summary: This Act regulates the holding of public assemblies within the Islamabad Capital Territory to maintain public order. It requires Event Coordinators to apply for permission from the District Magistrate at least seven days in advance, providing details such as route, time, and participant numbers. The District Magistrate can grant, refuse, or recall permission based on law and order situations and security risks. The Act defines specific offences for being part of an unlawful assembly, prescribing penalties up to ten years for repeat offenders, and establishes a revision process before the Secretary Ministry of Interior.

metadata.short_title: The Pensions Act, 1871
metadata.long_title: An Act to consolidate and amend the law relating to Pensions and Grants by Government of money or land-revenue
metadata.commencement: on the date of the passing thereof
repeals: Enactments repealed. Saving of Rules
key_definitions: grant of money or land revenue
metadata.one_line: Consolidates and amends laws regarding government pensions and grants of money or land-revenue.
metadata.summary: This Act consolidates and amends the law relating to pensions and grants provided by the Government of money or land-revenue. It establishes procedures for making claims to the Collector or other authorized officers, bars civil suits regarding these pensions, and defines the appropriate government responsible for federal versus provincial pensions. The Act also outlines rules regarding the payment, commutation, and alienation of pensions, as well as provisions for rewards to informers of fraud.

metadata.short_title: The Petroleum Act, 1934
metadata.long_title: An Act to consolidate and amend the law relating to the import, transport, storage, production, refining and blending of petroleum and other inflammable substances.
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Federal Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, appoint
repeals: THE SCHEDULE
metadata.max_penalty: fine of ten million Rupees
metadata.one_line: Consolidates and amends laws regarding the import, transport, storage, production, refining and blending of petroleum.
metadata.summary: This Act consolidates and amends the legal framework governing the import, transport, storage, production, refining, and blending of petroleum and other inflammable substances in Pakistan. It establishes rules for licensing, testing standards, and exemptions for specific uses like motor conveyances. The Federal Government is empowered to make rules regarding these activities and apply the Act to other dangerously inflammable substances.

name: Petroleum Products (Petroleum Levy) and Climate Support Levy Ordinance, 1961

metadata.short_title: The Petroleum Products (Petroleum Levy) and Climate Support Levy Ordinance, 1961
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the levy and collection of a [Petroleum Levy] [and Climate Support Levy] on petroleum products and for matters connected therewith.
metadata.commencement: at once; deemed to have taken effect on 1959-08-01
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance provides for the levy and collection of Petroleum and Climate Support Levies on petroleum products.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the legal framework for levying and collecting a Petroleum Levy and a Climate Support Levy on various petroleum products. It defines specific terms such as 'Company', 'Refinery', and 'Petroleum Product' to determine liability and pricing mechanisms. The Federal Government is empowered to notify rates, grant exemptions, authorize refunds, and make rules regarding the collection of these levies.

metadata.short_title: The Pharmacy Act, 1967
metadata.long_title: An Act to establish Pharmacy Councils to regulate the practice of pharmacy
metadata.one_line: Establishes Pharmacy Councils to regulate the practice of pharmacy and registration of pharmacists across Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes Pharmacy Councils, including a Central Council and Provincial Councils, to regulate the practice of pharmacy in Pakistan. It provides for the composition of these councils, the registration of pharmacists and apprentices, approval of examinations and courses, and the maintenance of registers. The Act also outlines the powers to make bye-laws and provisions regarding offences related to unregistered practice.

name: Pir Roshaan Institute of Progressive Sciences and Technologies, Miranshah Act, 2023

metadata.short_title: Pir Roshaan Institute of Progressive Sciences and Technologies, Miranshah Act, 2023
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of Pir Roshaan Institute of Progressive Sciences and Technologies at Miranshah and to provide for matters connected therewith and ancillary thereto
establishes: Pir Roshaan Institute of Progressive Sciences and Technologies, Miranshah
metadata.administering_body: Ministry of Federal Education and Professional Training, Islamabad
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Pir Roshaan Institute of Progressive Sciences and Technologies in Miranshah and defines its authorities.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Pir Roshaan Institute of Progressive Sciences and Technologies at Miranshah in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. It creates various governing bodies including the Board of Governors, Syndicate, and Academic Council to manage the institute's affairs. The legislation outlines financial provisions, staff appointment procedures, and rules for amending statutes and regulations.

metadata.short_title: The Plant Breeders' Rights Act, 2016
metadata.long_title: An Act to encourage the development of new plant varieties and to protect the rights of breeders of such varieties
metadata.commencement: at once except section 10 which shall come into force on such date as the Federal Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, appoint
metadata.administering_body: Federal Seed Certification and Registration Department
metadata.one_line: This Act establishes a registry to protect plant breeders' rights and regulate the seed industry in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: The Plant Breeders' Rights Act, 2016 was enacted to encourage the development of new plant varieties and protect the rights of their breeders. It establishes a Registry and an Advisory Committee to administer these rights, while also providing for compulsory licenses and benefit sharing mechanisms. The Act applies to the whole of Pakistan and includes provisions for infringement suits, penalties, and incentives for research scientists.

metadata.short_title: The Poisons Act, 1919
metadata.long_title: An Act to consolidate and amend the law regulating the importation, possession and sale of poisons
repeals: Act I of 1904
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both
metadata.one_line: Consolidates and amends laws regulating the importation, possession, and sale of poisons in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Act consolidates and amends the law regarding the importation, possession, and sale of poisons. It empowers Provincial Governments to regulate possession and sale through rules, including licensing and fee structures. The Federal Government is authorized to prohibit importation without a licence and to issue search warrants. Penalties are prescribed for unlawful importation or breach of conditions, with exemptions for medical and veterinary practitioners acting in good faith.

metadata.short_title: The Police (Incitement to Disaffection) Act, 1922
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide a penalty for spreading disaffection among the police and for kindred offences.
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Provincial Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, direct
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to two hundred rupees, or with both
metadata.one_line: Penalizes spreading disaffection among the police and inducing them to withhold services or breach discipline.
metadata.summary: This Act provides penalties for intentionally causing disaffection among members of a police force or inducing them to withhold services. It defines 'member of a police-force' based on specific enactments listed in the Schedule. The law requires sanction from a District Magistrate for trials and prohibits summary trial, ensuring cases are heard by a Magistrate of the first class.

metadata.short_title: The Police Act, 1861
metadata.long_title: An Act for the Regulation of Police
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of Pakistan (extended to the whole of Pakistan on 14th October 1955)
repeals: Police Act 1888 (superseded by extension to whole Pakistan)
sections relating to 'number' and 'gender' (Repealed by Repealing and amending Act, 1914)
establishes: Capital City District Public Safety Commission
metadata.one_line: An Act to re-organize the police and regulate its functions, including the establishment of District Public Safety Commissions.
metadata.summary: This Act regulates the organization and administration of the police force in Pakistan. It establishes the powers of the Inspector-General, defines the duties of police officers, and provides for the regulation of public assemblies and processions. The Act also creates District and Capital City District Public Safety Commissions to oversee police conduct and handle complaints regarding neglect or excesses by police personnel.

metadata.short_title: The Police Act, 1888
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Law relating to the regulation of Police
key_definitions: officer in charge of a police-station
metadata.one_line: Amends laws regulating police by allowing employment of officers across provinces and creation of special districts.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the law relating to the regulation of police, specifically relaxing restrictions on employing police officers outside their original province. It empowers the Federal Government to create special police districts spanning multiple provinces and extend jurisdiction accordingly. The Act also governs the discharge of functions by police officers beyond provincial limits and requires consent from the relevant Provincial Government for exercising powers in another province's area.

metadata.short_title: The Police Order, 2002
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to reconstitute the police establishment and provide for its organization, discipline, powers and functions.
repeals: The Police Act, 1861 (V of 1861)
establishes: Capital City District Public Safety Commission
key_definitions: Capital City District Public Safety Commission
metadata.one_line: This Order reconstitutes the police establishment, establishes various safety commissions and complaint authorities, and repeals the Police Act, 1861.
metadata.summary: The Police Order, 2002 reconstitutes the police establishment in Pakistan and provides for its organization, discipline, powers, and functions. It establishes multiple Public Safety Commissions at district, provincial, and national levels, as well as Federal and Provincial Police Complaints Authorities to handle grievances. The Order also repeals the Police Act, 1861, while saving existing rights and liabilities acquired under the repealed Act.

name: Population Welfare Planning Programme (Appointment and Temination of Service) Ordinance, 1981

metadata.short_title: The Population Welfare Planning Programme (Appointment and Termination of Service) Ordinance, 1981
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the restructuring and reorganisation of, and appointment of persons in, the Population Programme
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance regulates the appointment, termination, and service conditions of employees in the Population Programme.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance provides for the restructuring and reorganization of the Population Programme and governs the appointment and termination of its employees. It defines specific terms such as 'appointing authority' and 'Board', which includes various provincial family planning boards. The document outlines procedures for selection, seniority determination, and terminal benefits, while also empowering the Federal Government to make rules for its implementation.

name: Port Authorities Lands And Buildings (Recovery Of Possession) Ordinance, 1962

metadata.short_title: Port Authorities Lands and Buildings (Recovery of Possession) Ordinance, 1962
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the speedy recovery of possession from unauthorized occupants of lands or buildings belonging to Port Authorities within the limits of major ports, and for matters ancillary thereto.
metadata.one_line: Provides for the speedy recovery of possession of lands and buildings belonging to Port Authorities from unauthorized occupants.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance empowers Port Authorities to recover possession of their lands and buildings located within major ports from lessees who fail to vacate or unauthorized occupants. It establishes a procedure involving notices, inquiries by an Authorized Officer (a Magistrate), and the power to evict persons and demolish structures if necessary. The Ordinance also covers the recovery of costs for demolition and arrears of rent as land revenue.

metadata.short_title: The Port Qasim Authority Act, 1973
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of the Port Qasim Authority
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Port area
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Port Qasim Authority for planning, development, and management of Muhammad Bin Qasim Port.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Port Qasim Authority to manage the planning, development, and operations of Muhammad Bin Qasim Port at Phitti Creek. It defines the Authority's powers regarding tolls, land acquisition, environmental assessments, and financial management within the Federal Consolidated Fund. The legislation also outlines the composition of the Board, recruitment of officers, and procedures for the dissolution of the Authority with asset transfer to the Federal Government.

metadata.short_title: The Ports Act, 1908
metadata.long_title: An Act to consolidate the Enactments relating to Ports and Port-charges.
metadata.territorial_extent: the ports mentioned in the first schedule, and to such Parts of the navigable rivers and channels leading to such ports respectively as have been declared to be subject to Act XXII of 1855 (XII of 1875) or to the Indian Ports Act, 1875, or to the Indian Ports Act, 1889
repeals: enactments relating to ports and port charges
metadata.one_line: Consolidates enactments relating to ports, port charges, navigation safety, and vessel regulations in India.
metadata.summary: This Act consolidates previous laws regarding ports and port charges. It defines the powers of conservators and harbor masters to ensure navigation safety, manage wrecks, and prevent fires within port limits. The legislation also establishes the levy and recovery of port dues for various types of vessels and outlines penalties for offenses such as fouling moorings or discharging ballast improperly.

metadata.short_title: The Post Office Act, 1898
metadata.long_title: An Act to consolidate and amend the Law relating to the Post Office
repeals: The Post Office Act, 1874
metadata.max_penalty: fine which may extend to fifty rupees; imprisonment not specified in excerpts
key_definitions: in course of transmission by post
metadata.one_line: Consolidates and amends laws relating to the Post Office, covering postage, money orders, and penalties.
metadata.summary: This Act consolidates and amends the law relating to the Post Office in Pakistan. It establishes the government's exclusive privilege over mail, sets rules for postage rates and stamps, regulates the transmission of postal articles including prohibitions on injurious or indecent items, and provides for money orders and insurance. The Act also defines various offences related to postal misconduct and outlines procedures for prosecution by the Director General or Post Master General.

name: Post Office National Savings Certificates Ordinance, 1944

metadata.short_title: The Post Office National Savings Certificates Ordinance, 1944
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to make certain provision in respect of Post Office Twelve-Year National Savings Certificates and other classes of Savings Certificates.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of Pakistan (and India at the time of enactment)
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance regulates Post Office National Savings Certificates, restricting transfers and defining payment rules for minors and deceased holders.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance provides specific provisions regarding Post Office Twelve-Year National Savings Certificates and other classes of savings certificates. It restricts the transfer of these certificates without written consent from an authorized Post Office officer and outlines procedures for payment upon the death of a holder or when held by minors. The document also empowers the Federal Government to make rules regarding application, issue, limits, and interest conditions for these certificates.

metadata.short_title: The Power Alcohol Ordinance, 1959
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to make provision for certain matters connected with the development of the power alcohol industry.
metadata.commencement: at once for sections 1 and 2; rest on such date as the Federal Government may notify
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment up to six months or fine up to one thousand rupees or both; further fines for continued contravention
metadata.one_line: Regulates the production, disposal, and use of power alcohol in Pakistan under federal control.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance provides for the development of the power alcohol industry under Federal control. It defines key terms like molasses and power alcohol, restricts manufacturing to specific substances, and empowers the Federal Government to regulate production and mandate the admixture of power alcohol with petrol. The document also outlines penalties for contravention and grants powers to make rules regarding licensing, pricing, and storage.

metadata.short_title: The Powers-of-Attorney Act, 1882
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the law relating to Powers-of-Attorney
establishes: separate file of instruments in High Court
metadata.one_line: Amends the law relating to powers-of-attorney regarding execution, payment, deposit of instruments, and married women's powers.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the law relating to powers-of-attorney by regulating how attorneys execute instruments in their own names. It protects third parties making payments without notice of the donor's death or incapacity and establishes a system for depositing original power-of-attorney instruments in High Courts with certified copies available for inspection. The Act specifically grants married women the same power to appoint attorneys as unmarried women, while excluding Muslim married women from this specific provision.

name: President to hold Another Office Act, 2004

metadata.short_title: The President to Hold Another Office Act, 2004
metadata.long_title: An Act to enable the President of Pakistan to hold another office
metadata.one_line: Enables the President of Pakistan to simultaneously hold the office of Chief of the Army Staff.
metadata.summary: This Act enables the President of Pakistan to hold the office of Chief of the Army Staff in addition to their presidential duties. It declares that holding this military position does not disqualify the President under Article 63 or Article 41 of the Constitution regarding offices of profit. The provision is explicitly limited to the present holder of the office of the President at the time of enactment.

metadata.short_title: The President's Pension Act, 1974
metadata.long_title: An Act to make provision for the payment of pension to persons who have held the office of President.
repeals: Section 5
metadata.one_line: Provides pension and various facilities to former Presidents and their widows.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes a monthly lifetime pension for individuals who served as President for at least two years without removal for constitutional violations or gross misconduct. It grants extensive benefits including diplomatic passports, access to government guest houses, free medical aid, official residence allowances, and car allowances for the former President and their widows. All expenditures related to these pensions and facilities are charged upon the Federal Consolidated Fund.

name: President's Salary, Allowances and Privileges Act, 1975

metadata.short_title: The President's Salary, Allowances and Privileges Act, 1975
metadata.long_title: An Act to determine the salary, allowances and privileges of the President.
metadata.one_line: This Act determines the salary, allowances, and privileges of the President of Pakistan.
metadata.summary: The President's Salary, Allowances and Privileges Act, 1975 establishes the remuneration package for the President of Pakistan. It specifies monthly salaries, equipment allowances, travel expenses, and provisions for official residence and transport. The Act also outlines discretionary grants, sumptuary allowances, medical facilities, and membership in the General Provident Fund.

metadata.short_title: The Press Council of Pakistan Ordinance, 2002
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for Press Council of Pakistan
metadata.one_line: Establishes an autonomous Press Council of Pakistan to implement ethical codes and ensure press accountability.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Press Council of Pakistan as an autonomous and independent body to implement the Ethical Code of Practice. It defines key terms such as 'journalist', 'editor', and 'newspaper' to regulate the media landscape. The Council is empowered to conduct inquiries, censure members, and levy fees from registered newspapers to fund its operations.

name: Press Newspapers, News Agencies and Books Registration Ordinance, 2002

metadata.short_title: Press, Newspapers, News Agencies and Books Registration Ordinance, 2002
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend and consolidate the law relating to news agencies publications and printing presses
repeals: West Pakistan Press and Publications Ordinance, 1963 (W.P. Ordinance XXX of 1963)
metadata.administering_body: Ministry of Information and Media Development
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance consolidates laws regarding news agencies, publications, and printing presses while repealing the 1963 West Pakistan Press Ordinance.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends and consolidates the legal framework governing news agencies, publications, and printing presses in Pakistan. It establishes requirements for declarations by printers, publishers, and editors, along with registration procedures for newspapers and books. The document also outlines penalties for contraventions and repeals the West Pakistan Press and Publications Ordinance, 1963.

name: Prevention and Control of Human Trafficking Ordinance, 2002 (Repealed by Act XXXIV of 2018)

metadata.short_title: Prevention and Control of Human Trafficking Ordinance, 2002
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to prevent and control human trafficking.
metadata.status_evidence: [Repealed by Act XXXIV of 2018]
metadata.max_penalty: fourteen years imprisonment and fine
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance prevents and controls human trafficking, defines offences, sets penalties up to fourteen years, and protects victims.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance aims to prevent and control human trafficking by defining specific offences related to the trade in human beings. It establishes severe punishments, including imprisonment up to fourteen years and fines, for those involved in trafficking, kidnapping, or exploitative entertainment. The law provides mechanisms for victim compensation, shelter, and medical treatment, while ensuring investigations are conducted by specially empowered agencies. Proceedings under this Ordinance are additional to other laws, and the Government is indemnified for actions taken in good faith.

metadata.short_title: The Prevention of Anti-National Activities Act, 1974
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the more effective prevention of certain anti-national and treasonable activities
repeals: The Prevention of Anti-National Activities Ordinance, 1973 (XXIX of 1973)
key_definitions: secession of a part of the territory of Pakistan from the Federation
metadata.one_line: This Act prevents anti-national activities by declaring associations anti-national, establishing a Tribunal for review, and imposing penalties.
metadata.summary: The Prevention of Anti-National Activities Act, 1974 provides mechanisms to prevent anti-national and treasonable activities within Pakistan. It defines anti-national activities such as inciting secession or disrupting territorial integrity and allows the Federal Government to declare associations anti-national. A Tribunal is established to review these declarations within six months. The Act also outlines penalties for membership in anti-national associations, dealing with their funds, and contravening orders regarding notified places.

metadata.short_title: The Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947
metadata.long_title: An Act for the more effective prevention of bribery and corruption
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to ten years but not less than five years and with fine
metadata.one_line: This Act provides for the prevention of bribery and corruption by defining offences, presumptions, and procedures regarding public servants.
metadata.summary: The Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 aims to make provisions for the more effective prevention of bribery and corruption. It defines 'public servant' broadly to include employees of government-controlled bodies and establishes specific offences such as accepting gratification other than legal remuneration and possessing property disproportionate to known income. The Act creates presumptions in trials where a public servant accepts valuable things without adequate consideration and stipulates that accused persons are competent witnesses for their own defence.

name: Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1890

metadata.short_title: The Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1890
metadata.long_title: An Act for the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for three months or fine up to two hundred thousand rupees
metadata.one_line: This Act prevents cruelty to animals by defining offences and penalties for overdriving, overloading, phooka, baiting, and neglect.
metadata.summary: The Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1890 aims to prevent cruelty to domestic or captured animals. It defines specific offences such as overdriving, binding animals in painful positions, selling suffering animals, and employing unfit animals. The Act prescribes penalties including fines and imprisonment for these offences and grants powers for search, seizure, and making rules regarding animal care.

metadata.short_title: The Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act, 2016
metadata.long_title: An Act to make provisions for prevention of electronic crimes
establishes: Social Media Protection and Regulatory Authority
metadata.one_line: This Act prevents unauthorized acts on information systems, defines cybercrimes, and establishes authorities for investigation and prosecution.
metadata.summary: The Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act, 2016 provides a comprehensive legal framework to prevent unauthorized acts regarding information systems and data. It establishes the Social Media Protection and Regulatory Authority, creates specific offences such as cyber terrorism and child pornography, and outlines procedures for investigation and international cooperation. The Act applies to citizens within Pakistan and extends to acts committed outside if they affect persons or property in Pakistan.

metadata.short_title: The Prevention of Gambling Act, 1977
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the prevention of gambling
metadata.status_evidence: This Act has ceased to have effect w.e.f. 15-3-78 clue to the revocation of Proclamation of Emergency on 15-9-77, under Article 232 of the Constitution of Pakistan. 1973 except the Islamabad Capital Territory.
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years or fine up to two thousand rupees
metadata.one_line: An Act to prevent gambling by defining offenses, penalties, and powers to search gaming houses.
metadata.summary: This Act provides for the prevention of gambling by defining common gaming-houses and instruments of gaming. It prescribes penalties for owning, keeping, or being found in such places, as well as for gaming in public or private areas. The Act grants magistrates powers to enter and search suspected locations and includes provisions for pardoning accomplices who provide evidence.

metadata.short_title: The Prevention of Seditious Meetings Act, 1911
metadata.long_title: An Act to consolidate and amend the law relating to the prevention of public meetings likely to promote sedition or to cause a disturbance of public tranquility.
repeals: Repealed by the Repealing Act, 1927 (XII of 1927), s. 2 and Schedule
metadata.status_evidence: [Repeals.] Rep. by the Repealing Act, 1927 (XII of 1927), s. 2 and Schedule.
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to six Months, or fine, or with both
metadata.one_line: Consolidates laws preventing public meetings likely to promote sedition or disturb public tranquility.
metadata.summary: This Act consolidates and amends the law regarding the prevention of public meetings that may promote sedition or cause a disturbance of public tranquility. It empowers Provincial Governments to notify proclaimed areas where strict controls apply, requiring written notice to District Magistrates for such meetings. The Act defines public meetings, outlines penalties for holding unauthorized meetings or delivering speeches in public places, and designates the cognizance of offences to courts not inferior to a Magistrate of the first class.

metadata.short_title: The Prevention of Smuggling Act, 1977
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for effective prevention of smuggling and for matters connected therewith.
metadata.commencement: on such day as the Federal Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, appoint
repeals: Chapter VI of this Act (Amendment of the Customs Act, 1969)
Section 52 (Repeal)
metadata.status_evidence: Omitted by the Federal Laws (Revision and Declaration) Ordinance, 1981 (XXVII of 1981), s. 3 and Sch., II.
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a period not exceeding three years (for failure to give security); other penalties implied via fines and forfeiture
metadata.one_line: This Act provides for the prevention of smuggling, preventive detention, forfeiture of smuggled property, and establishes special courts and prosecutors.
metadata.summary: The Prevention of Smuggling Act, 1977 was enacted to effectively prevent smuggling and related matters. It empowers Federal and Provincial Governments to detain suspected smugglers, requires bonds from accused persons, and allows for the forfeiture of property acquired through smuggling. The Act establishes Special Judges and Special Appellate Courts to conduct inquiries and trials, while also providing indemnity to government officers acting in good faith under the law.

name: Prevention Of Smuggling Of Migrants Act, 2018

metadata.short_title: The Prevention of Smuggling of Migrants Act, 2018
metadata.long_title: An Act to prevent the smuggling of migrants
repeals: The Prevention of Smuggling of Migrants Ordinance, 2018 (VII of 2018)
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for fourteen years and fine up to ten million rupees
metadata.one_line: This Act prevents migrant smuggling, defines offences and penalties, and establishes investigative mechanisms.
metadata.summary: The Prevention of Smuggling of Migrants Act, 2018 provides effective measures to prevent the smuggling of migrants by land, sea, and air. It defines key terms such as 'migrant', 'smuggling of migrants', and 'organized criminal group' while establishing specific offences related to facilitating illegal entry and harbouring illegal residents. The Act empowers the Federal Investigation Agency to investigate these offences and mandates cooperation with international authorities.

name: Prevention of Trafficking In Persons Act, 2018

metadata.short_title: The Prevention of Trafficking in Persons Act, 2018
metadata.long_title: An Act to prevent and combat trafficking in persons especially women and children
repeals: The Prevention and Control of Human Trafficking Ordinance, 2002 (LIX of 2002)
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for fourteen years and fine up to two million rupees
metadata.one_line: An Act to prevent and combat trafficking in persons, especially women and children, defining offences and penalties.
metadata.summary: This Act provides effective measures to prevent and combat trafficking in persons, with a specific focus on protecting women and children. It defines key terms such as 'child', 'coercion', and 'compelled labour', and establishes severe penalties for recruiters, transporters, and those involved in organized beggary or sexual exploitation. The legislation also outlines provisions for the safety of victims and witnesses, compensation mechanisms, and the repeal of the previous 2002 Ordinance.

name: Price Control and Prevention of Profiteering and Hoarding Act, 1977

metadata.short_title: The Price Control and Prevention of Profiteering and Hoarding Act, 1977
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for price control and prevention of profiteering and hoarding.
repeals: The Price Control and Prevention of Profiteering and Hoarding Act, 1977
metadata.status_evidence: [Repeal.] Omitted by the Federal laws (Revision and Declaration) Ordinance, 1981 (XXVII of 1981), s. 3 and Sch., II.
establishes: Deputy Controller-General of Prices and Supplies
Assistant Controller-General of Prices and Supplies
metadata.one_line: This Act empowers the Federal Government to control prices and prevent profiteering and hoarding of essential commodities across Pakistan.
metadata.summary: The Price Control and Prevention of Profiteering and Hoarding Act, 1977 was enacted to regulate the prices, production, movement, and distribution of essential commodities in Pakistan. It grants the Federal Government broad powers to issue orders fixing maximum prices, restricting stock possession, and requiring dealers to maintain records and display price lists. The Act defines key terms such as 'dealer', 'essential commodity', and 'Controller-General' and establishes penalties for contraventions, including attempts and abetments. Although the text includes a repeal section indicating its omission by a later ordinance, the document outlines the mechanisms for equitable distribution of goods at fair prices.

name: Prime Minister's Salary, Allowances and Privileges Act,1975

metadata.short_title: The Prime Minister's Salary, Allowances and Privileges Act, 1975
metadata.long_title: An Act to determine the salary, allowances and privileges of the Prime Minister.
metadata.commencement: at once; deemed to have taken effect on the fourteenth day of August, 1973
metadata.one_line: This Act determines the salary, allowances, and privileges of the Prime Minister of Pakistan.
metadata.summary: The Prime Minister's Salary, Allowances and Privileges Act, 1975 establishes the financial compensation and benefits for the office holder. It defines specific terms such as 'family' and 'official residence', sets a fixed monthly salary, and outlines allowances for equipment, travel, and official use of vehicles and aircraft. The Act also provides for security arrangements and discretionary grants for official duties.

metadata.short_title: The Prisoners Act, 1900
metadata.long_title: An Act to consolidate the law relating to Prisoners confined by order of a Court.
metadata.one_line: Consolidates laws relating to prisoners confined by order of a Court in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Act consolidates the law regarding prisoners confined by court orders. It defines terms like 'Court' and 'prison', outlines the duties of prison officers regarding detention and discharge, and provides procedures for executing sentences and removing prisoners. The Act also empowers civil and criminal courts to require prisoner attendance for evidence or answering charges.

metadata.short_title: The Prisons Act, 1894
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the law relating to Prisons
repeals: Bombay Act, II of 1874
metadata.one_line: An Act to amend the law relating to prisons and provide rules for their regulation in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the law relating to prisons in Pakistan and provides rules for their regulation. It defines terms such as 'prison' and outlines the duties of various officers including Inspectors-General, Superintendents, Medical Officers, and Jailers. The legislation covers admission, removal, discharge, discipline, food, clothing, employment, health, visits, offences, and miscellaneous matters regarding prison administration.

name: Private Military Organizations (Abolition and Prohibition) Act, 1973

metadata.short_title: The Private Military Organisations (Abolition and Prohibition) Act, 1973
metadata.long_title: An Act to abolish, and provide a penalty for the formation of, certain organisations prohibited by the Constitution
metadata.max_penalty: five years imprisonment and fine
key_definitions: private organisation capable of functioning as a military organisation
organised, trained or equipped for use or display of physical force
metadata.one_line: Abolishes private military organisations prohibited by the Constitution and sets penalties for forming them.
metadata.summary: This Act abolishes private organisations capable of functioning as military units, which are prohibited under Article 256 of the Constitution. It empowers the Federal Government to declare such organisations illegal via official Gazette notification without disclosing facts against public interest. The law prescribes imprisonment up to five years and a fine for forming, joining, or participating in these prohibited groups.

name: Private Power and Infrastructure Board Act, 2012

metadata.short_title: The Private Power and Infrastructure Board Act, 2012
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for establishment of the Private Power and Infrastructure Board.
repeals: The Alternative Energy Development Board Act, 2010
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Private Power and Infrastructure Board to facilitate private sector investment in power projects.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Private Power and Infrastructure Board (PPIB) as an independent body corporate to implement power policies and develop infrastructure in the private sector. The Board aims to promote private investment, safeguard existing investments, and provide a one-window facility for investors in the power sector. It also facilitates the development of transmission, distribution, and generation of conventional and alternative energy to achieve sustainable economic growth.

metadata.short_title: The Private Security Companies Ordinance, 2001
metadata.long_title: An ordinance to provide for regulation of private security companies in the Islamabad Capital Territory and for matters connected therewith and ancillary thereto
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Islamabad Capital Territory, Islamabad
establishes: Competent Authority (Chief Commissioner Islamabad Capital Administration)
metadata.administering_body: Federal Government (via Competent Authority and Licensing Officer)
metadata.one_line: Regulates private security companies in Islamabad Capital Territory through licensing, uniform rules, and penalties.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance regulates the business of private security companies within the Islamabad Capital Territory. It establishes a licensing system managed by a Licensing Officer appointed by the Chief Commissioner, requiring registration under the Companies Ordinance, 1984. The law prohibits employees from wearing uniforms similar to armed forces or police and restricts the possession of arms without specific rules. It also defines offences related to unlicensed operation and outlines penalties for directors and officers who fail to prevent crimes committed by their staff.

metadata.short_title: The Privatisation Commission Ordinance, 2000
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the establishment of the Privatisation Commission for implementing the privatisation policy of the Federal Government and to provide for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto
repeals: existing Commission
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Privatisation Commission to implement federal privatization policy and manage related assets.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Privatisation Commission as a body corporate to implement the Federal Government's privatization policy. It provides for the Commission's functions, powers, management structure, and financial provisions including the creation of a Privatization Fund. The document also sets out procedures for asset valuation, modes of privatization, dispute resolution through an Appellate Tribunal, and grants immunity from taxes to the Commission.

metadata.short_title: The Privy Purses (Charged Expenditure) Act, 1968
metadata.long_title: An Act to declare the expenditure relating to privy purses of Rulers of certain former States to be a charge on the Central Consolidated Fund
metadata.one_line: Declares payments to former rulers as a charge on the Central Consolidated Fund.
metadata.summary: This Act declares that sums payable as privy purses to Rulers of certain former States are a charge on the Central Consolidated Fund. It applies to agreements between the Federal Government and these Rulers or their successors. The expenditure is deemed always to have been charged and paid out of that specific fund.

metadata.short_title: The Probation of Offenders Ordinance, 1960
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the release on probation of offenders in certain cases and for matters incidental thereto
metadata.commencement: on such date or dates as the Federal Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, appoint
metadata.one_line: Provides for the release on probation of offenders and establishes courts and officers to manage probation orders.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance allows courts to discharge offenders conditionally or make probation orders for those convicted of specific offences. It defines the roles of probation officers, who must visit offenders and ensure they adhere to bond conditions. The law also outlines procedures for varying conditions, handling failures to observe bonds, and paying compensation for injuries caused.

metadata.short_title: The Professions Tax Limitation Act, 1941
metadata.long_title: An Act to limit to a maximum of two hundred thousand rupees per annum the amount payable in respect of any person by way of tax on professions, trades, callings or employments.
repeals: The Schedule
metadata.one_line: This Act limits the annual tax on professions, trades, callings or employments to a maximum of one hundred thousand rupees.
metadata.summary: The Professions Tax Limitation Act, 1941 sets a maximum limit of one hundred thousand rupees per annum for taxes imposed by Provincial Assemblies on professions, trades, callings, or employments. It clarifies that such taxes shall not be regarded as improving income tax and validates levies made after July 1, 1977, within this limit. The Act extends to the whole of Pakistan and was originally enacted under Martial Law in 1941.

name: Prohibitation of Smoking and Protection of Non-Smokers Health Ordinance, 2002

metadata.short_title: The Prohibition of Smoking and Protection of Non-Smokers Health Ordinance, 2002
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for prohibition of smoking and other tobacco uses in places of public work or use and public service vehicles and to protect the health of non-smokers and for matters connected therewith or ancillary thereto
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Federal Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, specify
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment which may extend to three months or with a fine which shall not be less then one hundred thousand rupees, or with both
key_definitions: place of public work or use
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance prohibits smoking and tobacco use in public places and vehicles to protect non-smoker health.
metadata.summary: The Prohibition of Smoking and Protection of Non-Smokers Health Ordinance, 2002 was promulgated by the President to ban smoking and other tobacco uses in public places and service vehicles. It empowers the Federal Government to declare no-smoking zones, restrict tobacco advertisements, and prohibit sales to minors or near schools. The law establishes penalties including fines and imprisonment for violations and allows authorized officers to eject violators from public premises.

metadata.short_title: The Prohibition (Enforcement of Hadd) Order, 1979
metadata.long_title: An Order to modify the existing law relating to prohibition of intoxicants so as to bring it in conformity with the injunctions of Islam as set out in the Holy Qur'an and Sunnah.
repeals: The Prohibition Act, 1977 (XXIV of 1977)
The Balochistan Prohibition Ordinance, 1978 (Balochistan Ordinance No. XI of 1978)
The North-West Frontier Province Prohibition Ordinance, 1978 (N.-W.F.P. Ordinance No. VI of 1978)
The Punjab Prohibition Ordinance, 1978 (Punjab Ordinance No.VI of 1978)
The Sind Prohibition Ordinance, 1978 (Sind Ordinance No. IV of 1978)
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for life or imprisonment not less than two years, whipping not exceeding thirty stripes, and fine
metadata.administering_body: Provincial Government (via authorised medical officers) and Collector/Prohibition Officers
metadata.one_line: This Order enforces Islamic prohibitions on intoxicants, defines offences and penalties including Hadd, and repeals previous provincial prohibition laws.
metadata.summary: The Prohibition (Enforcement of Hadd) Order, 1979 was promulgated by the President to align prohibition laws with Islamic injunctions found in the Holy Qur'an and Sunnah. It applies to the whole of Pakistan and came into force on February 10, 1979. The Order defines various terms related to intoxicants, prohibits their manufacture, sale, and possession, and prescribes severe penalties including Hadd punishment for drinking and imprisonment for trafficking opium or coca derivatives. It also establishes a framework for issuing licences for bona fide medicinal purposes and repeals several earlier provincial prohibition ordinances.

name: Protection Against Harassment of Women at the Work Place Act, 2010

metadata.short_title: Protection Against Harassment of Women at the Workplace Act, 2010
metadata.long_title: An Act to make provisions for the protection against harassment of women at the workplace
metadata.one_line: This Act protects women from harassment at the workplace by establishing inquiry committees and an Ombudsperson.
metadata.summary: The Protection Against Harassment of Women at the Workplace Act, 2010 provides legal provisions to protect women from harassment in the workplace. It establishes mechanisms including Inquiry Committees and an Ombudsperson to handle complaints regarding sexual advances, stalking, or gender-based discrimination. The Act defines various roles such as employers, employees (including gig workers), and complainants, outlining procedures for inquiries and employer responsibilities to prevent retaliation.

name: Protection of Breast Feeding and Child Nutrition Ordinance, 2002

metadata.short_title: Protection of Breast-feeding and Child Nutrition Ordinance, 2002
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for protection of breast-feeding and nutrition for infants and young children
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years or with fine which shall not be less than fifty thousand rupees or more than five hundred thousand rupees, or both
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance protects breast-feeding and child nutrition by regulating designated products and establishing a National Infant Feeding Board.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance aims to ensure safe and adequate nutrition for infants and young children by promoting breast-feeding and regulating the marketing of breast milk substitutes. It establishes a National Infant Feeding Board and Provincial Committees to oversee implementation, prohibits specific advertising practices, and sets penalties for contraventions. The law applies to manufacturers, distributors, health workers, and facilities across Pakistan.

name: Protection of Communal Properties of Minorities Ordinance, 2001

metadata.short_title: The Protection of Communal Properties of Minorities Ordinance, 2001
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to protect the properties of minority communities meant for their communal use
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment up to seven years and fine not less than one hundred thousand rupees
key_definitions: Property (places of worship, monasteries, seminaries, vicarages, dharamshalas, gaoshalas, burial places, community centers, social welfare, educational, health and recreational institutions meant for communal use)
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance protects minority communal properties by banning their sale or transfer without Federal Government approval.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance aims to protect properties belonging to minority communities in Pakistan that are meant for their communal use. It prohibits the buying, selling, or transferring of such properties without a No Objection Certificate (NOC) from the Federal Government, which is issued based on recommendations from the National Commission for Minorities. The law explicitly excludes evacuee trust properties vested under the Evacuee Trust Properties Act, 1975. Violations attract imprisonment up to seven years and a fine of at least one hundred thousand rupees.

metadata.short_title: The Protection of Economic Reforms Act, 1992
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for furtherance and protection of economic reforms and other matters relating thereto
metadata.one_line: Provides legal protection for economic reforms including foreign currency freedom and investment security.
metadata.summary: This Act creates a liberal environment for savings and investments by providing legal protection to various economic reforms introduced since November 1990. It grants citizens the freedom to deal with foreign currency, ensures immunity for foreign currency accounts from tax inquiries, and protects fiscal incentives for industries. The legislation also safeguards private sector ownership transferred from the government and prohibits the compulsory acquisition of foreign or Pakistani investments.

name: Protection of Journalists and Media Professionals Act, 2021

metadata.short_title: The Protection of Journalists and Media Professionals Act, 2021
metadata.long_title: An Act to promote, protect and effectively ensure the independence, impartiality, safety and freedom of expression of journalists and media professionals.
establishes: Independent Commission for the Protection of Journalists and Media Professionals
metadata.one_line: This Act protects journalists and media professionals by establishing an independent commission, mandating insurance, and ensuring safety training.
metadata.summary: The Protection of Journalists and Media Professionals Act, 2021 aims to safeguard the rights, safety, and freedom of expression of journalists and media professionals in Pakistan. It establishes an Independent Commission to investigate threats and abuse, mandates life and health insurance for all covered professionals, and requires mandatory safety training provided free of cost by media owners. The Act also defines key terms such as 'Journalist' and 'Media professional', outlines obligations regarding remuneration and management diversity, and ensures equal implementation during peace or conflict.

metadata.short_title: The Protection of Pakistan Act, 2014
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for protection against waging of war or insurrection against Pakistan and the prevention of acts threatening the security of Pakistan
key_definitions: Preparing to commit a scheduled offence
metadata.one_line: Provides for protection against war/insurrection, defines militants, establishes special courts and prosecuting agencies for speedy trials of scheduled offences.
metadata.summary: This Act provides legal mechanisms to protect Pakistan against waging of war or insurrection and prevents acts threatening national security. It empowers armed forces and civil armed forces to use necessary force to prevent scheduled offences and allows for the establishment of Special Courts and a Prosecuting Agency. The Act defines key terms such as 'militant' and 'enemy alien', outlines procedures for investigation and trial, and specifies that it remains in force for an initial period of two years.

metadata.short_title: The Protection of Ports (Special Measures) Act, 1948
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for special measures to ensure the protection of ports.
metadata.territorial_extent: Pakistan (extendable to any port in Pakistan by notification)
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both
metadata.one_line: This Act empowers the Federal Government to declare ports as protected areas and regulate entry to ensure port security.
metadata.summary: The Protection of Ports (Special Measures) Act, 1948 provides special measures to ensure the protection of ports in Pakistan. It allows the Federal Government to declare specific areas around a port as 'protected areas' and make rules to control or regulate the admission and conduct of persons within those areas. The Act grants powers to restrict entry, remove persons, and deal with suspicious loitering, while establishing penalties for contravention and barring certain legal proceedings against officers acting in good faith.

metadata.short_title: The Provident Funds Act, 1925
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend and consolidate the law relating to Government and other Provident Funds
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Federal Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, appoint
repeals: Central Laws (Statute Reform) Ordinance, 1960 (21 of 1960), s.3 and 2nd Sch.
metadata.one_line: Amends and consolidates laws regarding Government and other Provident Funds, defining terms and protecting deposits.
metadata.summary: This Act amends and consolidates the law relating to Government and other Provident Funds. It defines key terms such as compulsory deposit, contribution, and dependant, while providing protection for compulsory deposits against attachment or assignment. The Act applies to the whole of Pakistan and comes into force on a date appointed by the Federal Government via notification.

metadata.short_title: The Provincial Employees' Social Security Ordinance, 1965
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to introduce a scheme of Social Security for providing benefits to certain employees or their dependents in the event of sickness, maternity, employment, injury or death and for matters ancillary thereto.
repeals: The Employees' Social Insurance Ordinance, 1962 (XXII of 1962)
metadata.one_line: Establishes a social security scheme for employees in West Pakistan providing benefits for sickness, maternity, injury, and death.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance introduces a comprehensive social security scheme for employees in the Province of West Pakistan. It establishes an Employees' Social Security Institution with a Governing Body to manage contributions and provide benefits such as sickness, maternity, injury, disablement, and death grants. The law also creates a Social Security Court to adjudicate disputes and repeals previous conflicting legislation regarding social security in that province.

name: Provincial Industrial Development Corporation (West Pakistan) Ordinance, 1962

metadata.short_title: The Provincial Industrial Development Corporation (West Pakistan) Ordinance, 1962
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to establish an Industrial Development Corporation.
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Pakistan Industrial Development Corporation to promote economic and industrial development.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Pakistan Industrial Development Corporation as a body corporate with perpetual succession. It defines the Corporation's share capital, management structure, and powers to make rules and regulations. The document outlines the industries covered in its schedule and provides for the winding up of the Corporation only by Government order.

metadata.short_title: The Provincial Insolvency Act, 1920
metadata.long_title: An Act to consolidate and amend the Law relating to Insolvency as administered by Courts having jurisdiction outside the Karachi Division.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of Pakistan except the Karachi Division
repeals: Insolvency (Karachi Division and Dacca) Act (III of 1909)
metadata.one_line: Consolidates and amends the law relating to insolvency proceedings outside the Karachi Division.
metadata.summary: This Act consolidates and amends the law regarding insolvency as administered by courts in Sindh (excluding the Karachi Division). It establishes procedures for petitions, adjudication of debtors, appointment of receivers, and the distribution of insolvent property among creditors. The Act also covers the annulment of adjudications, compositions with creditors, and penalties for undischarged insolvents.

metadata.short_title: The Provincial Motor Vehicles Ordinance, 1965
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend and consolidate the law relating to Motor Vehicles in the Province of West Pakistan.
repeals: The Motor Vehicles Act, 1939
The Motor Vehicles (Sind Amendment) Act, Sind XIV of 1948
The Motor Vehicles (North-West Frontier Province (Amendment) Act, 1950
The Motor Vehicles (Sind Amendment) Act, Sind XVIII of 1951
The Motor Vehicles (North-West Frontier Province (Amendment) Act, 1953
The Motor Vehicles (West Pakistan Amendment) Act, 1958
The Motor Vehicles (West Pakistan Amendment) Ordinance, 1960
The Motor Vehicles (West Pakistan Amendment) Ordinance, 1963
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance consolidates and amends laws regarding motor vehicles, licensing, registration, and traffic control in West Pakistan.
metadata.summary: The Provincial Motor Vehicles Ordinance, 1965 was promulgated by the Governor of West Pakistan to consolidate and amend existing laws relating to motor vehicles. It establishes a comprehensive framework for driver licensing, vehicle registration, transport permits, and traffic control measures applicable throughout West Pakistan. The document creates offences related to driving without a licence, speeding, and unsafe vehicle conditions, prescribing penalties up to Rs. 500. It also sets out provisions for compensation in case of passenger injury and repeals several previous Acts and Ordinances.

name: Provincial Service Tribunals (Extension of Provisions of the Constitution) Act, 1974

metadata.short_title: The Provincial Service Tribunals (Extension of Provisions of the Constitution) Act, 1974
metadata.long_title: An Act to extend the provisions of clause (2) of Article 212 of the Constitution to the Provincial Service Tribunals.
metadata.one_line: Extends Article 212(2) of the Constitution to Provincial Service Tribunals in Balochistan, NWFP, Punjab and Sind.
metadata.summary: This Act extends the provisions of clause (2) of Article 212 of the Constitution of Pakistan to Service Tribunals established by Provincial Assemblies. It responds to requests from the Assemblies of Balochistan, North-West Frontier Province, Punjab, and Sind to apply these constitutional safeguards to their respective tribunals. The Act came into force immediately upon enactment.

metadata.short_title: The Provisional Collection of Taxes Act, 1931
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the law providing for the immediate effect for a limited period of provisions in Bills relating to the imposition [, increase or reduction] or duties of customs or excise [, or sales tax].
repeals: Section 5 (as amended)
metadata.status_evidence: 6. [Repealed] ... Repealed by the Repealing Act, 1938 (Act No. I of 1938), s. 2 and Schedule.
metadata.one_line: This Act allows the Federal Government to give immediate effect to tax provisions in Bills before they are enacted.
metadata.summary: The Provisional Collection of Taxes Act, 1931 empowers the Federal Government to insert declarations into Bills relating to customs, excise, or sales tax duties. These declarations allow such provisions to have immediate force of law as if enacted on the day the Bill is introduced in the Central Legislature. The Act specifies conditions under which these declared provisions cease to have effect, either when the Bill becomes an enactment or after sixty days, and outlines mechanisms for refunds or demands if the rates differ from what was originally proposed.

metadata.short_title: The Public Accountants' Default Act, 1850
metadata.long_title: An Act for avoiding loss by the default of Public Accountants
metadata.territorial_extent: all the Provinces and the Capital of the Federation, except the Scheduled Districts (with specific extensions to certain Scheduled Districts in Punjab, Baluchistan, and Leased Areas)
repeals: former rules validated by section 6
metadata.one_line: This Act requires public accountants to provide security for the discharge of their office trusts and accounts.
metadata.summary: The Public Accountants' Default Act, 1850 mandates that every public accountant must give security for the due discharge of their office trusts and the proper accounting of all moneys under their control. It defines 'public accountant' to include officials like Official Assignees, Trustees, and government servants entrusted with money or lands. The Act empowers the head of an office to prosecute accountants and sureties for losses or defalcation as if it were a land-revenue arrear, applying relevant revenue recovery laws to such proceedings.

metadata.short_title: The Public Debt Act, 1944
metadata.long_title: An Act to consolidate and amend the law relating to Government securities and to the management of the public debt
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Federal Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, appoint
repeals: The Securities Act, 1920 (X of 1920)
key_definitions: Government (Federal or Provincial Government by whom the security is created and issued)
metadata.one_line: Consolidates and amends laws regarding Government securities, public debt management, and transfers.
metadata.summary: This Act consolidates and amends the law relating to Government securities and the management of the public debt. It defines terms such as 'Government security' and outlines procedures for transferring securities, handling deaths of holders, and issuing duplicate bonds. The Act empowers the State Bank of Pakistan (referred to as 'the Bank') to manage these securities and make rules regarding their transfer and administration.

metadata.short_title: The Public Finance Management Act, 2019
metadata.long_title: An Act to strengthen management of public finances with the view to improving definition and implementation of fiscal policy for better macroeconomic management, to clarify institutional responsibilities related to financial management, and to strengthen budgetary management.
repeals: The General Financial Rules
Federal Treasury Rules
Fundamental Rules and Supplementary Rules
Civil Service Regulations
Provident Fund Rules
Civil Pension Rules
Methods and procedures prescribed by the Auditor-General of Pakistan with reference to deposit and withdrawal of public money
Public Works Department Code
the New System of Financial Control and Budgeting, 2018
the Central Public Works Account Code
the Accounting Policies and Procedures Manual
establishes: committee to oversee implementation of this Act
metadata.one_line: This Act strengthens public finance management to improve fiscal policy and clarify institutional responsibilities.
metadata.summary: The Public Finance Management Act, 2019 aims to strengthen the management of public finances in Pakistan. It clarifies institutional responsibilities related to financial management and enhances budgetary processes. The Act applies to the Federal Consolidated Fund, Public Account, and all matters connected with the Federal Government's finances.

metadata.short_title: The Public Gambling Act, 1867
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the punishment of public gambling and the keeping of common gaming-houses in [the Punjab].
repeals: Act XVIII of 1874
metadata.status_evidence: [Repealed by Act I of 2019]
metadata.max_penalty: fine not exceeding six hundred rupees or imprisonment for a term not exceeding one year
metadata.one_line: This Act punishes public gambling and keeping common gaming-houses in Punjab with fines and imprisonment.
metadata.summary: The Public Gambling Act, 1867 provides for the punishment of public gambling and the operation of common gaming-houses. It defines a common gaming-house as any place where instruments of gaming are kept or used for profit. The Act grants police powers to enter suspected houses, seize instruments, and destroy them upon conviction. Penalties include fines up to six hundred rupees and imprisonment up to one year for subsequent offences.

metadata.short_title: The Public Health (Emergency Provisions) Ordinance, 1944
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to make special provisions in regard to public health.
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment which may extend to three months or with fine or with both
metadata.one_line: Empowers the Federal Government to take emergency measures for public health, supersede local authorities, and make rules.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance provides special powers to the appropriate Government (Federal or Provincial) to prevent the spread of human disease and safeguard public health during an emergency. It allows the government to direct local authorities to take specific measures, appoint additional health staff, assume superintendence of services, and even supersede local authorities if they fail to comply. The Ordinance also grants powers to modify existing rules, make new regulations with criminal penalties, and protect officials acting in good faith under its provisions.

metadata.short_title: The Public Investments (Financial Safeguards) Ordinance, 1960
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for financial safeguards in respect of certain investments made out of public revenues.
metadata.max_penalty: simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to three months, or with fine which may extend to ten thousand rupees, or with both
metadata.one_line: Provides financial safeguards for public revenue investments and empowers the government to prescribe procedures and give directions.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes financial safeguards for corporations, institutions, or undertakings established with the aid of public revenues. It empowers the appropriate Government to prescribe financial procedures, issue general or special financial directions, and depute officers to scrutinize transactions. The law also outlines penalties for non-compliance, false information, and offences by corporations, while excluding certain privatized bodies from its scope.

metadata.short_title: The Public Order (Meetings) Ordinance, 1958
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to make provision for the preservation of public order on the occasion of public meetings and to prevent disturbance thereat.
metadata.max_penalty: rigorous imprisonment which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both
metadata.one_line: Preserves public order at meetings and defines offences like disorderly conduct and carrying weapons.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance provides for the preservation of public order during public meetings and prevents disturbances. It defines terms such as 'public meeting' and 'public place', and establishes offences for disorderly conduct, carrying offensive weapons, and using insulting language intended to provoke a breach of peace. Offences under this law are cognizable and non-bailable, punishable by rigorous imprisonment up to two years or a fine.

metadata.short_title: The Public Order (Political Uniforms) Ordinance, 1958
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to prohibit the wearing of uniforms in connection with political purposes and the maintenance by private persons of associations of a military or semi-military character, and matters connected therewith.
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for two years or fine up to one thousand rupees or both
metadata.one_line: Prohibits wearing political uniforms and maintaining quasi-military associations in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance prohibits the wearing of uniforms for political purposes and the maintenance of private associations with military or semi-military characteristics. It applies to the whole of Pakistan and comes into force immediately. The law defines specific terms like 'Meeting' and 'Public meeting', outlines offences related to parades and quasi-military groups, and prescribes punishments including imprisonment up to two years or fines.

metadata.short_title: The Public Private Partnership Authority Act, 2017
metadata.long_title: An Act to create an enabling environment for development projects and the provision of public infrastructure and related services in Pakistan through private sector participation.
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Public Private Partnership Authority to regulate private sector participation in public infrastructure projects.
metadata.summary: This Act creates an enabling environment for development projects and public infrastructure provision through private sector participation in Pakistan. It establishes the Public Private Partnership Authority, its Board, and various funds including the P3A Fund and Viability Gap Fund to support economically justified but financially non-viable projects. The legislation outlines the institutional framework, approval processes for qualified projects, contractual relationships, dispute settlement mechanisms, and provisions for tax exemptions and hiring of consultants.

metadata.short_title: The Public Procurement Regulatory Authority Ordinance, 2002
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the establishment of Public Procurement Regulatory Authority for regulating public procurement of goods, services, works and disposal of public assets in the public sector and for matters connected therewith or ancillary thereto
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Public Procurement Regulatory Authority to regulate public procurement of goods, services, works and disposal of public assets.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Public Procurement Regulatory Authority as a body corporate to regulate public procurement in the federal sector. It defines key terms such as 'goods', 'services', 'works', and 'public procurement' and outlines the Authority's functions, powers, and management structure including a Board and Managing Director. The document also provides for financial provisions, grievance redressal mechanisms, and exemptions for certain privatized bodies.

name: Publication of Laws of Pakistan Act, 2016

metadata.short_title: The Publication of Laws of Pakistan Act, 2016
metadata.long_title: An Act to ensure publication of the text of the laws of Pakistan free from errors of reproduction, updating and printing
metadata.administering_body: the administrative division and each administrative department
metadata.one_line: This Act ensures accurate publication of Pakistani laws by regulating publishers and establishing a review cell.
metadata.summary: The Publication of Laws of Pakistan Act, 2016 aims to ensure that the text of laws in Pakistan is published without errors in reproduction, updating, or printing. It establishes a 'Laws of Pakistan Cell' within administrative divisions to register publishers, review proposed publications for accuracy, and maintain authentic versions of laws. The Act defines key terms such as 'publisher', 'law of Pakistan', and 'bookseller', and outlines offences and penalties for publishing inaccurate texts, while also providing mechanisms for appeals and indemnity for officials acting in good faith.

name: Publication of the Holy Quran (Elimination of Printing Errors) Act, 1973

metadata.short_title: The Publication of the Holy Quran (Elimination of Printing Errors) Act, 1973
metadata.long_title: An Act to ensure publication of the text of the Holy Quran free from errors of printing and matters connected therewith
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of Islamabad Capital Territory
metadata.max_penalty: three years imprisonment or fine not less than twenty thousand rupees or both
key_definitions: damaged or Shaheed copy of the Holy Quran
metadata.one_line: This Act ensures error-free publication and recording of the Holy Quran by regulating publishers and establishing a Quran Board.
metadata.summary: The Act aims to ensure that the text of the Holy Quran is published free from printing errors. It establishes a Quran Board comprising prominent Ulema, Huffaz, and Qaris to authenticate a standard copy of the Quran. The law regulates the registration of publishers and recording companies, mandates specific printing standards, prohibits certain types of translation without Arabic text, and prescribes penalties for offences related to the publication or recording of erroneous copies.

metadata.short_title: The Punjab Laws Act, 1872
metadata.long_title: An Act for declaring which of certain rules, laws and regulations have the force of law in the Punjab and for other purposes.
metadata.territorial_extent: the territories comprised in the Punjab
repeals: Reg. I of 1798
Reg. XVII of 1806
Reg. III of 1818
Reg. XI of 1825

Rules for the conservancy of Forests and Jungles in the Hill Districts of the Punjab Territories, Sanctioned by the Governor General in Council in letter of the Secretary to the Government of India, No. 1789, 21st May, 1855
metadata.repealed_by: Second Repealing and Amending Act, 1914 (XVII of 1914)
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to fifty rupees, or with both
