metadata.one_line: Declares which rules and laws have force in Punjab and consolidates local enactments.
metadata.summary: This Act declares which specific rules, laws, and regulations previously made for the Punjab shall continue to be in force. It consolidates various pre-existing statutes regarding civil and criminal judicature, land decrees, insolvency, and local customs. The Act also empowers the Provincial Government to establish watchmen systems and levy local taxes, while repealing numerous older enactments listed in its schedules.

metadata.short_title: The Qanun-e-Shahadat Order, 1984
metadata.long_title: An Act to revise, amend and consolidate the law of evidence so as to bring it in conformity with the injunctions of Islam as laid down in the Holy Quran.
repeals: The Evidence Act, 1872 (I of 1872)
metadata.one_line: Consolidates and revises the law of evidence in Pakistan to conform with Islamic injunctions.
metadata.summary: This Order consolidates and revises the law of evidence in Pakistan to align it with Islamic principles. It covers the relevancy of facts, competence of witnesses, admissions, confessions, and documentary evidence. The text also includes provisions for modern devices like video calls and explicitly repeals the Evidence Act, 1872.

metadata.short_title: The Quaid-e-Azam University Act, 1973
metadata.long_title: An Act to reconstitute and reorganize the University of Islamabad.
metadata.administering_body: University of Islamabad (later renamed Quaid-e-Azam University)
metadata.one_line: This Act reconstitutes and reorganizes the University of Islamabad, renaming it Quaid-e-Azam University and establishing its governing bodies.
metadata.summary: The Quaid-e-Azam University Act, 1973 was enacted to reconstitute and reorganize the University of Islamabad. It establishes the university as a body corporate with specific officers including a Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, Registrar, and Treasurer. The Act defines the composition and powers of various authorities such as the Syndicate, Academic Council, and Finance and Planning Committee, while also outlining provisions for affiliated colleges, statutes, regulations, and student discipline.

metadata.short_title: The Quaid-i-Azam's Mazar (Protection and Maintenance) Ordinance, 1971
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the protection and maintenance of the Quaid-i-Azam's Mazar.
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance protects and maintains the Quaid-i-Azam's Mazar, vests it in the Federal Government, and prohibits damaging acts or meetings.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance provides for the protection and maintenance of the Quaid-i-Azam's Mazar at Karachi. It declares the site a national historical monument and vests it in the Federal Government. The law prohibits meetings, demonstrations, and entry with weapons within the Mazar, while establishing a specific fund for its maintenance and prescribing penalties for contraventions.

metadata.short_title: Railway Regulatory Authority Ordinance, 2002
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the Establishment of the Railway Regulatory Authority
metadata.commencement: at once (except provisions in the First Schedule)
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Railway Regulatory Authority to foster competition and regulate railway operations in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Railway Regulatory Authority to foster competition, encourage private sector investment, and regulate passenger and goods train operations on the railway network. It grants the Authority exclusive power to issue licenses for track access and sets out its functions, powers, and enforcement mechanisms. The document also amends existing laws like the Railways Act, 1890 and the Pakistan Railways Police Act, 1977 to align them with the new regulatory framework.

metadata.short_title: The Railway Stores (Unlawful Possession) Ordinance, 1944
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to make special provision for the punishment of the offence of unlawful possession of railway stores.
metadata.status_evidence: Subs. by the Central Laws (Statute Reform) Ordinance No XXI of 1960, s. 3 and 2nd Sch.
metadata.repealed_by: Central Laws (Statute Reform) Ordinance No XXI of 1960
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to five years or with fine or with both
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance punishes unlawful possession of railway stores with up to five years imprisonment.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance was promulgated by the Governor-General under emergency powers to punish the offence of unlawful possession of railway stores. It applies to the whole of Pakistan and came into force immediately upon enactment. The law defines 'railway stores' broadly to include articles used in construction, operation, or maintenance of a railway. Possession of such articles without lawful proof is punishable by imprisonment up to five years, a fine, or both.

metadata.short_title: The Railways (Local Authorities' Taxation) Act, 1941
metadata.long_title: An Act to regulate the extent to which railway property shall be liable to taxation imposed by an authority within a Province.
metadata.one_line: Regulates the taxation liability of federal railway property to local authorities within Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Act regulates the extent to which property vested in the Federal Government for railway purposes is liable to taxation imposed by local authorities. It allows the Federal Government to declare such property liable via notification and determines the tax amount or a fair alternative sum payable to local authorities. The Act also permits railway administrations to enter into contracts with local authorities for services like water supply, lighting, and scavenging without being barred by this legislation.

metadata.short_title: The Railways (Transport of Goods) Act, 1947
metadata.long_title: An Act to confer for a limited period special powers for regulating the transport of goods on railways.
metadata.one_line: Confers special powers for a limited period to regulate the transport of goods on railways.
metadata.summary: This Act confers special powers for a limited period to regulate the transport of goods on railways. It allows the Federal Government to issue directions regarding the priority or refusal of carrying specific goods based on urgent public interest. The Act extends to the whole of Pakistan and remains in force for thirty-one years from its commencement.

metadata.short_title: The Railways Act, 1890
metadata.long_title: An Act to consolidate, amend and add to the law relating to Railways
repeals: THE FIRST SCHEDULE
metadata.one_line: Consolidates, amends and adds to the law relating to railways, covering traffic, accidents, penalties, and railway servant duties.
metadata.summary: This Act consolidates and amends laws regarding railways in Pakistan. It covers preliminary matters, inspection, construction, traffic facilities, working of railways, responsibilities of licensees, accidents, and penalties for offences by companies or servants. The Act defines key terms like 'accident' and 'Authority', sets rules for carriage of goods and passengers, and outlines liabilities and criminal offences related to railway operations.

metadata.short_title: The Railways Order, 1962
repeals: Railway Board Ordinance, 1959
metadata.one_line: This Order transfers railways to Provincial Governments and establishes a Railway Board for their management.
metadata.summary: The Railways Order, 1962 was promulgated by the President to transfer railway assets from the Federal Government to Provincial Governments under Article 233 of the Constitution. It establishes a Railway Board consisting of ex officio members and independent appointees to oversee the guidance, supervision, and management of railways in Pakistan. The Order defines the composition of the Board, outlines its powers and functions regarding track access and rail development, and details the transfer of assets, liabilities, and railway servants to the respective provinces.

name: Recognition and Enforcement (Arbitration Agreement and Foreign Arbitral) Act, 2011

metadata.short_title: The Recognition and Enforcement (Arbitration Agreements and Foreign Arbitral Awards) Act, 2011
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the recognition and enforcement of arbitration agreements and foreign arbitral awards
repeals: The Arbitration (Protocol and Convention) Act, 1937 (VI of 1937)
subjects: United Nations Convention on the Recognition and Enforcement of Foreign Arbitral Awards, 1958
metadata.one_line: Provides for the recognition and enforcement of arbitration agreements and foreign arbitral awards in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Act facilitates the recognition and enforcement of arbitration agreements and foreign arbitral awards within Pakistan. It applies to agreements made on or after its commencement but excludes foreign awards made before July 14, 2005. The Act grants exclusive jurisdiction to designated High Courts for adjudicating matters related to this legislation and repeals the Arbitration (Protocol and Convention) Act, 1937.

metadata.short_title: The Recusant Witnesses Act, 1853
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Law of Evidence in the Civil Courts of the East India Company in the Bengal Presidency.
repeals: Sections 1-18
Sections 19
Sections 20-25
Sections 27-39
Section 40
Sections 41-44
metadata.status_evidence: 1-18. [Repeals; who may be witnesses; manner of summoning witnesses; contents of summons; summons how served; person summoned to produce a document.] Rep. by Act X of 1861.
metadata.one_line: Amends the law of evidence in Bengal civil courts regarding witness summons and liability for damages.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the law of evidence in the Civil Courts of the East India Company in the Bengal Presidency. It establishes provisions for summoning witnesses, serving summons, and the liability of persons who abscond or refuse to obey a summons. The text indicates that most sections have been repealed by subsequent Acts.

metadata.short_title: The Reformatory Schools Act, 1897
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the law relating to Reformatory Schools and to make further provision for dealing with youthful offenders.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of Pakistan (with specific historical extensions to Baluchistan and N.W.F.P. mentioned in footnotes)
repeals: Act XV of 1869 (as applied to youthful offenders in Reformatory Schools)
metadata.one_line: This Act establishes Reformatory Schools for youthful offenders under fifteen and outlines their management, inspection, and legal procedures.
metadata.summary: The Reformatory Schools Act, 1897 amends the law regarding institutions for youthful offenders convicted of offenses punishable by imprisonment. It empowers Provincial Governments to establish and maintain these schools, providing industrial training and proper care for boys under fifteen years of age. The Act details the appointment of Superintendents and Boards of Management, procedures for sending offenders to these schools, licensing them for employment, and penalties for those who aid their escape or supply prohibited articles.

name:
Regional Development Finance Corporation and Small Business Finance Corporation
(Amalgamation and Conversion) Ordinance, 2001

metadata.short_title: The Regional Development Finance Corporation and Small Business Finance Corporation (Amalgamation and Conversion) Ordinance, 2001
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amalgamate the Regional Development Finance Corporation and the Small Business Finance Corporation and to convert them into a public limited company
repeals: The Regional Development Finance Corporation Ordinance, 1985 (XXXII of 1985)
The Small Business Finance Corporation Act, 1972 (XXIX of 1972)
establishes: public limited company formed from RDFC and SBFC
metadata.one_line: Amalgamates RDFC and SBFC into a public limited company and transfers their assets/liabilities.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance provides for the amalgamation of the Regional Development Finance Corporation (RDFC) and the Small Business Finance Corporation (SBFC) into a single public limited company. It mandates the transfer and vesting of all assets, contracts, liabilities, and undertakings from the two original entities to the new company upon its registration. The document also ensures the continuation of pending legal proceedings and grants indemnity to the Federal Government and involved parties for actions taken in good faith under the Ordinance.

name: Regional Development Finance Corporation Ordinance, 1985(Repeal by ord.LVi of 2001,s.14(w.e.f 01-01-2002))

metadata.short_title: Regional Development Finance Corporation Ordinance, 1985
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the establishment of the Regional Development Finance Corporation and for matters connected therewith or ancillary thereto.
metadata.status_evidence: [Repeal by ord.LVi of 2001,s.14(w.e.f 01-01-2002)]
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Regional Development Finance Corporation and defines its structure, capital, and functions.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Regional Development Finance Corporation to facilitate financial activities in less-developed areas of Pakistan. It defines the Corporation's share capital, which is partially contributed by the National Development Finance Corporation and nationalized banks. The document outlines the composition of the Board of Directors, the powers of the Federal Government to direct policy, and various definitions related to loans, advances, and judicial jurisdiction.

metadata.short_title: The Registered Designs Ordinance, 2000
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to repeal and to re-enact the law relating to industrial designs
repeals: Clause (5) of section 2 and sections 43,44,45,46,47, 48, 49, 50, 51, 51A, 51B, 52, 53, and 54 of the Patents and Designs Act, 1911
metadata.max_penalty: fine
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance repeals and re-enacts laws regarding the protection and registration of industrial designs in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: The Registered Designs Ordinance, 2000 was promulgated by the President to repeal and re-enact laws relating to industrial designs. It establishes a Patent Office for registering designs and defines key terms such as 'design', 'article', and 'proprietor'. The Ordinance outlines proceedings for registration, effects of registration, infringement liabilities, and offences related to falsification or false representation of registered designs.

name: Registered Layout-Designs of Integrated Circuits Ordinance, 2000

metadata.short_title: The Registered Layout-Designs of Integrated Circuits Ordinance, 2000
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the registration of layout-designs of integrated circuits
establishes: Controller of Patents (as Controller under this Ordinance)
metadata.one_line: Provides for the registration and legal protection of original layout-designs of integrated circuits in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes a system for the legal protection of registered layout-designs of integrated circuits to fulfill international trade obligations. It defines key terms such as 'layout-design' and 'integrated circuit', outlines criteria for originality, and grants rights to creators or their successors. The Ordinance regulates registration procedures, enforcement against infringement, and provides mechanisms for appeals to the High Court.

metadata.short_title: The Registration Act, 1908
metadata.long_title: An Act to consolidate the enactments relating to the Registration of Documents.
metadata.one_line: Consolidates enactments relating to the registration of documents, wills, and land records in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Act consolidates laws regarding the registration of documents, establishing a hierarchy of registering officers including Inspectors General, Registrars, and Sub Registrars. It outlines compulsory and optional registration requirements, procedures for presenting documents, fees, penalties for false statements, and exemptions for government records. The Act also covers the deposit of wills, the effects of registration on property rights, and the use of photography for copying documents.

metadata.short_title: The Registration of Foreigners Act, 1939
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the registration of foreigners in Pakistan
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees or with both
metadata.one_line: Provides for the registration and reporting requirements for foreigners entering, present in, or departing from Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes a legal framework for registering foreigners who enter, reside in, or leave Pakistan. It empowers the Federal Government to make rules requiring foreigners to report their presence, movements, and departure details to prescribed authorities. The Act also mandates that managers of hotels, boarding-houses, vessels, or aircraft must report foreigner information and produce identity proofs when demanded. Penalties are imposed for contravening these rules, with heavier punishments for foreigners than non-foreigners.

name: Regulation of Generation Transmission and Distribution of Electric Power Act, 1997

metadata.short_title: The Regulation of Generation, Transmission and Distribution of Electric Power Act, 1997
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the regulation of generation, transmission and distribution of electric power
metadata.commencement: at once, except sections 23A, 23B, 23G and 23H which shall come into force within a period of five years of coming into force of the Regulation of Generation, Transmission and Distribution of Electric Power (Amendment) Act, 2018 or on such earlier date as the Federal Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, appoint
metadata.one_line: This Act establishes the regulatory framework for generation, transmission, and distribution of electric power in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: The Regulation of Generation, Transmission and Distribution of Electric Power Act, 1997 provides a legal framework to regulate the electric power market in Pakistan. It establishes the National Electric Power Regulatory Authority (NEPRA) and an Appellate Tribunal to oversee generation, transmission, and distribution activities. The Act covers licensing requirements for various entities, tariff determination, performance standards, and enforcement mechanisms.

name: Regulation of Mines and Oil Fields and Mineral Development (Federal Control) Act, 1948

metadata.short_title: The Regulation of Mines and Oil fields and Mineral Development Government Control Act, 1948
metadata.long_title: An Act to make provision for certain matters connected with the regulation of mines and oil fields and mineral development.
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Federal Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, appoint
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both
metadata.one_line: This Act regulates mines, oil fields, and mineral development under government control in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Act provides for the regulation of mines, oil fields, and mineral development under government control. It empowers the appropriate Government to make rules regarding licensing, royalties, production control, and pricing. The Act also outlines penalties for rule breaches, provisions for production sharing agreements, and specific concessions for foreign nationals employed in the sector.

metadata.short_title: The Religious Societies Act, 1880
metadata.long_title: An Act to confer certain powers on Religious Societies
key_definitions: body of persons associated for the purpose of maintaining religious worship
metadata.one_line: This Act confers powers on religious societies regarding property vesting, trustee appointment, and dissolution.
metadata.summary: The Religious Societies Act, 1880 simplifies the manner in which bodies associated with maintaining religious worship can hold property. It provides mechanisms for appointing new trustees when no specific method is prescribed and allows for the dissolution of such societies with proper adjustment of affairs. The Act also outlines procedures for submitting questions regarding membership or appointment validity to the High Court.

metadata.short_title: The Removal from Service (Special Powers) (Repeal) Act, 2010
metadata.long_title: An Act to repeal the Removal from Service (Special Powers) Ordinance, 2000 (XVII of 2000)
repeals: The Removal from Service (Special Powers) Ordinance, 2000 (XVII of 2000)
metadata.one_line: This Act repeals the Removal from Service (Special Powers) Ordinance, 2000 and restores governance under existing civil service laws.
metadata.summary: The document is a short Act enacted by Parliament to repeal the Removal from Service (Special Powers) Ordinance, 2000. It applies to the whole of Pakistan and comes into force immediately upon enactment. Upon repeal, disciplinary matters for government servants revert to being governed by the Civil Servants Act, 1973 and related rules, while corporation service matters follow applicable laws.

metadata.short_title: The Removal of Accused Persons Act, 1973
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the removal of accused persons from one Province to another.
metadata.one_line: Provides for the removal of accused persons held in custody from one Province to another by Federal Government order.
metadata.summary: This Act empowers the Federal Government to remove any accused person or class of accused persons held in custody in one Province to another Province. It applies to the whole of Pakistan and comes into force immediately. The power is exercised through general or special orders issued by the Federal Government, overriding other laws for the time being in force.

metadata.short_title: The System of Sardari (Abolition) Act, 1976
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the abolition of the system of Sardari and for matters ancillary thereto.
repeals: The System of Sardari (Abolition) Ordinance, 1976
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment up to three years or fine up to ten thousand rupees or both
metadata.one_line: Abolishes the system of Sardari and related feudal privileges across Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Act abolishes the system of Sardari, which is described as a remnant of an oppressive feudal and tribal system. It prohibits recognized Sardars from exercising unauthorized judicial powers, maintaining private jails, arresting persons without legal authority, taking free labour, or demanding tribute. The Act applies to the whole of Pakistan and came into force immediately upon enactment.

metadata.short_title: The Requisitioned Land (Continuance of Powers) Ordinance, 1969
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the continuance of certain emergency powers in relation to requisitioned land
metadata.commencement: on the date on which the Defence of Pakistan Ordinance, 1965 ceases to have effect under clause (7) of Article 30 of the Constitution
metadata.one_line: Continues emergency powers regarding requisitioned land after the Defence of Pakistan Ordinance, 1965 ceases.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance provides for the continuance of certain emergency powers relating to land that was requisitioned under the Defence of Pakistan Ordinance, 1965. It applies to the whole of Pakistan and remains in force until the Defence of Pakistan Ordinance, 1965 ceases to have effect. The appropriate Government is empowered to use, deal with, or release from requisition any such land, acquire it under specific circumstances, and determine compensation payable for its continued subjection to requisition.

metadata.short_title: The Requisitioned Land (Continuance of Powers) Ordinance, 1977
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the continuance of certain emergency powers in relation to requisitioned land
repeals: Defence of Pakistan Ordinance, 1971
metadata.max_penalty: punishment under sections 176 and 177 of the Pakistan Penal Code (Act XLV 1860)
metadata.one_line: Continues emergency powers regarding requisitioned land after the repeal of the Defence of Pakistan Ordinance, 1971.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance provides for the continuance of certain emergency powers related to requisitioned land following the repeal of the Defence of Pakistan Ordinance, 1971. It applies to the whole of Pakistan and allows the Federal Government to use or deal with such land while establishing mechanisms for release from requisition and compensation payment. The document also grants the Federal Government power to obtain information regarding requisitioned land and provides indemnity against legal proceedings for actions taken in good faith under the Ordinance.

metadata.short_title: The Reservists (Reinstatement in Civil Employment) Ordinance, 1965
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the reinstatement in civil employment of reservists called up for service or training in any of the Defence Services and matters ancillary thereto
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to ten thousand rupees, or with both
metadata.one_line: Provides for the reinstatement in civil employment of reservists called up for Defence Services and sets out related procedures and penalties.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance ensures that reservists called up for service or training are reinstated in their previous civil employment upon termination of such service. It defines 'employer' and 'reservist', establishes a three-month window for reservists to apply for reinstatement, and grants the Federal Government power to exempt employers or specify terms if reinstatement is impracticable. The Ordinance also creates offences for non-compliance, prescribing imprisonment, fines, and compensation as penalties.

metadata.short_title: The Revenue Recovery Act, 1890
metadata.long_title: An Act to make better provision for recovering certain public demands
metadata.one_line: This Act provides mechanisms for collecting public demands and land-revenue arrears across districts.
metadata.summary: The Revenue Recovery Act, 1890 establishes procedures for recovering public demands, specifically land-revenue arrears, by Collectors. It allows a Collector in one district to send a certificate to another district's Collector to recover amounts where the defaulter has property elsewhere. The Act outlines the process for issuing certificates, prohibiting property transfers, and instituting civil suits for repayment if liability is denied.

metadata.short_title: The Revocation of Privileges Act, 1992
metadata.long_title: An Act to revoke and annual certain Bills passed by the National Assembly
metadata.commencement: at once and deemed to have come into force on the 3rd day of May, 1992
amends: The President's Salary, Allowances and Privileges (Amendment) Bill, 1992
The Prime Minister's Salary, Allowances and Privileges (Amendment) Bill, 1992
The Federal Ministers and Ministers of State Salaries, Allowances and Privileges (Amendment) Bill, 1992
The Members of Parliament (Salaries and Allowances) (Amendment) Bill, 1992
The Chairman and Speaker (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) (Amendment) Bill, 1992
The Deputy Chairman and Deputy Speaker (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) (Amendment) Bill, 1992
metadata.one_line: This Act revokes and annuls six specific amendment bills passed by the National Assembly in May 1992.
metadata.summary: The Revocation of Privileges Act, 1992 was enacted to revoke and annul certain Bills passed by the National Assembly on May 3, 1992. These Bills concerned amendments to salaries, allowances, and privileges for the President, Prime Minister, Federal Ministers, Members of Parliament, and Chairmen/Speakers. Following a unanimous resolution by the National Assembly on May 7, 1992, to withdraw these Bills, this Act declares them withdrawn, revoked, and annulled as of their passage date.

name: Rice Milling Control and Development (Repeal) Ordinance, 1977

metadata.short_title: The Rice Milling Control and Development (Repeal) Ordinance, 1977
metadata.long_title: An Ordnance to repeal the Rice Milling Control and Development Act, 1976 (LVIII of 1976) and to provide for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto
repeals: The Rice Milling Control and Development Act, 1976 (LVIII of 1976)
metadata.status_evidence: An Ordnance to repeal the Rice Milling Control and Development Act, 1976 (LVIII of 1976)
subjects: Regulation of paddy and rice movement
metadata.max_penalty: rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both
metadata.administering_body: Federal Government / Rice Milling Corporation of Pakistan
metadata.one_line: An Ordinance repealing the Rice Milling Control and Development Act, 1976 and providing for the return of establishments to previous management.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance was promulgated by the President to immediately repeal the Rice Milling Control and Development Act, 1976. It mandates the Rice Milling Corporation to deliver possession of acquired establishments back to their previous owners within a specified period, subject to the recovery of outstanding amounts. The document outlines provisions for employee continuance in service, compensation calculations for transferred assets, and regulations regarding the movement and pricing of paddy and rice until the Corporation is wound up.

name: Right of Access to Information Act, 2017

metadata.short_title: The Right of Access to Information Act, 2017
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the right of access to information in transparent and effective manner, subject only to reasonable restrictions imposed by law
repeals: The Freedom of Information Ordinance, 2002 (XCVI of 2002)
establishes: Pakistan Commission on Access to Information
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years or with fine which shall not be less than one hundred thousand Rupees or with both
metadata.one_line: This Act establishes the right of citizens to access information held by public bodies in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: The Right of Access to Information Act, 2017 provides for the right of access to information in a transparent and effective manner. It applies to all public bodies of the Federal Government and aims to promote government accountability, reduce corruption, and improve participation in public affairs. The Act establishes the Pakistan Commission on Access to Information to oversee requests and appeals regarding access to records.

name: Right to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2012

metadata.short_title: The Right to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2012
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for free and compulsory education to all children of the age of five to sixteen years
metadata.commencement: on such date and in such areas, as the Federal Government may, by notification in the Official gazette, appoint
repeals: The Islamabad Capital Territory Compulsory Primary Education Ordinance, 2002 (XIV of 2002)
metadata.max_penalty: fifty per centum of the amount of the maximum fine to which the person would have been liable if he had been convicted of the offence
metadata.one_line: This Act provides for free and compulsory education for children aged five to sixteen in the Islamabad Capital Territory.
metadata.summary: The Right to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2012 establishes a fundamental right for every child in the Islamabad Capital Territory to receive free and compulsory education between the ages of five and sixteen. It mandates that appropriate Governments provide infrastructure, ensure admission without discrimination or capitation fees, and monitor school functioning. The Act also defines specific duties for parents and teachers, sets norms for school registration, and repeals the previous 2002 Ordinance.

name: Riot and Civil Commotion Risks Insurance Ordinance, 1947

metadata.short_title: The Riot and Civil Commotion Risks Insurance Ordinance, 1947
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the insurance of certain property against Riot and Civil Commotion Risks.
establishes: Riot and Civil Commotion Insurance Fund
metadata.max_penalty: fine which may extend to one thousand rupees
metadata.one_line: Provides for insurance of specific property against risks arising from riots, civil commotions, strikes, or malicious acts.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes a framework for insuring certain properties, specifically factories and factory buildings, against losses caused by riots, civil commotions, strikes, or malicious intent. It defines the scope of insurable risks while explicitly excluding war, cessation of work, and consequential losses. The Federal Government is empowered to establish an insurance fund, employ agents, make rules for policy forms and premiums, and manage the recovery of unpaid premiums.

metadata.short_title: The Riphah International University Ordinance, 2002
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the establishment of Riphah International University at Islamabad and for the matters connected therewith or incidental thereto
establishes: Board of Advanced Studies and Research
metadata.one_line: Establishes Riphah International University at Islamabad and defines its structure, powers, and governing bodies.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes Riphah International University in Islamabad as a body corporate with perpetual succession. It outlines the university's powers to conduct education, research, and examinations while ensuring openness to all classes and creeds. The document creates various authorities including the Board of Governors, Academic Council, and Selection Board, and provides for the making of Statutes, Regulations, and Rules.

metadata.short_title: The Road Transport Workers Ordinance, 1961
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to regulate the hours of work and other conditions of employment of road transport workers in Pakistan.
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment up to six months and fine not exceeding one thousand rupees
metadata.one_line: Regulates working hours, rest, leave, and employment conditions for road transport workers in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance regulates the hours of work and other employment conditions for road transport workers across Pakistan. It establishes age limits for drivers and general workers, mandates specific rest intervals and weekly rest periods, and sets rules for overtime pay and leave entitlements. The document also empowers the Provincial Government to make rules, maintain registers, conduct inspections, and imposes penalties for violations.

name: Royal Pakistan Navy (Extension of Service) Act, 1950

metadata.short_title: The Pakistan Navy (Extension of Service) Act, 1950
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the retention in service of certain persons enrolled for service in the Pakistan Navy.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of Pakistan (with specific extensions to Baluchistan and associated areas noted in the text)
metadata.one_line: Provides for the retention in service of Pakistan Navy personnel whose term has expired.
metadata.summary: This Act allows certain persons enrolled for service in the Pakistan Navy to continue serving even after their original term expires. The Federal Government may notify the date until which this extension applies, with a maximum limit of five years from the original termination date. The law was subsequently extended to various regions including Baluchistan, Federated Areas, Leased Areas, and specific States.

name: Rulers of Acceding States (Abolition of Privy Purses and Privileges) Order, 1972

metadata.short_title: The Rulers of Acceding States (Abolition of Privy Purses and Privileges) Order, 1972
metadata.commencement: at once; deemed to have taken effect on the 22nd day of December, 1971
metadata.one_line: Abolishes privy purses and privileges of Rulers of Acceding States while providing maintenance allowances.
metadata.summary: This Order abolishes the right of Rulers of Acceding States to receive privy purses and other privileges guaranteed under Instruments of Accession. It empowers the Federal Government to grant maintenance allowances in lieu of these abolished benefits, subject to conditions regarding allegiance to Pakistan. The provisions apply specifically to certain Nawabs and Talukdars as well, ensuring their allowances are adjusted accordingly.

metadata.short_title: The Rules and Regulations Continuance Act, 1937
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the continuance in force of certain rules and regulations.
metadata.one_line: Continues rules under the Electricity Act, 1910 and regulations under the Boilers Act, 1923 made before March 1937.
metadata.summary: This Act ensures that certain rules and regulations remain in force after specific dates in 1937. It applies to rules made under the Electricity Act, 1910, and regulations made under the Boilers Act, 1923 by the Governor General in Council before March 31, 1937 and March 28, 1937 respectively. The provisions deem these instruments to have been made by the authority substituted for the Governor General in Council by subsequent amendment acts of 1937. They continue until superseded by new rules or regulations made under the relevant sections of the Electricity Act or Boilers Act.

metadata.short_title: Rules of Business, 1973
metadata.commencement: on the fourteenth day of August 1973
metadata.parent_law: Articles 90 and 99 of the Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan
repeals: Rules of Business, 1962
metadata.one_line: Federal Government rules defining business allocation, cabinet procedure, and legislative processes.
metadata.summary: These rules define the allocation of business among federal divisions and establish procedures for the Cabinet and Parliament. They outline consultation mechanisms between divisions, legislative processes including bill introduction and ordinance promulgation, and emergency provisions. The rules also detail relations with provinces and miscellaneous administrative matters like official information protection.

metadata.short_title: The Sacked Employees (Re instatement) Act, 2010
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide relief to persons in corporation service or autonomous or semi autonomous bodies or in Government service who were dismissed, removed or terminated from service.
metadata.max_penalty: removal from service or any other major or minor penalty as may be determined by the appointing authority
metadata.one_line: Provides relief and reinstatement for government, corporation, or autonomous body employees dismissed between 1993 and 1999.
metadata.summary: This Act provides relief to persons in government, corporation, or autonomous/semi-autonomous service who were dismissed, removed, or terminated between November 1, 1993, and October 12, 1999. It establishes a Sacked Employees' Review Board to handle petitions from affected employees and outlines procedures for their re-instatement and regularization of service. The Act also defines specific categories of sacked employees, sets penalties for obstructing implementation, and overrides conflicting laws or court judgments regarding these cases.

metadata.short_title: The Safeguard Measures Ordinance, 2002
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the imposition of Safeguard Measures
metadata.one_line: Provides framework for imposing safeguard measures on imports causing serious injury to domestic industry.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes a legal framework in Pakistan to impose safeguard measures on imported products causing serious injury or threat thereof. It empowers the National Tariff Commission to conduct investigations into increased imports and determine if such imports are harming domestic industries. The document outlines procedures for initiating investigations, gathering evidence from interested parties, and applying provisional or definitive safeguard duties or quotas. It also includes provisions protecting employees who assist the Commission during inquiries.

metadata.short_title: The Sale of Goods Act, 1930
metadata.long_title: An Act to define and amend the law relating to the sale of goods
repeals: Act IX of 1872
metadata.one_line: Defines and amends the law relating to the sale of goods in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Act defines and amends the legal framework governing the sale of goods. It establishes rules for contract formation, property transfer, and the rights and duties of sellers and buyers. The legislation also covers specific scenarios such as stoppage in transit, unpaid seller's liens, and remedies for breach of contract.

name: Sales Tax Act, 1990 (Same as on the official website of FBR dated 30-06-2026)

metadata.short_title: Sales Tax Act, 1990
metadata.long_title: An Act to consolidate the law relating to sales tax.
metadata.one_line: Consolidates the law relating to sales tax, registration, returns, and recovery of arrears in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Act consolidates the law regarding sales tax in Pakistan, covering scope, payment, registration, and record-keeping requirements. It establishes mechanisms for input tax credit, refunds, and exemptions while defining liabilities for registered persons. The Act includes specific provisions for ship-breaking industries, minimum production calculations, and powers of tax authorities for audit and recovery.

metadata.short_title: The Sarais Act, 1867
metadata.long_title: An Act for the regulation of public Sarais and Puraos.
repeals: Bengal Regulation XIV of 1807
metadata.max_penalty: twenty rupees plus one rupee a day for every day during which the offence continues
metadata.one_line: Regulates public Sarais and Puraos by requiring registration, defining keeper duties, and imposing penalties for non-compliance.
metadata.summary: This Act regulates public Sarais and Puraos to ensure the safety and accommodation of travellers. It requires keepers to register their establishments and maintain specific standards regarding cleanliness, security, and reporting infectious diseases. The Act empowers Magistrates to inspect premises, refuse registration to unqualified keepers, and impose penalties for infractions or allowing filthy conditions.

name: Secretariat Allowance (Rescission of Orders, etc) Ordinance, 2000

metadata.short_title: The Secretariat Allowance (Rescission of Orders, etc.) Ordinance, 2000
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for rescission of certain orders relating to Secretariat Allowance
metadata.one_line: Rescinds orders granting Secretariat Allowance to Federal Government employees and deems them rescinded from July 1, 1988.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance provides for the rescission of certain orders relating to Secretariat Allowance granted to employees of the Federal Government. It declares that these orders are deemed to have been rescinded on July 1, 1988, and prevents any financial benefit from accruing under them despite previous court decisions. The Ordinance also validates payments already made before its commencement and empowers the Federal Government to make orders to provide recompense if difficulties arise in giving effect to its provisions.

metadata.short_title: The Securities Act, 1920
metadata.long_title: An Act to consolidate and amend the law relating to Government securities.
metadata.one_line: Consolidates and amends the law relating to Government securities issued by Federal or Provincial Governments.
metadata.summary: This Act consolidates and amends the law regarding Government securities, including promissory notes, treasury bills, stock-certificates, and bearer bonds. It defines key terms like 'Government security' and outlines rules for endorsements, holding by public officials, and rights of survivors in joint payee scenarios. The Act also provides procedures for discharge, inspection of documents, and penalties for violations.

metadata.short_title: The Securities Act, 2015
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend and consolidate law for the regulation of the securities industry and the protection of investors
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Government may notify
amends: The Listed Companies (Substantial Acquisition of Voting Shares and Take Overs) Ordinance 2002 (CIII of 2002)
repeals: Securities and Exchange Ordinance, 1969 (XVII of 1969)
The Listed Companies (Substantial Acquisition of Voting Shares and Take Overs) Ordinance 2002 (CIII of 2002)
Companies Ordinance, 1984 (XLVII of 1984)
metadata.one_line: This Act consolidates and amends laws regulating the securities industry, licensing exchanges, and protecting investors.
metadata.summary: The Securities Act, 2015 consolidates and amends existing laws to regulate the securities industry in Pakistan. It establishes a framework for licensing securities exchanges, clearing houses, and central depositories while defining their duties and powers. The Act also regulates public offers of securities, prohibits insider trading and market manipulation, and provides mechanisms for investor protection and dispute resolution.

name: Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan Act, 1997

metadata.short_title: Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan Act, 1997
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of the Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan and to provide for matters connected therewith and incidental thereto.
establishes: Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan
metadata.administering_body: Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan to regulate capital markets and corporate entities.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan (SECP) to regulate capital markets, supervise corporate entities, and ensure beneficial regulation. It creates the Commission, a Policy Board, and an Audit Oversight Board with specific powers for investigation, enforcement, and issuing directions. The Act defines key terms, outlines the Commission's functions, and grants powers to impose penalties and prosecute offences related to securities violations.

name: Securities and Exchange Ordinance, 1969 (Repealed by Act XIV of 2016)

metadata.short_title: Securities and Exchange Ordinance, 1969
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the protection of investors, regulation of markets and dealings in securities and for matters ancillary thereto
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Federal Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, appoint
metadata.status_evidence: (Repealed by Act XIV of 2016)
establishes: Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance regulates securities markets, protects investors, and establishes the Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan.
metadata.summary: The Securities and Exchange Ordinance, 1969 was promulgated to protect investors and regulate dealings in securities across Pakistan. It defines key terms such as brokers, banks, and asset management companies while establishing the framework for stock exchanges and commodity futures trading. The Ordinance empowers the Federal Government and later the Commission to make regulations governing market conduct, listing requirements, and dispute resolution procedures.

metadata.short_title: The Security of Pakistan Act, 1952
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for special measures to deal with persons acting in a manner prejudicial to the defence, external affairs and security of Pakistan
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both
metadata.one_line: Provides special measures for detention and movement restrictions of persons prejudicial to Pakistan's security.
metadata.summary: This Act empowers the Federal Government to detain individuals suspected of acting against national security or defence. It restricts their movements, requires reporting, and controls subversive associations and publications. The Act establishes a Review Board and creates specific offences with non-bailable penalties, while barring most court jurisdiction over its proceedings.

metadata.short_title: The Seed Act, 1976
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for controlling and regulating the quality of seeds of various varieties of crops
establishes: National Seed Development and Regulatory Authority
metadata.administering_body: National Seed Development and Regulatory Authority
metadata.one_line: This Act regulates seed quality, establishes certification authorities, and defines offences related to seed business in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: The Seed Act, 1976 provides for controlling and regulating the quality of seeds of various crop varieties across Pakistan. It establishes the National Seed Development and Regulatory Authority, a Federal Seed Certification Agency, and Provincial Seed Councils to oversee seed production, certification, and distribution. The Act defines key terms such as certified seed, basic seed, and genetically modified varieties, while also outlining offences, penalties, and procedures for appeals and tribunals.

metadata.short_title: The Senate (Election) Act, 1975
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the conduct of election to the Senate and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto
repeals: Senate (Election) Act, 1973
metadata.one_line: Provides for the conduct of elections to the Senate, including procedures, offences, and dispute resolution.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the legal framework for conducting elections to the Senate of Pakistan. It outlines the administrative machinery, nomination processes, voting procedures, and restrictions on election expenses. The legislation also defines corrupt practices, sets up tribunals to adjudicate election petitions, and specifies disqualifications for candidates.

metadata.short_title: The Senate Secretariat Services Act, 2017
metadata.long_title: An Act to regulate the appointment and the terms and conditions of service of persons in the Senate Secretariat, under clause (2)of Article 87 of the Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, 1973
repeals: Senate Secretariat (Recruitment) Rules, 1973
metadata.one_line: Regulates appointment and service terms for Senate Secretariat employees under Article 87 of the Constitution.
metadata.summary: This Act regulates the appointment, terms, and conditions of service for persons employed in the Senate Secretariat. It applies to all such employees regardless of location and establishes that their service conditions cannot be varied to their disadvantage. The Act empowers the Chairman, with concurrence from the Finance Committee, to manage pay, allowances, and other privileges, while repealing the previous 1973 Recruitment Rules.

metadata.short_title: The Service Tribunals Act, 1973
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of Service Tribunals to exercise jurisdiction in respect of matters relating to the terms and conditions of service of civil servants.
metadata.territorial_extent: all civil servants wherever they may be
metadata.one_line: Establishes Service Tribunals with exclusive jurisdiction over civil servants' terms and conditions of service.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes Service Tribunals to exercise exclusive jurisdiction regarding the terms and conditions of service for civil servants. It defines the composition, appointment, and powers of these tribunals, including their ability to review final orders and execute decisions. The Act also outlines procedures for appeals against departmental authorities' orders and specifies that suits pending in courts before the Act's commencement shall abate.

metadata.short_title: The Settlement Commissioners (Validation of Orders) Act, 1972
metadata.long_title: An Act to validate certain orders passed by Settlement Commissioners
metadata.commencement: at once and deemed to have taken effect on the 26th day of March, 1958
repeals: The Settlement Commissioners (Validation of Orders) Act, 1972
metadata.status_evidence: Omitted by the Federal Laws (Revision and Declaration) Ordinance, 1981 (XXVII of 1981), s. 3 and Sch., II.
metadata.one_line: Validates orders by Settlement Commissioners deemed invalid under the Displaced Persons Act, 1958.
metadata.summary: This Act validates certain orders passed by Settlement Commissioners that were previously declared or rendered invalid. It applies to the whole of Pakistan and deems these specific orders to have always been validly made despite any conflicting court decrees or other authority orders. The Act operates notwithstanding provisions in the Displaced Persons (Compensation and Rehabilitation) Act, 1958. However, Section 3 of this Act has been omitted by the Federal Laws (Revision and Declaration) Ordinance, 1981.

name: Shaheed Zulfiqar Ali Bhutto Medical University, Islamabad, Act, 2013

metadata.short_title: The Shaheed Zulfiqar Ali Bhutto Medical University, Islamabad, Act, 2013
metadata.long_title: An Act to establish Shaheed Zulfiqar Ali Bhutto Medical University, Islamabad
establishes: Shaheed Zulfiqar Ali Bhutto Medical University, Islamabad
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Shaheed Zulfiqar Ali Bhutto Medical University, Islamabad as an autonomous body corporate.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Shaheed Zulfiqar Ali Bhutto Medical University, Islamabad as an autonomous body corporate with perpetual succession. It defines the university's functions, including instruction, research, examinations, and degree conferral. The Act outlines the structure of authorities such as the Senate, Syndicate, and Academic Council, along with provisions for officers, staff, finance, and student discipline.

metadata.short_title: The Shifa Tameer-e-Millat University Act, 2012
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of Shifa Tameer-e-Millat University, Islamabad.
metadata.one_line: Establishes Shifa Tameer-e-Millat University in Islamabad with academic and administrative autonomy.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes Shifa Tameer-e-Millat University at Islamabad as a non-profit body corporate with perpetual succession. It grants the university academic, financial, and administrative autonomy, including the power to employ staff and manage property without external interference on policy matters. The Act defines the structure of the university, comprising a Chancellor, Senate, Vice-Chancellor, Syndicate, and Academic Council, while also incorporating existing Shifa College of Medicine and Nursing as constituent colleges.

metadata.short_title: The Short Titles Act, 1973
metadata.long_title: An Act to assign short titles to certain Martial Law Regulations and Martial Law Orders
metadata.one_line: This Act assigns short titles to specific Martial Law Regulations and Orders for easier reference.
metadata.summary: The Short Titles Act, 1973 was enacted under the Interim Constitution of Pakistan to assign short titles to various Martial Law Regulations and Orders. It facilitates legal reference by citing these laws by their new designated names rather than their original lengthy titles. The Act applies to the whole of Pakistan and came into force immediately upon enactment.

metadata.short_title: The Sikh Gurdwaras (Supplementary) Act, 1925
metadata.long_title: An Act to supplement certain provisions of the Sikh Gurdwaras Act, 1925
metadata.commencement: on the date appointed by the Provincial Government under sub-section (3) of section 1 of the Sikh Gurdwaras Act, 1925
metadata.one_line: Supplements the Sikh Gurdwaras Act, 1925 and validates certain provisions of Punjab Act VIII of 1925.
metadata.summary: This Act supplements specific provisions of the Sikh Gurdwaras Act, 1925 (Punjab Act VIII of 1925). It validates parts of the said Act regarding High Court jurisdiction and procedure as if passed by the Central Legislature. The Act comes into force on a date appointed by the Provincial Government.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Co-operative Societies Act, 1925
metadata.long_title: An Act to consolidate and amend the law relating to co-operative societies in [the Province of Sind]
repeals: Co-operative Societies Act, 1912
metadata.one_line: This Act consolidates and amends the law relating to co-operative societies in the Province of Sind.
metadata.summary: The Sind Co-operative Societies Act, 1925 consolidates and amends the law regarding co-operative societies in Sindh. It facilitates the formation of societies for thrift, self-help, and mutual aid among agriculturists and others with common economic needs. The Act covers preliminary provisions, registration requirements, rights and liabilities of members, duties of societies, privileges, property management, liquidation procedures, arbitration, and offences.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Textile Board Ordinance, 1949
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to incorporate and regulate the Sind Textile Board.
metadata.commencement: at once; deemed to have taken effect on 1947-12-05
metadata.administering_body: Committee of the Sind Textile Board
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance incorporates and regulates the Sind Textile Board to improve cloth procurement and distribution in Sind.
metadata.summary: The Sind Textile Board Ordinance, 1949 was promulgated by the Governor-General under emergency powers to incorporate a trading corporation for the Province of Sind. Its primary purpose is to regulate the wholesale distribution and procurement of cloth within Sind and the Karachi Division. The document establishes the Board as a body corporate with perpetual succession, defines its membership criteria, financial subscriptions, and governance structure through an Executive Committee.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Incumbered Estates Act, 1896
metadata.long_title: An act to amend the law providing for the relief of jagirdars and zamindars in Sindh.
metadata.one_line: Provides relief to jagirdars and zamindars in Sindh through inquiry, management orders, and liquidation schemes.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the law regarding the relief of jagirdars and zamindars in Sindh who are subject to debts or liabilities. It establishes a process where an application can be made to the Commissioner for an inquiry into the debtor's property and debts. Upon inquiry, the Commissioner may appoint a manager to oversee the estate, determine debts, create a liquidation scheme, and manage the sale or mortgage of assets to pay off liabilities. The Act defines specific terms like 'jagirdar' and 'zamindar' based on land revenue assessments and possession dates, and grants powers to managers including summoning witnesses and making rules.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Revenue Jurisdiction Act, 1876
metadata.long_title: An Act to limit the jurisdiction of the Civil Courts in Sindh and the Karachi Division in matters relating to the Land-revenue, and for other purposes.
repeals: Act XXIII of 1871
section 32 of Act XIV of 1869
section 13 of Regulation XVII of 1827 of the Bombay Code
metadata.one_line: Limits Civil Court jurisdiction in Sindh regarding land revenue matters and defines related terms.
metadata.summary: This Act limits the jurisdiction of Civil Courts in Sindh and the Karachi Division concerning land-revenue matters. It bars suits against the Government regarding specific land tenures, objections to revenue assessments, and claims arising from revenue realization proceedings. The Act also provides for the immunity of Revenue-officers from civil suits for damages and outlines exceptions where Civil Courts may still entertain suits.

name: Sir Syed-CASE (Center for Advanced Studies in Engineering) lnstitute of Technology Islamabad Act 2018

metadata.short_title: The Sir Syed-CASE (Center for Advanced Studies in Engineering) Institute of Technology, Islamabad Act, 2018
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of Sir Syed-CASE (Center for Advanced Studies in Engineering) Institute of Technology, Islamabad and for matters connected therewith or ancillary thereto
establishes: Sir Syed-CASE (Center for Advanced Studies in Engineering) Institute of Technology, Islamabad
metadata.one_line: Establishes Sir Syed-CASE Institute of Technology, Islamabad as a body corporate with perpetual succession.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Sir Syed-CASE (Center for Advanced Studies in Engineering) Institute of Technology, Islamabad as a body corporate. It defines the powers, purposes, and functions of the Institute, including its ability to award degrees and conduct research. The Act creates various authorities such as the Board of Trustees, Board of Governors, and Academic Council to manage the Institute's affairs.

name: Small and Medium Exterprises Development Authority Ordinance, 2002

metadata.short_title: Small and Medium Enterprises Development Authority Ordinance, 2002
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the establishment of the Small and Medium Enterprises Development Authority as an autonomous body under the Federal Government for encouraging and facilitating the development and growth of small and medium enterprises in Pakistan
repeals: The Federal Government's Notification No. 5(20) E&FI/98, dated the 13th October, 1998
establishes: Small and Medium Enterprises Development Authority
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Small and Medium Enterprises Development Authority as an autonomous federal body to support SME growth.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Small and Medium Enterprises Development Authority (SMEDA) as an autonomous body under the Federal Government. Its purpose is to encourage and facilitate the development and growth of small and medium enterprises in Pakistan through policy making and provision of resources and support services. The Authority is structured with a Board, a Chief Executive Officer, and an Executive Secretary, possessing powers to enter contracts, manage funds, and issue regulations. It also repeals a prior Federal Government Notification from 1998.

name: Small Claims and Minor Offences Courts Ordinance, 2002

metadata.short_title: The Small Claims and Minor Offences Courts Ordinance, 2002
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to consolidate and enact the law relating to small claims and minor offences and matters incidental thereto or connected therewith for providing inexpensive and expeditious disposal of such claims and offences.
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Federal Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, appoint
repeals: The Provincial Small Cause Courts Act, 1887 (IX of 1887)
establishes: Small Claims and Minor Offences Courts
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance establishes Small Claims and Minor Offences Courts to provide inexpensive and expeditious disposal of small claims and minor offences.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance consolidates the law regarding small claims and minor offences to ensure their inexpensive and expeditious disposal. It establishes Small Claims and Minor Offences Courts presided over by a Civil Judge-cum-Judicial Magistrate with jurisdiction over suits not exceeding one hundred thousand rupees and specific minor offences. The document outlines procedures for civil and criminal trials, including amicable settlement through conciliation or mediation, evidence rules, and appeal limitations.

name: Smart Institute of Science and Technology Act, 2022

metadata.short_title: The Smart Institute of Sciences & Technology Act, 2022
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of the Smart Institute of Sciences & Technology
establishes: Director of Office of Research, Innovation and Commercialization (ORIC)
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Smart Institute of Sciences & Technology as a private body corporate in Rawalpindi.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Smart Institute of Sciences & Technology as a body corporate with its principal seat at Rawalpindi. It defines the institute's structure, including the Patron, Chancellor, Board of Governors, Syndicate, and various directorates. The legislation outlines the powers of these authorities, provisions for teaching, examinations, and the management of an institute fund.

metadata.short_title: The Societies Registration Act, 1860
metadata.long_title: An Act for the Registration of Literary, Scientific and Charitable Societies.
metadata.territorial_extent: all the Provinces and the Capital of the Federation, except the Scheduled Districts (with specific extensions to Baluchistan, Sind, N.W.F.P., etc. as per footnotes)
metadata.one_line: This Act provides for the registration of literary, scientific, and charitable societies in British India.
metadata.summary: The Societies Registration Act, 1860 establishes a legal framework for registering societies formed for literary, scientific, charitable, or political education purposes. It requires seven or more persons to subscribe to a memorandum of association and file it with the Registrar of Joint-stock Companies. The Act outlines requirements for registration fees, annual filing of managing body lists, vesting of property in the governing body, and procedures for dissolution without profit distribution to members.

metadata.short_title: The Soldiers (Litigation) Act, 1925
metadata.long_title: An Act to consolidate and amend the law to provide for the special protection in respect of civil and revenue litigation of soldiers serving under special conditions.
repeals: Act IX of 1918
Act XII of 1924
metadata.one_line: Provides special protection for soldiers in civil and revenue litigation when serving under special or war conditions.
metadata.summary: This Act consolidates and amends the law regarding the special protection afforded to soldiers involved in civil and revenue litigation. It defines specific circumstances under which a soldier is deemed to be serving under special conditions, such as during war, overseas, or in remote areas. The legislation grants powers to courts and collectors to intervene, postpone proceedings, and modify limitation laws for soldiers. It also extends the application of these provisions to other persons in the service of the State.

name: South Asian Strategic Stability Institute University Islamabad Act, 2013

metadata.short_title: The South Asian Strategic Stability Institute University Islamabad Act, 2013
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of South Asian Strategic Stability Institute (SASSI) University, Islamabad and for matters connected with and ancillary thereto
establishes: South Asian Strategic Stability Institute (SASSI) University Islamabad
metadata.one_line: Establishes the South Asian Strategic Stability Institute University Islamabad and defines its structure, powers, and officers.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the South Asian Strategic Stability Institute (SASSI) University in Islamabad as a body corporate with perpetual succession. It outlines the composition of the university's authorities, including the Patron, Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, and Board of Governors, and grants them powers to manage property and set up campuses. The legislation also provides for the creation of a University Fund, the making of statutes and rules, and includes general provisions regarding the commencement of terms, disputes about membership, and indemnity for officials acting in good faith.

name: Special Courts for Speedy Trials (Repeal) Act, 1996

metadata.short_title: The Special Courts for Speedy Trials (Repeal) Act, 1996
metadata.long_title: An Act to repeal the Special Courts for Speedy Trials Act, 1992
repeals: The Special Courts for Speedy Trials Act, 1992 (IX of 1992)
metadata.status_evidence: shall stand repealed from the twenty-sixth day of July, 1994
metadata.one_line: Repeals the Special Courts for Speedy Trials Act, 1992 and provides for savings regarding pending cases.
metadata.summary: This Act repeals the Special Courts for Speedy Trials Act, 1992, effective from July 26, 1994. It preserves orders, convictions, and investigations made under the repealed Act before its repeal. Pending cases are transferred to respective Courts of Session or other courts to be tried under the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898.

metadata.short_title: The Special Economic Zones Act, 2012
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for setting up and operation of special economic zones in Pakistan
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Federal Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, appoint
metadata.administering_body: Federal Government (via BOI and SEZ Authorities)
metadata.one_line: This Act provides for the creation, development, and efficient operation of special economic zones in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: The Special Economic Zones Act, 2012 establishes a legal framework to create and operate special economic zones across Pakistan. It defines various types of zones, such as export processing zones and free trade zones, and sets up governing bodies like the Board of Approvals (BOA) and SEZ Authorities. The Act outlines requirements for zone applications, developer responsibilities, incentives for investors, and mechanisms for dispute resolution through arbitration.

metadata.short_title: The Special Marriage Act, 1872
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide a form of Marriage in certain cases
repeals: Act IV of 1869
establishes: Registrar of Marriages under Act III of 1872
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment and fine
metadata.one_line: Provides a legal form for marriage registration in Pakistan for persons of specified religions and outlines procedures, objections, and penalties.
metadata.summary: This Act provides a specific legal form for solemnizing marriages in cases where parties do not profess certain religions or wish to regularize doubtful marriages. It establishes the role of Marriage Registrars appointed by the Provincial Government and sets conditions regarding age, consent, and relationship status. The Act details the procedure for filing notices, handling objections, and obtaining certificates, while also prescribing penalties for bigamy and false declarations.

metadata.short_title: The Special Technology Zones Authority Act, 2021
metadata.long_title: An Act to ensure the development of scientific and technological eco-system through development of zones to accelerate technology development in the country
repeals: The Special Technology Zones Authority Ordinance, 2020
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Special Technology Zones Authority to develop technology zones and accelerate technological development in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Special Technology Zones Authority to foster a scientific and technological ecosystem through the development of special technology zones. It aims to attract foreign direct investment, promote innovation, and increase productivity by creating internationally competitive structures. The Authority is empowered to manage zone developers, grant incentives, and oversee the operation of these zones across the whole of Pakistan.

metadata.short_title: The Specific Relief Act, 1877
metadata.long_title: An Act to define and amend the law relating to certain kinds of Specific Relief.
repeals: The Specific Relief Act, 1877 (as amended by the Amending Act, 1891)
metadata.one_line: Defines and amends the law relating to specific relief obtainable in civil suits including injunctions and specific performance.
metadata.summary: This Act defines and amends the law regarding specific relief in civil suits. It covers recovering possession of property, enforcing contracts through specific performance, rectifying instruments, rescinding or cancelling contracts, and granting declaratory decrees. The Act also provides for preventive relief such as injunctions to restrain breaches of negative agreements.

metadata.short_title: The Sports (Development and Control) Ordinance, 1962
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to regulate the development and control of Sports
establishes: Board for the control of Sports in Pakistan
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance regulates sports development and control in Pakistan by establishing a Board with rule-making powers.
metadata.summary: The Sports (Development and Control) Ordinance, 1962 was promulgated to regulate the development and control of sports throughout Pakistan. It empowers the Federal Government to constitute one or more Boards to oversee sports on a national basis. These Boards are granted corporate status and the exclusive right to make rules for uniformity in sports standards comparable to international levels.

metadata.short_title: The Stage-Carriages Act, 1861
metadata.long_title: An Act for licensing and regulating Stage-Carriages
metadata.max_penalty: one hundred rupees and six calendar months imprisonment
metadata.one_line: An Act to license and regulate stage carriages used for conveying passengers for hire in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Act provides a legal framework for licensing stage carriages used to transport passengers for hire. It outlines the requirements for obtaining a license from a Magistrate, including details about the proprietor and the carriage itself. The legislation also specifies penalties for operating unlicensed carriages, failing to display license particulars, or allowing unsafe conditions. Additionally, it grants powers to Provincial Governments regarding exemptions and rule-making.

metadata.short_title: The Stamp Act, 1899
metadata.long_title: An Act to consolidate and amend the law relating to Stamps
repeals: SCHEDULE II
metadata.one_line: Consolidates and amends the law relating to stamp duties on various instruments in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Act consolidates and amends the law regarding stamp duties applicable to instruments executed within or outside Pakistan. It defines chargeable instruments, outlines duty payment methods using adhesive or impressed stamps, and establishes penalties for executing unstamped documents. The Act also provides mechanisms for adjudication of proper stamps, allowances for spoiled stamps, and procedures for criminal prosecutions related to revenue evasion.

metadata.short_title: The Standard Time (Interpretation of References) Ordinance, 1943
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the interpretation in enactments in force in Pakistan of references to Standard Time.
metadata.territorial_extent: Pakistan (extended to the whole of Pakistan with effect from 14th October, 1955)
key_definitions: Federal Government order fixing Standard Time
metadata.one_line: Interprets references to Standard Time in Pakistani enactments based on Federal Government orders.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance provides for the interpretation of references to Standard Time in enactments in force in Pakistan. It stipulates that such references must be interpreted according to the current order of the Federal Government fixing Standard Time relative to Greenwich Mean Time, rather than a fixed interval. The law came into force immediately upon promulgation and was later extended to the whole of Pakistan following the creation of the state.

metadata.short_title: The Standards of Weight Act, 1939
metadata.long_title: An Act to establish standards of weight throughout Pakistan
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Federal Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, appoint
repeals: The Standards of Weight Act, 1939
metadata.status_evidence: [Repeal]
metadata.repealed_by: The Repealing and Amending Act, 1942 (XXV of 1942)
metadata.one_line: Establishes standards of weight throughout Pakistan using the standard grain as the unit.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes standards of weight throughout Pakistan, defining the standard grain based on an iridio-platinum cylinder. It specifies various standard weights including the tola, seer, maund, pound, ounce, hundredweight, and ton. The Federal Government is authorized to prepare sets of these standard weights and supply them to Provincial Governments and other entities upon payment.

metadata.short_title: The Staple Cotton (Excise Duty) Ordinance, 1978
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the levy of a duty of excise on staple cotton produced by ginning factories and sold to textile mills.
metadata.commencement: at once; deemed to have taken effect on 1976-07-01
repeals: Staple Cotton (Excise Duty) Ordinance, 1976
metadata.status_evidence: Provided that, unless the Federal Government, by notification in the official Gazette, otherwise directs, it shall not apply to staple cotton of any crop following the crop of 1976-77 and shall stand repealed on the first day of July, 1978.
key_definitions: factory (cotton ginning factory producing staple cotton for sale)
sale price (415 rupees per maund inclusive of duty)
staple cotton (ginned cotton other than desi-cotton)
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance levies excise duty on staple cotton produced by ginning factories and sold to textile mills.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance provides for the levy and collection of excise duty on staple cotton produced by ginning factories and sold to textile mills. It defines key terms such as 'staple cotton', 'factory', and 'sale price', and sets specific duty rates for public and private sector factories. The Central Board of Revenue is empowered to make rules and grant exemptions, while the provisions of the Central Excises and Salt Act, 1944 apply where not inconsistent.

metadata.short_title: The State Bank of Pakistan Act, 1956
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of the State Bank of Pakistan.
metadata.commencement: at once; except section 46, deemed to have taken effect on and from the twelfth day of May 1948
repeals: The State Bank of Pakistan Ordinance, 1955 (XVIII of 1955)
metadata.one_line: An Act establishing the State Bank of Pakistan to regulate monetary and credit systems.
metadata.summary: This Act provides for the establishment, incorporation, and management of the State Bank of Pakistan. It outlines the Bank's objectives, including domestic price stability and supporting economic policies, while defining its functions such as issuing bank notes and acting as a lender of last resort. The legislation details the composition of the Board of Directors, regulatory powers over scheduled banks, and provisions for audits and reserves.

name: State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) Banking Services Corporation Ordinance, 2001

metadata.short_title: The SBP Banking Services Corporation Ordinance, 2001
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the establishment of SBP Banking Services Corporation as a subsidiary of the State Bank of Pakistan, and for the management and control thereof
metadata.one_line: Establishes SBP Banking Services Corporation as a subsidiary of the State Bank and transfers part of its undertaking.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the SBP Banking Services Corporation as a body corporate and a subsidiary of the State Bank of Pakistan. It provides for the transfer of a part of the State Bank's undertaking and certain employees to the new corporation.
