The document outlines the Bank's functions, including handling bank notes, issuing prize bonds, and performing activities delegated by the State Bank. It also grants powers to make rules and regulations and defines the status of its officers as public servants.

metadata.short_title: The State Immunity Ordinance, 1981
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend and consolidate the law relating to the immunity of States from the jurisdiction of Courts.
repeals: Sections 86 and 87 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (Act V of 1908)
metadata.one_line: Amends and consolidates law on state immunity from Pakistani court jurisdiction with specific exceptions.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends and consolidates the legal framework regarding the immunity of States from the jurisdiction of Courts in Pakistan. It establishes general immunity rules while defining specific exceptions for commercial transactions, employment contracts, and submissions to jurisdiction. The document also outlines procedural requirements for serving process on States and provides mechanisms for the Federal Government to restrict or extend immunities via notification.

metadata.short_title: The State-Owned Enterprises (Governance and Operations) Act, 2023
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for governance and operation of the management and financial efficiency of state-owned enterprises owned and controlled by the Federal Government
metadata.one_line: This Act establishes governance, operational, and financial efficiency standards for Federal Government-owned state-owned enterprises.
metadata.summary: The State-Owned Enterprises (Governance and Operations) Act, 2023 provides a legal framework for the management and financial efficiency of state-owned enterprises owned and controlled by the Federal Government. It outlines principles for prudent management, board composition, independent directorship, and transparent performance reporting. The Act also establishes a Central Monitoring Unit to oversee disclosures and ensures compliance with procurement standards and public service obligations.

name: Stock Exchange (Corporatisation, Demutualization and Integration) Act, 2012

metadata.short_title: The Stock Exchanges (Corporatisation, Demutualization and Integration) Act, 2012
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the corporatisation, demutualization and integration of stock exchanges in Pakistan
subjects: Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan
metadata.administering_body: Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan
metadata.one_line: This Act provides for the corporatisation, demutualization, and integration of stock exchanges in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: The Stock Exchanges (Corporatisation, Demutualization and Integration) Act, 2012 was enacted to facilitate the development of capital markets by converting stock exchanges from companies limited by guarantee to public companies. It establishes a framework for demutualizing ownership rights, integrating multiple exchanges, and regulating their operations under the supervision of the Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan. The Act defines key terms such as 'corporatisation' and 'demutualization', outlines procedures for share issuance and trading rights, and grants the Commission powers to make regulations and give directions to ensure compliance.

metadata.short_title: The Succession Act, 1925
metadata.long_title: An Act to consolidate the law relating to succession in British India.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of British India (now Pakistan)

metadata.one_line: Consolidates laws relating to succession, domicile, and testamentary/intestate distribution of property.
metadata.summary: This Act consolidates the law relating to succession in British India. It defines domicile and kinship rules for intestate and testamentary succession. The Act provides specific rules for the distribution of property among widows, children, parents, and other relatives, including special provisions for Parsis. It also governs the execution, revocation, and interpretation of wills.

metadata.short_title: The Sugar Export Subsidy Fund Ordinance, 1970
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the establishment of a Sugar Export Subsidy Fund for promoting export of sugar.
metadata.territorial_extent: Baluchistan, the North-West Frontier Province, the Punjab and Sind
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both
metadata.administering_body: Federal Government / Federal Board of Revenue
metadata.one_line: Establishes a Sugar Export Subsidy Fund to subsidize sugar exports and levies related taxes.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Sugar Export Subsidy Fund to promote the export of sugar. It authorizes the levy of sales tax on sugar-cane sold to mills and excise duty on cane grown by mills and sugar produced, with proceeds credited to the fund after collection costs. The Federal Government is empowered to apply the fund for subsidizing exports, authorize repayments of excise duty on exported sugar, and require registration of export contracts. It also grants powers to call for information, inspect factories, and imposes penalties for contraventions or false statements.

metadata.short_title: The Sugar-cane Act, 1934
metadata.long_title: An Act to regulate the price of sugar-cane intended for use in sugar factories.
metadata.commencement: at once for this section; on such date as the Provincial Government may appoint for remaining sections
metadata.max_penalty: fine which may extend to two thousand rupees
metadata.one_line: Regulates sugar-cane prices for factories, defines controlled areas and establishes rules for purchasing agents.
metadata.summary: This Act regulates the price of sugar-cane intended for use in sugar factories to assure growers a fair price. It empowers Provincial Governments to declare controlled areas, fix minimum prices, and prohibit unauthorized purchases. The Act also provides for the establishment of Advisory Committees, licensing of purchasing agents, and organization of grower societies, with penalties for contravention.

metadata.short_title: The Suits Valuation Act, 1887
metadata.long_title: An Act to prescribe the mode of valuing certain suits for the purpose of determining the jurisdiction of Courts with respect thereto
metadata.commencement: on such dates as the Provincial Government directs (Part I); on the first day of July, 1887 (Part II and Part III)
metadata.one_line: Prescribes the mode of valuing certain suits to determine court jurisdiction.
metadata.summary: This Act prescribes the method for valuing specific suits to determine the jurisdiction of courts. It grants Provincial Governments the power to make rules for land valuation and establishes that in certain suits, the court-fee value and jurisdictional value must be identical. The Act also outlines procedures for handling objections regarding improper valuation on appeal or revision.

name: Superior Courts (Court Dress and Mode of Address) Order (Repeal) Act, 2020

metadata.short_title: The Superior Courts (Court Dress and Mode of Address) Order (Repeal) Act, 2020
metadata.long_title: An Act to repeal the President's Order No. 15 of 1980
repeals: President's Order No. 15 of 1980
metadata.status_evidence: The Superior Courts (Court Dress and Mode of Address) Order, 1980 (P.O. No. 15 of 1980), is hereby repealed.
metadata.one_line: Repeals the President's Order No. 15 of 1980 regarding superior court dress and address.
metadata.summary: This Act serves to repeal the Superior Courts (Court Dress and Mode of Address) Order, 1980. It was enacted by Parliament on February 21, 2020, and came into force immediately upon enactment. The legislation removes the previous presidential order concerning court attire and modes of address for superior courts.

metadata.short_title: The Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Act, 1997
metadata.long_title: An Act to determine the number of the judges of the Supreme Court of Pakistan
key_definitions: Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan
metadata.one_line: This Act determines that the Supreme Court shall have a maximum of thirty-three judges other than the Chief Justice.
metadata.summary: The Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Act, 1997 was enacted to determine the number of judges serving in the Supreme Court of Pakistan. It specifies that the maximum number of judges, excluding the Chief Justice, shall be up to thirty-three. The Act comes into force immediately upon enactment.

metadata.short_title: The Supreme Court (Practice and Procedure) Act, 2023
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for certain practices and procedures of the Supreme Court
metadata.commencement: at once and deemed to have taken effect on the date of commencement of the Constitution (Twenty-sixth Amendment) Act, 2024
metadata.one_line: This Act regulates the practice and procedure of the Supreme Court, including bench composition and counsel rights.
metadata.summary: The Supreme Court (Practice and Procedure) Act, 2023 establishes rules for hearing causes and matters before the Supreme Court. It defines the composition of benches, grants parties the right to appoint counsel of choice for review applications, and sets timelines for urgent matters. The Act also mandates the recording of proceedings and provides that its provisions override other laws.

name: Supreme Court (Review of Judgments and Orders) Act, 2023

metadata.short_title: The Supreme Court (Review of Judgments and Orders) Act, 2023
metadata.long_title: An Act to facilitate and strengthen the Supreme Court of Pakistan in the exercise of its powers to review its judgment and orders
metadata.one_line: This Act facilitates and strengthens the Supreme Court's power to review judgments by enlarging jurisdiction, mandating larger benches, and allowing appointed counsel.
metadata.summary: The Supreme Court (Review of Judgments and Orders) Act, 2023 aims to facilitate and strengthen the Supreme Court of Pakistan in exercising its powers to review judgments and orders. It enlarges the court's jurisdiction under Article 184 to match that of appeals under Article 185 regarding facts and law. The Act mandates that review petitions be heard by a larger bench than the one that passed the original judgment, grants petitioners the right to appoint their own counsel, and sets specific limitation periods for filing reviews.

name: Supreme Court and High Court (Extension of Jurisdiction to certain Tribal Areas) Act, 1973

metadata.short_title: The Supreme Court and High Court (Extension of Jurisdiction to certain Tribal Areas) Act, 1973
metadata.long_title: An Act to extend the Jurisdiction of the Supreme Court and the High Court to certain Tribal Areas
metadata.territorial_extent: the Provincially Administered Tribal Areas of Chitral, Dir, Kalam, Swat and Malakand Protected Area
metadata.one_line: Extends Supreme Court and Peshawar High Court jurisdiction to specific Tribal Areas in NWFP.
metadata.summary: This Act extends the jurisdiction of the Supreme Court of Pakistan and the Peshawar High Court to certain Provincially Administered Tribal Areas. Specifically, it grants these courts the same jurisdiction over Chitral, Dir, Kalam, Swat, and Malakand Protected Area as they possess over other areas of the North-West Frontier Province. The Act came into force immediately upon enactment.

name: Supreme Court and High Court (Extension of Jurisdiction to Federally Administered Tribal Areas) Act, 2018

metadata.short_title: The Supreme Court and High Court (Extension of Jurisdiction to Federally Administered Tribal Areas) Act, 2018
metadata.long_title: An Act to extend the jurisdiction of the Supreme Court of Pakistan and the Peshawar High Court to the Federally Administered Tribal Areas
metadata.commencement: on such date or dates and in such Federally Administered Tribal Areas or part thereof, as the Federal Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, determine from time to time
metadata.one_line: Extends Supreme Court and Peshawar High Court jurisdiction to the Federally Administered Tribal Areas.
metadata.summary: This Act extends the jurisdiction of the Supreme Court of Pakistan and the Peshawar High Court to the Federally Administered Tribal Areas. The extension grants these courts the same jurisdiction they possess in relation to the province of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. The Federal Government is authorized to determine the specific dates and areas within the FATA where this Act comes into force via official Gazette notifications.

metadata.short_title: The Surrender of Illicit Arms Act, 1991
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the surrender of illicit arms and improvement and control of the law and order situation
metadata.commencement: in such areas and on such date as the Federal Government may, on recommendation of the respective Provincial Governments, by notification in the official Gazette appoint
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for life and forfeiture of property
metadata.one_line: Provides a legal framework for the surrender of illicit arms to improve law and order in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes a mechanism for persons possessing illicit arms to surrender them to designated authorities within specific timeframes. It defines 'illicit arms' broadly to include various types of firearms, explosives, and containers holding harmful substances. The legislation offers indemnity from legal action for those who surrender weapons but retains criminal liability for any prior offenses committed with them. Additionally, it empowers the Federal Government to conduct searches, scrutinize existing licenses, and cancel them if they are not conducive to public peace.

name: Survey for Documentation of National Economy Ordinance, 2000

metadata.short_title: The Survey for Documentation of National Economy Ordinance, 2000
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for documentation of economy and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment up to three months or fine up to twenty five thousand rupees or both
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance empowers the Central Board of Revenue to conduct economic surveys and assess tax liabilities through questionnaires.
metadata.summary: The Survey for Documentation of National Economy Ordinance, 2000 was promulgated by the President to address large-scale non-reporting and under-reporting of assets, income, and taxable activities. It authorizes the Central Board of Revenue to constitute survey teams comprising officials from federal and provincial departments, utility agencies, and armed forces to collect information via specific questionnaires. The collected data is used for assessing turnover, value, wealth, income, and tax liabilities under laws administered by the Central Board of Revenue. The Ordinance prescribes penalties for refusing to fill questionnaires or providing false information, including imprisonment and fines, and outlines procedures for cognizance of offences by Executive Magistrates.

metadata.short_title: The Surveying and Mapping Act, 2014
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for constitution and regulation of survey of Pakistan
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment up to five years and a fine of five million rupees
metadata.one_line: This Act constitutes the Survey of Pakistan and regulates surveying, mapping, and geospatial data activities in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: The Surveying and Mapping Act, 2014 establishes the Survey of Pakistan as the national organization for surveying and mapping. It defines various technical terms related to geospatial data, remote sensing, and map-making. The Act outlines the functions of the Survey of Pakistan, including research, data management, and protection of survey markers. It also prescribes offences and penalties for unauthorized use or dissemination of incorrect maps and geospatial data.

metadata.short_title: The System of Sardari (Abolition) Act, 1976
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the abolition of the system of Sardari and for matters ancillary thereto.
repeals: The System of Sardari, (Abolition) Ordinance, 1976 (XV of 1976)
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine which may extend to ten thousand rupees, or with both
metadata.one_line: Abolishes the system of Sardari and prohibits associated judicial powers, private jails, forced labor, and tribute collection.
metadata.summary: This Act abolishes the system of Sardari prevalent in certain parts of Pakistan, which is described as a remnant of an oppressive feudal and tribal system. It prohibits recognized Sardars from exercising unauthorized judicial powers, maintaining private jails, arresting persons without legal authority, taking free labor, demanding tribute, or deriving benefits from tribal land. The Act applies to the whole of Pakistan and came into force immediately upon enactment.

name: Tea (Control of Prices, Distribution and Movement) Ordinance, 1960

metadata.short_title: The Tea (Control of Prices, Distribution and Movement) Ordinance, 1960
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for special measures for the control of prices, distribution and movement of tea.
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance provides special measures to control the prices, distribution, and movement of tea in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: The Tea (Control of Prices, Distribution and Movement) Ordinance, 1960 was promulgated by the President to regulate the tea market in Pakistan. It establishes a registration system for dealers including bidders, blenders, importers, wholesalers, and retailers under the supervision of the Controller-General. The Ordinance bans forward transactions, fixes prices and quantities, restricts movements, and imposes penalties for non-compliance or false statements.

metadata.short_title: The Tea Ordinance, 1959
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide measures for the expansion of export of tea, for the setting up of bodies to establish new tea gardens and rehabilitate derelict tea gardens, and generally for the promotion of the tea industry, and for levying a cess on tea produced in Pakistan
repeals: Tea Ordinance, 1947
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years or with fine or with both
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Pakistan Tea Board and Tea Development Committee to promote tea industry, control exports, and levy cess.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance provides measures for expanding tea exports and establishing bodies to manage new and rehabilitated tea gardens. It creates the Pakistan Tea Board and a Tea Development Committee with specific functions regarding cultivation control and export auctions. The law also empowers the Federal Government to make rules and imposes penalties for false statements or violations of export controls.

metadata.short_title: The Tea Plantations Labour Ordinance, 1962
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the welfare of labour, and to regulate the conditions of work, in tea plantations
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance regulates labour welfare and working conditions in tea plantations across Pakistan.
metadata.summary: The Tea Plantations Labour Ordinance, 1962 was promulgated to ensure the welfare of workers and regulate their working conditions specifically within tea plantations. It establishes a system of Chief Inspectors and Inspectors appointed by the Provincial Government to enforce provisions regarding hours of work, medical facilities, canteens, and leave entitlements. The Ordinance applies initially to large tea plantations but allows for extension to smaller areas via provincial notification, defining specific terms like 'worker' and 'tea plantation' to determine applicability.

metadata.short_title: The Telegraph Act, 1885
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the law relating to Telegraphs in Pakistan
establishes: Director-General, Pakistan Telegraph and Telephone Department
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both
metadata.one_line: This Act amends the law relating to telegraphs in Pakistan, defining terms and granting powers to the government.
metadata.summary: The Telegraph Act, 1885 amends the law regarding telegraphs in Pakistan. It grants the Federal Government exclusive privileges over telegraphs and the power to establish lines on various properties. The Act defines key terms like 'telegraph', 'message', and 'telegraph authority' while outlining offences related to unauthorized use, tampering, and interference with telegraphic communication.

name: Territorial Waters and Maritime Zones Act, 1976 (Repealed by Act.XVIII of 2023)

metadata.short_title: The Territorial Waters and Maritime Zones Act, 1976
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the declaration of the territorial waters and maritime zones of Pakistan.
metadata.status_evidence: name field in catalogue entry: 'Territorial Waters and Maritime Zones Act, 1976 (Repealed by Act.XVIII of 2023)'
metadata.one_line: Declares Pakistan's territorial waters and maritime zones, regulates foreign ship passage, and defines sovereign rights over the continental shelf.
metadata.summary: This Act declares the territorial waters, contiguous zone, continental shelf, and exclusive economic zone of Pakistan. It establishes limits for sovereignty, regulates innocent passage by foreign ships, and grants the Federal Government powers to enforce laws regarding security, immigration, customs, and marine pollution in these zones. The Act also outlines offences related to maritime violations and procedures for prosecution.

metadata.short_title: The Terrorist Affected Areas (Special Courts) Act, 1992
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the suppression of acts of terrorism, subversion and other heinous offences in the terrorist affected areas.
metadata.one_line: This Act establishes Special Courts to suppress terrorism and related offences in declared terrorist affected areas.
metadata.summary: The Terrorist Affected Areas (Special Courts) Act, 1992 provides for the suppression of acts of terrorism, subversion, and other heinous offences in specific areas declared as terrorist affected zones. It empowers the Federal Government to declare such areas and establish Special Courts with enhanced powers for police and civil armed forces operations. The Act outlines procedures for arrests, searches, witness protection, and defines various offences under the Pakistan Penal Code and other laws that fall within its scope.

name: THE CENSUS ORDINANCE, 1959(Repealed by Act XiV of 2011 section 63 (w.e.f 31-05-2011)))

metadata.short_title: The Census Ordinance, 1959
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the taking, from time to time, of census for Pakistan and for obtaining certain information with respect to the population of and housing conditions in Pakistan.
metadata.status_evidence: [Repealed by Act XiV of 2011 section 63 (w.e.f 31-05-2011)]
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months or with fine which may extend to fifteen thousand rupees, or with both
metadata.one_line: Provides for the taking of census in Pakistan and obtaining population and housing information.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance empowers the Federal Government to conduct periodic censuses across Pakistan to gather data on population and housing conditions. It establishes a hierarchy of Census Officers, including a Chief Commissioner and Provincial Commissioners, who are appointed by the Federal Government. The law outlines specific duties for various officials and citizens, such as military commanders and local council members, to assist in data collection. It also defines offences related to refusing assistance or providing false returns, prescribing penalties including imprisonment and fines.

metadata.short_title: The Family Courts Act, 1964
metadata.long_title: An Act to make provision for the establishment of Family Courts.
metadata.commencement: on such date or dates as Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, specify
metadata.one_line: Establishes Family Courts to expeditiously settle disputes relating to marriage and family affairs.
metadata.summary: This Act provides for the establishment of Family Courts in each district or other places deemed necessary by the Provincial Government. The courts are empowered to hear and adjudicate upon matters such as dissolution of marriage, dower, maintenance, custody of children, and guardianship. The Act also grants Family Courts jurisdiction over specific offences where one spouse is a victim of the other and outlines procedures for instituting suits, recording evidence, and enforcing decrees.

name: The International Islamic Institute for Peace (IIIP) Act, 2024

metadata.short_title: The International Islamic Institute for Peace (IIIP) Act, 2024
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of an International Islamic Institute for Peace (IIIP) at Islamabad and Narowal in the private sector, and for matters connected therewith and ancillary thereto
metadata.one_line: Establishes the International Islamic Institute for Peace (IIIP) as a private sector body corporate with academic autonomy.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the International Islamic Institute for Peace (IIIP) at Islamabad and Narowal as a private sector institution. The Institute is granted perpetual succession, a common seal, and full academic, financial, and administrative autonomy. It empowers the Board of Directors to manage operations, appoint staff, and set up campuses within Pakistan or abroad while adhering to relevant higher education regulations.

name: THE MARKETING OF PETROLEUM PRODUCTS (FEDERAL CONTROL) ACT, 1974.(Repealed by ord.89 of 02 s.3)

metadata.short_title: The Marketing of Petroleum Products (Federal Control) Act, 1974
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the management and development of marketing facilities in petroleum products.
metadata.status_evidence: [Repealed by ord.89 of 02 s.3]
metadata.repealed_by: Ordinance No. 89 of 1982 (implied by 'ord.89 of 02' and context of 1981 revision, though exact title truncated in text)
metadata.one_line: This Act provides for the Federal Government's management and development of marketing facilities in petroleum products.
metadata.summary: The Marketing of Petroleum Products (Federal Control) Act, 1974 empowers the Federal Government to take over the management or acquire shares of marketing companies engaged in petroleum products. It establishes a Board of Management to control these affairs and allows for the appointment of Managing Directors who exercise board powers. The Act outlines principles for compensating shareholders when shares are acquired by the government, including payment via cash or bonds.

metadata.short_title: The Tolls (Army and Air Force) Act, 1901
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the law relating to the exemption from tolls of persons and property belonging to the Army or Air Force.
repeals: The Tolls (Army and Air Force) Act, 1901
metadata.status_evidence: [Repealed by the Repealing and Amending Act, 1914 (X of 1914), s. 3 and Schedule II.]
metadata.max_penalty: fine which may extend to fifty rupees
metadata.one_line: This Act exempts Army and Air Force personnel and property from tolls and defines related penalties.
metadata.summary: The Tolls (Army and Air Force) Act, 1901 amends the law regarding exemptions from tolls for persons and property belonging to the Army or Air Force. It defines specific terms such as 'authorised followers', 'carriage', and 'Irregular Corps' while granting exemptions to officers, soldiers, airmen, and their baggage. The Act also establishes penalties for contravention of its provisions and empowers the Federal Government to make rules and award compensation.

metadata.short_title: The Tolls Act, 1851
metadata.long_title: An Act for enabling Government to levy Tolls on Public Roads and Bridges.
metadata.territorial_extent: the Province of the Punjab and any other Province as extended by notification
repeals: Acts (general)
metadata.status_evidence: This Act should be read with the Tolls Act, 1864 (15 of 1864), and the Tolls Act, 1888 (8 of 1888).
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for any term not exceeding six calendar months, or to fine not exceeding two hundred rupees
metadata.one_line: Enables the Federal Government to levy tolls on public roads and bridges made or repaired by it.
metadata.summary: This Act empowers the Federal Government to levy tolls on public roads and bridges constructed or repaired at its expense. It outlines procedures for collecting these tolls, including the seizure and sale of property for non-payment, and grants police officers assistance in enforcement. The Act also specifies exemptions for police duties, penalties for unlawful toll collection, and the application of proceeds as public revenue.

name: Torture and Custodial Death (Prevention and Punishment) Act, 2022

metadata.short_title: The Torture and Custodial Death (Prevention and Punishment) Act, 2022
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide protection to a person during custody from all acts of torture perpetrated by public officials
key_definitions: cruel or inhuman or degrading treatment
metadata.one_line: This Act protects persons from torture by public officials, defines custodial death, and mandates speedy trials.
metadata.summary: This Act provides protection to individuals during custody against acts of torture committed by public officials. It defines key terms such as 'custody', 'torture', and 'custodial death', and declares evidence obtained through torture inadmissible in court proceedings. The legislation mandates strict timelines for investigation, trial, and appeals, while also establishing special protection mechanisms for victims and witnesses.

metadata.short_title: The Toshakhana (Management and Regulation) Act, 2024
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for management and regulation of Toshakhana.
metadata.max_penalty: fine equal to five times the assessed market value of the gift
metadata.administering_body: The division to which business of this Act stands allocated
metadata.one_line: This Act regulates the management, acceptance, and disposal of gifts received by public office holders in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Act provides for the management and regulation of the Toshakhana, a repository of gifts maintained by the Government of Pakistan. It applies to public office holders, including federal and provincial officials, as well as private individuals acting as members of official delegations. The Act mandates that gifts be deposited within thirty days, requires open auctions for disposal, and directs auction proceeds toward promoting female primary education in backward areas.

name: Trade Development authority of Pakistan Act, 2013

metadata.short_title: The Trade Development Authority of Pakistan Act, 2013
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for establishment of the Trade Development Authority of Pakistan
repeals: Government of Pakistan, Export Promotion Bureau's Resolution No.P-5(5)/65, dated the 22nd January, 1966
Government of Pakistan, Ministry of Commerce's Order No. 28(19)-CE/63, dated the 4th December, 1963
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Trade Development Authority of Pakistan under the Ministry of Commerce to promote exports.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Trade Development Authority of Pakistan (TDAP) as a body corporate under the administrative control of the Ministry of Commerce. The Authority is responsible for developing and promoting Pakistan's exports, providing support to stakeholders, and formulating trade policies. It replaces the Export Promotion Bureau and transfers its assets and liabilities to the new Authority upon commencement.

metadata.short_title: The Trade Dispute Resolution Act, 2022
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of a comprehensive regime in Pakistan for the swift and effective resolution of disputes relating to the export and import of goods and services including import and export through e-commerce.
repeals: Sections 5A, 5B and 5C of the Imports and Exports (Control) Act, 1950 (Act No. XXXIX of 1950)
establishes: Commercial benches of the High Court
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years, or a fine not exceeding five million rupees, or both
metadata.one_line: Establishes a comprehensive regime for resolving trade disputes involving imports, exports, and e-commerce through a new Commission and commercial benches.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Trade Dispute Resolution Commission (TDRC) to handle disputes related to the import and export of goods and services, including those arising from e-commerce. It creates a comprehensive framework encompassing negotiations, determinations by the Commission, conciliation processes, and referrals to commercial benches of the High Court. The legislation defines specific terms such as 'conciliation' and 'arbitration', outlines the powers of the Commission to acquire information and issue interim determinations, and prescribes penalties for providing false information or failing to comply with findings.

metadata.short_title: The Trade Marks Ordinance, 2001
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend and consolidate the law relating to trade marks
repeals: The Trade Marks Act, 1940
metadata.one_line: An Ordinance to amend and consolidate the law relating to trade marks in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance consolidates and amends the legal framework governing trade marks in Pakistan. It establishes the Trade Marks Registry and outlines procedures for registration, opposition, and renewal of marks. The document also details remedies for infringement, including customs seizure of infringing goods, and incorporates international obligations under the Paris Convention.

metadata.short_title: The Trade Organizations Act, 2013
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the registration and regulation of trade organizations
repeals: Trade Organisations Ordinance, 1961 (XLV of 1961)
metadata.one_line: This Act provides for the registration, regulation, licensing, and governance of trade organizations across Pakistan.
metadata.summary: The Trade Organizations Act, 2013 establishes a regulatory framework for trade organizations operating in Pakistan. It mandates that no trade organization can be registered unless it holds a license granted by the Regulator appointed under the Act. The legislation defines the structure, autonomy, and operational codes for these organizations while repealing the previous Trade Organisations Ordinance, 1961. It also outlines penalties for contraventions and provides transitional provisions to validate actions taken before the Act's commencement.

metadata.short_title: The Traffic Offences (Special Courts) Ordinance, 1981
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to constitute Special Courts for the speedy disposal of cases pertaining to traffic offences.
metadata.one_line: Constitutes Special Courts for the speedy disposal of traffic offences across Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes Special Courts to ensure the speedy disposal of cases related to traffic offences. It defines a Special Court as one constituted under Section 3 and a traffic offence as one punishable under the Provincial Motor Vehicles Ordinance, 1965. The Provincial Government is empowered to constitute these courts using local dignitaries, Local Council members, advocates with five years' standing, or serving Magistrates. All pending cases in regular courts are transferred to these Special Courts upon their constitution, and appeals lie to the Court of Session.

metadata.short_title: The Trained Paramedical Staff Facility Act, 2023
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the facility of trained paramedical staff in public and private institutions and for the purposes connected therewith and ancillary thereto
metadata.max_penalty: fine up to one hundred thousand rupees or imprisonment for six months
metadata.one_line: Provides for the facility of trained paramedical staff in public and private institutions within Islamabad Capital Territory.
metadata.summary: This Act ensures the provision of trained paramedical staff at all educational institutions to provide immediate medical assistance and first aid. It mandates both Federal and private institutions to have such staff available whenever needed. Non-compliance attracts a warning, followed by fines up to one hundred thousand rupees or imprisonment for six months in subsequent cases.

metadata.short_title: The Tramways Act, 1886
metadata.long_title: An Act to facilitate the construction and to regulate the working of tramways
metadata.territorial_extent: the Punjab and the North-West Frontier Province (extendable to other territories by notification)
repeals: section 54 of Railway Act
metadata.max_penalty: double the penalty to which a promoter acting otherwise than in accordance with an order is liable under section 27
metadata.one_line: This Act facilitates the construction and regulates the working of tramways in specified territories.
metadata.summary: The Tramways Act, 1886 provides a legal framework for constructing and operating tramways. It outlines procedures for obtaining government orders, defines terms like 'local authority' and 'road', and establishes rules regarding licenses, tolls, and traffic rights. The Act also details penalties for non-compliance, insolvency proceedings for promoters, and provisions for the discontinuance or transfer of control over tramway undertakings.

metadata.short_title: The Transfer of Evacuee Deposits Act, 1956
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide, in pursuance of an Agreement with India, for the transfer to that country of certain deposits belonging to evacuees, the reception in Pakistan of similar deposits belonging to refugees and matters connected therewith.
repeals: The Transfer of Evacuee Deposits Act, 1956
metadata.status_evidence: [Repealed by the Repealing and Amending Ordinance, 1965 (X of 1965), s. 2 and 1st Sch.] (Footnote on Page 7)
metadata.one_line: Provides for the transfer of evacuee deposits to India and reception of refugee deposits in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Act facilitates the transfer of certain deposits belonging to evacuees to India and the reception of similar deposits belonging to refugees in Pakistan, pursuant to an Agreement with India. It establishes a Custodian and Assistant Custodians to manage these deposits, defines key terms such as 'evacuee' and 'refugee', and outlines procedures for transferring movable property held by courts or managers. The Act also bars civil court jurisdiction over the Custodian's actions and provides protection for acts done in good faith.

name: Transfer of Evacuee Land (Katchi Abadi) Act, 1972

metadata.short_title: The Transfer of Evacuee Land (Katchi Abadi) Act, 1972
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for transfer of certain evacuee land to the occupants thereof
metadata.commencement: at once in the Province of the Punjab and the Capital of the Federation; on such date as the Federal Government may appoint in other Provinces
repeals: The Transfer of Evacuee Land (Katchi Abadi) Ordinance, 1972
metadata.max_penalty: rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both
metadata.one_line: This Act transfers evacuee land in Katchi Abadi areas to occupants and repeals the corresponding Ordinance.
metadata.summary: The Transfer of Evacuee Land (Katchi Abadi) Act, 1972 provides for the transfer of specific evacuee lands to their occupants within declared Katchi Abadi areas. It grants proprietary rights to eligible occupants upon payment of a determined price and allows for the resumption of land not transferred. The Act overrides other laws, establishes penalties for resistance, and repeals the Transfer of Evacuee Land (Katchi Abadi) Ordinance, 1972.

metadata.short_title: The Transfer of Offenders Ordinance, 2002
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for transfer of a citizen of Pakistan convicted of an offence in a foreign country to Pakistan and a citizen of a foreign country convicted of an offence in Pakistan to that country.
metadata.administering_body: Ministry of Interior and Narcotics Control (Interior Division)
metadata.one_line: Provides for the transfer of Pakistani citizens convicted abroad to Pakistan and foreign citizens convicted in Pakistan to their home countries.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance facilitates the mutual transfer of offenders between Pakistan and specified countries that have entered into relevant agreements. It establishes a Competent Authority within the Ministry of Interior to manage applications for transfer, issue warrants, and coordinate with appropriate authorities in foreign nations. The document outlines conditions for transfer, procedures for custody during transit, and clarifies that transferred offenders remain subject to remission rules and presidential pardon powers in their country of conviction.

name: Transfer of Population Welfare Programme (Field Activities) Ordinance, 1983

metadata.short_title: The Transfer of Population Welfare Programme (Field Activities) Ordinance, 1983
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the transfer of field activities of the Population Welfare Programme to the Provincial Governments.
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Federal Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, appoint
metadata.one_line: Transfers field activities of the Population Welfare Programme from the Federal to Provincial Governments.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance transfers the field activities of the Population Welfare Programme from the Federal Government to the Provincial Governments for speedy implementation and effective supervision. It defines specific field activities such as family health services, contraception provision, and community involvement, while retaining federal functions in policy, planning, and coordination. The Ordinance also addresses the transfer of employees, assets, liabilities, and legal proceedings related to these activities, along with provisions for financing and auditing.

metadata.short_title: The Transfer of Property Act, 1882
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the law relating to the Transfer of Property by act of Parties.
metadata.territorial_extent: the territories to which this Act extends
repeals: 27 Hen. VIII, c.10
13 Eliz., c.5
27 Eliz., c.4
4 Wm. and Mary, c.16
XI of 1855
XXVII of 1866
IV of 1872
Regulations I of 1798 and XVII of 1806
I of 1877
key_definitions: Mercantile document of title to goods
metadata.one_line: This Act defines and regulates the transfer of property by act of parties, including sales, mortgages, leases, and actionable claims.
metadata.summary: The Transfer of Property Act, 1882 amends the law relating to the transfer of property by act of parties. It covers transfers of movable and immovable property, defining terms like sale, mortgage, lease, and actionable claim. The Act outlines the rights and liabilities of buyers, sellers, mortgagors, mortgagees, lessors, and lessees, while also addressing fraudulent transfers and the registration requirements for certain transactions.

name: Transplantation of Human Organs and Tissue Act, 2010

metadata.short_title: The Transplantation of Human Organs and Tissues Act, 2010
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for removal, storage and transplantation of human organs and tissues for therapeutic purposes
metadata.one_line: Regulates the removal, storage, and transplantation of human organs and tissues for therapeutic purposes in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Act provides a legal framework for the removal, storage, and transplantation of human organs and tissues strictly for therapeutic purposes. It establishes an Evaluation Committee to assess donations and a Monitoring Authority to oversee the entire process, ensuring that all activities are voluntary and free from coercion. The legislation defines specific terms such as 'brain dead' and 'donor', prohibits commercial dealings in organs, and outlines penalties for unauthorized removal or transplantation.

metadata.short_title: The Travel Agencies Act, 1976
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the development, regulation and control of the profession of travel agencies in Pakistan
metadata.max_penalty: twenty-five thousand rupees
metadata.one_line: This Act regulates and controls the profession of travel agencies in Pakistan through licensing and a regulatory committee.
metadata.summary: The Travel Agencies Act, 1976 provides for the development, regulation, and control of travel agencies in Pakistan. It establishes a Regulatory Committee to advise the Federal Government and approve service charges. The Act mandates that no person shall operate as a travel agency without a license granted by the Federal Government, subject to specific conditions regarding experience, financial position, and office standards. It also creates a business guarantee fund requirement and outlines penalties for contravention of the Act or rules.

metadata.short_title: The Treasure-trove Act, 1878
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the law relating to Treasure-trove
repeals: enactments relating to Treasure-trove (prior to this Act)
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both
key_definitions: Treasure: anything of any value hidden in the soil, or in anything affixed thereto
Collector: (1) any Revenue-officer in independent charge of a district, and (2) any officer appointed by the Provincial Government to perform the functions of a Collector under this Act
Owner: when any person is entitled, under any reservation in an instrument of transfer of any land or thing affixed thereto, to treasure in such land or thing
metadata.one_line: This Act amends the law relating to treasure-trove, defining ownership, procedures for claimants, and penalties for concealment.
metadata.summary: The Treasure-trove Act, 1878 amends the legal framework regarding hidden valuables found in soil. It defines 'treasure', 'collector', and 'owner' while establishing a procedure where finders must notify authorities and deposit treasure or provide security. The Act outlines how claims are adjudicated by the Collector, including timelines for suits and conditions under which treasure is declared ownerless or given to the Government.

metadata.short_title: The Tribal Areas (Restoration of Jurisdiction) Act, 1964
metadata.long_title: An Act to restore the jurisdiction of the Supreme Court and the High Court in relation to the Tribal Areas of the Quetta Division
metadata.territorial_extent: the Tribal Areas of the Quetta Division
metadata.commencement: at once; deemed to have taken effect on 1964-01-10
metadata.one_line: Restores Supreme Court and High Court jurisdiction over Tribal Areas of Quetta Division.
metadata.summary: This Act restores the jurisdiction of the Supreme Court and the High Court of Baluchistan in relation to the Tribal Areas of the Quetta Division. It applies to matters concerning which this jurisdiction is created or restored, specifically referencing the period before the Constitution (First Amendment) Act, 1963. The Act also extends limitation periods by excluding the time between January 10, 1964, and the date the Act came into force.

metadata.short_title: The Trusts Act, 1882
metadata.long_title: An Act to define and amend the law relating to Private Trusts and Trustees.
repeals: enactments repealed by the Federal Laws (Revision and Declaration) Ordinance, 1981
metadata.status_evidence: The Trust Act, 1882 is repealed to the extent of I.C.T by Act NO. XXV of 2020,s.111.
metadata.one_line: Defines and amends the law relating to private trusts and trustees in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Act defines and amends the law regarding private trusts and trustees. It outlines the creation, duties, liabilities, and powers of trustees, as well as the rights of beneficiaries. The Act also covers constructive trusts and obligations in the nature of trusts, while explicitly excluding Muslim waqf rules.

name: Unani, Ayurvedic and Homoeopathic Practitioners Act, 1965

metadata.short_title: The Unani, Ayurvedic and Homoeopathic Practitioners Act, 1965
metadata.long_title: An Act to regulate the qualifications and to provide for the registration of practitioners of Unani, Ayurvedic and Homoeopathic systems of medicine.
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment not less than one year nor more than five years and fine up to twenty thousand rupees
metadata.one_line: This Act regulates qualifications and registration for Unani, Ayurvedic, and Homoeopathic medical practitioners in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: The Act establishes National Councils for Tibb and Homoeopathy to regulate education, research, and the practice of specific traditional medicine systems. It provides for the recognition of teaching institutions, the registration of practitioners, and the maintenance of registers. The legislation also defines offences related to unregistered practice and unauthorized use of titles, prescribing penalties including imprisonment and fines.

name: United Nations (Declaration of Death of Missing Persons) Act, 1956

metadata.short_title: The United Nations (Declaration of Death of Missing Persons) Act, 1956
metadata.long_title: An Act to give effect to the United Nations Convention on the Declaration of Death of Missing Persons.
metadata.one_line: This Act gives effect to the UN Convention on declaring death of missing persons who disappeared between 1939-1945.
metadata.summary: This Act enables Pakistan to give legal force to the United Nations Convention regarding the declaration of death for missing persons. It applies to individuals who disappeared in Europe, Asia, or Africa between 1939 and 1945 due to war or persecution. The Federal Government is empowered to make notifications and rules to implement these provisions and extend them to cases occurring after 1945.

metadata.short_title: The United Nations (Privileges and Immunities) Act, 1948
metadata.long_title: An Act to give effect to the Convention on the Privileges and Immunities of the United Nations.
metadata.one_line: This Act gives effect to the UN Convention on Privileges and Immunities in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: The United Nations (Privileges and Immunities) Act, 1948 gives legal force in Pakistan to the Convention on the Privileges and Immunities of the United Nations. It grants the UN juridical personality, immunity from legal process, tax exemptions, and customs duty relief for its official use. The Federal Government is empowered to extend similar privileges to other international organizations and to make rules for carrying out the Act's purposes.

metadata.short_title: The United Nations (Security Council) Act, 1948
metadata.long_title: An Act to enable effect to be given to certain provisions of the Charter of the United Nations.
key_definitions: measures not involving the use of armed force
metadata.one_line: Enables the Federal Government to apply UN Security Council measures and make necessary rules.
metadata.summary: This Act empowers the Federal Government to implement decisions of the United Nations Security Council under Article 41 of the Charter without using armed force. It allows the government to make orders with extra-territorial effect and to create rules or delegate powers as needed. The Act also provides indemnity for persons acting in good faith under its provisions.

metadata.short_title: The University of Islamabad Act, 2021
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for establishment of the University of Islamabad and for the matters connected therewith and ancillary thereto
establishes: Foundation for the Advancement of Innovation, Research and Education (FAIRE)
metadata.one_line: Establishes the University of Islamabad as a body corporate with perpetual succession and defines its authorities.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the University of Islamabad in Islamabad as a body corporate with perpetual succession. It defines the composition of the University, including the Patron, Chancellor, Board of Governors, and Executive Committee. The Act outlines the powers and purposes of the University, provisions for teaching, and the management of existing colleges or institutes becoming constituent institutions.

metadata.short_title: The Usurious Loans Act, 1918
metadata.long_title: An Act to give additional powers to Courts to deal in certain cases with usurious loans of money or in kind.
repeals: Usury Laws Repeal Act, 1855
key_definitions: Suit to which this Act applies
metadata.one_line: This Act empowers courts to reopen transactions and relieve debtors from excessive interest on usurious loans.
metadata.summary: The Usurious Loans Act, 1918 grants additional powers to courts to handle cases involving usurious loans of money or in kind. It allows courts to reopen unfair transactions, adjust accounts, and relieve debtors from liability regarding excessive interest. The Act applies to suits for loan recovery, enforcement of security, or redemption of security made after its commencement, while protecting bona fide transferees without notice.

metadata.short_title: The Vaccination Act, 1880
metadata.long_title: An Act to give power to prohibit inoculation and to make the vaccination of children compulsory in certain Municipalities and Cantonments.
metadata.territorial_extent: the Punjab, the North-West Frontier and the district of Sylhet (as extended by Provincial Government notification)
repeals: West Pakistan Ordinance 27 of 1958
metadata.status_evidence: This Act has been repealed in its application to the Province of West Pakistan by West Pakistan Ordinance 27 of 1958, s. 16.
metadata.max_penalty: simple imprisonment for six months or fine extending to one thousand rupees or both
metadata.one_line: This Act prohibits inoculation and mandates compulsory vaccination for children in specific municipalities and cantonments.
metadata.summary: The Vaccination Act, 1880 empowers the prohibition of small-pox inoculation and makes vaccination compulsory for children in designated municipalities and cantonments. It establishes vaccination circles, appoints vaccinators (public and private), and defines the duties of parents and guardians regarding unprotected children. The Act outlines procedures for successful or unsuccessful vaccinations, issues certificates of insusceptibility, and prescribes penalties for non-compliance, including fines and imprisonment.

metadata.short_title: The Vagrancy (Karachi Division) Act, 1950
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for dealing with vagrancy in the Karachi Division
metadata.commencement: on such day as the Federal Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, appoint
metadata.max_penalty: rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years or with fine or with both
metadata.one_line: This Act provides for dealing with vagrancy in the Karachi Division through detention, poor houses, and special magistrates.
metadata.summary: The Vagrancy (Karachi Division) Act, 1950 establishes a legal framework to deal with vagrancy specifically within the Karachi Division. It defines terms such as 'vagrant', 'child', and 'poor house' and empowers Special Magistrates to declare individuals as vagrants after inquiry. The Act authorizes police arrest without warrant for suspected vagrants and mandates detention in Poor Houses or for up to six months depending on the individual's status. It also outlines penalties for escape from custody and procedures for prosecution.

metadata.short_title: The Validation of Laws Act, 1975
metadata.long_title: An Act to validate certain President's Orders, Martial Law Regulations, Martial Law Orders and other laws.
metadata.one_line: Validates various President's Orders, Martial Law Regulations, and Ordinances made between March 1969 and December 1971.
metadata.summary: This Act validates specific laws, orders, and regulations issued during the martial law period in Pakistan. It declares these instruments to have been validly made by the competent authority under Article 270 of the Constitution. The Act covers a wide range of subjects including judicial appointments, financial matters, electoral processes, and provincial administration across West Pakistan and other provinces.

metadata.short_title: The Virtual Assets Act, 2026
metadata.long_title: An Act to establish a regulatory Authority for the licensing, regulation and supervision of Virtual Assets and Virtual Asset Service Providers
repeals: Virtual Assets Ordinance, 2025 (VII of 2025)
key_definitions: Virtual Asset Transfer and Settlement Services
metadata.one_line: Establishes a regulatory authority to license, regulate, and supervise virtual assets and service providers in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Pakistan Virtual Assets Regulatory Authority to oversee virtual asset services and ensure market integrity. It defines various virtual asset services, sets licensing requirements, and imposes prudential standards for issuers and service providers. The legislation also incorporates anti-money laundering measures, consumer protection rules, and provisions for cybersecurity and data privacy.

metadata.short_title: Virtual University Ordinance, 2002
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for establishment of Virtual University of Pakistan
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Virtual University of Pakistan as a body corporate with perpetual succession.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Virtual University of Pakistan as a body corporate with its principal seat at Islamabad. It defines the structure of the university, including the Chancellor, Rector, Board, and various councils responsible for academic and administrative functions. The document outlines the powers to provide instruction in information technology and other fields, set up campuses, and regulate affiliated institutions through specific committees.

name: Voluntary Declaration of Domestic Assets Act, 2018

metadata.short_title: The Voluntary Declaration of Domestic Assets Act, 2018
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for voluntary declaration of domestic assets in Pakistan
metadata.one_line: Provides a mechanism for voluntary declaration of undisclosed domestic assets in Pakistan with associated tax liability.
metadata.summary: This Act facilitates the voluntary declaration of undisclosed domestic assets held by citizens, companies, and associations in Pakistan. It applies to assets acquired before April 10, 2018, excluding holders of public office and their families. The Act mandates a specific declaration format accompanied by evidence of tax payment, which is electronically submitted to the Federal Board of Revenue. Declarations made under this Act are confidential and inadmissible as evidence in proceedings against the declarant.

name: Voluntary Social Welfare Agencies (Registration and Control) Ordinance, 1961

metadata.short_title: The Voluntary Social Welfare Agencies (Registration and Control) Ordinance, 1961
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the registration and control of voluntary social welfare agencies.
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Provincial Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, appoint
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance regulates the registration, control, and dissolution of voluntary social welfare agencies in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance provides for the registration and control of voluntary social welfare agencies operating in various fields such as child welfare, women's welfare, and family planning. It prohibits the establishment or continuation of any agency without a certificate of registration issued by the Registration Authority. Registered agencies must maintain audited accounts, submit annual reports, and comply with conditions set by the Provincial Government. The Ordinance also outlines procedures for appeals, amendments to constitutions, suspension, and dissolution of registered agencies.

metadata.short_title: The War Injuries (Compensation Insurance) Act, 1943
metadata.long_title: An Act to impose on employers a liability to pay compensation to workmen sustaining war injuries and to provide for the insurance of employers against such liability
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Federal Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, appoint
metadata.one_line: Imposes liability on employers to compensate workmen for war injuries and provides for employer insurance against such liability.
metadata.summary: This Act imposes a liability on employers to pay compensation to workmen who sustain war injuries. It also establishes a mechanism for the insurance of employers against this liability through a specific scheme. The Federal Government is responsible for administering the fund and managing the insurance policies, including the recovery of unpaid premiums.

metadata.short_title: The War Injuries Ordinance, 1941
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to make provision for the grant of relief in respect of certain personal injuries sustained during the continuance of hostilities.
metadata.max_penalty: fine which may extend to three hundred rupees; imprisonment for a term which may extend to three months; fine which may extend to one thousand rupees
metadata.one_line: Provides relief for personal injuries sustained during hostilities and regulates compensation liability.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance empowers the Federal Government to make schemes granting relief to persons injured during hostilities. It relieves liable parties from paying compensation or damages for such injuries and requires information regarding the earnings of injured persons. The law also mandates medical attention in dispensaries and hospitals for specified injuries and imposes penalties for false statements made to obtain payments.

metadata.short_title: The War Risks Insurance Ordinance, 1971
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the insurance of certain goods and property in Pakistan against war risks.
metadata.commencement: at once and shall be deemed to have taken effect on the third day of December, 1971
metadata.max_penalty: fine which may extend to five thousand rupees and with a further fine which may extend to one thousand rupees for every day after the first during which the contravention continues
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance provides for compulsory insurance of goods and property in Pakistan against war risks.
metadata.summary: The War Risks Insurance Ordinance, 1971 establishes a scheme to insure specific goods and property in Pakistan against war risks. It defines key terms such as 'factory', 'goods', and 'building' for the purpose of the Act. The Ordinance mandates insurance for factories, buildings, and goods in transit, with provisions for penalties for non-compliance and mechanisms for recovering arrears.

metadata.short_title: The Waste Lands (Claims) Act, 1863
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the adjudication of claims to waste lands
metadata.territorial_extent: all the Provinces and the Capital of the Federation, except the Scheduled Districts (with specific exceptions for certain districts)
repeals: section 24
metadata.status_evidence: This Act has been repealed to the extent of Islamabad Capital Territory, see Ordinance No. 27 of 1981, s. 4 and 3rd Sch.
metadata.administering_body: Provincial Government / Board of Revenue / Financial Commissioner
metadata.one_line: Provides for the speedy adjudication of claims to waste lands proposed to be sold or otherwise dealt with by the Provincial Government.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes a procedure for the speedy adjudication of claims regarding waste lands proposed to be sold or disposed of by the Provincial Government. It empowers Collectors to make enquiries into claims or objections, postpone sales pending these enquiries, and stop sales if a claim appears established. The Act provides for the constitution of Special Courts to try such claims and outlines the powers of the Provincial Government (or its delegated authorities like the Board of Revenue) to award compensation when claims are proved, even if not preferred within the prescribed time limits.

metadata.short_title: The Weights and Measures (International System) Act, 1967
metadata.long_title: An Act to establish standards of weights and measures based on the [International] system.
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Federal Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, appoint
repeals: The Measures of Length Act, 1889 (II of 1889)
The Standards of Weight Act, 1939 (IX of 1939)
The Weights and Measures of Capacity Act, 1871 (XXXI of 1871)
The Sind Weights and Measures Act, 1932(Sindh Act XV of 1932)
The Bombay Weights and Measures Act, 1932, as applicable to Karachi Division
The Punjab Weights and Measures Act, 1941 (Punjab Act XII of 1941)
The Bahawalpur State Weights and Measures Act, 1946
The NorthWest Frontier Weights and Measures Act, 1947 (N.W.F.P. Act XXIII of 1947)
establishes: Deputy Controller of Weights and Measures
Assistant Controller of Weights and Measures
Assistant Inspector of Weights and Measures
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to two thousand and five hundred rupees, or with both
key_definitions: International Bureau of Weights and Measures
metadata.one_line: Establishes standards for weights and measures based on the International system across Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes standards for weights and measures based on the International system to replace previous local and colonial standards. It defines primary units like the kilogram, metre, and litre, and sets up a hierarchy of standards including reference, secondary, and working standards. The Act empowers the Federal Government to appoint Controllers and Inspectors to verify instruments and prohibits the use of non-standard weights and measures, prescribing penalties for offences.

name: West Pakistan Agricultural Bank (Recovery of Dues) Ordinance, 1959

metadata.short_title: The West Pakistan Agricultural Bank (Recovery of Dues) Ordinance, 1959
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide facilities to the Agricultural Bank for recovering its dues.
metadata.one_line: Provides facilities to the Agricultural Bank for recovering its dues through pledging of property.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance empowers the Agricultural Bank to recover its dues by disposing of any property pledged, mortgaged, hypothecated, or assigned to it. It allows agriculturists and cooperative societies to pledge movable or immovable property to secure loans advanced by the Bank under the Agricultural Bank Act, 1957. The Ordinance ensures that nothing in other laws affects the rights or powers of the Bank conferred by this provision.

name: West Pakistan Agricultural Development Finance Corporation (Recovery of Arrears) Act, 1958

metadata.short_title: The West Pakistan Agricultural Development Finance Corporation (Recovery of Arrears) Act, 1958
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide facilities to the Agricultural Development Finance Corporation for recovering its dues.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of West Pakistan, except the Tribal Areas
repeals: West Pakistan Agricultural Development Finance Corporation (Recovery of Arrears) Ordinance, 1957
metadata.one_line: Provides facilities to the Agricultural Development Finance Corporation for recovering its dues by pledging property.
metadata.summary: This Act provides facilities to the Agricultural Development Finance Corporation to recover its dues. It allows agricultural concerns to pledge, mortgage, hypothecate, or assign movable or immovable property to secure loans from the Corporation. The Corporation is empowered to dispose of such property to recover dues, overriding other laws that might affect these rights.

metadata.short_title: The West Pakistan Agricultural Pests Ordinance, 1959
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend and consolidate the law relating to the eradication of agricultural pests in the Province of West Pakistan.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of West Pakistan, except the Tribal Areas
metadata.commencement: on such date or dates as Government may, by notification, specify
repeals: The North-West Frontier Province Sugarcane (Protection against Pyrilla Pest) Act, 1950 (N.W.F.P. XXIII of 1950)
The Sind Boll Worm Act, 1947 (Sind XIV of 1947)
The North-West Frontier Province Fruit-Fly (Preventive Measures) Act, 1950
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance consolidates laws for eradicating agricultural pests in West Pakistan and empowers inspectors to enforce preventive measures.
metadata.summary: The West Pakistan Agricultural Pests Ordinance, 1959 was enacted to amend and consolidate laws regarding the eradication of agricultural pests in the Province of West Pakistan. It defines key terms such as 'agricultural pest' and 'occupier', and grants the Government powers to prohibit cultivation methods or crop transport that spread pests. The Ordinance empowers appointed Inspectors to enter land, seize infested crops, and enforce preventive measures at the occupier's expense, while also establishing appeal mechanisms against notices.

metadata.short_title: The West Pakistan Agriculturists' Loans Act, 1958
metadata.long_title: An Act to consolidate the law relating to the advancement and recovery of taccavi loans for agricultural purposes in the Province of West Pakistan.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of West Pakistan, except the Tribal Areas
repeals: the Agriculturists' Loans Act, 1884 (XII of 1884)
the Agriculturists' Loans (Punjab Amendment) Act, 1951 (Punjab X of 1951)
the Agriculturists' Loans (Punjab Amendment) Act, 1955 (Punjab V of 1955)
the Agriculturists' Loans (Sind Amendment) Act, 1941 (Sind X of 1941)
the Khairpur State Agriculturists' Loans Act, 1952 (Khairpur VIII of 1952)
the West Pakistan Agriculturists' Loans Ordinance, 1958 (West Pakistan Ordinance III of 1958)
metadata.one_line: Consolidates laws for advancing and recovering agricultural taccavi loans in West Pakistan excluding tribal areas.
metadata.summary: This Act consolidates the legal framework for providing and recovering taccavi loans intended for agricultural purposes within the Province of West Pakistan. It grants the Government authority to make rules regarding distress relief loans, land purchases, cattle, seed acquisition, and credit sales of seed to land owners and occupiers. The Act establishes that these loans, along with interest and recovery costs, are recoverable as arrears of land revenue from borrowers or their sureties. Additionally, it clarifies the internal liability shares among joint borrowers within a village community based on signed statements.

name: West Pakistan and Control of Loudspeakers sound Amplifiers, 1965

metadata.short_title: The West Pakistan Regulation and Control of Loudspeakers and Sound Amplifiers Ordinance, 1965
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to regulate and control the use of loudspeakers and sound amplifiers in the Province of West Pakistan.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of West Pakistan, except the Tribal Areas
repeals: The West Pakistan Regulation of Loudspeakers and Sound Amplifiers Ordinance, 1964 (W.P. Ord. XIII of 1964)
metadata.max_penalty: simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine up to fifty thousand rupees, or with both
metadata.one_line: Regulates and controls the use of loudspeakers and sound amplifiers in West Pakistan to prevent public nuisance and disorder.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance regulates and controls the use of loudspeakers and sound amplifiers in the Province of West Pakistan to prevent public nuisance and maintain public order. It prohibits their use in residential areas, near hospitals or places of worship during specific times, and for voicing controversial sectarian utterances. The document outlines punishments including imprisonment and fines, powers of seizure by police officers, and the repeal of a previous 1964 Ordinance.

name: West Pakistan Animals Slaughter Control Act, 1963

metadata.short_title: The West Pakistan Animals Slaughter Control Act, 1963
metadata.long_title: An Act to prohibit the slaughter of useful animals and to regulate the slaughter of other animals in the West Pakistan.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of the West Pakistan, except the Tribal Areas
metadata.commencement: at once for section 1; remaining provisions on such date as Government may notify
repeals: The Karachi Cattle Slaughter Control Act, 1950
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years or fine or both
metadata.one_line: This Act prohibits slaughtering useful animals and regulates the slaughter of others in West Pakistan.
metadata.summary: The West Pakistan Animals Slaughter Control Act, 1963 prohibits the slaughter of useful animals while regulating the slaughter of other animals within the Province of West Pakistan. It establishes requirements for animal examination in stock yards by Veterinary Officers before approval for slaughter and designates specific days and locations for slaughtering activities. The Act also defines key terms such as 'useful animal' and 'carcass', outlines penalties for contraventions including fines and imprisonment, and provides powers for entry, search, seizure, and forfeiture of animals involved in offences.

metadata.short_title: The West Pakistan Anti-Corruption Establishment Ordinance, 1961
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the constitution of a special agency for the investigation of certain offences relating to corruption by public servants and for holding preliminary inquiries against such servants in West Pakistan.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of West Pakistan, except the Tribal Areas
repeals: The Sind Prevention of Bribery and Corruption Act, 1950 (Sind XXIV of 1950)
metadata.one_line: Constitutes a special agency to investigate corruption offences by public servants in West Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Anti-Corruption Establishment to investigate specific corruption offences committed by public servants and conduct preliminary inquiries. It grants the Director and officers powers of search, arrest, and seizure similar to police officers within West Pakistan. The legislation also provides legal immunity for actions taken in good faith under the Ordinance and repeals the Sind Prevention of Bribery and Corruption Act, 1950.

metadata.short_title: The West Pakistan Civil Courts Ordinance, 1962

metadata.commencement: at once in the Divisions of Bahawalpur, Dera Ismail Khan, Hyderabad, Khairpur, Lahore, Multan, Peshawar, Quetta, Rawalpindi and Sargodha and the District of Karachi; on such date or dates as Government may appoint for remaining parts

The Sind Courts Act, 1926

The British Baluchistan Courts Regulation, 1939
The North-West Frontier Province Courts Act, 1952

The Karachi Courts Order, 1956

metadata.one_line: This Ordinance consolidates and amends the law relating to Civil Courts in West Pakistan, establishing court classes and repealing prior enactments.
metadata.summary: The West Pakistan Civil Courts Ordinance, 1962 was promulgated to amend and consolidate laws regarding civil courts in the Province of West Pakistan. It establishes three classes of civil courts: District Judges, Additional District Judges, and Civil Judges, defining their jurisdiction and appointment processes. The document repeals various earlier enactments concerning courts in Punjab, Sindh, NWFP, Baluchistan, and Karachi, while providing for the continuation of pending suits and the transfer of jurisdiction to new courts.

name: West Pakistan Consolidation of Holdings Ordinance, 1960

metadata.short_title: The West Pakistan Consolidation of Holdings Ordinance, 1960

the North-West Frontier Province Consolidation of Holdings Act, 1946 (N.W.F.P. IX of 1946)

metadata.summary: This Ordinance was promulgated to consolidate and amend the law relating to the consolidation of holdings within the Province of West Pakistan. It establishes procedures for moving applications for consolidation, preparing schemes, and appointing Advisory Committees to assist in these processes. The document defines key terms such as 'estate', 'holding', and 'land-revenue' and outlines the powers of the Board of Revenue and Consolidation Officers. Additionally, it repeals previous consolidation acts from Punjab and the North-West Frontier Province.

name: West Pakistan Control of Goondas Ordinance, 1959

metadata.one_line: This Ordinance consolidates and amends laws regarding the control of disorderly persons (goondas) in West Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance was promulgated to consolidate and amend laws concerning the control of disorderly persons known as goondas within the Province of West Pakistan. It establishes Tribunals consisting of District Magistrates or empowered Magistrates to conduct inquiries, declare individuals as goondas, and impose restrictions on their movements or detention. The document also outlines procedures for summoning persons, handling absconders, appealing orders, and repealing previous provincial acts related to goondas.

metadata.short_title: The West Pakistan Departmental Inquiries (Powers) Act, 1958
metadata.long_title: An Act to confer powers for compelling attendance of witnesses and production of documents on officers conducting departmental inquiries against Government servants in the Province of West Pakistan.

metadata.max_penalty: same penalties to which he would have been liable if he had disobeyed a process issued by the civil court
metadata.one_line: Confers powers on officers to summon witnesses and compel document production during departmental inquiries in West Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Act empowers officers conducting departmental inquiries against Government servants in West Pakistan to summon witnesses and compel the production of documents. These powers mirror those exercisable by a civil court under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908. The Act applies to the whole of West Pakistan except the Tribal Areas and prescribes penalties for disobeying such processes.

metadata.short_title: The West Pakistan Epidemic Diseases Act, 1958
metadata.long_title: An Act to consolidate the law relating to the prevention of the spread of dangerous epidemic diseases in the Province of West Pakistan.

the Khairpur State Epidemic Diseases Act, 1941 (Khairpur Act of 1941)
