metadata.one_line: Consolidates laws for preventing dangerous epidemic diseases in West Pakistan and empowers the Provincial Government to take special measures.
metadata.summary: This Act consolidates legislation regarding the prevention of dangerous epidemic diseases within the Province of West Pakistan. It grants the Provincial Government authority to prescribe temporary regulations, inspect travellers, and segregate suspected infected persons when ordinary laws are deemed insufficient. The Act also provides legal protection for individuals acting in good faith under its provisions and establishes penalties for disobeying prescribed orders.

metadata.short_title: The West Pakistan Essential Services (Maintenance) Act, 1958
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the maintenance of certain essential services.

The West Pakistan Essential Services (Maintenance) Ordinance, 1957
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year and a fine
metadata.one_line: This Act maintains essential services in West Pakistan by regulating employment, wages, and imposing penalties for disobedience.
metadata.summary: The West Pakistan Essential Services (Maintenance) Act, 1958 provides for the maintenance of certain essential services within the Province of West Pakistan. It applies to all employment under the Government, its agencies, local authorities, or services relating to transport and civil defence. The Act empowers the Government to order persons in these employments to remain in specified areas and regulates their wages and conditions of service. It defines offences related to disobedience, abandonment of work, or departure from specified areas, prescribing penalties including imprisonment up to one year and fines.

metadata.short_title: The West Pakistan Fisheries Ordinance, 1961
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend and consolidate the law relating to fisheries in the Province of West Pakistan.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of West Pakistan, except the Tribal Areas

The Bahawalpur State Fisheries Act, 1951
metadata.max_penalty: fine not exceeding fifty rupees or composition up to twenty-five rupees
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance consolidates and amends laws regarding fisheries, licensing, and penalties in West Pakistan.
metadata.summary: The West Pakistan Fisheries Ordinance, 1961 was enacted to amend and consolidate the law relating to fisheries in the Province of West Pakistan. It establishes the Director of Fisheries and Inspectors of Fisheries, regulates the use of fishing gear, defines prohibited species and seasons, and sets out penalties for offences such as using explosives or poisons. The Ordinance also provides powers to lease water bodies, issue permits, and compound certain minor offences.

metadata.short_title: The West Pakistan Foodstuffs (Control) Act, 1958
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the continuance of powers to control the supply and distribution of, and trade and commerce in foodstuffs.

metadata.one_line: An Act empowering the Government of West Pakistan to control the supply, distribution, and trade of foodstuffs.
metadata.summary: This Act provides powers to the Government of West Pakistan to regulate the supply, distribution, movement, and trade of foodstuffs. It allows for the issuance of orders to control prices, require licenses, seize property, and punish contraventions with imprisonment or fines. The Act defines specific commodities as foodstuffs and establishes procedures for prosecution and burden of proof.

metadata.short_title: The West Pakistan Goats (Restriction) Ordinance, 1959
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to restrict the number of goats in West Pakistan.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of West Pakistan, except the Tribal Areas
repeals: West Pakistan Ordinance No. XXVII of 1961
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment up to six months or fine up to five hundred rupees or both
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance restricts the number of goats in West Pakistan by regulating grazing, movement, and slaughter.
metadata.summary: The West Pakistan Goats (Restriction) Ordinance, 1959 was promulgated to restrict the number of goats in the Province of West Pakistan. It grants the Government power to declare areas where grazing and keeping goats are unlawful, regulate the movement and slaughter of goats, and make rules for these purposes. The Ordinance establishes penalties including imprisonment, fines, and forfeiture of goats for contraventions, while also providing for summary trial and arrest powers.

name: West Pakistan Government Dues Recovery Ordinance, 1962

metadata.short_title: The West Pakistan Government Dues Recovery Ordinance, 1962
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the recovery of Government dues as arrears of land revenue in the Province of West Pakistan.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of West Pakistan except the Tribal Areas
metadata.administering_body: Government of the Province of West Pakistan
metadata.one_line: Provides for the recovery of government dues as land revenue arrears in West Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance facilitates the recovery of government dues that are treated as arrears of land revenue within West Pakistan. It empowers the Government to issue notifications declaring specific dues recoverable under the Revenue Recoveries Act, 1890. The Ordinance also grants the authority to make rules necessary for giving effect to its provisions and defines key terms such as 'defaulter' and 'Government'.

name: West Pakistan Government Educational and Training Institutions Ordinance, 1960

metadata.short_title: The West Pakistan Government Educational and Training Institutions Ordinance, 1960
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to establish Boards of Governors for Government Educational and Training Institutions in West Pakistan.
metadata.commencement: on such date as may be notified by Government
metadata.one_line: Establishes Boards of Governors to manage government educational and training institutions in West Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes Boards of Governors for government educational and training institutions in West Pakistan to ensure their efficient management and control. The Board is a body corporate with powers to recruit staff, manage property, formulate budgets, and frame regulations subject to government approval. It also provides for the transfer of existing staff and vesting of government property into the Board upon notification.

name: West Pakistan Government Servants Benevolent Fund Ordinance, 1960

metadata.short_title: The West Pakistan Government Servants Benevolent Fund Ordinance, 1960
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to constitute a Benevolent Fund for relief of Government servants and their families.
metadata.commencement: on such date as Government may, by notification, appoint
establishes: West Pakistan Government Servants Benevolent Fund
metadata.one_line: Constitutes a benevolent fund for financial relief of government servants and their families in West Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the West Pakistan Government Servants Benevolent Fund to provide financial relief to government servants and their families. The Fund is divided into two parts for gazetted and non-gazetted servants, financed by compulsory contributions, grants, donations, and investment income. Management is vested in specific Boards of Management responsible for investing funds, sanctioning expenditure, and distributing assistance for deceased servants, invalided-out servants, and exceptional cases.

name: West Pakistan Graveyards (Preservation and Maintenance) Act, 1958

metadata.short_title: The West Pakistan Graveyards (Preservation and Maintenance) Act, 1958
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the preservation and maintenance of graveyards in West Pakistan.
metadata.territorial_extent: the graveyard known as the Miani Sahib Graveyard, Lahore, and any other graveyard in West Pakistan to which provisions are extended by notification
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment up to three months or fine up to one thousand rupees or both
metadata.one_line: This Act provides for the preservation and maintenance of graveyards in West Pakistan, specifically Miani Sahib Graveyard.
metadata.summary: The West Pakistan Graveyards (Preservation and Maintenance) Act, 1958 establishes a Committee and a Tribunal to manage specific graveyards. The Committee investigates encroachments, defines graveyard limits, and prepares management schemes. It empowers the Government to acquire land for graveyards after excluding titles established by the Tribunal. The Act also outlines penalties for unauthorized encroachment or damage to graveyard property.

name: West Pakistan Hindu Women�s Rights to Agricultural Land Ordinance, 1959

metadata.short_title: The West Pakistan Hindu Women's Rights to Agricultural Land Ordinance, 1959
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to consolidate the Hindu Law governing Hindu Women's rights to agricultural land in the Province of West Pakistan.

The Hindu Women's Rights to Property (Sind Extension to Agricultural Land) Act, 1943
metadata.one_line: Consolidates Hindu law regarding widows' rights to agricultural land in West Pakistan and repeals earlier acts.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance consolidates the Hindu Law governing women's rights to agricultural land specifically within the Province of West Pakistan. It applies when a Hindu dies intestate, granting widows shares equivalent to sons under specific schools of law or customary rules. The document defines limited interests known as Hindu women's estates and clarifies partition rights for these widows.

name: West Pakistan Historical Mosques and Shrines Fund Cess Ordinance, 1960

metadata.short_title: The West Pakistan Historical Mosques and Shrines Fund Cess Ordinance, 1960
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the raising of funds for the repair, maintenance and endowment of mosques [and shrines] of historical importance in West Pakistan.

metadata.one_line: Imposes a cess on land revenue and urban property tax to fund the repair and maintenance of historical mosques and shrines in West Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes a mechanism to raise funds specifically for the repair, maintenance, and endowment of historically significant mosques and shrines in West Pakistan. It imposes a cess on land revenue and urban immovable property tax payable by Muslims within the province. The collected funds are placed into a dedicated Fund under Government control, which is utilized for operational expenses and the specific maintenance projects outlined in the Ordinance.

name: West Pakistan Horse-race Betting Tax Act, 1958

metadata.short_title: The West Pakistan Horse-race Betting Tax Act, 1958
metadata.long_title: An Act to consolidate the law relating to the levy of taxes on horse-race betting in West Pakistan.

metadata.one_line: Consolidates laws for levying taxes on horse-race betting in West Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Act consolidates the legal framework for imposing taxes on horse-race betting within West Pakistan. It establishes mechanisms for levying totalizator and betting taxes, defining roles for managers and book-makers, and outlining procedures for assessment and collection. The legislation also repeals earlier betting tax acts from Sindh and Punjab to create a uniform basis for taxation in the province.

name: West Pakistan Industries (Control on Establishment and Enlargement) Ordinance, 1963

metadata.short_title: The West Pakistan Industries (Control on Establishment and Enlargement) Ordinance, 1963

metadata.one_line: This Ordinance regulates the establishment and enlargement of industrial undertakings in West Pakistan requiring government permission.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance provides for the organized and planned growth of industries in West Pakistan by restricting the establishment or enlargement of industrial undertakings without prior written government permission. It grants the Government and the Director powers to obtain information, enter premises, and issue orders to stop unauthorized construction. The text also outlines penalties for contravention, procedures for revision and appeal, and exemptions from its provisions.

The legislation serves to remove the earlier ordinance's provisions within this specific territorial jurisdiction.

metadata.summary: This Act consolidates and amends the laws regarding land-revenue in the Province of West Pakistan. The Act also covers the maintenance of records-of-rights, surveys, boundaries, and the powers of village officers.

name: West Pakistan Maintenance of Public Order Ordinance, 1960

It grants powers to arrest, detain, and control suspected persons, as well as control over publications and entry into the province. The text also establishes procedures for trial, defines specific offences related to sabotage and rumours, and repeals several earlier state-level public safety acts.

The document also outlines procedures for payment, defines key terms like 'employer' and 'Establishment', and repeals earlier maternity benefit acts from Sindh, Bombay, and Punjab.

name: West Pakistan Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1958

metadata.summary: This Act consolidates the laws regarding the imposition of taxes on motor vehicles within the Province of West Pakistan. It establishes obligations for vehicle owners to declare their vehicles and pay quarterly or lifetime taxes, issues licenses, and defines penalties for non-compliance. The Act also provides mechanisms for tax recovery and repeals previous provincial taxation acts.

name: West Pakistan Muslim Personal Law (Shariat) Application Act, 1962

It applies to all questions regarding succession, marriage, divorce, wills, and family relations where the parties are Muslims, overriding any contrary custom or usage. The Act terminates limited estates under customary law held by Muslim females and alters the devolution of property upon the termination of life estates or the death of legatees-in-enjoyment. It also repeals several earlier enactments related to personal law application in Punjab, NWFP, Sind, and princely states.

name: West Pakistan National Calamities (Prevention and Relief) Act, 1958

name: West Pakistan Private Colleges (Management and Control) Ordinance, 1970

It mandates the establishment of a Governing Body for each college, defining its constitution, powers, duties, and the roles of the Principal and teachers. The document outlines procedures for meetings, financial management through a College Fund, and grants exemptions to the Government from legal proceedings regarding actions taken in good faith under the Ordinance.

name: West Pakistan Prohibition of Opium Smoking Ordinance, 1960

The document also repeals several earlier enactments related to opium prohibition in various regions.

metadata.summary: This Act consolidates the legal framework for redeeming and restoring possession of mortgaged lands within the Province of West Pakistan. It empowers the Collector to order redemption upon petition and deposit of dues, while also providing mechanisms for the restitution of possession for long-term usufructuary mortgages. The legislation outlines specific procedures for petitions, deposits, and the extinguishment of mortgage rights, repealing earlier acts applicable to Punjab and N.W.F.P.

metadata.summary: This Ordinance provides for the registration of unrecognized private educational institutions in the Province of West Pakistan to supervise their functioning. It mandates that no such institution shall be established or run without registration, though existing ones have a grace period. The Registering Authority grants certificates upon satisfying conditions regarding location, staff, facilities, and fees, while also outlining penalties for non-compliance.

name: West Pakistan Relief of Indebtedness Ordinance, 1960

The North-West Frontier Province Agriculturists Debtors' Relief Act, 1939
The Sind Agriculturists Relief Act, 1940
metadata.one_line: Amends and consolidates laws providing relief to indebted agriculturalists in West Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends and consolidates the law relating to the relief of indebtedness in the Province of West Pakistan. It defines specific categories of debtors, primarily those engaged in agriculture with limited assets, and grants them protections against arrest and attachment of essential property like houses and milch animals. The document empowers courts to limit recoverable interest, order payment by instalments, and allows for deposits in court to stop interest accumulation.

name: West Pakistan Requisitioning of Stage Carriages (Temporary) Ordinance, 1970

metadata.short_title: The West Pakistan Requisitioning of Stage Carriages (Temporary Powers) Ordinance, 1970
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for requisitioning of stage carriages.

metadata.one_line: This Ordinance empowers District Magistrates in West Pakistan to requisition stage carriages for maintaining passenger transport services.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance provides legal authority for the temporary requisitioning of stage carriages in West Pakistan to maintain passenger transport services. It grants District Magistrates the power to order the requisitioning of motor vehicles, manage their maintenance and repair costs, and pay compensation to owners at a rate of fifty rupees per diem. The document also outlines procedures for appeals to the Commissioner, powers to search and seize vehicles, penalties for sabotage or contravention, and protections for actions taken in good faith under the Ordinance.

metadata.short_title: The West Pakistan Requisitioned Land (Continuance) Act, 1958
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the continuance of certain powers in relation to requisitioned land.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of West Pakistan, except the Tribal Areas

metadata.max_penalty: punishment under sections 176 and 177 of the Pakistan Penal Code, 1860
metadata.one_line: Continues requisition powers in West Pakistan and provides for compensation and acquisition of requisitioned land.
metadata.summary: This Act ensures the continuance of requisition powers over immovable property previously requisitioned under the Defence of India Act, 1939. It allows the Provincial Government to use or deal with such lands, release them from requisition, or acquire them if specific conditions regarding works constructed or restoration costs are met. The Act also outlines procedures for releasing possession, determining compensation based on existing rules, and protecting government actions taken in good faith.

name: West Pakistan Rice (Restrictions on Cultivation) Ordinance, 1959

metadata.short_title: The West Pakistan Rice (Restrictions on Cultivation) Ordinance, 1959
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to regulate the cultivation of rice in the Province of West Pakistan.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of West Pakistan, except the Tribal Areas
metadata.max_penalty: fine extending to ten times the land revenue assessment chargeable for the crop or simple imprisonment not exceeding six months or both
metadata.one_line: Regulates rice cultivation in West Pakistan to prevent land damage from water-logging and salinity.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance regulates the cultivation of rice in the Province of West Pakistan to check the increase of water-logging, salinity, and seepage which cause damage to land. It empowers the Board of Revenue to prohibit or impose restrictions on rice cultivation in specified areas while allowing cultivators to gather standing crops before such notifications. The Ordinance also provides for relaxing restrictions for reclamation operations, defines key terms like 'Board of Revenue' and 'Government', and establishes penalties for contravention along with specific jurisdictional limits for civil courts.

name: West Pakistan Shops and Establishments Ordinance, 1969

metadata.short_title: The West Pakistan Shops and Establishments Ordinance, 1969
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend and consolidate the law relating to the hours and other conditions of work and employment of persons employed in shops and commercial, industrial and other establishments in West Pakistan and matters connected therewith.
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance consolidates laws regarding working hours, conditions of employment, and leave for shops and establishments in West Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends and consolidates the law relating to work hours and employment conditions for persons in shops, commercial, industrial, and other establishments. It defines key terms such as 'employee', 'employer', and 'commercial establishment', while regulating daily and weekly working hours, overtime pay, leave entitlements, and the prohibition of child employment. The document also establishes a system for registering establishments, appointing inspectors to enforce compliance, and maintaining records.

name: West Pakistan Small Industries Corporation (Dissolution) Act, 1972

metadata.short_title: The West Pakistan Small Industries Corporation (Dissolution) Act, 1972
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the dissolution of the West Pakistan Small Industries Corporation.
repeals: The West Pakistan Small Industries Corporation Ordinance, 1972 (XXIV of 1972)
metadata.one_line: This Act dissolves the West Pakistan Small Industries Corporation and transfers its assets and employees to the Provinces.
metadata.summary: The Act provides for the dissolution of the West Pakistan Small Industries Corporation established under the 1965 Ordinance. It authorizes the President to transfer the Corporation's projects, properties, and liabilities to the various Provinces before the appointed day. Additionally, it facilitates the transfer of the Corporation's employees to the respective Provinces on terms determined by the President.

name: West Pakistan Survey and Rectangulation of Lands Ordinance, 1959

metadata.short_title: The West Pakistan Survey and Rectangulation of Lands Ordinance, 1959

metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees or with both
metadata.one_line: Provides for the survey and rectangulation of lands in West Pakistan, excluding Tribal Areas.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance authorizes the Board of Revenue to direct surveys and rectangulations of land within West Pakistan. It outlines the assessment and recovery of costs from affected landowners while allowing for partial or full remission by the Provincial Government. The text establishes penalties for obstructing operations and grants indemnity to public servants acting in good faith, while barring civil court jurisdiction over related claims.

metadata.short_title: The West Pakistan Tobacco Vend Act, 1958

metadata.summary: This Act consolidates the law regarding the regulation of retail sales of manufactured tobacco in urban areas within West Pakistan to protect public health. It establishes a licensing system where dealers must obtain a licence from the Collector, subject to fees and conditions set by the Commissioner. The Act defines key terms such as 'manufactured tobacco' and 'urban area', outlines penalties for unlicensed dealing or breach of licence conditions, and grants investigation powers to Excise officers.

name: West Pakistan Tolls on Roads and Bridges Ordinance, 1962

metadata.short_title: The West Pakistan Tolls on Roads and Bridges Ordinance, 1962

metadata.one_line: This Ordinance consolidates and amends laws regarding tolls on roads and bridges in West Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance provides the legal framework for levying, collecting, and managing tolls on public roads and bridges in West Pakistan. It empowers the Government to set up toll gates, lease out toll collection rights, and impose penalties for non-payment or unlawful acts. The document also outlines procedures for cancelling leases, compensating lessees, and seizing vehicles for unpaid tolls.

metadata.short_title: The West Pakistan Undesirable Companies Ordinance, 1959

metadata.summary: This Ordinance prohibits the registration of companies in West Pakistan that carry on business for specified undesirable purposes, such as lottery schemes. It mandates the immediate cessation of functioning, deposit of assets, and winding up of existing undesirable companies upon commencement. The text empowers the registrar to call for information, inspect documents, seize assets, and take over management of offending companies, while defining specific offences and penalties for contravention.

metadata.summary: This Act consolidates the legal framework for levying a tax on urban immovable property within the Province of West Pakistan. It establishes the authority responsible for assessment, defines the annual value calculation methods, and sets specific tax rates with provisions for owner-occupied buildings. The legislation outlines exemptions for government properties, educational institutions, and low-value holdings, while detailing procedures for valuation lists, appeals, and tax recovery.

metadata.summary: This Ordinance consolidates the law relating to usurious loans in the Province of West Pakistan. It applies to suits for loan recovery, enforcement of security, or redemption of security instituted after its commencement. The document empowers courts to re-open transactions where interest is deemed excessive or the transaction was substantially unfair, allowing relief for debtors and ordering repayment of excessive amounts.

metadata.summary: The West Pakistan Vaccination Ordinance, 1958 was enacted to consolidate and amend the law relating to vaccination within the Province of West Pakistan. It imposes a duty on local authorities and Smallpox Eradication Officers to enforce vaccination provisions for all unprotected children and persons. The document defines key terms such as 'child', 'guardian', and 'vaccination', outlines procedures for certificates of protection or unfitness, and prescribes punishments for breaches of the Ordinance.

metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends and consolidates the law relating to vagrancy in the Province of West Pakistan. It establishes welfare homes for the detention and rehabilitation of vagrants and their dependents, excluding those with contagious diseases or mental conditions. The document defines key terms such as 'vagrant' and 'public place', grants police powers to arrest and search, and outlines procedures for trial, sentence, and appeal. It also repeals the Sind Vagrancy Act, 1947.

metadata.short_title: The White Phosphorus Matches Prohibition Act, 1913

metadata.summary: This Act prohibits the importation, manufacture, and sale of matches containing white phosphorus. It grants inspectors the power to take samples from manufacturers and imposes fines for violations or refusal to allow inspection. The law applies to the whole of Pakistan with specific commencement dates for different sections.

name: Wild Birds and Animals Protection Act, 1912

metadata.summary: This Act provides for the protection and preservation of certain wild birds and animals in their natural state. It empowers Provincial Governments to declare close times during which capturing, killing, or trading these species is unlawful. The legislation outlines penalties for contraventions, provisions for confiscation of seized items, and exceptions for scientific research or defence of property.

metadata.summary: This Act regulates the possession of wireless telegraphy apparatus in Pakistan. It prohibits possession without a license issued by the Director General, Pakistan Post Office or authorized officers. The Federal Government has powers to exempt persons, make rules, search for unlicensed apparatus, and confiscate it. Penalties include fines for first and subsequent offences.

name: Witness Protection, Security and Benefit Act, 2017

metadata.summary: This Act provides for the protection, security, and benefit programs for witnesses involved in serious offences. It establishes a Witness Protection Advisory Board to advise on policies and oversee the Witness Protection Unit, which is responsible for implementing the program. The Act outlines various measures such as identity changes, relocation, financial assistance, and security arrangements for protected persons and their families.

metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Women in Distress and Detention Fund to provide financial and legal aid to females needing assistance due to detention or litigation. The Federal Government is responsible for establishing the Fund, which receives contributions from various sources including government grants and international agencies. A Board of Governors manages the Fund's affairs, with powers to sanction disbursements, appoint staff, and manage properties. The Act also provides tax exemptions for contributions to the Fund.

metadata.short_title: Women's University Ordinance, 1985

It incorporates the University as a body corporate with perpetual succession and grants it powers to provide instruction, conduct examinations, confer degrees, and affiliate colleges. The document outlines the composition of various authorities including the Syndicate, Academic Council, and Finance and Planning Committee, while also providing for the establishment of research centers and discipline committees.

metadata.short_title: The Workers' Children (Education) Ordinance, 1972
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the education of workers' children and matters ancillary thereto.
metadata.one_line: Provides for free education of workers' children and levies an education cess on employers.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes a framework to provide free education up to Matric level for the children of workers employed in establishments with ten or more workers. It mandates employers to pay an annual education cess calculated per worker, which is collected and administered by the Provincial Government or designated agencies like the Social Security Institution. The funds raised are used exclusively to cover educational costs including textbooks and fees for selected children.

metadata.short_title: The Workers' Welfare Fund Ordinance, 1971

metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Workers' Welfare Fund to provide residential accommodation and other facilities for workers. It defines the composition of the Fund, including initial contributions from the Federal Government and payments from industrial establishments. The Ordinance creates a Governing Body to manage the fund and sets out procedures for payment recovery, rule-making powers, and tax exemptions.

metadata.short_title: The Workmen's Compensation Act, 1923

metadata.one_line: Provides for payment of compensation to workmen injured by accident by certain employers.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the liability of certain employers to pay compensation to their workmen for injuries caused by accidents. It defines key terms such as 'workman', 'employer', and 'dependent', and outlines methods for calculating wages and compensation amounts. The Act also provides for the appointment of Commissioners to handle claims, procedures for fatal accident reporting, and specific provisions regarding poisoning cases.

metadata.short_title: The Works of Defence Act, 1903
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for imposing restrictions upon the use and enjoyment of land in the vicinity of works of defence in order that such land may be kept free from buildings an other obstructions, and for determining the amount of compensation to be made on account of such imposition.

metadata.summary: This Act provides a legal framework to impose restrictions on land use near military, naval, or air force works of defence to prevent obstructions. It establishes the powers of the Collector to declare restrictions, assess damages, and determine compensation amounts through inquiry and court proceedings. The legislation also outlines procedures for appeals, exemptions from stamp duty, and the enforcement of terms by magistrates.

name: Zainab Alert, Response and Recovery Act, 2020

It defines key terms such as 'Alert', 'Abduction', and 'Child' and outlines the powers and functions of ZARRA and the ICT Child Protection Advisory Board. The Act mandates coordination between ZARRA, local police stations, and other governmental agencies to ensure rapid response and recovery operations.

metadata.short_title: The Zakat and Ushr Ordinance, 1980

metadata.summary: The Zakat and Ushr Ordinance, 1980 establishes a legal framework for the assessment, collection, and distribution of Zakat and Ushr in accordance with Shariah principles. It applies to Muslim citizens of Pakistan and creates various administrative bodies, including Central and Provincial Zakat Councils, to manage these funds. The Ordinance outlines specific rates for different assets like agricultural produce, livestock, and financial investments, while also providing mechanisms for exemptions and declarations by individuals who do not wish to pay.

metadata.short_title: The Carriage by Air Act, 1934

metadata.summary: The Carriage by Air Act, 1934 enables Pakistan to accede to the 1929 Warsaw Convention on international carriage by air. It applies rules concerning passenger tickets, luggage, air consignment notes, and carrier liability for death, destruction, loss, or delay. The Act also provides for combined carriage and specifies that it extends to the whole of Pakistan with commencement by Federal Government notification.

metadata.short_title: The Federal Court Act, 1937

metadata.summary: This Act confers supplemental power upon the Federal Court to make rules for regulating the service of processes issued by the Court. It specifically addresses scenarios where an appeal has been preferred to the Supreme Court, requiring a High Court to serve processes issued by the Supreme Court in connection with that appeal. The legislation was enacted to enable the Court to more effectively exercise jurisdiction under the Government of India Act, 1935.

metadata.short_title: The Arbitration (Protocol and Convention) Act, 1937

It enables the Protocol on Arbitration Clauses and the Convention on the Execution of Foreign Arbitral Awards to become operative by defining foreign awards and conditions for their enforcement. The Act allows courts to stay proceedings when matters are referred to arbitration and outlines the evidence required for enforcing foreign awards.

It empowers the Federal Government to appoint various census officers responsible for collecting specific data on land ownership, crop production, livestock, and employment. The Act outlines procedures for information collection, including access to premises and compensation for crop-cutting experiments, while defining penalties for obstruction or false returns.

The document outlines specific duties for census officers, penalties for non-compliance or providing false information, and provisions for prosecution under other laws.

metadata.summary: The Trade Organizations Ordinance, 1961 provides for the regulation and control of trade organizations in Pakistan. It mandates that no trade organization can be registered under the Companies Act without a licence granted by the Federal Government. The Ordinance establishes the Director of Trade Organizations to oversee these entities, restricts their names, controls their internal amendments, and imposes penalties for contraventions.

metadata.summary: The Carriage by Air (International Convention) Act, 1966 gives legal force in Pakistan to the Warsaw Convention as amended at The Hague in 1955. It applies rules concerning international carriage of persons, baggage, or goods performed by aircraft for reward and establishes liability limits for carriers. The Act also provides mechanisms for suits against High Contracting Parties, handles cases involving the death of a passenger, and allows the Federal Government to apply these rules to non-international carriage with specified modifications.

metadata.short_title: The Carriage by Air (Supplementary Convention) Act, 1968
metadata.long_title: An Act to give effect in Pakistan to the Convention, Supplementary to the Warsaw Convention, for the Unification of Certain Rules Relating to International Carriage by Air performed by a Person Other than the Contracting Carrier.
metadata.commencement: at once; deemed to have taken effect on 19th September, 1965
amends: The Carriage by Air (International Convention) Act, 1966
metadata.one_line: Gives effect in Pakistan to the Supplementary Convention on International Carriage by Air performed by a person other than the Contracting Carrier.
metadata.summary: This Act gives legal force in Pakistan to the Convention supplementary to the Warsaw Convention regarding international air carriage. It applies to any such carriage regardless of the aircraft's nationality and supplements existing Pakistani air carriage laws from 1934 and 1966. The rules define the roles and liabilities of contracting carriers versus actual carriers, establish jurisdiction for legal actions, and set limits on liability for cargo damage.

metadata.short_title: The War Risks Insurance Continuance Ordinance, 1969
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the continuance of the War Risks Insurance Fund established under the War Risk Insurance Ordinance, 1965, and of the provisions of that Ordinance relating to the Fund.
metadata.commencement: on the day on which the War Risks Insurance Ordinance, 1965 ceases to have effect under clause (7) of Article 30 the Constitution
key_definitions: said Ordinance (referring to War Risk Insurance Ordinance, 1965)
metadata.one_line: Continues the War Risks Insurance Fund and related provisions after the expiry of the 1965 Ordinance.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance provides for the continuance of the War Risks Insurance Fund established under the War Risk Insurance Ordinance, 1965. It ensures that all sums paid into or out of the fund and liabilities incurred before its commencement remain valid. The provisions continue in force regarding appointments, schemes, rules, and orders related to the fund and pre-commencement liabilities.

metadata.short_title: The Equity Participation Fund Ordinance, 1970
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the establishment of an Equity Participation Fund.
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Equity Participation Fund to promote private sector investment in less developed areas.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Equity Participation Fund as a body corporate to promote and generate investment in the private sector, specifically targeting entrepreneurs in less developed areas. The Fund is managed by the Industrial Development Bank of Pakistan under the direction of a Board of Directors. It outlines the fund's share capital structure, borrowing powers, accounting requirements, and exemptions from certain taxes and duties.

metadata.short_title: The Development of Industries (Federal Control) Act, 1972
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for certain matters relating to the development of industries under Federal control.
repeals: Ordinance XXXVI of 1972
metadata.one_line: This Act establishes the Board of Industrial Management to oversee federal control over specified industries.
metadata.summary: The Development of Industries (Federal Control) Act, 1972 provides for federal control over specific industries such as iron and steel, heavy engineering, and public utilities. It establishes the Board of Industrial Management, a body corporate with powers to manage establishments efficiently and ensure sound business principles. The Act creates a fund to cover the Board's expenses and grants the Federal Government authority to issue directions and appoint officers.

metadata.short_title: The National Development Finance Corporation Act, 1973
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of the National Development Finance Corporation.
metadata.one_line: Establishes the National Development Finance Corporation and defines its powers, structure, and functions.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the National Development Finance Corporation as a body corporate with perpetual succession. It outlines the composition of the Board of Directors, share capital structure, and borrowing powers for eligible enterprises. The Act also grants tax exemptions to the Corporation and empowers it to make rules and regulations to carry out its purposes.

name: Marketing of Petroleum Products (Federal Control) Act,1974

metadata.short_title: The Marketing of Petroleum Products (Federal Control) Act, 1974
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the management and development of marketing facilities in petroleum products.
metadata.one_line: This Act empowers the Federal Government to take over management and acquire shares of petroleum marketing companies.
metadata.summary: The Marketing of Petroleum Products (Federal Control) Act, 1974 provides for the management and development of marketing facilities in petroleum products. It empowers the Federal Government to take over the management or acquire shares of any marketing company if deemed necessary in the public interest. The Act establishes a Board of Management, defines key terms related to petroleum products and companies, and outlines procedures for compensation upon acquisition of shares.

name: President's Salary Allowances and Privileges Act, 1975

metadata.short_title: The President's Salary, Allowances and Privileges Act, 1975
metadata.long_title: An Act to determine the salary, allowances and privileges of the President.
metadata.one_line: This Act determines the salary, allowances, and privileges of the President of Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the financial compensation and official privileges for the President of Pakistan. It defines specific terms such as 'family', 'furnishings', and 'maintenance' to clarify entitlements regarding official residences, vehicles, and aircraft. The legislation also outlines provisions for discretionary grants, medical facilities, provident funds, and exemptions from certain customs duties.

metadata.short_title: The Representation of the People Act, 1976
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the conduct of elections to the National Assembly and the Provincial Assemblies.
repeals: The National and Provincial Assemblies (Elections) Ordinance, 1970 (XIII of 1970)
The National and Provincial Assemblies (Elections to Reserved Seats) Act, 1976 (XVIII of 1976)
metadata.one_line: Provides for the conduct of elections to National and Provincial Assemblies, guards against corrupt practices, and determines election disputes.
metadata.summary: This Act governs the conduct of general and bye-elections to the National Assembly and Provincial Assemblies in Pakistan. It establishes the Election Commission and outlines procedures for nomination, polling, voting, and result declaration. The legislation also defines corrupt and illegal practices, sets penalties for offences, and provides mechanisms for election petitions and tribunals to resolve disputes.

metadata.short_title: The Capital Territory Local Government Ordinance, 1979
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the constitution of Local Government institutions in the Capital Territory.
metadata.territorial_extent: the rural areas of the Capital Territory
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance establishes Local Government institutions in the rural areas of the Capital Territory.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance provides for the constitution, composition, and election of Union Councils in the rural areas of the Capital Territory. It outlines their executive powers, functions, local taxation, and administration of services including animal control and public health regulations. The document also details offences, penalties, and provisions for supervision and coordination between councils.

name: National Tariff Commission Act, 1990 (Repealed by Act XII of 2015)

metadata.short_title: The National Tariff Commission Act, 1990
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of the National Tariff Commission and for matters connected therewith or ancillary thereto

metadata.max_penalty: fine not exceeding fifty thousand rupees or imprisonment up to three months
metadata.one_line: Establishes the National Tariff Commission to advise on tariff measures and industry protection.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the National Tariff Commission as a body corporate to advise the Federal Government on tariff measures, industry protection, and export promotion. The Commission consists of a Chairman and two members appointed by the Federal Government and has powers of a civil court for its inquiries. It operates with funds from the Federal Government, fees, and international aid, submitting reports within 120 days.

name: Supreme Court Judges (Leave, Pension and Privileges) Order, 1997

metadata.short_title: The Supreme Court Judges (Leave, Pension and Privileges) Order, 1997
repeals: The Supreme Court Judges (Leave, Pension and Privileges) Order, 1968
metadata.one_line: This Order regulates leave, pension, privileges, and allowances for Judges of the Supreme Court of Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Order determines the privileges, allowances, rights regarding leave of absence, and pension entitlements for every Judge of the Supreme Court. It establishes rules for various types of leave, leave accounts, salary rates during leave, and official facilities such as residence, cars, and security guards. The document also outlines pension commutation, subsidiary conditions of service, income tax exemptions, and family gratuities for widows and children of retired or deceased Judges.

metadata.short_title: The Marriages (Prohibition of Wasteful Expenses) Act, 1997
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the prohibition of wasteful expenses on marriages and ceremonies related thereto
metadata.commencement: on the sixteenth day of March, 1997 and shall remain in force a period of two years from its commencement
metadata.status_evidence: It shall come in to force on the sixteenth day of March, 1997 and shall remain in force a period of two years from its commencement.
metadata.max_penalty: fine not less than one hundred thousand rupees and not more than three hundred thousand rupees
metadata.one_line: This Act prohibits wasteful expenses on marriages, restricts decorations and fireworks, and establishes Ehtesab Committees for enforcement.
metadata.summary: The Marriages (Prohibition of Wasteful Expenses) Act, 1997 aims to curb extravagant spending on wedding ceremonies across Pakistan. It bans the use of lights, fireworks, and explosives during celebrations while allowing only necessary lighting and soft drinks at public venues like hotels and restaurants. The Act empowers Provincial Governments to establish Ehtesab Committees in each sub-division to enforce these restrictions and imposes fines for violations.

metadata.summary: This Order is made by the President under powers conferred by the Fifth Schedule to the Constitution of Pakistan. It specifies the monthly salary for the Chief Justice of Pakistan and other Supreme Court judges, as well as the Chief Justices and other judges of High Courts. The salaries are set at Rs.43,000 and Rs.40,000 for the Supreme Court, and Rs.39,000 and Rs.38,000 for High Courts respectively.

metadata.summary: This Ordinance regulates the business of the insurance industry in Pakistan to ensure the protection of policy holder interests. It establishes a Commission to oversee insurers, mandates registration, sets solvency and capital requirements, and governs reinsurance arrangements. The document also defines roles for intermediaries like agents and brokers, outlines market conduct rules, and provides mechanisms for amalgamation and claims settlement.

name: Adhoc Members of the shariat Appellate Bench (Allowance for Attending of Sittings) Order, 2000

metadata.long_title: AN ORDER to provide for payment of allowance to ad hoc members of the Shariat Appellate Bench
metadata.one_line: Provides allowances and privileges for ad hoc members attending the Shariat Appellate Bench.
metadata.summary: This Order prescribes financial allowances and privileges for ad hoc members appointed from the panel of Ulema to attend sittings of the Shariat Appellate Bench. It grants a daily sitting allowance capped at one month's salary of a Supreme Court Judge, plus travelling and accommodation benefits equivalent to those of a Judge. The provisions come into force immediately upon promulgation by the President under Article 203F of the Constitution.

metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Removal from Service (Special Powers) Ordinance, 2000 to provide legal protections for authorities acting in good faith. It grants immunity against suits or prosecutions for actions taken under the Ordinance and bars courts from questioning orders made by the competent authority. The provisions also prevent injunctions regarding decisions made pursuant to powers conferred by this legislation.

metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes a comprehensive framework for local governments within the Islamabad Capital Territory. It creates various tiers of administration including Zila Councils, Union Councils, Village Councils, and Neighbourhood Councils, along with specific bodies like the Citizen Community Board and Musalihat Anjuman for dispute resolution. The document outlines the composition, functions, powers, and financial mechanisms for these local bodies while defining electoral processes and administrative responsibilities.

metadata.one_line: This Ordinance mandates compulsory primary education for children in the Islamabad Capital Territory and establishes penalties for non-compliance.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance provides for compulsory primary education within the Islamabad Capital Territory. It defines key terms such as 'child' (ages 5-10) and 'primary school', and establishes a Union Committee on Education to oversee attendance. Parents are legally required to ensure their children attend school, with specific exemptions for illness or lack of nearby schools. The document outlines offences for parents or employers who fail to comply with attendance orders, punishable by fines.

metadata.short_title: The Finance Act, 2011
metadata.long_title: An Act to give effect to the financial proposals of the Federal Government for the year beginning on the first day of July, 2011 and to amend certain laws.
metadata.commencement: on the first day of July, 2011
amends: The Members of Parliament (Salaries and Allowances) Act, 1974
metadata.one_line: This Act gives effect to the Federal Government's financial proposals for 2011 and amends various tax and parliamentary laws.
metadata.summary: The Finance Act, 2011 implements the Federal Government's financial proposals for the fiscal year beginning July 1, 2011. It amends several existing statutes including the Customs Act, Sales Tax Act, and Members of Parliament Salaries Act to adjust duties, allowances, and tax provisions. The Act also introduces new transit fees and modifies rules regarding input tax adjustments and inland revenue inspections.

name: Salary of Judges of Superior Court Order, 2013

metadata.short_title: Salary of Judges of Superior Courts Order, 2013
metadata.long_title: An Order
metadata.commencement: at once and deemed to have taken effect on and from the first day of July, 2013
repeals: Salary of Judges of Superior Courts Order, 2013 (P.O. No. 1 of 2013)
metadata.status_evidence: The Salary of Judges of Superior Courts Order, 2013 (P.O. No. 1 of 2013), is hereby repealed.
key_definitions: Chief Justice of a High Court
metadata.one_line: This Order sets salaries for superior court judges and repeals a previous order.
metadata.summary: This Order determines the monthly salaries for the Chief Justice of Pakistan, other Supreme Court Judges, Chief Justices of High Courts, and other High Court Judges. It exercises powers conferred by the Fifth Schedule to the Constitution regarding judicial remuneration. The Order comes into force immediately but is deemed effective from July 1, 2013, and explicitly repeals a previous order numbered P.O. No. 1 of 2013.

name: Salary of Judges of Superior Court Order, 2015

metadata.short_title: Salary of Judges of Superior Courts Order, 2015
metadata.commencement: at once and deemed to have taken effect on and from the first day of July, 2014
repeals: Salary of Judges of Superior Courts Order, 2013 (P.O. No. 6 of 2013)
metadata.one_line: Sets the monthly salaries for judges of the Supreme Court and High Courts effective July 1, 2014.
metadata.summary: This Order prescribes the specific monthly salaries to be paid to the Chief Justice of Pakistan, other Supreme Court Judges, the Chief Justices of High Courts, and other High Court Judges. It derives its authority from the Fifth Schedule of the Constitution regarding judicial remuneration. The Order came into force immediately but is deemed effective from July 1, 2014, and it repeals the previous Salary of Judges of Superior Courts Order, 2013.

name: Auditor General (Term and Condition of Service) Order, 2015

metadata.short_title: The Advocate-General (Terms and Conditions of Service) Order, 2015
metadata.long_title: An Order to appoint an Advocate-General for Islamabad Capital Territory and to provide for matters connected therewith and ancillary thereto
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Islamabad Capital Territory
metadata.parent_law: Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan
metadata.one_line: This Order appoints the Advocate-General for Islamabad Capital Territory and defines their terms of service.
metadata.summary: This Order appoints an Advocate-General for the Islamabad Capital Territory to provide legal advice to the Provincial Government. The document outlines the qualifications required, the tenure during the pleasure of the President, and specific salary and allowances. It also grants the Federal Government power to make rules for matters not covered in the Order.

metadata.short_title: The Public Interest Disclosures Act, 2017
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide a mechanism for public interest disclosures and protection of persons making such disclosures
metadata.one_line: Provides a mechanism for public interest disclosures and protects persons making them in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes a legal framework for making public interest disclosures to prevent corruption and protect whistleblowers. It defines the roles of the Competent Authority, complainants, and organizations covered, including both public and specified private sector entities. The legislation outlines procedures for inquiries, protections against adverse actions, exemptions from disclosure regarding national security, and penalties for false or frivolous complaints.

name: Transgender Persons (Protection and Rights) Act, 2018 (Act No_ XIII of 2018)

metadata.short_title: The Transgender Persons (Protection and Rights) Act, 2018
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for protection, relief and rehabilitation of rights of the transgender persons and their welfare and for matters connected therewith and incidental thereto
establishes: National Commission for Status of Women
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment up to six months or fine up to fifty thousand rupees or both
metadata.one_line: This Act protects the rights, welfare, and identity of transgender persons in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: The Transgender Persons (Protection and Rights) Act, 2018 provides for the protection, relief, and rehabilitation of transgender persons in Pakistan. It recognizes their self-perceived gender identity and grants them rights to education, employment, healthcare, property, and fundamental rights without discrimination or harassment. The Act establishes an enforcement mechanism involving the Federal Ombudsman, National Commission for Status of Women, and NCHR to address grievances.

metadata.short_title: The National University of Technology Act, 2018
metadata.long_title: An Act to set up National University of Technology at Islamabad
metadata.one_line: Establishes the National University of Technology at Islamabad with perpetual succession and research facilities.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the National University of Technology at Islamabad to promote applied research, development, and training in science, engineering, and technology. The University is a body corporate with the power to acquire property and set up campuses within Pakistan and abroad. It defines various authorities including the Chancellor, Board of Governors, Rector, Syndicate, and Academic Council to manage academic and administrative affairs.

metadata.short_title: The National Civic Education Commission Act, 2018
metadata.long_title: An ACT to provide for and promote Civic Education and create awareness relating to fundamental rights and obligations of citizens
metadata.one_line: Establishes the National Civic Education Commission to promote civic competence and awareness of fundamental rights in Islamabad.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the National Civic Education Commission to foster civic competence and responsibility among citizens. The Commission is tasked with educating people on fundamental rights, developing courses for constitutional objectives, and promoting values like unity, tolerance, and respect for laws. It applies specifically to the Islamabad Capital Territory and involves a Board of Governors comprising members from Parliament, Provincial Assemblies, media, and experts.

metadata.short_title: The Apprenticeship Act, 2018
metadata.long_title: An Act to make provisions for promoting, developing and regulating systematic apprenticeship programmes in the establishments for securing certain minimum standards of skill and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
metadata.territorial_extent: such areas in the Federation as are not included in any province
repeals: The Apprenticeship Ordinance, 1962 (LVI of 1962)
metadata.administering_body: National Vocational and Technical Training Commission (NTVTC)
metadata.one_line: This Act regulates systematic apprenticeship programmes to ensure minimum skill standards for employers and apprentices.
metadata.summary: The Apprenticeship Act, 2018 establishes a legal framework for promoting and regulating apprenticeship training in establishments across Pakistan. It defines the roles of employers and apprentices, mandates written contracts, and sets stipend requirements at a minimum of fifty percent of federal minimum wages. The Act creates an apprenticeship fund to support training costs and establishes committees to monitor compliance. It also provides mechanisms for terminating contracts, resolving disputes, and exempting establishments during natural calamities.

name: West Pakistan Prohibition of Smoking in Cinema Houses (Repeal)Act, 2019

metadata.short_title: The West Pakistan Prohibition of Smoking in Cinema Houses (Repeal) Act, 2019
metadata.long_title: An Act to repeal the West Pakistan Prohibition of Smoking in Cinema Houses Ordinance, 1960 to the extent of Islamabad Capital Territory
repeals: West Pakistan Prohibition of Smoking in Cinema Houses Ordinance, 1960
metadata.status_evidence: to repeal the West Pakistan Prohibition of Smoking in Cinema Houses Ordinance, 1960 (Ordinance No. IV of 1960) to the extent of Islamabad Capital Territory
metadata.one_line: Repeals the West Pakistan Prohibition of Smoking in Cinema Houses Ordinance, 1960 within Islamabad Capital Territory.
metadata.summary: This Act repeals the West Pakistan Prohibition of Smoking in Cinema Houses Ordinance, 1960 specifically for the Islamabad Capital Territory. It was enacted by Parliament on January 31, 2019, and came into force immediately. The legislation removes the previous prohibition on smoking in cinema houses within this specific territory.

metadata.short_title: Transfer of Railways (Amendment) Ordinance, 2025
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance further to amend the Transfer of Railways Order, 1962
amends: Transfer of Railways Order, 1962 (P.O. No. 33 of 1962)
metadata.one_line: Amends the Transfer of Railways Order, 1962 to regulate track access for private parties.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Transfer of Railways Order, 1962 to facilitate private party access to the Pakistan Railways network. It establishes a regulatory framework where the Board oversees track access agreements for freight and passenger services while protecting defence traffic priorities. The document also clarifies the roles of the Board and Railways Division regarding agreement approvals and dispute resolution.

name: Pakistan Nursing and Midwifery Council Ordinance, 2025

metadata.short_title: Pakistan Nursing and Midwifery Council Ordinance, 2025
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend and consolidate the laws relating to registration and training of nurses, nurse practitioners, midwives, midwifery associate and nurse auxiliaries
repeals: Pakistan Nursing Council Act, 2023 (V of 2023)
establishes: Provincial and Regional Nursing and Midwifery Examination Board
Pakistan Nursing and Midwifery Council Fund
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance amends and consolidates laws regarding the registration and training of nurses and midwives in Pakistan.
metadata.summary: The Pakistan Nursing and Midwifery Council Ordinance, 2025 is an Ordinance promulgated by the President to amend and consolidate existing laws concerning the registration, licensing, and training of nursing and midwifery professionals. It establishes the Pakistan Nursing and Midwifery Council along with Provincial and Regional Examination Boards and a dedicated Fund. The Ordinance applies to the whole of Pakistan and comes into force immediately upon publication.

name: Defence Industrial Production and Regulatory Authority of Pakistan Ordinance, 2026

metadata.short_title: Defence Industrial Production and Regulatory Authority of Pakistan Ordinance, 2026
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for establishment of Defence Industrial Production and Regulatory Authority
establishes: Defence Industrial Production and Regulatory Authority of Pakistan
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Defence Industrial Production and Regulatory Authority to oversee Pakistan's defence industrial sector.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Defence Industrial Production and Regulatory Authority of Pakistan to supervise, oversee, and regulate the defence industrial sector. It aims to enhance national security, defence preparedness, and technological sovereignty by integrating public and private sectors. The Authority is empowered to manage subsidiaries, issue regulations, and ensure compliance with policies related to defence production and procurement.
